review_text:
Overall a Pleasant Game.

I played Sniper Elite 4 back in January and absolutely loved it. I waited for the Steam Summer Sale and grabbed the full game, honestly the main campaign is worth the full price, but I wouldn’t say the DLCs are. The DLC maps feel either uninspired or empty, adding little to the overall experience. So unless you're after special weapons or skins, the best value is to buy the main game solo.

For gameplay, the mechanics feel similar to the previous game, the battlefield has moved from Italy to France. At first you're limited to regular ammo, but as progress there will be non-lethal, suppressed, armor-piercing rounds, which are useful for quieter takedowns or vehicles. Since you can't keep enough ammo to fully clear a map, you’ll need to scavenge from enemies or search workbenches (which also offer weapon upgrades), unless you play stealth pass or melee kills. But after all Sniper Elite is all about taking out Nazis, not like Splinter Cell or Hitman franchise where the focus is on avoiding kills. That said, I find it odd that the system scores higher for knocking Nazis unconscious instead of killing them. But I reached max level 40 before starting the last main campaign, so it seems playstyle doesn’t matter in the end.

Speaking of level up, I recommend fully exploring maps. Most optional missions won’t appear until you're close to the mission area or gathered enough intel. You'll also need tools like a wrench, bolt cutter and crowbar to infiltrate certain areas, and most importantly, dynamite for destroying safe doors, AA guns or Panzers. While Instinct highlights these tools, you’ll still need to get close to locate them.

My favorite map is Spy Academy. It offers a fantastic sniper spot near the camp, allowing a great view of the entire basilica-town across a long bridge. With a long range, big scope powerful rifle, empty the clip is incredibly satisfying, and I earned the 500+ meter shot medal. Just be patient, and manage the bullet drop. As you pass the bridge or go underneath it, the sea-shore town is filled with details, there are always multiple paths to explore. This map is like some of the Italy maps from the previous game, and the basilica (Spy Academy) is a stunning Gothic structure. The stained glass inside looks amazing when you climb to the top and enter photo mode, and the flying buttresses outside are excellent. The level encourages thorough exploration as the meeting point is located in a room at the top of the basilica, making it nearly impossible to miss the beauty of the architecture . The exit point is located in a joint church, I ended up replaying it more than twice because of how enjoyable it was.

Other maps are more focused on armory than cities, with missions in metal melting factories, rocket bases, navy submarines...These aren’t as appealing to me, the sabotage missions feel tedious especially when waypoints are unclear. I particularly dislike missions that require locating people, unless I go loud and attract Nazis, the targets always wander randomly around the map.

Regarding difficulty, I started on Normal then switched to Hard. The AI seems easier than in the previous game, with longer reaction times and less intelligence, and it’s not fun shooting at dummy. That said, Authentic difficulty (highest level) is too much for me, mainly because I can’t see the hit points in the scope.

My complaints are (1) Karl can only carry one rifle, yet he is able to carry one extra big gun like a submachine gun or a shotgun. It would be perfect for dual rifle gameplay - one quieter for short range killing and one badass long range louder rifle that can kill over 500 meters. (2) Panzerfaust not a default weapon. (3) Logo in photo mode doesn't work.

The most frustrating issue I encountered was in the Secret Weapon mission. Near the end of the game, I ran into a game-breaking bug where the cutscene wouldn’t trigger at the goal point. It kept saying, "Did we miss something? Where is Moller?" and I had to restart the level. I think I ran into a similar bug in the Wolf Mountain DLC.

I finished and replayed the main campaign and all 4 DLC maps in 22 hours on hard difficulty. Despite the bugs and the underwhelming DLCs, it’s still a solid game. I recommend it especially when it's on sale.

review_text:
Almost the perfect Sniper Elite Game... Almost.

Sniper Elite 5 is a game I had been looking forward to while playing through the series, mainly because it takes place in France and it is by far my favorite Theatre of War in WWII.
And while I was pleasantly surprised and had a TON of fun with the game, putting pretty much the most hours into this title than the rest of the franchise, I was left amazed but at the same time baffled at the changes made in this game.

So let us start with the positives.

- Invasion Mode. This is THE gamechanger for me, an absolute stroke of genius by Rebellion!
In Invasion Mode you have the chance to be invaded by an enemy player whose job it is to hunt you down, or you can do so yourself to other Karls out there.
This mode has single-handedly made the game 200 times more fun for me, because it fundamentally changed the way that I played the game and approached every objective; I'd survey the terrain, start putting traps in important bottlenecks or booby traps on soldiers with the knowledge that at ANY time, somebody could come for me, and it has made for some great moments where I would start an alert and as if clockwork, get invaded at the same time, leading to a lot of panicked running and hiding while trying to dispatch my pursuers before the Invader catches up and has me dead to rights.
Or the times where I was able to take out an invader because he stuck his head out of his little cover for just a second too long, allowing me to get that perfect headshot on him.
The reverse is also true, where I outmaneuver a Karl in such a way that I am no longer where he thinks I am, only to pop up behind him with a knife in his back, or flank him and give him a shot to the side of the head.

These moments MADE Sniper Elite 5 for me, and I could no longer imagine playing without the mode (Unless im just going for challenges and achievments since I finished the game now.)

- Spy Academy & Secret Weapon. Both these levels are PHENOMENAL and Spy Academy in particular to me is considered the peak in Level Design within the Sniper Elite series so far, no level comes close to the amount of fun I had traversing it. Secret Weapon is also notable for just the sheer amount of length I spent on it, clocking in at around 3 hours of playtime on my first run through the map, including several invaders coming for me throughout which was a blast!

- The weapons as usual feel incredible, and the art of -learning- your rifle, how it performs, how your shots are affected and mastering it, are a great deal of fun!

- Vehicles are more threatening. In SE4 it was very easy to just snipe into the slits of vehicles to take out driver and/or gunner, which made the vehicles quite easy to deal with and formulaic. You make sure to take out around it first and then you have free reign to bully it. While vehicles are still somewhat easy to deal with, they require a lot more work to take down. Slits are gone and the most reliable way is to use a satchel charge on the back and then fire away at the engine of each vehicle.

So then, let me get into some of the nitpicks I have with the game:

- In SE4, missions sometimes had enemies fighting with Resistance members, that is gone. Why? This was a great deal of fun, using the firefight to flank around and get a bead on the Nazis was so much fun in 4, why did it not return here?

- In SE4, the levels were either wonderful and blow me away, or awful (Monastery, Inception). While the Levels in SE5 are more average, the design is more consistently good across the board. The only mission I outright disliked ended up being the War Factory because of the way it literally railroads (pun not intended) you into paths, and most of the level taking place inside buildings.
Also where are all the Sniper Nests? The rooftops? In SE4 missions like the Dockyard and Inception you were able to enter buildings and go up to rooftops, cranes and all sorts of places. Where are my overlooking areas like the start of San Celini? Most of this is missing in SE5 and there is just a huge lack of any real sniper nests in a game called SNIPER Elite
And even when you find a Snipers Nest, the only enemies you are able to snipe from your limited view (be it a window or a ton of trees around) are only 50-100m away... Where the hell are my 300-500m snipes at? I have to go out of my way to position myself to get those sometimes.

- Where did Radio Men and Spotters go? The only infantry we face in this game are normal Infantry, Spotters, Snipers and slightly more resilient Ausland Infantry. Thats it? You introduce a new enemy type to spice up the game in 4 and then just...Don't bring them back for 5? You didn't even replace them with anything new this is just backspace coding, honestly.

- The Shadow/Light system is SIGNIFICANTLY downgraded. In SE4 the light affected your visibility, shooting out street lights or lamps in buildings became an integral part of the stealth gameplay, and while it is still possible in 5, it seems to have little to no effect on enemy's detection radius, or none that is perceivable, despite there being a detection ring on the radar that expands and shrinks based on -SOME- lightsources you walk into...

- Movement. Sniper Elite 4 had phenomenal movement, and while I do feel more control in SE5, I absolutely miss the crouch running that SE4 had, why was it removed? It just aims to make the game slower for no real reason, let us crouch run in the future please!
Climbing in general also still feels like an afterthought, it is slow and tedious and by the time I am done climbing a wall up to something, I could've spent that same amount of time running around it while taking down the enemies in my path, but the movement is truly just a small nitpick.

- Too many surpressed weapons & Availability of subsonic ammo. It was too easy to snipe people or take them out close range thanks to how easy it is to have quite literally 3 surpressed weapons on you, or even just run subsonic ammo. The level design seems to reflect this as well, because there is just significantly less opportunities to use soundmasking to your advantage. Generators are often in spots that don't even work for sniping, vehicles can now be sabotaged to serve as soundmasks too, but are also usually in spots that don't serve much of a sniping purpose either. This is a huge shame and it made the game a cakewalk to just be able to load into the map with 20 subsonic rifle rounds and KNOW that somewhere in the level, you will find more of it.

This isn't even the worst game, Zombie Army 4 had THREE Season Passes.
This is penny-pinching at its finest, even Sniper Elite Resistance, which according to many reviews I have read so far, is a standalone DLC which was developed at the fraction of the cost of a truly new Sniper Elite title, also launched with a Season Pass, how many more will that game get?

All in All. Sniper Elite 5 is nearly perfect, but it is a game that takes steps back in certain areas and it feels like the game is starting to cater less to...you know... Sniping, and more towards Close Quarters Action.

But even with all of the issues above, I still had an absolute blast playing the game thanks to Invasion Mode and the level design that mostly still holds up despite my grievances. But when I get to Sniper Elite Resistance, or SE6, less run n gun please.

Sniper Elite 5, what is, in my opinion, mechanically speaking, the best Sniper Elite game in the series.

Bought in Winter sales, refunded and now bought back in Autumn Sales. So what's with all of these about?

As a fans of this game, written so many reviews for this franchise for a decade now since the reboot of Sniper Elite, I think 5 is still true to its root, a WW2 sniper shooting game with our failure Austrian artist as a staple DLC to the franchise and gameplay improvement every installments.

People might criticize that this game barely change from Elite 4, Italian Campaign, but I disagree. Being a person who put nearly 30-40 hrs in 4, 5 improved a lot of QoL and AI (more on this later). 
More variety of ammunition to choose from. Apart from Subsonic introduced in 4, there are Match, Armor piecing (as some players said that it was too easy to kill vehicles/tanks in previous installments so there you have it), non-fatal and soft point are debuted in this game.

The map design also improved on what makes the charm for Elite 4. It connects the each zone together which is better than 4 imo which basically like many sandboxes connected together to form 1 map.

Gunplays a lot better now. You can aim down sight on the iron sight now so no more rage inducing where you have to switch left & right to aim the guy with SMG/Pistol.

Customization also improved. Back in 4, I barely customized my weapon, just one time and done. With 5, you have to adapt with the situations.

So it's all sunshine and rainbow from 4 to 5?

Not quite.

Like I mentioned the AI, it's smarter that's for sure but sometimes it's more annoying now as it's harder to shake them off or reduce the awareness to normal. It's quite a challenge for veteran or seasoned players but for the one that's new to the series this would be annoying. I think this is one of the reason why I refunded at the first time.

Second, the maps. There's a lot more plain field or urban compared to Italian's slope and mountain in 4 so that's why it's a lot more challenging than previous one.

Third, customization plays a lot more factor in here than previous installments, meaning you have to spend time to find the best one for you. While you can find the workbench in the field, I encourage any player to test in the shooting range than in the mission as you have to stick with that setup until you can find the workbench which a lot of the time doesn't appear on the maps until you walk into the zone.

You have to loot the body or eavesdropping what soldier said (you can use the binocular, zoom in and listening to them despite being like hundreds of meter far away) to get the intel/insight where you should headed. This is not for anyone who's going gun blazing as you will absolutely missed a lot of opportunity to finish sub-missions.

Talking about sub-missions, You have to finish these tasks to unlock more guns and customization. My first 6 hours into the game, I only used the starting weapon in the game until I realized I have to finish tasks to unlock the rest.

Btw, they changed the looting system from switching your weapon permanently, you only temporary pick and use it. The second you switch to your 2ndary or sidearms, that weapon will drop. This is somehow annoying as the game should encourage you to find better sniper rifles by hunting other snipers and pick their rifles to unlock that setup. This is a missed opportunity, sadly.

Lastly, the invasion system. It's basically a PVP mode that you can allow other players to join in your campaign mission (or invading others), posing as whatever you want from plain cloth officers, soldiers to elite snipers in a ghillie suit. Your only task is to kill the invader/other players. 
It might sounds good to hear but I think you can imagine how bad this can turn out to be. There are systems to prevent people from camping and stuff but the fact is nobody wants to play this mode. The toggle to turn off the invasion also doesn't encourage anyone to toggle it on. The rewards are quite interesting as many characters/customizations are behind the invasion rewards but I guess with how the game has already passed its peak I probably wouldn't be able to unlock it forever.

Overall.
The same old sniper elite, as usual. Improved gameplay and slightly better story (may not be everyone cup of tea). Despite some odd decisions from developers, this game is still recommended. But with their decisions or monetization lately (both this and dead war), I guess it's mostly recommendable only if it's on sales.

review_text:
I got sniper elite 5 a few days ago, and I don't see it getting much recognition. I'll admit, when I first started it, I had mixed feelings. It's very clear that the game took heavy inspiration from Hitman, and at first, I was worried that the game would suck, that the developers had given up on it, and were just trying to cash in on a successful game. I played it further, and was really pleasantly surprised.

First, I'll put it into context. Sniper elite is a stealth game with a heavy emphasis on sniping, with x-ray cams when you kill enemies. Originally, SE was a very linear game, but as the series went on, the level design got more and more open with each game, but I think didn't truly blossom until the fourth entry to the series.

Sniper Elite 5 took what made sniper elite 4 good, and then slapped on a lot of the stuff that made hitman good, and the result is this really addictive open level structure where you're encouraged to go back and explore the same giant levels several times over, getting tangible rewards for doing so, but not restricting how you do it in the same way that hitman did. Don't get me wrong, I love Hitman, but I felt like some of the tasks and challenges in it got so specific that it felt less open than it actually was.

Sniper Elite has TONS of optional objectives per map, and you get rewards for doing them. But these optional objectives are set up so that you can usually do them in a multitude of ways, rather than following a script to do it. As an example, I'm only on the 3rd mission after around a week, because I've been doing the second level to unlock stuff I want. I realized you could unlock a suppressor for the 1911 pistol, which is semi-automatic, unlike the pump action pistol you start with. But then I didn't like the weapon sway. So I did optional stuff to unlock the carbine kit for the pistol. And then I learned you could convert it to 22 caliber, making it even more quiet. So once again, I went through the level, did a challenge tk unlock that. Then i unlocked a rifle I'd missed in the level, by playing it again, only to decide the rifle had too much weapon sway. So now I'm trying to unlock stuff for that rifle.

It's an absolutely addictive gameplay loop. And each map is big enough that whenever i replay them, I find new routes, or secret passages.

But i think the most important part of all of this is that you don't even have to play it as a stealth game. It steers you in that direction, obviously. But you're not really punished if you're seen - there's no "right" way to do it. The punishment is having to deal with whoever else goes after you. Or leaving a trail behind if another player invades your game (which you can turn off if you like). So if you're able to blow a truck up and get away before they see you, or machine gun your way through a corridor of Nazis, you don't get penalized for using loud options. It takes away the frustration that you'd normally get from grinding a game like Hitman for unlocks, because you can kind of just do it however you want, and with each replay of a mission, you've got a new route to try, or a new weapon you just unlocked, or the option to have a friend help you. I love Hitman, but my issue is I find myself grinding and grinding with the same loadout every single time until I get what I want. In SE, I feel like I'm not restricted from using all of these gadgets I've unlocked.

review_text:
Sniper Elite is a series that got better with every entry up to SE4. Unfortunately SE5 isn't continuing on this path and instead takes that of many other AAA developers these days, replacing their franchises unique charm for mediocracy, likely to appeal to a wider, more mentally challenged audience, the superficial and absolutely unnecessary skill-tree included.

Pros:
The game can sometimes be somewhat enjoyable.
The game seems to be very well optimized. I have a decent PC and got 110+ fps on Ultra.
I like the art style and most maps are quite beautiful.
The weapon customization is actually not that bad. While not very realistic, it at least enables the player to build for different play styles. There is the usual "suppressor decreases muzzle velocity and damage" bull$#!7 and most pros/cons make absolutely no sense, but this doesn't really have a negative effect on the gameplay, so i can let this slide.
The annoying SFX from SE4 when entering tall grass has been removed. Unfortunately with something similarly annoying, see below.

Cons:
The Maps are mostly boring and more often, than not strongly discourage actual sniping in favor of close quarter engagements.
The amount of invisible walls, areas the player can't enter and environmental obstacles, which cannot be climbed or vaulted over is insane. Pre-alpha-level of insane.
Enemy AI is disgusting. This is, without a doubt, the single worst AI, that i have seen in a video game. It is utterly atrocious!
The controls are very clunky and inconsistent. Fast crouched walking from SE4 has been removed. Climbing and especially dropping from ledges often doesn't work.
Clipping is a huge issue and so is enemies spotting and shooting the player through the edges of solid cover.
Ballistics are infuriatingly terrible, especially considering this is a game about sniping.
I know this game is not about the story, but it has to be mentioned that the story, the voice acting and the characters are pretty lame and often awkward, to the point of it being distracting, e.g. the protagonist having to mention every single time he enters tall grass and generally talking to himself constantly.
The game is an unfinished mess.
DLCs are overpriced!

In my opinion the flaws heavily outweigh the very negligible positives. 3.5/10 Do not buy!
And don't buy SE Resistance. It's an overpriced DLC for SE5, suffering from mostly the same issues.

If you enjoyed any AC after Origins, buy the same game under a different name every year at full price, support sells-tactics, like pre-order, season passes, micro-transactions and NFTs and regularly find yourself defending the indefensible, due to your fan-boyish nature and intellectual integrity of a blob-fish, this might just be the perfect game for you: Buy the Complete Edition at full price! Also, hot coffee is hot, cruise control isn't autopilot and please, for the love of sky-daddy, use contraception, always, no exceptions, ever!

This game needed more polish before ever being released...

AI breaks quite often. At first I thought the enemy state indicator was bugged, but no. AI really does "hide" while standing out in the middle of the road. Explosions have absolutely no regard for walls or floors, so get ready to die to a grenade someone tossed on the other side of a big cobblestone wall from you. And don't sit right up against that wall or small arms fire will hit you with no effort at all.

AI also seems far too omniscient. If I shoot an explosive barrel 100m away with a suppressed weapon and nobody was around to hear me fire that shot and the only mention of sound on the bottom left of the screen is "explosion heard," why are they coming right for me? Why is my position marked? If all they heard was the exlposion, they should go to where the explosion happened or search randomly, not all come toward the player's vicinity single file. I refuse to believe that they just "guessed" I was in that particular direction approximately that far away from the explosion they heard.

If I press "W", why am I suddenly going right, then left, *then* forward? Why is that enemy investigating the same dead body over and over? Why did my grenade that I threw 30-40 meters away from me kill me outright? How did my mine just kill me when I was an entire floor up with a full physical barrier between me and it? HOW DID A NAZI FLAG BILLOWING SOFTLY IN THE WIND COMPLETELY STOP MY .308 ROUND?

I literally can't believe the drop in quality here. Some of these are just blatant issues that I suspect definitely should have been caught during QA, and others just seem like downright oversight or lack of care. Please stop rushing your games and properly test them. While code and engines get more complex with each passing year, a lot of the processes wind up far more streamlined and useful with each iteration. Use it. And hire/pay your QA team. Stop outsourcing to non-gamers or people with no idea how to break a game. 

It was 2022. And you have had 3 years to improve or fix this game. You decided instead to release buggier DLC because you don't care about the quality of your game. You care about the money you get from the franchise.

It's 2025. We already know that game development is hard. But we should also know by now that games take time. If you rush it, it will not be good. Stop overhiring. Stop overfiring. Create more efficient communication methods for your team. Don't overwork people. No crunch. There are so many things we can do outside of the programming/designing of the game itself to improve the process and product.

review_text:
- Played on AMD Ryzen 7 1700x, 32GB RAM, ROG STRIX 1070ti 8GB.
- 2560x1440  (2k quality)
- Mix of High, ultra and medium (for more demanding video options) settings.
- Game ran mostly at 60fps+. There would be some drops to 40fps at times due to the amount of things shown on the screen. However, game was fully playable and I didn't encounter any bugs or crashes throughout my single-player playthrough.

To start with, I have played the previous installments (Sniper Elite 2, 3, 4 and their zombie spin-offs) and, compared with its predecessors, [b]Sniper Elite 5 feels almost like the ultimate package so far.[/b]

[i]This review will be only based on the single-player part of the game as I haven't touched either the 'Axis Invasion' or 'Multiplayer' modes.[/i]

The campaign maps are massive and give you plenty of freedom. You are basically dropped into a semi-open world area for each mission where they give you multiple objectives (main and secondary ones, only the main ones are mandatory) and also more than one way to tackle them. Let's say you have to destroy a generator, you can either blow it up with explosives or cut out the wires that powers it up. Or maybe you have to clear out a checkpoint of soldiers, this can be done stealthily up close, rushing in guns-blazing or also far away from a sniper spot. Besides, there's usually more than one way to reach your objective, whether is it through climbing or finding a secret locked door (in which you have to find the key beforehand with one of the soldiers or around the door area) or tunnels. Something worth mentioning about the campaign is that, if you play with minimal to no HUD (like I did for my entire playthrough), the protagonist gives you clues/hints or updates you about new objectives that you encounter in the field which can be amazingly helpful when you combine it with the in-game map to check out your mission progress. Just remember to not rush the campaign. As the maps are huge, take your time. Try to do missions stealthily, explore as much as you can so you can discover various collectibles, exotic weapons, items, etc. Enjoy what each map has to offer as they were undoubtedly beautifully crafted.

Even though the campaign mode is wonderfully made, [b]one downside for me would be the customization[/b]. And why is that? As I've mentioned before, the maps are massive and obviously filled with collectibles, intel for objectives and there are also the 'workbenches' which works like a 'loadout switcher' during the mission. However, you have to find these 'workbenches' around the map to unlock more attachments for your weapons (suppressors, gun barrels, grips, etc). So, in case you finish your main mandatory objectives and want to exfiltrate but missed one of these workbenches, you'll have to replay the mission later and find them and unlock any desired attachments. Despite that, even though the weapons arsenal is significantly smaller than previous sniper elites, you can greatly customize your main sniper, secondary weapon and pistol. During each mission, you can also carry a 'temporary weapon' (dropped weapons, basically) and they don't replace your main weapons that you've chosen before the mission.

As for difficulty, I love that it is 100% customizable. You can have super intelligent enemies that flank you constantly and are not bullet spongy or overly accurate, which is usually what the 'hard difficulties' are disguised of and all about. You can also customize the 'sniper shooting' experience (gravity and wind) and also the hud. For my playthrough, I set the HUD to minimal (used the in-game map to guide myself, it's the classic 'M' key on your keyboard), disabled the empty lung assistance indicator (where the shot would land, basically), activated gravity impact and disabled the wind effects. As for the enemies, I set them to be overly experienced/intelligent but not bullet spongy. This way, they would spot me easily, flank me, but once we engaged out of stealth, I could take them down easily if my awareness and reaction times were on point. Furthermore, when it came to tanking bullets, I did not change this option, I kept it on default. To me, this made the game fun and challenging, it had a great balance between both. It wasn't overly easy but it wasn't also superbly difficult that it would ruin the fun.

Character movement is certainly an improvement. In Sniper Elite 4, the protagonist would move around too slowly (even when crouched) and that kind of ruined the fun for me. Now in SE5, the character walks around a bit faster and movement is much more fluid.

Weapons as a whole feel great and the gun sounds are also on point. To my mind, the gunplay in shooting games need to have its fair share of realistic sounds and weapon feel otherwise the game feels bland and the guns feel that they are made out of plastic. Thankfully, this doesn't happen here. Guns are loud and heavy as they are supposed to be. Landing headshots from far far away is deeply satisfying and it truly makes you feel somewhat like a real sniper.

Graphics are outstandingly great here, you have its fair share of places to go and climb and enjoy the view for some beautiful screenshots. On the other hand, they were not the selling point for me. I guess the gameplay itself counted much more at the end of the day.

Would I recommend Sniper Elite 5? Obviously! If you are a hardcore fan of the series, simply go for it! As mentioned previously, Sniper Elite 5 combines all the elements from its predecessors and tries to create the ultimate sniping experience for you. 
In case you are still unsure, wait for a sale. Just don't sleep on this game, you certainly won't be disappointed.

review_text:
I sometimes wish Steam had a middle of the road option for reviewing games because while Sniper Elite 5 isn't a terrible game, it's clearly a downgrade in what made Sniper Elite 4 very fun. Allow me to explain.

Sniper Elite 5 takes pride in itself in a few ways. One such pride is with its campaign's maps being very large. They are very welcoming to exploration and in a sense, adventure. There is no pressure against the player, you aren't timed as you move around, allowing to find all the little nooks and crannies as you move through these maps. Depending on the difficulty you want to play on, the game can easily make you feel pressured though, but that is entirely up to you in the end. So what's the problem then?

The major flaw with SE5 is its "expanded sandbox experience". While on first glance, it seems pretty welcoming with how you can approach enemies and dealing with them. It as a whole is a huge downgrade in interaction. An example of this is how Karl can knock out enemies, while neat and an interesting way to play pacifist, it becomes a double edged sword when a single guard you happened to miss wanders about and discovered the knocked out buddy and wakes him back up. But hey, there is a way to prevent this and keep your pacifist way right? Well there are those yellow supply chest, seemingly inspired by Hitman where you can store up to two enemies in them to effectively keep them out of the fight for the remaining part of your mission. There is also the tall grass too, which works just as well funny enough.

But the issue isn't how Karl takes down enemies in pacifistic way, its how he approaches them lethally. One of the huge flaws in this game which confused me was how the player approaches enemies in a more lethal sniper format. Now you can just point and click on the head, sure, but in the previous games you had the ability to target a grenade on an enemy's uniform or belt, causing it to explode, creating a distraction as well as panic among enemies. 90% of enemies in this game don't have grenades physically equipped to their belts anymore which is odd since they throw them like candy when they do spot you. 

Another large downgrade is the approach to vehicle combat, in this game weapon customization is a very strong boon the player has and the ability to make a suppressed anti-armor rifle is pretty neat, but the interaction between vehicles and the player is extremely limited. The very first level, Atlantikwall introduces you to vehicle patrols right after you complete the tutorial piece of the game and again, at first its pretty neat seeing a traveling patrol of trucks, wagens and bikes roaming around the maps (until it breaks, I'll get that towards the end of the review), but targeting of vehicle weakpoints is extremely hit or miss in SE5, even with Anti-Armor ammo, sometimes it takes up to two, four shots before you blow up a troop truck, even a wagen. Later in the same level, you encounter the first major flaw of this issue, the patrol boat. On the water in front of the beach bunkers is a boat with spotlight and turret.

In previous games, you could target the driver AND gunner of the boat, but in SE5 only the spotlight can be broken and the driver can be killed. The gunner can't be targeted at all and even looking at the gunner position reveals there is no visible soldier there, just a rotating empty combat position with a gun that seems to be alive on its own or operating via remote control. Its weird. Same thing applies to the Armored Car, the Sd. Kfz 222, its driver can be killed but for some reason, unlike SE4, the gunner can't be targeted at all. The same can be said of the Tiger II tank enemy where you can't even kill the driver or gunner. Its just a strange and odd choice of sandbox limitations given how "expanded" its suppose to be.

But now that I got my personal gripes out of the way, lets talk about the real reason why you should only buy it if you just want to play Sniper Elite. The bugs and the DLC consumer model. Oh golly. The bugs in this game are extremely visible and from what I've noticed, there has been little to zero attempt to fix them. In my 100+ hours of play, I've seen so many strange and odd bugs regarding the sandbox and how the AI interacts with it. Again, jump back to the first level, Atlantikwall again. One of the secondary objectives is blowing up a series of three Flak 38 emplacements (fun fact two enemies incorrectly call the 38s, 88s in their dialogue for some reason, another oddity moment), now its pretty straightforward, you blow up the first one and the second one without issue, its the last one by the Naval Cannon objective that breaks the game's sandbox. Upon blowing up that AA gun, enemies by the nearby road will come over to investigate and even some vehicle patrols will stop, hop out and investigate as well, but that's the issue. They will never stop investigating, leaving on your mini-map a strangely permanent mark of investigation. Even after all the enemies are dead or knocked out, it will not remove the mark.

This causes so many issues, no matter how far away you are. Enemies will stop reacting to your Whistle tool and reset their pathing, throwing a Bottle will aggro any enemies on the spot regardless if you are across the way, they'll know where you are at and open fire on your exact position. Vehicle pathing breaks as vehicles will stop in strange spots, get stuck and remain like this. The whole thing just breaks entirely and this happens on every single map. Its a "sandbox" problem and just from a glance, it seems be literally the AI unable to restore itself back to a normal pattern. It gets stuck, completely flubbing up how your mission flows as a result. Its bizarre.

Now then, the other reason why you should be wary. The DLC consumer model. Its bad. Its really bad. 10$ for a weapon and skin pack? 15$ for a single mission and weapon pack? It really screams money grubbing given the fact the maps are weirdly smaller and more compact compared to the base game content. The ONLY pack that is actually worth the 10$ is Kraken Awakens, given that its mission is placed on a decently big map and it properly wraps up the final strings on the campaign's story.

But what about the shooting funny mustache man DLC (Wolf Mountain DLC)? My disappoint is extreme and very depressing, this is one of the most bugged things I've ever seen. While the map is not as large as others, it has a lot of flow problems (ie, only one way to get to the main structure, through the tunnel where vehicle patrols come through commonly as example). On top of that Mr. H's AI is extremely broken. For some reason 90% of the game, he'll be standing in the open (spawned there) or just in sitting in his staff car not moving or doing anything. His bike escorts also seemingly stuck in place too (after peeking under the game's hood, it seems his front bike escort driver isn't even loaded properly most of the time; usually characters assigned to a mission have a set name and a bio. The rear bike escort does have this and on rare moments when the mission actually works, the front bike driver ALSO has a set name and bio, but if the driver is listed as "Unknown Soldier" aka a temporary soldier spawned in for vehicle patrolling, the mission breaks entirely; this is your reason right here). The fact that there was never a bug fix or addressing of this issue should tell you a lot about SE5 and its problems. There are other things but for me, gameplay and just general flow are my major points of frustration.

In the end however, it's a decently good game marred by a lot of issues and a lot more bugs. A lot of questionable downgrades as well, but I do find myself enjoying the whole sneaking around the maps, and self imposed challenges I gave myself as I play it. Regardless, its one of those games where you should think about before you buy. If you do wanna play it, I'd suggest waiting for a sale.

A very fun game i'm glad I decided to finally play to get into the series. The stealth is tight and rewarding, sniping is clearly done justice with the realism, and overall the campaign was a good time, even if the story wasn't what i'd consider to be anything to write home about.

The introduction of passive play- in the form of leaving enemies alive, feels a little odd for a game about... killing nazis. But I like the variance in playstyle that can offer, and can't really complain about that. The difficulty customisation is next level, you can change anything you want, to make it as helpful, or as immersive as you desire it. Stealth play can be really fun on some missions, where you just need to sneak in, eliminate some enemies, and use that high ground to snipe, although this is double edged (i'll get to it). The weapon customisation was exceptional, and allowed a large variance in playstyles during my campaign, and operation führer (which should be in the basegame, and not DLC, but it's cheap enough to where I can't be too annoyed) was fine... I did not play with the online features, and im happy the game lets you disable it's anticheat for offline play, and i'm even more glad that it's not forced upon you as quite frankly I take these missions slow, and don't want some sweat joining my game trying to kill me.

My main gripes with this game come from just the nature of stealth games being a bit finicky, and constantly having to use quicksaves just to get by some of its jank. Some of the enemies have a serious level of omnipotence and like to dodge bullets that otherwise would kill them. And there are times where bullets that *absolutely* would kill, would otherwise not kill them, creating a situation where now you need to kill them fast or they'll shoot & alert the others. Some of the enemy snipers are annoying because if they even remotely spot you, they'll just start shooting endlessly at the location you last were, giving your location away, even though they have 0 confirmation that something was actually there. The level designs in a lot of these levels were questionable, for a game about sniping, there feels like an active discouragement to actually use the sniping mechanics as there isn't quite enough spaces on the map where sniping feels worth it. The Spy Academy & Factory Maps were almost good at being sniping maps, but you couldn't really snipe much at all from the points the game clearly wanted you to snipe from. Operation Führer, which is a massive part of the appeal to sniper elite games, killing the man himself, was a painful map, not much sniping opportunities, constantly having vehicles drive past making any kills immediately visible. Doing the side objectives alerted enemies at the tunnel, the tunnel that is the *ONLY* way to cross into the 2nd section of the map. But I'll complain more about that with the DLC review.

Overall, while I haven't too much to say about the game, I did end up enjoying my time with it, and can recommend it if you like the calm methodical approach that comes with stealth-sniping games. Or if you really want to go guns blazing, the game caters to that playstyle too, even if it's discouraged. I have gripes with the game, many infact, but even though they take the majority of the review, the gameplay itself was so solid that i ended up just getting by them just fine. While they effect my opinion of the game, it's not enough to say that it's not worth a play. Give it a go!

review_text:
Sniper Elite 5 is a third person/first person hybrid shooter, where you are deployed in locations across Europe during World War II as, you guessed it, an elite sniper. With a decent array of weapons to choose from and customize with unlock-able extensions and attachments, it is another solid entry in the Sniper Elite series of video games. I have always enjoyed the series, from the zombie titles, to the straight forward shoot Nazi's themes, and would recommend this game to anyone who enjoys a mission oriented shooter with a variety of strategy options. 

You can choose to confront the enemies, have the alarms blare and take everyone on as they come, or you can do what I do, which is sneak around, mask the sound of my gun with any nearby masking source, and snipe people from as far away as possible. If not, I pull out a silenced pistol and ensure nobody finds the body and raised the alarm. 

There is a decent amount of missions in the base game, with a load of areas and secondary objectives to complete. The DLCs are underwhelming in terms of content, but I did pick up the Season One pass for the extra missions and completed them, out of obligation really. In addition to the missions, you can do some single player modes like 'endless' which is defending a location from a number of enemy waves, and there is a deep and natural ability to coop the missions and modes with a friend, which I highly recommend!

While I didn't partake in the multiplayer options, there is a variety of options in terms of gameplay, including 'Axis Invasion', where an online player joins your mission to try to stop you from completing it, which is a very cool concept. Standard deathmatch-like and other modes are also available, if that's what tickles your fancy. 

Overall, I'd give this game a solid [b]8/10[/b], I enjoyed the time I put into it both in coop and by my lonesome in single player. I'm looking forward to the next entry in the series!

It's certainly enjoyable but so far i've felt like the game is more suited to either super sneaky play or CQB than sniping. There are many opportunities for longer shots and you can certainly find places to pick off enemies at range but many of the mission targets are found in enclosed areas and you still have to go collect intel which requires either CQB or sneaking around. 

Keep in mind that sniping involves a few shots then moving. It also, rather necessarily, includes the alerting of nearby enemies when their comrades lose their marbles. You can't just sit in one place and punch tickets for an hour. It's not a marksmanship game.

You can try to spend a great deal of time tagging all the bad guys and sniping them before you enter a building, but it's largely a moot point as there will be some you miss and others that come and go in vehicles  as you begin your exploration of the area. 

Overall it's still a great game and provides many hours of enjoyable play time. Far more than worth the winter sale price of $15 as of December '24. Just pick your play style and run with it. Play it again in a different way if you want different achievements.

review_text:
[h1] A new refreshing entry in a stealth franchise that survived three console generations [/h1]

  I admit, this is my first sniper elite since the OG on the PS2. I initially played sniper elite 5 on PS+ out of curiosity and nostalgia, I had tried  SE 2 and  SE 3 years ago but couldn't for some reason get into them, they lacked something the original SE had, they felt more floaty and arcadey in a bad way.

 Playing Sniper Elite 5,  i was expecting the same outdated formula. But instead, i found the closest thing to a hitman game set in WWII .

  You can unlock new starting locations, the soldiers have that hitman-like NPC banter when you eavesdrop on them, they could reveal information about the target... All of this on top of a competent, decent looking third person sniper game with the usual and ever engaging and well built x ray cams that the franchise is known for.

  Add to that one element that sold me on the game and its merit ( and made me excited for the its eventual sequels), ''Invasion mode''.
 A mode that single-handedly, in my opinion, gives a new life to the formula and the whole stealth genre as a whole, for all of us single player stealth lovers.

   Imagine you are sneaking around , hiding in a bush, waiting for a guard to turn his back so that you can move to the giant french castle ahead, all of the sudden you get a prompt that you are invaded.  You panic ,hide for a bit , get a prompt that a phone can be used to determine your location, and sure enough , the invader uses it and can see where you are now, You run as far as you can and just like that, the invader hits you out of nowhere. That feeling is something new to me in a single player stealth game, its refreshing. 

  You might think that frustration will follow after that ''unfair'' game over'' ,after all you are minding your business, doing your single player objective. Don't worry, you can reload your last checkpoint, You can even disable this mode, but i suggest you don't.
As frustrating as it might get , you will defeat  your invader and eventually ( most likely after you finish the campaign), you will invade others.. 

  i understand games like hunt showdown has an excellent PvPvE stealth driven game loop, but that is still in its core a multiplayer game and its not the same as playing a dedicated single player stealth game.

   If you are like me and want something new added to the same hide, throw a bottle to distract and sneak behind the enemy brand of stealth, this game will offer that and more .

TLDR: The game's focus has changed from picking off targets from 100s of metres away on a vantage point, to melee executions and silenced pistols in close quarters

The last major problem is the considerably strange objectives for a stealth / sniper game, such as 'use explosives to destroy an AA gun', which automatically alerts all the guards thanks to a giant explosion and their equipment being destroyed?

review_text:
Goodness, where to begin.
As someone who has played SE4 through to completion and started mastering the weaponry, I'd like to think I'm fairly familiar with how the game should play, and SE5 builds heavily on all the strengths of it's predecessor, whilst also cutting out a lot of the less-than-useful features.
I'll make a bullet point list, as I'll just be rabbiting on otherwise
The weapons are extremely varied and versatile, and the ability to modify them to suit your personal preference is an excellent feature
The levels are gigantic and filled with hidden secrets, it makes you want to explore rather than just go from objective to objective
The enemies are smarter, almost lifelike, but still daft enough to be easily mown down, whilst also posing a good challenge if they get the drop on you instead
Similarly, their ability in some cases, to block melee takedowns, whilst utterly infuriating when they end an otherwise perfect run, does have the benefit of teaching you to be more careful about who you do and do not shoot right off the bat, and when stealth is preferable 
The dialogue is a vast improvement, along with the rest of the VA'ing. It's far less stiff, much less repetitive, and sounds far more natural
Overall, I'd say the game is well worth your time if you appreciate FPS games... but only in singleplayer, or co-op multiplayer
By far the game's worst addition is Axis Invasion, which is a shame as it's an incredible concept. The ability to invade another players campaign mission is genius in theory, but the inconsistencies between Campaign and Axis, coupled with the unfathomably blatant Allies bias make it nigh-on impossible to play, unless you're either a highly experienced player who has spent hundreds of hours with nothing better to do, which some of us don't have the luxury of being able to do anymore, or you're the intelligent scum of the earth and have cheats. Heed my words, do not play Axis Invasion if you value your sanity. if you thought you had patience, trust me, this has the capacity to make Ghandi himself scream in rage.
Let us begin, shall we?
You're thrown right into an existing mission, fair enough in theory. Problem; you have no idea where the opposing player is, how far in they are, or how far away you are. I can understand not having both players start from the very beginning of the mission, you are invading an existing campaign afterall, but it puts you at an immediate and severe disadvantage, especially when you're just starting off with the bottom-of-the-barrel equipment that is neither use nor ornament.
You lack a focus bar, and have to tag your own AI teammates to see where they are. The first I can understand, that would be extremely unfair, the second is absurd. Granted, you are not an officer, but it would seem fairly reasonable for you to have at least a general idea of where your own damned teammates are, rather than have to scope or binocular tag them, which takes an eternity as you can't click to tag like in SE4, you've got to hover over them for half a millenia, by which point they've almost certainly moved behind cover or otherwise out of your view, leaving you stood there like a right plonker.
The Anti-Camping system. How shall we prevent players from holding a defensive sniping position, in a game about sniping, in a gamemode where they are playing a defending sniper? I know, let's broadcast their exact position to the enemy. We won't do it to them of course, that would be working in the Axis' favour, and we can't have that... see the issue here? if you don't, congratulations, you're part of the problem.
The weapon and trap damage is so absurdly unbalanced it would be laughable if it wasn't so infuriating. The opposing Fairburne can wander calmly over no less than two teller mines and brush it off as though he were grazed lightly by a gentle autumn leaf blowing in the wind. You on the other hand, can't take two shots from an SMG at 60 meters without crying enough and keeling over. Ask me how I know this. The opposing sniper's shots can travel clear through a brick wall to hit you if they must, your's are intercepted by the greatest obstruction ever conceived: Some mild foliage you can still see through.
Then we come to the tagging system. I can perfectly understand the tags wearing off, they would defeat the point of the gamemode if you could see where the other player was at all times, but why in the actual infernal hell does the game let them know you've tagged them? If you've been spotted by someone in real life without your knowledge, does a great red banner appear in front of you letting you know you've been perceived by a person currently unknown to you? NO. So why does it here? The whole point is for each player to kill the other, warning them makes it unfathomably hard for the wrong reason. Why not rely on the pre-existing, and still fully functional scope glint to see if you're being observed?
And finally we come to the piece-de-resistance of the whole debacle, the lack of options on matchmaking.
Some of us aren't exactly comfortable on higher difficulties, so why can't we filter out what lobbies we want to connect to? The game tells you the settings of the game you're invading in minute detail, so why can't we stop it from connecting to ones we don't want? Even F2P PvP games can do that, I'd expect the same from one that costs £9.99, let alone one that costs £45.
I understand that by playing Axis Invasion you are willingly stepping into the shoes of the losing side, but holy actual sh!te does the game tell you about it. It's so unbalanced that if you affixed it to a wheel you'd have the world's first perpetual motion device.
Worst part is it doesn't even feel good when you lose. As I say, I've been playing FPS's for a great number of years, and I'm an avid Mega Man fan to boot, I like hard games, I crave the difficulty because I find it rewarding. But even I come away from a perfect losing streak of Axis Invasion and if I wasn't so busy punching my desk to try and relieve the rage and stress it causes, I'd feel so dead inside I'd have to check if I still had a pulse. The blatant favouritism of the host player, evident by the weaponry bias alone if nothing else makes the game feel like you are unwelcome in the situation, and the fact the disconnect button is labelled as "Surrender" just drives home the point that you're the outsider the very game itself is treading on before the player even gets to you.

Bottom line; Is the game good? Hell yes, if you appreciate FPS games or have played any of the preceding SE games, throw your wallet at the screen already, why are you still here?
Is the campaign good? Very much so, the levels are expansive and highly interactive, the story is great, the voice acting is superb, the animations are fluid, the cutscenes make you want to watch them, even if you've already seen them. It is a veritable masterpiece, and the ability to enjoy it with a friend in co-op multiplayer is just the icing on the cake
Is the versus multiplayer good? ...I don't even know what to put here, I think it should be fairly obvious by now that it's a steaming pile that even the Geneva Convention would list as a forbidden torture method. If you have a mortal enemy that you wish to inflict suffering upon, subject them to Axis Invasion as Axis, then you can go to them and beg for forgiveness for your crimes against them.

review_text:
Sniper Elite 5 delivers thrilling sniping action and stunning visuals, but when it comes to stealth mechanics, the game falls short in several areas. While the series has always emphasized stealth as a core gameplay element, this installment struggles to maintain a consistent and rewarding stealth experience.

One notable issue is the AI behavior. While enemy soldiers can be challenging to outsmart at times, their reactions can be inconsistent. There are moments when enemies seem oblivious to your presence, even when you're in plain sight, undermining the tension that stealth gameplay is meant to create. Conversely, they can also detect you far too quickly if you make even the slightest noise, leading to frustrating trial-and-error situations.

The level design, while visually impressive, often feels overly linear, which limits the ways players can approach objectives stealthily. Many areas funnel you into specific paths, reducing opportunities for creative tactics and exploration. This rigidity can make stealth encounters feel formulaic, rather than allowing players to experiment with different strategies.

In addition, the game’s mechanics for distraction and stealth kills can feel somewhat underdeveloped. While you can create distractions to draw enemy attention, the effectiveness of these tactics varies. Sometimes, enemies will ignore noise entirely, while at other times, they’ll respond in ways that feel arbitrary. This inconsistency can make planning your stealth approach frustrating, as it’s hard to gauge how the AI will react.

On the other hand, the shooting mechanics in Sniper Elite 5 are superbly executed, making the core experience immensely satisfying. The sniping feels incredibly rewarding, with the game’s signature X-Ray kill cam providing a visceral sense of impact that amplifies the thrill of a well-placed shot. The ballistics are realistic, requiring players to account for factors like bullet drop and wind, which adds depth and strategy to each shot.

The addition of new weapon customization options allows players to tailor their loadouts to their preferred playstyle, further enhancing the shooting experience. Whether you're going for long-range precision or adapting to close-quarters combat, the game offers a satisfying array of tools to master.

Overall, while Sniper Elite 5’s stealth mechanics may leave something to be desired, its shooting mechanics shine brightly. The thrilling sniping, immersive visuals, and engaging multiplayer options create a compelling experience that will resonate with fans of the genre. For those who appreciate the art of shooting, this installment is a must-play, even if the stealth elements could use a bit more polish.

review_text:
Sniper Elite 5, as the name would suggest, is the 5th title in what is a pretty acclaimed series. It sees you take on the role of an OSS Operative in Europe, going behind enemy lines to disrupt the war effort of the Third Reich through a number of decently long missions. 

Whilst the name would suggest that you are a sniper (which is true) there are a good selection of other weapons from handguns and submachineguns to tripwires, mines and shoulder fire AT rocket launchers/ Panzerfausts with the small arms also having a number of attachments and modifications that you can put on them to fit your style. On the topic of playstyle, you can go loud or you can go quiet. You can shoot your way, be it stealthy or loud or indeed use a number of booby traps etc and allow the enemy to effectively kill themselves. This also allows for a good amount of replayability as you can go through missions trying different routes and techniques.....also slow-mo headshots/ vital organ shots never really get dull. 

I would thoroughly recommend this game to players of all skill levels as there is a great deal of difficulty customisation which can even be changed during the mission. At the easiest end you'll have a ton of health, enemies will not be as quick to spot you, nor will their tactics be as aggressive in flushing you out and you'll have a great deal of help with lining up those crucial shots. On the other end of the scale, you'll have a reduced hud, reduced stamina/ longer wait for heart-rate to recover and will have to work out the elevation and windage yourself in order to make your rounds meet their mark. 

All in all a brilliant game, made better by finally allowing first person sights for pistols and submachine guns, making them more useful (something which irritated me with earlier titles). 

Now, what I'd like to see next is a redux of the first sniper elite that I had on PS2 (and also have on PC) but repacked into this game engine! 

This game is worth the money and if you can get it on sale then honestly you're cheating yourself if you don't get it.

review_text: One of the most challenging yet satisfying games I have had the opportunity to play. The game itself is the same formula of what Sniper Elite enthusiasts have been able to experience. The game mechanics and gameplay is smooth with only the occasional clipping to certain areas and locations. The game offers large maps with exploration but at time requires you to bottleneck to certain areas which at times takes away from the exploration and maneuvering. However, it is a tactical game which requires you to think about strategizing how to get passed these choke points. Preferably, it would have been best to allow for wider maneuvering but I understand where the developers are trying to impose on the player and make it a more engaging experience than simply avoiding all confrontation. Nevertheless, besides very few minor bugs and body physics the game is great for anyone that enjoys the Sniper Elite series or has a taste of sniper games with a bit more to offer. The one part I feel that it is necessary to include is that although I enjoyed the game for the most part I do no believe it is worth the full price tag. I was fortunate to purchase the game on sale and strongly recommend you wait until a sale comes along your way. Even with moderate difficulty the game can be beaten in a relatively short time. The lengths of the game, along with the repetitiveness of certain tasks and shooting may become underwhelming for players as they progress through the campaign. Therefore, I recommend you save the most that you can of your hard earned money to purchase this game at a heavy discount. Nevertheless, the game is an enjoyable experience for both the casual and hardcore gamer, combined with beautiful scenery and smooth gameplay mechanics I would find it difficult for someone to have negative feedback for game that has stood the test of time giving its fanbase with the same qualities of the previous Sniper Elite games and a little bit more! Happy Sniping!

review_text:
[b]Foreword[/b]

This is my 1000th review. My journey began in 2012 with Left 4 Dead 2. I had one more review in that year and only two the next year. I really started writing regularly 10 years ago. I try to be informative (not always) but first and foremost these are just snippets of my gaming life. Mostly positive, rarely ranting about games but all in all I am really grateful for this feature offered by Steam. If you liked the words my brain managed to conjure up in a foreign language many of us use only as a lingua franca, if you took the time to read at least some of it or if you read all or perhaps gave an award... or in case you decided to make a purchase because of these lines then I thank you! It means a lot to me!

[b]Allons enfants de la patrie[/b]

France. The perfect choice after Italy. v2 had way too many demolished buildings and dark colours everywhere, episode 3 was better but a little too bright for my taste. I really started enjoying the series with Sniper Elite 4. Now, with this one the resistance Karl teams up with has a different kind of accent. And the theme we hear regularly has been [i]Frenchified[/i].

[b]Le jour de gloire est arrivé ![/b]

8 missions. The all too familiar number. Well, it is actually 9 with an added bonus you can consider as the boss fight. A short, straight-to-the-point scenario while the rest gives us the usual vast areas with lots of objectives and different ways to solve the ones designated as our primary ones. A returning optional objective is when, for instance, we have an officer to eliminate. Find where he is patrolling and decide if you want to proceed in the recommended way (by causing an accident) or just in the good old SE way. Complete every objective you have to and get the best rating after each chapter. 

[b]Contre nous de la tyrannie,[/b]

A tyrant is what Möller is! The new antagonist Karl needs to face. The story has him converse with resistance members and there are cutscenes showing Möller addressing his men. These mostly include phone conversations after missions where he desperately wants to stop [i]The Shadow[/i], the one who annoyed the bad guys by sabotaging their grand plans in previous episodes. Again, no special awards here for the plot but I liked how infamous Karl is, plus, there is the introduction of Jeff Sullivan. He is from the US Army Rangers and thinks Karl causes more harm and opposes essentially everything he does. It's nice to see how their relationship changes throughout the story.

[b]L'étendard sanglant est levé[/b]

But what new things Sniper Elite 5 has to offer? It already looked beautiful in episode 4, Kill Cam already had many layers (organs, bones, muscles and veins). Well, Kill Cam now shows a lot of destruction done to the bone. Lots of pieces flying off. And even your SMG or a well-aimed shot from your Welrod can result in a slow-mo bullet path. In a way this wasn't really needed and hearing the exploding sound of a shot from a pistol with an attached suppressor actually looks (and sounds) pretty silly. Perhaps the most satisfying shots are those involving traps with the many flying shrapnels.

[b]L'étendard sanglant est levé[/b]

And let's not forget about the new focus mode. A special vision that allows us to see through walls. Not very far though! Just to see where the silhouettes of those soldiers are who are fast approaching since they have just heard a shot. Focus is not needed for a win but its activation (that also elevates the footsteps of incoming soldiers) can definitely reduce the number of quickloads. 

[b]Entendez-vous dans les campagnes[/b]

What about the upgrades and the skills? They have been reworked and thank God for that! As we proceed with the story we get XP and eventually rank up. Upon reaching level 40 (which is the maximum in single player) we can purchase all skills. They make our focus use better, add extra slots for our special ammos or allow us to revive ourselves with a medkit. Nothing special but if you do all objectives and try to be as stealthy as possible you will reach max level by the last mission.

As for weapons: no silly requirements to eliminate tons of enemy soldiers. There are many attachments available and we get them as we find workbenches. Consider them secret places and add them to the list of already vast collectibles such as personal letters, orders, level-specific items we can pick up and stone eagles we need to shoot from afar. Karl can also be replaced by resistance members and his clothing can be modified along with his hat. I noticed that when you pick another character that one does not make any comments on story progression. Too bad as it would have been nice listening to their different comments on the tasks ahead when you do another walkthrough. I picked Marie Chevalier but she mostly remained silent.

[b]Mugir ces féroces soldats ?[/b]

Now, hardcore fans will hate Sniper Elite 5. There is Authentic but there is no Authentic Plus. Naturally, this difficulty setting removes the focus ability since this is also considered an aid during a mission, but saving regularly remains a possibility. If you want, you can change the setting in a very detailed way and create a mix between, let's say, Hard and Authentic. This is a fully customisable feature!

[b]Ils viennent jusque dans vos bras[/b]

Multiplayer and Survival modes return. And of course the cooperative mode. But Overwatch is nowhere to be found and while Invasion mode is interesting I wasn't interested in it, at all. In this mode you join in on another player's campaign but as an enemy sniper! Making eliminations in such way unlocks some character and weapon skins. It's interesting how the achievement system has been reworked in favour of this. No coop achievements, at all. One you get for doing a lot of waves in Survival and one for completing a match in multiplayer. Perhaps the creators pulled a report, looked at the numbers and realised Sniper Elite is best played alone. I heard the Invasion mode is something that Elden Ring has, too. 

[b]Égorger vos fils et vos compagnes ![/b]

What else? Some new enemy types such as the Vampir Jägers. They are snipers with infrared scopes, tailored for night missions. They have more health but if you don't go guns blazing but do everything in a stealthy way you barely notice their presence. And, naturally, the game comes with lots of DLCs. 5 missions in 2 packs labelled as seasons. Weapon and skin packs, too, and the usual mission for eliminating Hitler. This is perhaps the funniest of all!

There are many achievements but to increase the game's longevity we can acquire medals if a given challenge is completed or ribbons that can be regularly obtained by killing enemy soldiers. Oh, and soldiers can now be pacified. Making them unconscious means extra XP at the end of each level. I hate the mastery achievements that require enemies killed by pistols, rifles and our secondary weapons. All of them! Now, that's the real grind in SE 5.

[b]Aux armes, citoyens ![/b]

Sniper Elite 5 is a fantastic game! Rarely do we see improvement constantly in a series where episode 5 is pretty much the best Sniper Elite has to offer. It has semi open-world missions with great replayability, decent DLC packs and some extra modes if you are tired of picking up your rifle alone. I had fun with the game... I have had fun ever since I launched v2 many years ago. And while the zombie titles can also be fun this is the series with the real sniping experience!

review_text:
This one's a weird kind of "recommend" for me. I've played Sniper Elite since V2 and enjoyed all of them, including 5; however, I feel at this point that the formula is starting to get a bit tired and that Rebellion has nearly exhausted Karl and this franchise as a whole. Basically, if you like Sniper Elite and want more of it, 5 will definitely give you that. If you're expecting much new mechanically or design-wise from it, though, you'll be left wanting.

SE5 continues the trends from the previous game with how SE looks, feels, and plays. The spotting, sneaking, and shooting mechanics haven't changed at all outside of the continued reduction of natural soundmasks in favor of suppressed weapons and precisely placed generators just waiting to be sabotaged. The games have leaned into a more Hitman-esque murder-puzzle loop with each entry, and SE5 is the latest there--for better or worse.

As has been the case for a while now, half of the arsenal is locked behind DLC paywalls, but there's enough variety in the vanilla arsenal to get you through the game. Although it doesn't matter so much as you won't even recognize half of your guns once you're through customizing them, as SE5 has been infected by the Modern-Warfare-reboots-and-Tarkov-sourced "granular weapon customization" pathogen. I actually enjoy that feature in other games, but in a WWII shooter attempting to brand itself as "authentic" for the whole series--including in its hardest difficulty--it feels odd and against that vision. To be fair, it's not as bad as COD Vanguard, but something about putting a Russian PU scope, shoulder stock, foregrip, and bulky suppressor on a WWII-era M1911 doesn't feel right to me. It's a minor complaint, since that's just how many modern mainstream games are--chase the trends whether it clashes with the identity of your game or not.

The story is also pretty mediocre, as you'd expect from Sniper Elite--you're not here for it anyway, and I think Rebellion knows that. There's a short intro and outro to each mission narrated by Karl and/or a British SOE handler of sorts, as well as intro cutscenes featuring the game's "characters"--if you can really call them that. They're only present to provide Karl and the player with the thinnest thread of context for each mission, as well as linking them to the larger war as a whole. I'm impressed they resisted a full-on D-Day mission, to be honest, since this game skips over the week the landings took place. I'm glad Karl got a bit of a break.

As a more serious issue, however, Sniper Elite 5 is buggy--and I mean it's infested with them. The detection system frequently bugs out, leaving enemies frozen behind a single piece of cover as they "Investigate" the gunshot they heard. Enemies hear sounds that they shouldn't or don't hear whistles and distraction devices when you're ten feet away. Some enemies will randomly become untagged--as far as I know there's no limit to tags and they're the regular guards as opposed to the trucks that sometimes drive through the map and despawn on the other end. Sometimes dropping a body will send them into the Earth's core, never to be seen again. If you want to guarantee that happening, quicksaves often result in that exact behavior--or them falling through floors or off ledges rather than where you left them. And I promise you will want to use quicksaves, given that SE5's missions are long (my pace of play is admittedly slow and methodical on the Hard difficulty, and I try to complete most if not all of the side objectives, so all in all I'm spending 2-3 hours on each level). If you're not careful you will get set back 20-30 minutes if you decide to reload and forget the all-important F5 key. Surfaces that should be easily shot through, like some leaves on a bush, sometimes aren't when the game randomly decides they're actually those rare rolled-steel bushes the Germans farm all of their tank armor from.

While nothing is totally game-breaking, it's a lot of minorly frustrating things that add up; some to the point where I've had to put down the game for a few hours or a day and come back later. Nothing like losing 30 minutes of progress where the game had a dozen opportunities for a fine, safe autosave to get you to take a break for a while.

I will admit I didn't touch the multiplayer or the Axis Invasion modes at all. Going through the first time I didn't really want some fanatical sniper spawning in and doming me midway through a mission--if anyone even still plays this game at all--so I turned it off. I remember watching some gameplay years back, and it looked fun and like an interesting twist for those into that sort of disruption, but it wasn't for me and not what I'm playing Sniper Elite to experience. I also tried one round of Survival and found it incredibly tedious. I ended up quitting on Wave 3 when I realized the five waves were going to take almost an hour. I'm sure it's more fun in a group but so is everything so it's not much of a feature-add for me.

Regardless though, it's still...fine. The game looks decent even a couple years out, runs well, doesn't crash or hitch outside of a mildly frequent (and more annoying than anything) crash-to-desktop immediately after hitting "Play" in the launcher, and is overall fun despite the shortcomings I mentioned. Would I recommend it to someone looking to get into Sniper Elite? I guess; I'd prefer you tried V2 or 3 first but there's nothing wrong with 4 or 5 besides how tired they feel at this point. It's clear that there's not many places they can or want to push the franchise to, and are risking stretching Karl's continuity to the breaking point. I think a time period change and return to the more sniper-focused gameplay would do this game well--although I imagine Rebellion is very comfortable inside the relatively low-nuance and "safe" setting of WWII. Killing Nazis is only going to make weirdos upset, whereas you might raise some eyebrows with, say, a Vietnam, Gulf War, or GWOT setting--where you don't have the broad cultural consensus of a "just and good war" as you do with WWII.

As I said at the top, I softly recommend Sniper Elite 5. It's more "modern" Sniper Elite, so if you liked SE4 you'll absolutely love this since it's more of the exact same. If you liked V2 and 3, you'll probably find it alright. If you're not into Sniper Elite at all...well, your mileage may vary but you'll probably have a decent time.

[h1]Sniper Elite never disappoints.[/h1]

The only thing you could slightly nitpick about in Sniper Elite V is the presentation. The grafics are notably dated, but they still look decent and the leveldesign and artstyle more than make up for it. The music is a bit meh and here or there the voice-acting is cheesy af, but apart from that Sniper Elite V is high quality entertainment all the way.

Compared to the previous Sniper Elite games, there are no big innovations or improvements, apart from a few gameplay aspects that were sloppily stolen from the latest Hitman games. Sniper Elite has basically been the same game ever since Sniper Elite III, not due to lazy devs, but because there is so little room for improvement in my opinion. Once again, the biggest strength is the completely scalable difficulty setting with a lot of options to make it easier or harder, which greatly benefits the replay value, too. The semi-open-world missions provide a lot of tactical freedom: You are an absolute noob and just want to play it like a casual run-and-gun-Third-person-shooter? No problem. You‘re a military-trained Navy Seal elite soldier looking for a borderline realistic sniper challenge? Have at it.

When it comes to WWII-themed games, the Sniper Elite series is up there with the finest WWII games in general. It‘s basically the best WWII Stealth game/Third-person-shooter out there and the fifth installment is among the best of the bunch. A very strong 6/8.

Great game. However since I am a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, here are some complaints:

-Climbing over stuff is very inconsistent. Some barriers and walls which you should totally able to climb aren't and some are. You can't jump over a lot of tiny obstacles

-The map Saint Denis is awful. It looks stunning but the design sucks. You gotta work your way up the city, which is overly hard because you never got any high ground. Every building looks kinda the same aswell.

-Despite great graphics, the antialiasing is still awful. This has been an issue since the last game and they didn't fix it. Even at high resolutions and upscaling, the whole screen flickers from the lack of proper antialiasing.

-In some points of maps, there is literally zero cover. I got stuck near the beach and there was literally only one way out with 0 bushes and 0 walls or rocks. Each time I loaded the save I got overrun by enemies and there was only one path out of there. There are multiple location where this can happen. Again, I think this is kind of a map design flaw.

-There are less sound masking options for the sniper rifle than in SE4. Generators are rare and the occasional plane and artillery fire also don't occur very often. I ended up using a rifle with a built in suppressor, which as a downside has a terrible range.

-A.I. can be very unfair at times. They can track you through walls even when you're not spotted.

-The DLC's, as already mentioned by other players, are way too expensive. Most of them are not worth it anyways (a fckin skin and a gun for 10 bucks).

Overall I enjoyed Sniper Elite 4 and 5 the most. The map design of both games is comparable I'd say. It has its flaws and I wish you had even more options to kill enemies, like in other stealth titles such as Hitman.
