9.5/10 sniping
9/10 stealth

Apart from Sniper Ghost Warrior Contracts 2 this is the best sniping gets. just turn off the easymode breath holding diamond and have a blast lining up 200-800m shots. 

my only sniping gripe is the overall lack of extreme long range sniping spots (minus .5 on sniping). i can only think of a few off the top of my head and they are very limited in number of enemies you can go for especially once theyre alert. 

authentic is a very good challenge if you really like stealth but i dont think the binos and sniper scopes should have locked zoom levels (minus .5 stealth), its not exactly realistic which is what theyre going for and its one less tool u have that you really need but thats only on authentic. my only other stealth issue is fluidity. Karl isnt that great at not getting seen doing inconspicuous ♥♥♥♥. knifing a guy from brush with other guys around gets you seen. corner hugging and knifing a guy pulls karl from cover and gets you seen. etc etc etc. why am i walking around with weapons silenced into the dirt if im getting seen doing things that shouldnt get me caught (minus .5 stealth). bit of a minor gripe i suppose but getting the fluidity of movement and takedowns right is a MUST in stealth games

Overall fantastic game made from the trial and error of its predecessors. the wind and bullet drop indicators are actually accurate in this game so you can trust your shot will hit where you want it to be 99% of the time unlike SE4. the upgrade tree has useful passives but towards the end you kind of forget about all of them cuz they are things you just need to survive on higher difficulties. not really a negative but karl isnt really a superhero hes just a good sniper with wallhacks (unless your on authentic). all the secondary tools are really useful if you know how to set up a sniping nest you can just trap it to hell and back so no one ever finds you even if you go somewhat loud.

multiplayer is pretty fun, its nice to be able to walk around the map as a nazi and get the lay of the land if you havent played the mission yet. noting objectives and caches. not having to worry about stealth for a change is really refreshing. using loud weapons and running til ur close to the enemy sniper is a nice change. your locked to your hosts difficulty level which i suppose only i see as a negative but im sure more people would complain if everyone accepting invasions played on authentic XD. hopes and dreams. in my experience most of the invasions devolve into who ever knifes the other first. majority of the time i cant find the host from a distance because as mentioned above there arent many long range sniping spots maybe 1-2 a mission if your lucky and find it. when you do get into a sniping battle with another player tho its pretty exhilerating. they definitely got that part right. i just wish there were more chances for it.

Pros
Variable Difficulty. True sniper aim is now separate from the enemy difficulty. I'm not a fan of the bullet drift mechanic and I am not looking for a realistic sniping experience. I want my bullet to go where I aim. But that doesn't mean I want the enemies to always be easy either. In SE4, in order to disable true aim, you were forced to run in easy mode. Difficulty settings have been split up so you can choose easy aim with difficult enemies.
Non-lethal ammo and take-downs. When I first saw these, I passed them by as useless. Boy was I wrong. Knocking out enemies causes nearby soldiers to investigate rather than freak out when they see their comrades being killed. Extremely useful in an area filled with enemy soldiers.
4th weapon. Yep, keep your perfect load-out and when you see that tank buster, you can pick it up in addition to your 3 custom weapons.
Melee attacks. In higher difficulties, if an enemy knows where you are, your melee attack will not always work! They can break your attack wasting your time while reinforcements arrive. 

Cons
No more unlimited satchel charges. You have to search for them.
No more unlimited rocks to throw to cause distractions. Now you have to find and collect bottles.
Vehicle destruction is now very difficult. Gone are the single shot destruction of trucks and cars.
The maps are large and interesting...but imho, not as interesting as in SE4. Some areas the enemies are feast or famine. There are large areas with no enemies and small areas with many enemies.
Harder to spot enemies. You will be relying on your radar far more in this game. Enemies show up as a large circle on your radar before they are tagged. Once tagged, the circle disappears. Sometime the large circle makes it easier to spot an enemy than when they are tagged.

[h1]A Missed Shot at Innovation[/h1]

Snagged this game on a 70% off sale, and let me tell you, even at that discount, it felt like I overpaid. Sniper Elite 5 takes you on a nostalgic journey back to the first Medal of Honor, except without the charm of it being 1999. You're funneled down the same unimaginative, rigid paths that could bore even the most ardent history buffs to tears.

On 'Sniper Elite' difficulty it's like playing on 'toddler mode.' Make a blunder so colossal it should have you ousted from the brotherhood of snipers? No problem! This game forgives like your grandma, letting even the worst mistakes slide with barely a slap on the wrist.

The graphics? Oh, they've got high-quality textures, alright. People and objects sometimes look so sharp you’d swear they could cut glass. Too bad that’s where the innovation ends. The first cutscene? It's like a B-movie zombie apocalypse minus the suspense and horror, complete with characters sporting the dead-eyed stare of a department store mannequin and movements as fluid as a robot dance from a 1980s pop video.

In conclusion, if you’re looking for a game that manages to simultaneously bore and annoy, Sniper Elite 5 might just be your perfect match. It's a lackluster parade of missed opportunities wrapped in the thin veneer of modern graphics, proving once again that not all upgrades are for the better. So, buckle up for this snooze-fest; you’ll need the sniper’s focus just to stay awake.

review_text:
I’ve quite enjoyed Sniper Elite 4 about 6 years ago. It was hardly as detailed or inventive as the titles it directly pulled from, like Hitman or Metal Gear Solid V, but what it had was extremely fun and satisfying. So I was looking forward to playing a sequel, yet when Sniper Elite 5 came out I was too stressed due to living through early months of the full scale russian invasion, I was rather picky about which games I was comfortable playing. Plus, a lot of the initial user reviews on the game were surprisingly negative, commenting on its inferiority to the fourth game. Two years since its release and one year since the release of its final DLC mission, I’ve decided to give it a shot and was not disappointed.

A lot of Sniper Elite 5 can be described as “Sniper Elite 4, but improved”. If in the previous title the franchise have finally found itself, here the developers were trying to polish and perfect its ideas, without reinventing the game again. It’s still a stealth third person shooter with emphasis on using the sniper rifle. You still get huge open maps with several main and optional objectives. You have Hitman-like traversal abilities and an automated sticky cover system. There are systems in place to simulate different aspects of shooting and a lot of the stealth is based around using traps and making it hard for enemies to triangulate and figure out your exact position. And, of course, the slow motion x-ray kill cameras are back again, but are made even more customizable and tied to more systems. All of this is as good, and often better, than it used to be in the previous game with lots of very smart and helpful UI improvements and changes to make things easier to understand.

But on top of just improving things, there are expansions of systems and new ideas added. Enemies, for example, are no longer clearly shown on the map before you tag them, and are instead shown as a big vague circle, making it all the more important to recon before engaging unless you want to be caught completely off guard. The “see through walls” vision is here to help with it, without it being too overpowered and helpful at the same time. More things can be found on the maps, like hidden modification tables and starting points, in addition to just intel and collectibles, making it even harder to “do everything” on your first go, unless you are very thorough.

Amount of trap items is decreased to an essential minimum, but more elements can be trapped and more things in the environment can be turned into a sound producing thing that hides the sounds of your shots. All maps have two types of tools hidden in them, lack of which makes some interactions slower or completely unavailable. The skill concept is changed, but it still feels like an afterthought as none of its improvements are that gameplay changing. Also, non-lethal approach is made possible, though I fail to see how it fits this setting and this story… Oh and more additional modes, that I personally never cared much about, are added – including an invasion mechanic, where other players can join your game as enemy snipers if you enable it. I didn’t want to bother with installing anti-cheat, so I didn’t, but it sounds like a cool idea.

Some elements of the game remain quite rough. It’s still possible to find spots of geometry on the map working against you in a “level designers missed this spot” kind of way. Climbing stuff and sticky cover never feel reliable and can misfire or not activate when they should. Enemies can and will glitch out in silly ways. Spawning enemies is still proximity based and while most levels hide it well, using level geometry to make it hard or impossible to engage with enemies across the entire map, or by having new enemies arrive or be inside a building thus explaining their absence from afar. But you will notice this issue from time to time, even though most of the time when you have a good vantage point, you can see at least some of the enemies from very very far away (and kill them).

DLCs are still a mixed bag. Missions are quite alright, but are basically “more of the same”. And some of them, most notably Kraken Awakens, have an especially egregious examples of enemy spawning very noticeably. You get your obligatory “kill Hitler” mission once again, and you get a selection of maps that will give you more of the fun and satisfying Sniper Elite 5 gameplay, if you want it. But I’d not recommend getting them until after you’re done with the main game as you might feel that you don’t want more. And the weapons and skins DLCs… I haven’t used them, as with the previous game. All of these titles are very good with providing you with a fun loadout from the beginning and since you can customize elements of weapons, it’s far easier to get what you want with just that and not by having more different guns.

Overall, I could easily recommend Sniper Elite 5. Just like its predecessor, it’s not the best stealth game out there, but landing sniper shots and utilizing traps to kill nazis is very satisfying and doesn’t get boring across a rather long campaign, if you try to do all objectives and find as much optional stuff as you can. The improvements of the game also make it an easy recommendation over Sniper Elite 4, but at the same time, I feel like it’s still worth playing the fourth game as well. I’m very curious to see where the series can go next from here, but if it’s going to be more of this, I probably won’t mind.

review_text:
I am a long term Sniper Elite player, particularly SE4 on Authentic Plus difficulty, so arrived into this via a Steam sale for the complete package at what seems finally a fair deal for the mixed bag that was both the season passes.  Firstly the good: the graphics are a major upgrade, the sound is exceptional, Karl is voiced incredibly even if some of the other voice actors aren't so good.  The plot so far has been cohesive and made sense.  

The maps are substantially larger and seem mostly varied and really well designed, from the rolling hills of the French countryside to the maze like chateau city, to the channel islands, it's great variety and they have well designed options allowing for many ways to approach situations.  

Now for the bad: the game is too easy.  I am playing on Authentic (top difficulty mode) and think it's overly generous: many times I get an enemy opening fire on me and I have time to turn around, kill them and heal as if nothing happened.. no, I should be dead if we're being authentic here! 

Similarly the weapon realism has been downgraded substantially because many weapons can now be unrealistically suppressed to crazily low sound levels (eg a Welrod can be taken down deom 50m+ in SE4 to just  7m audible distance in SE5.. you can sit in long grass popping off around enemy and apparently they can't hear you even on Authentic!).  Long distance sniping now includes a visual aim assist for bullet drop that is always on in the HUD.  In SE4 you just got a wind indicator then needed to use binoculars to gauge distance of a target then all the rest was your own skill and estimation to snipe a target.. at distances over 200m it was a massive challenge and accomplishment.  Now?  Long distance sniping becomes very easy indeed even on the top difficulty mode.  Another issue I have are the edges of the map: several times they're weird holes in the middle of the maps, but also on the edges they are roads you look like you can walk down then just are told you can't.   A well placed mountain or blockade would be 10x better than a message reminding you it's a map edge.

Overall, Sniper Elite 5 is a great game.  I haven't even turned on Invasion Mode yet or played any of the DLC, but I fully expect to get a lot of replayability out of this.  What does concern me though, is that it isn't going to ever be the fiendishly difficult challenge of Sniper Elite 4 Authentic Plus difficulty.  To get through any single map on that mode is a huge achievement: near impossible for most players.  That's what we want: the challenge, the danger, the need to use skill at the highest levels and stealth and tactics to survive.  

By contrast in Authentic mode on this, you can run around with a machine gun half the time and play it almost like an arcade action shooter.  Fine for lower difficulty, as is the aim assist etc, but the lack of a proper high difficulty authentic plus mode is a problem for Sniper Elite veterans. I suspect I'll go back to SE4 again over this in a few months once I've exhausted all the content, and that's not how it should be.  Overall I give this game a 7.5/10: it's solid but the lack of authentic plus loses it a full point for long term replayability.

review_text:
While I will give a thumbs down for this game review, I *do* like the game, fun to mess around in and nothing else. This review will only be for single-player, non-axis invasion.

 [h1]The Pros[/h1]
- Weapon Customization. It's very fun to fiddle around with different types of weapon accessories, even if most don't really need to exist.

- Weapon x-rays. It's cool to see where you end up hitting a target with a pistol, or any secondary, really.

- First person aiming on non-rifle weapons. This helps GREATLY when trying to be accurate and even sometimes discreet when doing stealth.

- Multiple starting points in every map. These are fun to change up how you play the given mission greatly. All starting points should be unlocked after completing the mission instead of finding them.

-Being able to bodyshot enemies in authentic mode. Semi-auto rifles still suffer greatly with a lack of power, however.

[h1]The Cons[/h1]
- Lack of scope marking customization. The T-post tactical of SE4 make authentic (plus) mode a far more enjoyable experience. Sure, there is the bullet drop indicator when you have a scope, but it's too far off to the right to be of any use.

- Reinforcement phone boxes are a waste of time. The enemy become easy pickings as you keep killing them trying beeline to it. Rigging, or creating a loud noise area is never worth it, non of the boxes are in a hidden location to make it worthwhile.

- Gun cycling/reloading sounds. They sound like hollow tin cans being clinked together.

- Nonlethal fighting. There's no real reason to do non-lethal other than to offset killing officers/soldier in a pure stealth run.

- Animations and model detail. Cut-scene animations and characters suffer this the most, they look really, really bad. The weapons look/are animated nice however.

- DLC/Skins. Too much money for what it is worth. If you want to buy a DLC, get the one with the DeLisle in it and don't buy anything else. 

- Bottles instead of rocks. I don't use bottles at all because of the max 6 bottles you can carry. Whistling is far more effective. Also why is it that you start every mission with 4 instead of 6 even when you unlock the perk to maximize the number of bottles you can carry?

- Lack of better stealth hiding places. Long grass is fine, but it would be interesting to hide inside boxes or crates. Would also be nice to have it so soldier get curious when they see a gun sticking out from a corner or grass.

- Big maps that only really have sniping action in small areas. Best you can do is snipe out some sentrys  and use that as your way in if the body doesn't get discovered.

-Decoys. They are useless. I have yet to see effective use with them that doesn't immediately cause them to find out that it's a decoy and now they are enclosing on your position. Decoys also have a big time to set up to be effective so it's not worth having.

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]
All-in-all my view is still negative despite it being a game  that I am still sinking time into since I have bought a few DLCs and whatnot. An OK game to get on a heavily discounted sale, and never full-price.

Absolutely astonishing game, much better than I expected. Paying for it was worth it. Gun mechanics significantly improved, the graphics became slightly more realisitc and most importantly, there's no german soldier who shoots a flare gun to bring an airstrike. To be honest, those airstrikes in Sniper Elite 4 were extremely annyoing. I also liked the alarm, made it much more realistic.

The campaign was very good, although I honestly prefer Sniper Elite 4's campaign, however, the Wolf Mountain mission is the very best level of any Sniper Elite game, much better than any of the Hitler's assassination missions in any other games. 

In the Wolf Mountain mission there are many fun and exciting ways of killing Hitler, such as by shooting his only testicle with a sniper when he's in the balcony, blowing him up with a rat bomb, replacing his mail with a grenade, poisoning his food or even impaling him with a bowling pin. The dialogues are excellent as well, loved hearing the German soldiers talking to each other about random subjects whilst I sneaked behind them. I swear, I did burst out laughing when Hitler yelled ''give me some room you buffoons'' to the soldiers who were following him.

Despite all that, there are some downsides of Sniper Elite 5. The most noticeable is the fact that there's no crouch running as in the previous game. Something else that bothered me was how some enemies can defend themselves from melee attacks when they are in combat mode despite Karl Fairburne being an extremely skilled fighter.

Overall, I definitelly do recommend Sniper Elite 5.

The question is, of course, whether the same development team was involved in each case... But I have to say that I usually play either solo or co-op campaign/max. co-op survival, otherwise I completely ignore the MP area.

BTW. of course the invasion mode is a welcome addition that would have suited the predecessor well, but beyond that SE5 seems in some places to have been quickly put together with the most necessary set pieces. At this point it should be mentioned that the controls have improved for Pc, but in my opinion the controller has deteriorated significantly.
Well, maybe the developers ran out of steam after creating the medieval island fortress (2nd mission) :D 
Because it's quite impressive, just like the rest of the maps, which look pretty nice when you compare them to real photos, and are also fun to play, but still have that typical Unreal look from the basic construction kit...or, as in the case of some cutscenes (or patrolling torpedo boats, for example), just look lovelessly thrown in. When has ''unfortunately'' probably worked according to schedule and didn't have the time to design it lovingly

As long as you don't want to carry over the demands from the predecessors and want something to shoot with your friend(s) with sniper or SE vibes, you'll get your money's worth here.

Sniper Elite 5 is definitely fun. My wish for the next SE would be that you put more time into stories and the game again, then I'm optimistic that it will be something xd

I wanted to love this game. I was a MASSIVE fan of Sniper Elite 4, and despite a few new features, the developers have made one single catastrophic mistake. Bigger doesn't always mean better.

What I loved most about Sniper Elite 4 was that the opening level was replayable. Grindy. You could predict where everyone was, complete the level in about 15 minutes when you knew it, and just have some fun... but Sniper Elite 5 has completely lost that.

It took almost an hour and a half to complete the first level, the same on the second, the third I got an hour into before I gave up, and (as much as it's a good game), I just don't have time for that. I need a game that I think "hey, I've got an hour spare, I'll play that and snipe some people"... but every level so far, keeping in mind I've tried 3 of the original 9, have been in depth large maps with a LOT of enemies, and this game compared to its predecessor has totally lost what made it "fun". It's become more of a simulator which really doesn't suit it at all.

In SE5 they've gone for "Hey, let's make massive maps because everyone is craving huge open worlds" without stopping to think if it actually suited the game, and it doesn't which is a massive shame. Partly because it's made SE5 almost unplayable for me, but mainly because I can see the level of work that they've put in to actually creating these huge levels, and that work has been the reason they've made me go back to Sniper Elite 4 again. Sniper Elite 5 is quite the disappointment. There are no innovations, just the same engine and mechanics. Gameplay is also frustrating, the leaves and trees seem to be a second barrier preventing the player from moving to the other location. Sometimes for a sniper and stealth game you don't feel the immersion at all. However, It brings a few new features and at the same time removes mechanics and simplifies the gameplay into normie levels that shouldn't be possible. This is a case of “one step forward and two steps back” and, unfortunately, the end result is not an evolution and despite a few curious moments, the new game fails to be better than its predecessor.

Rebellion unashamedly copied mechanics from higher profile franchises such as Hitman and Splinter Cell and plasted them on this mess. A game titled "Sniper" doesn't really have many sniping moments like in SE3 and SE4, mainly becoming "Pistol Elite" in cramped spaces more suited to Solid Snake than Karl Fairburne. Also, the inclusion of non-lethal takedowns is mind-boggling and lazy. There is no mission in which you have to incapacitate someone, so the ham-fisted non-lethal option is useless. It is like the devs simply got hold of a checklist of "What do the cool kids like nowadays?" and started swinging.

Following the hot string of lazyness, there are less tanks in this game, with only the King Tiger and without a creative use for them like in SE3: Afrika. Not a single French tank is in the game and the German uniforms are all wrong. The dev team was not even trying.

Sniper Elite 5 is fun mainly if played in co-op, but don't expect too much. The devs banked all their chips on the new Invasion Mode and if you take it away, SE5 becomes an inferior SE4 copy-paste. The map design is dumbed down, being more linear and close-combat. Might as well just play SC: Blacklist, with its far superior mechanics.

Don't expect too much, the story is very generic, the protagonists are weak and you won't remember anyone, basically the plot only serves as a background and the focus is on the gameplay. Long gone is the historical fiction from V2 and SE3, just look at the pretty colors.

The game is said to be set in France but it could take place anywhere. The only French thing in the entire campaign is the RSC rifle. There is no mention of Vichy troops such as the Milice Française or the risk of Resistance members being exposed and summarily executed. The Lebel? The MAS-38? Forget about them. France, Italy, Germany... whatever, the game could take place in downtown London; especially for the Germans being stabbed left and right, at any rate.

The Japanese conexion was a big deal in the promotion of this game but were, in reality, a disappointing afterthought, without the promising idea of a showdown with a Japanese elite guard protecting their admiral.

The game is also full of bugs and invisible walls. The floor just disappears from time to time, plunging Karl into Hades. Recycled animations and recycled burning cities from Sniper Elite V2 are also a sign of the lazy approach Rebellion took while making this game. A really sad final product, especially because I love the Sniper Elite franchise.

I waited on SE5 quite a while because I had heard some bad things about it. Bad reviews on Steam and other places. I'm pretty sure it started out as "mixed" on launch. But I eventually picked it up on Xbox gamepass and played through it on Authentic and felt the base campaign was very good. I hate the concept of multiplayer in single player (especially an Authentic campaign being ruined that way)

I recently picked up SE5 on Steam and went through the whole thing again, this time pretty much doing a no death Authentic run through the campaign because I knew the map layout. With the "perks" system it's much easier than old school Authentic but also much more accessible to single player gamers.

Final Score: 7.0

review_text:
I like it, despite its many, many flaws. 

Sure, the whole game ought to be a better game than it is. But the essence: unhurried sneaking around and head-shotting a finite number of bad guys from a safe distance is something I really enjoy. And it's fun too, when you miss too often and are forced to fight. 

The two co-op modes are campaign and survival. I’ve played a lot of survival with my brother, and with only 2 players on 4-player maps, it’s challenging enough to be fun – we get wiped out often enough :-) There are five survival maps to choose from. Each asks the players to repel (usually) 3 waves of Germans at a series of 4 command/ammo-resupply posts. Each map has a choice of 3-5 operations, that put the command posts in different places, so the survival games can feel quite different even on the same maps. Sadly, in SE5, no maps allow a long-ranged sniping game.

(And FYI, the steadiest way to join a friend's co-op game is for him to set up a lobby (For example: Play, Survival, Host) then for him to click on his own name in the top right to reveal an invite code. You click on your own name, see a form where you can type in his invite code, and you can now join your friend, even in a private game, even if you suffer a disconnect later...so long as you still have the code written down.)

The graphics are improved from SE4. Lots of green. Better faces. The settings are much more beautiful than say, L4D2 or Killing Zone, or most maps of World War Z. The voice-acting is good. The story, well...Sniper Elite stories are terrible :-)

And the user interface is still crap. It is adapted from a console layout. One example: stand/crouch/prone is controlled by one key instead of three. A second example: you select an item with one key, on a radial menu, then apply/use/deploy the item with a different shared key. Why a different key? Worse, the game won't let you select an empty item slot, and if you run out of an item, it auto-switches you to another item you still have in stock. So, many times I've selected a bandage, not realised I had no bandage, or had just run out of bandages, and instead of healing myself, I lobbed the explosive which had popped into my never-allowed-to-be-empty hand. Another example, but this is avoidable: the default hold breath key is the space bar. (Try assigning Breath-hold to shift.) With default settings, you often press space when NOT yet in scope, and when not in scope, space means hop over the cover in front of you...so you jump over a railing or wall in front of you and hang from it in full view of the enemy. Shared function keys.

(Just played some SE4. The F key isn’t so over-used. There are different keys for searching a corspe, using equipment, defusing a mine, or picking up a discarded weapon. Ammo is automatically picked up.)

Oh! I forgot. When your chosen cover is a bit too tall, you can observe over it, look downrange through your gun's scope, but cannot shoot. I simply had to stand before shooting, but there was NO indication of why I could not shoot. Similarly, my brother ran out of special ammo once and thought his main rifle was glitched - he had plenty of regular ammo but the game would not let him fire that weapon again until he switched ammo-type manually.

YouTube reviews are ambivalent about the new maps. They are more closely based on real environments than SE4, so there aren't as many long sniping opportunities. The new maps do feel more real. And that's nice. But the SE5 maps also feel more cramped. At distances under 100 meters, wind and bullet drop are somewhat insignificant, so the biggest skill in SE4, aiming your rifle over 100m, taking bullet drop and wind into your estimate, rarely becomes necessary.

In SE5, the combat distances are so short that aim-assist is turned on by default, except at the hardest difficulty, since aim-assist doesn't make much difference most of the time. Happily, one can customise the difficulties fairly finely, and turn off the aim-assist if one prefers to play that way. I think it's MUCH better. (With no aim assist, it feels GREAT when you get a head-shot over a 150m in a strong cross wind.) Unhappily, the fine difficulty management is really uneven. For example, in SE5 you can tune the mine defusal distance to about either 5, 6, or 7 feet. But you the HUD can only be adjusted by turning it off completely, or keeping it completely on, including its sixth-sense warning that the enemy is looking at you, and from which direction.

Yes, I finished on authentic difficulty, but no, I won't play authentic again. I like either lots of ammo, or the ability to conserve unused parts of my magazine when I reload. In authentic, I particularly don't like checking my health by trying to apply bandages (at full health, you get a message that you can't bandage yourself anymore.)

Gun modifications are a big, big thing in SE5. There are very detailed stats for each gun that you can examine while setting up your loadout. Vertical, horizontal recoil. Shot grouping. Damage. Audible range. Audible range is what I look at most. It can vary from about 4m to over 160m. Even with a quiet gun, eventually, the enemy will spot you, if you keep shooting. But a very quiet gun lets you shoot much more often without moving between shots.

Most of the mods and many of the guns only unlock after discovering particular workbenches, located in enemy territory on the campaign maps. (You do NOT have to return to the same workbenches to re-apply the mods after they are unlocked.) Some of the mods unlock after certain feats, like total headshots with the weapon, or kills within or beyond a certain distance. 

In my second playthrough of the campaign, I used the D.L. (De Lisle) Carbine, a highly suppressed rifle - only easily audible within 17m. It's a DLC gun. Well...the game is old now, so if you want to play, wait for a deep sale and get the DLC too - how else will you get a chance to kill Hitler in a dozen different ways?

In my first playthrough of SE5, I was pleased that tanks were realistically hard to kill. In SE4, it was always presumed that tank drivers and gunners had had their vision blocks damaged, and hence had removed them, and hence could be sniped through their small vision ports. Not in SE5. I used panzerfausts and TNT and teller mines to disable tank tracks and had to leave the tanks damaged but dangerous behind me; sometimes they'd burn out over the next 10 minutes or so. Unhappily, I later learned that SE5 simply has different weak points than SE4. Armoured cars have engine port covers that can be destroyed with bullets, after which the armored car can be blown up by shooting a couple of bullets into the engine. Tanks? Yeah, tanks too. With bullets, one can (not simply pierce a hole through, but instead) blow a big chunk of armor off the back of a King Tiger, between its exhaust ports, then blow up the tank completely by shooting its exposed engine. Bullets. A full-health King Tiger. Sigh. 

It can also feel a bit disappointing that even on the highest difficulty level, the enemy often stands still and peers about after a near miss, or when an explosive goes off nearby. The highest difficulty should feature bad guys that keep their heads down, or move a few feet behind cover before exposing themselves again. (Checked: SE4 enemies don't keep their heads nearly as still as enemies in SE5.)

And of course, even on authentic difficulty, there were plenty of magic healing kits to restore you to 100% health, and enemy snipers continued to reveal their position with lens flare on their scope that shows up like a search light.

Did I mention that when you crouch and concentrate ("focus"), you can see through walls out to a distance of about 50 feet? But you can turn that off in the the fine difficulty settings if you want.

And yet, I enjoyed the game. I really did. And I'm going to try SE4 again too, now that I've forgotten most of its maps.

Hmmm, Sniper Elite 5. 
Spent enough time playing it. Played all the other games in the series before it. So yeah I am aware of a lot of people not liking the game. Compared to the previous entry Sniper Elite 4. But let me tell you. This is probably the best Sniper Elite game I've ever played. And yes there are some drawbacks to this game. But if I could rate this game based on just one level. That level would be the Mission 3 location. Beaumont-Saint-Denis. This is by far the best location I've ever played in any sniper game. It has the combination of sniping from a great distance to close-up sneaking. The verticality, the variety of environmental details. Extreme detail of the architecture. And everything else about this map feels mesmerizing. I would rate this map 10 out of 10. However, you will not like it if you go all gun blazing or play it on easier difficulties. Sniper Elite 5 is a bit different when it comes to infiltration. It's much more like a Metal Gear Solid or a Splinter Cell game. You may have to rely on sneaking a lot more than just sniping from a vantage point. Also, you may have to rely on stealth takedowns as well. All I can say is to enjoy this game fully. Play it on at least sharpshooter difficulty, and have patience. Don't go gun blazing. Wait for the perfect moment. And have an idea about the distance and the loudness of your gun. The different kinds of ammunition you can use for different situations. Like if a good amount of enemies are scattered close by, they'll hear your shots even if it's from a silenced pistol. In that case, you could switch to subsonic ammo, which makes your gun so quiet that they won't hear your shots unless they're very close to you. The same goes for enemies that are very far away. Sometimes your gun doesn't have enough muzzle velocity to travel the bullet so far without dropping a significant amount. In that case, you can use match rounds that have higher velocity. And many other ammunition options.  If you have a good understanding of your surroundings and your weapons. you can clear a whole level with just your pistol. About the online modes. I'd say the invasion mode is unique. I liked it. But to fully engage in the story mode without any disruption, I'd recommend turning the invasion mode off for your first playthrough, 

If I talk about things I didn't like. It's probably the reduced option for carrying explosives. Some explosives are even missing. No option to take down a tank like before from afar. And of course, the way they limit you by putting invisible walls or objects that are seemingly easily traversable. But I got used to it soon. Would have been a much nicer experience for the big maps if they didn't have these barriers.
And finally, I rate this game 8/10.

Sniper Elite 5: French Fries, X-Ray Kill Cams, and Exploding Innards (Oh My!)
Picture this: Sun-drenched French beaches, quaint seaside villages, and the satisfying crack of a bullet connecting with a Nazi skull. No, it's not a Tarantino fever dream, it's Sniper Elite 5, a game where precision sniping meets explosive carnage and history gets a healthy dose of Hollywood.

Let's dissect this bad boy:

Vive la France! (With a Few Bullet Holes): The French countryside is stunningly rendered, from sprawling salt marshes to towering cliffs. But like a baguette left out in the sun, some parts get a little stale. Repetitive textures and generic towns can dampen the initial awe.

The Art of the Kill Shot: Lining up that perfect long-range headshot is pure dopamine gold. Wind whispers secrets in your ear, gravity plays its cruel hand, and that visceral thump of a bullet finding its mark is like a symphony for your trigger finger. The X-ray kill cam? Well, let's just say it's not for the faint of heart, but undeniably gruesomely fascinating.

Stealth or Rambo? You Decide: You're not just a walking gun turret, Agent Fairburne. You can stalk enemies like a shadow, utilizing silenced pistols and takedowns for a clean kill. Or, if subtlety isn't your forte, unleash your inner John Wick with a hail of bullets. The choice is yours, though the AI can be as predictable as a mime at a birthday party, making the stealth approach sometimes less than thrilling.

Open World…Open Questions: The sprawling map allows for exploration, but like a plate of overcooked fries, it can start to feel greasy after a while. Repetitive side missions and fetch quests can make you yearn for more depth.

Verdict: Sniper Elite 5 is a mixed bag of French fries and exploding innards. The core sniping gameplay is top-notch, offering a unique blend of challenge and satisfaction. But technical hiccups, repetitive elements, and a forgettable story hold it back from being a truly memorable experience. Still, if you crave long-range kills, X-ray-induced nightmares, and a chance to rewrite history with a sniper rifle, there's fun to be had here. Just don't expect a Michelin-starred meal.

Now go forth, OSS operatives, and liberate France one bullet at a time. Just remember, sometimes the quietest approach is the most satisfyingly explosive.

Overall Score: 7.5/10 - A solid sniping experience with a few burnt fries on the side.

Bonus Round:

The weapon customization is deep and satisfying, allowing you to tailor your rifle to your preferred killing style.
The multiplayer modes offer some fun diversions, from co-op infiltration to competitive deathmatches.
Don't underestimate the power of a well-placed trap. Those Nazis won't know what hit them (literally).
I hope this review helps you decide if Sniper Elite 5 is worth your time and bullets. Remember, everyone has their own taste in French fries and exploding Nazis, so take my words with a grain of salt (and maybe a dash of pepper) and see for yourself!

P.S. Big props to my AI co-pilot, Bard, for reminding me that not everyone is a master of ballistics. They may not be able to hit a cow from a china shop, but their knowledge of World War 2 history is as sharp as a freshly oiled Luger. Plus, they saved me from using the phrase "Nazi-popping" even once. So yeah, give Bard some love too. Maybe a few extra terabytes of storage or a shiny new language upgrade. They deserve it.

Sincerely,

review_text:
I 100%'d this a while ago and never got around to write the review. 

SE5 tends to be a downgrade from SE4. But I'll start with the one good thing SE5 did first:

[h1]Weapon customization[/h1]

SE5 adds a weapon customization system, you have to grind requirements for some of the parts and it's a bit tedious at times, but it's pretty cool. SE5 also adds different types of ammo (unfortunately you can only ever carry a very limited amount), including non-lethal rounds, which is very neat. 
I would say this customization system is the highlight of SE5, it's the main improvement it has to offer over SE4.

So now we can get on with the bad.

[h1]The movement[/h1]

The movement in SE5 is vastly inferior to SE4. I don't know why/how. Maybe Rebellion changed engine or needed to rework movement to allow for a feature and ♥♥♥♥♥♥ it up. The result is, the movement will attempt to kill you. Ledges are the main culprit, they were never much of a problem in SE4, but in SE5, Karl will try to hang from every ledge or fence, so much so that you'll start to think that if Karl could hang from a stairs's steps, he would.

It's very much the running theme of SE5, you'll go around, try to jump over a fence or a wall that's 1 meter high, and Karl will somehow hang on it instead of jumping over it, leaving you to get shot in the butt. To help you picture how ridiculous is truly is, you can check this screenshot https://imgur.com/a/5yJi0VI

[h1]Tiger IIs, Tiger IIs, and Tiger IIs.[/h1]

In Sniper Elite 4, the tanks you'll most often see were Panzer IIIs. Maybe a Panzer IV (I'm not sure there even was a 4). Otherwise you'll find italian armored cars and german armored cars. That was variety enough I'd say.

In Sniper Elite 5, all you'll see is Tiger IIs, Tiger IIs and more Tiger IIs. More Tiger IIs than germany ever produced in real life. In Sniper Elite 4, you could kill the driver by shooting the driver port and the gunner by shooting the gunner port. You cannot here. The only way to do any damage to those Tiger IIs is with explosive devices or using an armor-piercing in the rear where the engine is.

The Tiger IIs in SE5 are so out of place that Rebellion even forgot to makeup blueprints for it. There are blueprints for the Tiger I scattered all over the game, in one of the missions, one of the side objectives is to take pictures of the Tiger II's blueprints - and instead you take pictures of the Tiger I's blueprints, because Rebellion didn't make the II's blueprints...
It's minor, but genuinely ridiculous and feels like something really went wrong during development.

[h1]The plot[/h1]

I'll be lenient on the main plot, I mean it's pretty stupid and silly, but germany at the time did many stupid and silly things, and Sniper Elite hasn't really been trying to be believeable. The plot of the DLC however is so terrible that I have to say something. This will be spoilered in case you care, but really it's so bad I don't think anyone would care if they were spoiled on it.
[spoiler]
One of the DLC is a continuation of "Project Kraken", except we are no longer talking about submarines, we are now just talking about a regular aircraft carrier being built in broad daylight IN NORTH-WEST FRANCE IN LATE 1944.

Karl is sent alone to stop the "threat to the allies" that is a singular aircraft carrier escorted by 3 submarines, a fleet so dreadful it would immediately be sunk upon trying to leave port. Karl is sent deep into enemy territory to stop this great threat, "deep into enemy territory" as in, IN THE MIDDLE OF ALLIED-CONTROLLED FRANCE, IN THE RANGE OF 100 ALLIED AIRFIELDS THAT COULD JUST GO BOMB THE DAMN CARRIER THAT IS, AGAIN, BEING BUILT IN BROAD DAYLIGHT IN AN OPEN-AIR DRYDOCK.
[/spoiler]

[h1]The common complaints[/h1]

Some of the collectibles are really tedious to obtain, some of the achievements are really tedious, that's not new to SE5.

[h1]End words[/h1]

Alright Rebellion, you can let Karl go now. Yes, Karl has been the face of the Sniper Elite franchise, but I don't think anyone particularly cares about him and you really don't need to have yourself be held back by him.

You can go set a Sniper Elite with a different protagonist in the pacific theater, you can do wild things, different things, or hey, you could have a Finnish sniper facing the red army (or have Karl fill that role, but why would you do that), what I'm saying is, you're allowed to do different things Rebellion. 

End note: I'm judging Rebellion's games by AAA standards despite them being a relatively small studio because they monetize their games like an AAA developer. (Stop that. Have some decency. Please?)

review_text:
Sniper Elite 5 came off to a rough start at launch, but it didn't take the developers long to patch it up and make it essentially bug free. From that perspective, it's one of the best in the series in my opinion. From fantastic graphics to the sound effects and music, everything shows an attention to detail. The story is moderately interesting and does it's job as intended although, like the other games in this series, the realism is a bit out there :) 

I can't speak to the PvP experience as I did very little of it. 

+ Graphics. Some of the best I've ever seen in a PC game up to this point. Especially the damp wet and mud really stand out. The light reflecting off surfaces and the realism of tracks and grooves in the ground. 
+ Sound. Both the ambient effects as well as the music do their jobs outstandingly. Most of the time it's in the background where it should be, but you would miss it if it was gone. 
+ For achievement hunters, the achievements are fairly easily doable, with a couple of more "grindy" ones. If you enjoy the game, it gives you a reason to keep playing. All work as you'd expect. 
+ As with previous titles, there's a plethora of ways to kill Hitler, making that level nearly endlessly re-playable. The achievements allude to some, but there's many more not mentioned for the astute player.

I have no negatives for this game. I give it 10/10. I look forward to the next game in the franchise!

I could just copy and paste my review for Sniper Elite 4, because that's essentially what the makers of this game did. It's 4 with new maps. Although the maps are big, they are riddled with invisible walls, which gets pretty infuriating after a while. One great addition is the unlocking of two more infiltration points on each map, which definitely adds to the replay value.

I've played it through twice now, mainly because I didn't take the achievements - especially the weapon related ones - into account on my first playthrough. So now I'm just farming kills. 

For a game about snipers, there are surprisingly few long shots to be made. Most are mid-range (<100m). It's not that it's difficult to score headshots for the rifle mastery medals - Nazis heads are like bullet sponges - it's that a lot of enemies are too close for the 100+ m requirement. It's says quite a lot that in order to get a rifle gold medal you need 50 kills, but for a secondary gold medal you need 150 (!) kills. The game is telling you that sniping is secondary. So anyway I started blasting.

One thing which has remained constant however, is the main character. He's a supposedly elite soldier who is in worse shape than I am, panting and wheezing after a five meter sprint. But at least the running animation is better than in the previous games. And there is something peculiar about a game released in 2022 where there isn't a jump button. Time and time again super soldier gets stumped if a curb happens to be more than two inches high. Clearly they blew their load on the kill cam function, but it's still strange how they seemingly disregarded just about everything else.

I bought it on sale and the DLC is only worth it for the maps. I personally don't care about skins, but the ones they give you are absolutely horrendous. It's like they were designed by a five year old on crack.

OK if you can find it on sale, but not worth getting a full price.

I would like to give a neutral rating.

Is this a good game? Yes.

Is this the best Sniper Elite? I don’t think so.

My favorite to date is Sniper Elite 4, with the best balance of stealth, snipe, traps, infiltration, parkour…

I played Sniper Elite 5 in coop (two players doing the campaign). The game is solid, with very few bugs. It is very fun to be two snipers so we can cover each other. And this happens a lot of the time, because as soon as you get loud, the whole map (I am exaggerating, but you get the idea) will rush on your position.

You can customize weapons, but the way you unlock stuff is by completing challenges and finishing each mission. I don’t like that because first, you don’t know what the secret challenges are (if you don’t cheat by asking Internet), then there is the problem that the gear you are interested in will be unlocked in the last missions, and so you will not have much time to enjoy it… (at least for me who does not replay games).

The level design is not as good as in Sniper Elite 4: There are a lot of false calls, tempting you to climb a wall or something and you cannot do it because it is just a bit too tall, or just because the level designers decided that this is not the right place to do so…

All in all, this is a good game, but I would give it a 75% rating compared to Sniper Elite 4 (and maybe Sniper Elite 3). If you can buy everything, then go for it especially on sale. If you hesitate, buy just buy the 4 instead.

review_text:
[u] Sniper Elite 5 is a third person shooter developed and published by Rebellion Developments in 2022. Set during World War II, Sniper Elite 5 is the fifth entry to the Sniper Elite series of video games and features both a full 2 player cooperative campaign. This review will focus on the single player campaign played in cooperative mode. [/u]

[h3] TL;DR – Moving from one strength to another, Sniper Elite 5 is a progressive update of the Sniper Elite series and is easily the best to date with its huge levels and levels of freedom. [/h3]

Story (3/5) – Sniper Elite 5 takes place after the events of Sniper Elite 4 and is chronologically a year before the events of Sniper Elite V2. We are back with the titular sniper, Lieutenant Karl Fairburne, as he works his way through various parts of France and Germany to uncover the mysterious Nazi superweapon, “Operation Kraken”. While the overarching plot is interesting with plenty of lore bits along the way scattered in journals and posters, they merely act as a pre-tense to Sniper Elite 5’s gameplay loop of infiltrate, kill/blow up and exfiltrate. It’s neither overtly memorable nor, offensive in anyway which is perfectly fine. 

Controls (5/5) – Played with mouse and keyboard, Sniper Elite 5 adopts the same control scheme as the previous titles. The default key bindings are logical and easily accessible. Shooting feels natural and the option to adjust sensitivities really help to dial in aiming. Each action/key can be reconfigured to user’s preferences. Moreover, the use of a radial wheel to quickly access the various weapons, ammo types and gadgets make for very intuitive controls of the player’s otherwise very large arsenal.  

Gameplay (4/5) – Just like the games before it, Sniper Elite 5 features a large single map with a main objective and sub-objectives to be completed. How and in what order this is done, is entirely up to the player(s). Everything Sniper Elite 4 does well, 5 does better. Larger maps, more guns, improved traversal and stealth, more verticality, those are just the few improvements Rebellion has made. Stealth and sniping remain to be the core gameplay elements of the Sniper Elite series though, 5 makes it more acceptable than ever to simply go guns a blazing. This level of freedom in such a large playing field makes Sniper Elite 5 such a treat especially when played with a coop buddy. Points are docked for re-playability and some rather questionable enemy AI behaviours. 

Graphics (4/5) – Built on Rebellion’s in-house game engine, Asura, Sniper Elite 5 looks downright gorgeous from its incredibly detailed European castles and cottages to the spanning vistas and artillery shelled trenches. Excellent shadows and lighting also play a key role in bringing these large sets to live especially in the nighttime maps. The core art style and presentation does not differ much from the Sniper Elite series giving it an immediately recognizable feel and look that not many game franchises can claim to have these days. Almost a perfect score if not for the frequent graphical clipping issues encountered when interacting with enemy soldiers. 

Audio (4/5) – From the pop of each silenced gunshot to the boom of a large artillery round landing, the audio experience in Sniper Elite 5 is certainly a treat. Positional audio is serviceable for spotting enemy movements and gun shots. By far the best part is how the myriad of guns in the game have their own audio signature. 

Issues/Optimization – Sniper Elite 5 is very well optimized for the PC and ran well on my system. I had no issues running the game at 4K120 with most of the settings topped out. There were 1-2 hard crashes throughout my playthrough, but nothing serious otherwise. The most common bug you would probably encounter is a graphical one where dead enemies clip through terrain and rag doll in odd ways.

Overall (4/5) – Sniper Elite 5 builds upon all the strengths of Sniper Elite 4 and adds upon it with new gameplay elements that continues to make the game enjoyable. By far the biggest standout for me would be the huge, detailed maps which gives players so much freedom to tackle objectives in however way they see fit. Truly the best in series thus far and a benchmark for a game of this genre. If you can find a cooperative buddy to play this game with, it just makes it that much better. Highly recommended!

review_text:
For having only played a small bit of a Sniper Elite game probably 8 years ago, this was a hell of a place to jump in. Tight gunplay, excellent stealth combat, plenty of objectives and achievements to tackle, and...well, unfortunately, not enough people open their games up for Invasion mode, but it's awesome when it works.

Sniper Elite 5: France wastes none of your time in making for a bloody, strategic good time. Every map and mission can be approached in seemingly countless ways; mostly landing on either aggressive, kick-down-the-door style offensive tactics or more by-the-book, stealthy approach to slowly pick apart your enemy from within and afar. It's a f$&!%ing good time!

Gameplay pacing is fairly slow, even if you try rushing things. It truly is intended to be more methodically approached, person-by-person or squad-by-squad. You can push the boundaries a bit but don't expect it to play like a sandbox. It may have very large, open maps that can be approached in many ways - but there are its limits. There are only so many different stealth traps, explosives, or ways to maim your enemy before it starts getting at least slightly repetitive.

While I went in with fairly high expectations, I was still surprised by some of the more standout elements. The level design is top-notch. Take the second mission, this massive chateau with layers upon layers inside. Streets, passages, tunnels—it's like exploring three levels in one. Every replay, I discover something new. And the audio, they've really gone above and beyond. Something I was not expecting at all was after finishing the campaign, you can replay levels with different characters. The kicker— those other characters are ALL fully voiced, responding to what's happening in the game. Adds a whole new layer to the experience. I get the feeling most miss out on even trying this.

While Rebellion didn't stray too far from the mold, something new they did feature is called the Invasion mode. It really spices up the game if you’re willing to take a risk and I wish I had a whole, whole lot sooner. Far too few players ever enable this, not to mention, often wait until very, very late to toggle it on. Basically, if you switch the Invasion option on, as you play the campaign another player can join your game as the enemy sniper. You get more experience by completing objectives while having that option active, but there is always that danger of other players sneaking up on you and messing up your game. It makes you constantly on the edge and looking in all directions while sneaking around. You will usually think twice before sprinting in the open. Anxiety-inducing gameplay has never been so fun! Again though, not enough people seem to utilize this and it will only dwindle further as the game ages out. I do hope they implement this in future releases as it is a lot of fun and holds a lot of potential for more.

Sniper Elite 5 is a prime example of why you shouldn't mess with what's working. Too many sequels try to reinvent the wheel and end up misfiring. With an appropriately cruel twinkle in its eye, Sniper Elite 5 provides yet another 1,000 different ways to eliminate a Nazi and I applaud it for that. I can only imagine what I've missed in the previous entries of the franchise. It seems they regularly go for an 80-93% discount when on sale, so I will likely be picking one or more of those up to check out.

I'd say this is a must-buy for fans of stealth-based combat or for those who enjoy more objective-based, strategic shooters in general. With its still famous kill cam, new weapons, dynamic levels, and that invasion mode—you've got yourself a winner. Until the next sequel, Sniper Elite 5 stands tall as the pinnacle of the franchise.

As a fan of WW2 games and stealth games, I thought this was an amazing game. There are a variety of game modes, such as the campaign, PvP multiplayer, and survival. As an added bonus, if you enjoy hunting achievements like I do, this was a fairly easy game to 100%.

Campaign: I played through the campaign solo on the hardest difficulty as I like to take my time to explore and try to be as stealthy as possible, so I can't say how good the co-op is in this one. I thought the campaign was great, and you'll have even more missions if you get the DLC, and they are worth it in my opinion, especially on sale. The maps are huge, so you can tackle objectives in any order you like, and many objectives have several ways of completing them. Along the way you'll find collectibles and unlock weapons and mobs to customize them. The only real issue I had was the sniping opportunities, as I felt there weren't enough. To get gold medals for snipers, you must get headshots from at least 100m away with them, and I constantly found myself moving around and retreating in certain areas just to achieve that 100m distance. There is a lot of close quarters combat, which I also like, but I think there needs to be more vantage points for sniping.

PvP Multiplayer: I only played one round of this to get the achievement, but I didn't feel the desire to continue playing anymore than that. This isn't really the type of game I'd get for PvP matches. Aside from the base PvP modes, there is also invasion. Invasion allows you to enter someone's game as a German sniper or you can open yours for invading snipers. This adds a good challenge to your game if you find the AI is too easy.

Survival: This is a wave-based game mode where you must survive against 12 waves on enemies. There are a variety of survival missions on a variety of maps. The objective is to hold the command post, and after three waves, you'll unlock the next command post. You do not lose the match if you lose a post, but without them, you won't be able to access their resupply caches. I only played a few rounds of this, but it was quite fun and I recommend this mode if you're a fan of wave-based games.

It pains me to say, that for a studio that did SE4 - I am shocked and embarrassed by this effort.  Overall, there are a few slight improvements, but this game is SO poorly programmed and the movement is incredibly clunky.  My final opinion is that Rebellion thinks you are stupid, and need guidance for every part of the game.  You will see why if you buy it.  

PROS - good graphics and good core sniping mechanics.

CONS:

First and foremost -  it is just nuts that you can almost never use you sniper in a sniper game.  With enemies everywhere, the noise and alert distances are so far that you will ALWAYS get the alarm tripped no matter what and have to restart.  The noise generators and very occasional loud map theme noise allow for maybe 2 shots and then back to waiting for another 2 minutes, rinse and repeat.  ZZZZZZ.  

Whoever decided it was a good idea to get rid of the crouch half run should be fired.  The only choice now is to super creep taking a ♥♥♥♥ ton of time to move around the map (again, they think you are stupid) or to occasionally stand up to move faster and get spotted immediately.  

One of the first insights into the poor programming is when you get spotted, but the yellow or red triangle area doesn't go away for 10 minutes, even as you sit in a bush, invisible.  Most investigations take a full 10 minutes easy. Sometimes the triangle will stay on your map for the whole game.

There is zero vertical movement now.  Almost all of the action happens at the same horizontal level.  Sniper game?  Its just another example of their movement to forced and linear game play(as the game is transitioning to Hitman and Splinter Cell style game play).  There are very few opportunities to get higher. which is as anti sniper in a sniper game as you can do.

The movement is super clunky.  This game suffers from what I call "pixel disease" and is another example of how poorly coded this game is.  Your TINY white dot in the middle only recognizes what it is EXACTLY over.  You are going to be constantly frustrated about looking at items to pick them up.  Same with spotting - its so difficult to keep that single dot over your target in your binoculars at range and you will find more often than not that cant use them well.  Almost none of the movements or actions are smooth and effortless.

And why cant you tag through your scope?  You are already looking far in the same way, but yet you STILL have to switch to the horrible bulky binoculars (which by the way, cannot be set to open at the widest angle) which is more clumsiness and more because you have to widen the view upon using each time - even more clumsiness and more example of the poor programming.  

And speaking of clunkyness - its almost useless to hide bodies.  First and again (the poor programming) even if you are crouched and pick up a body, which is already very slow, you are unable to persist back to a crouch mode when you drop the body and will always stand up.  I stopped trying to be stealthy in this "sniper game" because you get spotted more than hiding a body helps because you always stand up at the end of it.  In fact, leave them all out and booby trap them all because refilling your traps in this game is super easy. 

The melee "combat system" could possibly be the dumbest part of this game.  Even if you are not seen when you go in and try to execute a stealth kill, some types of enemies fight back - which is fine, but you can basically only "stagger" someone and again the clunky animations ensure you are gonna be spotted. 

Even though you have a clear sight picture through a fence, you cannot fire through it.  Also, bullets hit bushes.

Climbing up or down a ladder many times results where you grab but go back down and then back up - clumsy.

Throwing the distraction rocks does nothing 90% of the time.  I prefer to play stealth style and again, i was sitting around waiting.

You cannot close any doors...In a stealth game??

No way to make the HUD even a little bit bigger...really?

Aside from a few alternate openings, there is only one way to go through out the map - the opposite of SE4.  Plus, it's very hard to tell where you can go, and where you can't.  There are no markers for anything and I was constantly bumping into invisible fences.

Oh, and other than the orange vines, it's very hard to tell where you can go up and where you cant.

Sniper Contracts 2 is everything this game wishes it could be and it's $6.  If you want a real stealth and sniping experience, get that instead.

review_text:
It pains me not to recommend a Sniper Elite game but this is probably the worst one since Sniper Elite V2. The main problem with V2 was how often they forced you into close quarters combat. This one is ambitious but they ultimately fell short.

The sniping is solid, it's been the same pretty much the whole series. The X-Ray mode is still fun to take a long distance shot, track the bullet, and watch as it kills an enemy, dealing damage to whatever organ you hit. The maps are quite large but the game really forces you to try to sneak instead of snipe.

There are enemies practically everywhere and they hear everything. There aren't many levels with loud noises that can muffle your shots and everything you do is incredibly loud. Enemies hear you moving unless you move at a snail's pace but you can't always move very slowly because you'll get spotted by enemies that can see a long range. The worst part of the sound is there are times enemies shouldn't be able to hear you but still can. For example, there are vehicle patrols in certain maps. If you run 50 feet behind a loud motorcycle, the person on the motorcycle will stop because they hear you. For a game that focuses on ambient sound to muffle your actions, how do you not have that affect a loud motorcycle muffling your footsteps of all things?

The stealth can just be very frustrating and you feel forced to do it. There are certain areas where you can't crawl or you can't crouch and the game doesn't stop you from moving into those areas, it just forces you to stand up. The problem is now you're suddenly running when you expect to be crouch walking and everyone near you hears you, giving away your position. This particularly happened when I had to go under a bridge to disarm bombs. I had to reload my save multiple times because I would step in just the wrong spot, forcing me to stand and alerting all nearby guards. 

Furthermore, there are a lot of areas you think you can vault over but you can't. You'll take your time and the risk of moving through an open area to move towards some cover, with the plan to vault over some sand bags and flank the enemy, to find that you can't vault over these particular sandbags. It happens a lot and there are a lot of these small walls blocking paths you want to take.

​Since there are so many enemies practically everywhere, taking a shot with your sniper rifle will alert most guards and one of them will surely run to an alarm where you'll be left outnumbered and forced to reload your last save. The sniping is fun but you constantly feel punished for doing it and feel forced to move around, silently taking out guards with melee whenever possible. 

This is definitely not one of the better Sniper Elite games. Go play a different one. Hopefully if and when they make Sniper Elite 6, they'll go back more towards what made 3 & 4 feel so fun.

This is a very good game. I mainly play slow, focusing on stealth, completing missions without raising and alarm, trying for all of the objectives and to completely clear the map. I love the gameplay, the locations are really thematic, and the graphics are pretty good. Because I play primary stealth, the mission stake quite some time to complete, meaning that the base game has a lot of hours of content for me.

I can often see where I need to be but have trouble figuring out how to actually get there, not because of enemies I need to avoid but because of artificial obstacles placed to block access by my sniper; this happens even on open landscape maps, where small obstacles/vegetation/walls are often unclimbable/uncrossable. And, of course, I really dislike the way they sell the game, with zillions of pieces of over-priced DLC (the same point many people complain about).

Despite those kinds of problems I really enjoy this game and look forward to playing more. I have completed every game in Sniper Elite series (though not yet done with all of the missions in 5), plus the Zombie Army games, and I enjoyed them all. Sniper Elite 5 is a welcome addition to the Sniper Elite franchise, offering a satisfying stealth experience with its slow-paced gameplay and realistic environments. The game's core mechanics remain unchanged from previous installments, but the new maps and missions provide a refreshing challenge for seasoned players.

The game's stealth mechanics are top-notch, encouraging players to carefully plan their approach and take out enemies silently. The X-ray kill cam remains a highlight, providing a gruesome yet satisfying reward for well-placed shots.

My character Karl was wearing a ghillie suit in the game, but he appeared in his default uniform during cutscenes. This created a jarring disconnect and felt like a programming oversight, especially for a game with a premium price tag.

Despite these minor issues, Sniper Elite 5 remains a solid stealth game with plenty to offer fans of the genre. The slow-paced gameplay, realistic environments, and satisfying stealth mechanics make it a worthwhile addition to the series.

review_text:
It's a step sideways for the franchise and that's not always a terrible thing. And some disclosure here, I got the main game and some DLC on a hefty sale (around 40% off) so perhaps my cost to fun ratio is skewed more in its favor than some other reviewers. I have one big complaint that pops up in other reviews but mostly I'm seeing the same game here.

I'm not going to go do a point for point rehash for my Sniper Elite 4 review, which was pretty solid and a lot of what I said there holds true here. I say that 4 is just more of 3, and in some ways 5 here is just more of the last two.

In 4, I found the open maps to be rather exhausting after a while to the point where on many levels I ended up just going "loud" and whipping out my assault weapon just to speed things up so I could get to some new scenery. My experience with that here in 5 is more of a mixed bag. So far in 9 hours I haven't felt 'bored' by the maps. Enemy patrols are a bit tighter in some places, even clustered, so I spend more time methodically figuring out what I'd consider be a "safe" kill or not, typically considering patrol paths. Don't wanna kill a guy in a gazebo when I know he's got two buddies that wander around the courtyard and might find him. As a result I feel a lot more stealthy and methodical than I did in the previous entry.

My main, big complaint is just the level design.

I find a lot of the design here is a lot more railroad-y than before. The maps have barbed wire, gates, and tunnels that sort of force you down paths and bridges that leave you open to spotters and spawning car patrols. I'll elaborate more on that in a second but I had trouble exfiltrating during the first mission because there was a Y road crossing where I had to go that vehicles kept spawning and piling on top of each other because they'd be constantly "alerted" at my recent dealings there (an exploded car, maybe a body or two) so I had to deal with nearly a full platoon of guys because the game apparently just keeps spawning cars.

So I can't just pick a direction to approach my attack from. Honestly this is fairly realistic, during wartime it makes sense that you'd barb up some hills so any potential stealth teams have a harder time getting to you. I get that but I wish there were more options than "you can only progress through this level by getting past this one bridge". You can have your barbed wire while being a bit more clever with design.

The second level, an estate, is a real crapshow of design. It has the aforementioned three bridges but the real problem is that you're trying to navigate the estate itself. This isn't a problem for say, assassin's creed where most of the game is done with silent stabbings or a bamboo dart tosser. But here, each gun has a "range" of audibility. I have a DLC rifle where its range is pretty short but that 30 or so meters doesn't mean much when I'm trying to snipe at an estate. Once one guy goes down, one of the forty guys gets alerted and it starts a chain reaction that turns my entire minimap yellow and I just had to deal with that for several minutes. I let them wander towards my last known location where I then botch a shot and get forced into open combat, then my minimap is flooded with red because I now have 20 nazis gunning for me. My second run at this level was more successful but I did still have to gun down an entire hallway of six dudes before being able to get out of their sightlines and reset the encounter. I cannot imagine trying to attempt a pure stealth run of that level. There's no way.

That's not the only level where it's like this, either. It's just one of the first ones that made me think "Oh, COME ON."

Previous games had full on sniper nests, typically with a nearby sound masking generator you could kick to start a full sniper spree with, to clear out defensive structures in relative safety as long as you timed your shots right. That's basically gone here. Every now and then your minimap might denote a good spot to snipe from but I've found that generators seem randomly placed and are rarely useful to me. In the estate level there's a generator near the base of one of these towers and when I cleared the camp of enemies I got up and found absolutely no enemies at the edge of the estate to shoot at. So I just cleared the camp and was rewarded with a sound mask and tower with no visible enemies to take advantage of. Come on.

A minor complaint is that you're rewarded with more experience by going for non-lethal takedowns and keeping more Nazis alive or incompacitated. Why... why would I, or anyone, ever want to do that?

I get that this is two paragraphs of good and four of bad but considering the good points of the franchise are still present, it just seems to accentuate what really went wrong with the design. I'm enjoying it though and I'm yearning to play more of it as my Youtube recordings of it are processing in my video editor. Might do some co-op in it. So that's a pretty good sign if a game leaves me with that feeling of "I want to see more".

But yeah the practices around the DLC are pretty bad.

review_text:
Not a big fan of this game. The series peaked with SE4. This game is basically Hitman: WWII. Which is fine, but I find some the missions far too restrictive with pathways and routes you can take. There are a lot of fences and sandbags you should be able to vault over, there are so many fences that you can't vault over just to be a path blocker. The worst offenders are the little sheet metal piles on the train tracks on War Factory. Why are those there? Why can I not traverse them? Why does it seem like the devs made lanes and avenues and staircases with roof access on many buildings just to block it with a copy/paste debris? Vantage points are very few and far between imo. The game feels linear when each mission is touted as a sandbox.

I have always enjoyed the survival modes ever since SE2. In each installment it is easily the best part of the game. This game's survival mode is bland. The maps stink, there are very few vantage points. If there is a vantage point you can bet it has no sight lines to objective. That means if you're solo you have to sit on OBJ with your secondary or if you are in a group someone has to babysit OBJ while the others have fun sniping.

The weapons. I'm fine with the creative liberty Rebellion took in regard to weapon customization. It's not for me, I find it a little immersion breaking but for others I can understand if someone likes it. The ballistics seem to be overhauled which I like, no more shooting at an enemy who is at 100 meters and I'm zeroed for 50 meters and I'm shooting at his toes. Or being zeroed at 50 meters and my target is 30 meters and I'm shooting the sky behind him. Well done, it is a *little more realistic.* What I do not like about the weapons is lack of variety in base game. This has always been a Sniper Elite problem but Rebellion has shown they do not necessarily care for equipment being outside it's theater of war. Why not add in legacy weapons  from previous games locked behind challenges? 

The axis invasions and multiplayer are okay. I like the invasion system, gives the campaign a neat dynamic. 

This is nit picky but I cannot stand the sound track. SE4 had a pretty epic soundtrack, and the previous games had fine soundtrack. I had to turn the music off in this game. I have never turned off game music before in any other game. 

Overall the worst offense SE5 makes is monetization. The DLC packs. I think its pretty lame that there is like $250 of content you can buy. I feel really bad for those that bought deluxe with season pass thinking they would get all content. Especially considering how little meat is on the bones of the base game.

review_text:
Alright, listen up, folks! This game, right, it's like the lovechild of Sniper Elite 4 and a bunch of new cool features. Rebellion didn't mess with the winning recipe; they just sprinkled in some extra spice. You know that saying, "If it ain't broke, don't fix it"? Well, Rebellion got the memo, and in the world of modern gaming, that's like finding a vegan at a barbecue – unexpected and refreshing.

The gameplay is tighter than my jeans after Thanksgiving dinner. Movement, weapons – it's like they've been on a CrossFit regimen. The AI got a facelift, too, but let's be real, it's a stealth game, not a Mensa meeting. Invasion Mode? That's the cherry on top – it's like playing hide and seek, but with bullets. And who doesn't love non-lethal options? I mean, sparing Nazis for XP is a bit like getting a participation trophy for world-saving, but hey, options are options.

The story? Yeah, it's there, like a background hum. Think John Wick – you're not here for Shakespeare; you're here for headshots. The multiplayer? It's a party!

Killcams? They've upgraded from a boring organ slideshow to a full-blown action movie. Bullet holes, blood spats – it's like Tarantino joined the dev team. Sure, I have a few gripes – like, why no destruction physics on character models? I want to blow a guy's jaw off and see the aftermath, not a pristine chin!

In a nutshell, this game might be the franchise's MVP. It's a must for Sniper Elite veterans, shooter enthusiasts, and stealth nerds. Go ahead, grab it – maybe throw in the DLC for good measure. It's like a gaming buffet, and you're the VIP guest.
