Sniper Elite 4 was an overall wonderful game. The maps had dozens of spots where you can set up a sound mask to conceal your shots, grab some cover and wait for the perfect shot. Despite not being an open world game the maps felt large and full enough to give you a lot of freedom. 

When I read that Rebellion was bring open world to Sniper Elite 5 I thought this might just be the master piece game of the Sniper Elite series. Instead this open world game is somehow more closed off than it's non-open world counterparts. There are only 1-2 to paths you can take just like in 4. However, they offer much more limited opportunities for sniping. In 4 Rebellion would set up sniper nets with sound masking, long field of views, and multiple enemies visible that could be spotted if you were patient. In short, they encouraged you to play like a sniper move quietly and slowly to a good vantage point. Observe the enemy, conceal your shots, and wait patiently for the perfect shot. 

In 5 Rebellion will either give you cover or a sound masker almost never both and never a place that offers a good view of multiple enemies at a time with sound masking and cover. Instead, you will be funneled into trenches and buildings where enemies are too far for CQC but in perfect pistol range. Rebellion has replaced the Welrod pistol of the previous games with an overpowered 1911 equipped with a modern style suppressor. The pistol is way overpowered and in the cramped quarters of Sniper Elite 5 is way more useful than the rifle. 

If you try to play as a sniper and not a pistol toting cowboy the game will become much more difficult. Since the sound masked locations really only give a god view of one or two enemies and little cover you will find yourself taking one shot and running away quickly. Many enemies can’t even be seen from logical sniping locations. So you’ll be forced to fire one shot which will be detected by enemies and runaway from all the return fire. You’ll soon give up on snipping for most of the game as it becomes an exercise in frustration brought on by poor level design. 

If you are a Sniper Elite fan this game is an easy miss. I wish I missed it and I am sad that I missed the return window hoping that his game would get better. Rest assured it does not.

Played this one fresh after playing through 4 again. This game overall was an improvement on the series and I hope they can find additional stories to tell in the future. As for the unique differences compared to the previous, here's what I've noticed:
- Virtually no more grenade kills? Idk if they removed them or the chance of hitting one but I still haven't been able to snipe a grenade on somebody, which I did frequently (maybe too so) in 4
- Vehicle combat is very different now. This actually is one of my few real complaints with the game; they went from a system of being able to snipe out gunners and snipers to "blow up the back and then shoot the engine a bunch." At first I was actually wasting resources because I didn't realize once the engine is exposed you just have to shoot it repeatedly until *kaboom*. 
- Much more linear maps overall, compared to Italy you're generally more restricted in this game. More walls you van't vault, more gray areas on your minimap. This coupled with sometimes vague mission instructions left me running back an forth across the several lanes of map to find my objective. (Don't call destroying a radio "neutralizing defenses", it's misleading at best. 
- Much better "quiet" options in the loadouts. While we don't have really more options than previous games, they've made suppressors more accessible and subsonic ammo a great option on all guns. I really have a wide range of configurations to decide on how loud I want to be. For 4 I actually purchased a DLC just to get the suppressed pistol in it (only quiet option base game is the Welrod) while in this game basically all pistols can. 
- Slow-motion controls are kinda neat if you really wanna get cinematic with your shots. I only wish the slow motion focused more on bullet entry/cavitation and less on after the bullet has passed through, but that's nitpicking. 
- I'm too much of a ♥♥♥♥♥ to do Axis invasion, because I hate pvp in most games, but I'll happily join an easy coop. This is something made easy to use and though connections are tenuous at times it can be a fresh change to play a map through with someone. 

Overall recommending to anyone who's enjoyed the previous games, any sniper games, or some Nazi-smashing therapy.

So im gonna explain something incase anyone sees this review..

This is not your normal sniper elite and heres why

Maps : Bigger than any of the series.
Weapons: Very limited even with the road map for season pass users
Attachments: they're cool and okay. Nothing specifically special
Bullet-cams: You end up staring at the exit wound than anything. in SE2-4 you could be satisfied by the bone shattering bullet cams but in sniper elite 5, you trade all of that to see the muscles and more detailed looking character models getting shot. Its not satisfying in this game. Infact bullet cams is why i enjoyed the series but this game is probably the most failed of the series..
Objectives: Really prolonged and poorly explained. Some missions give you a broad objective "Neutralize enemy defenses".
Now to the mind of a SE user, you think AAA guns or cannons right? Nope.. You gotta find a crowbar and disable a radio in one of the buildings of a town.

And for the finale of my review....

BUGS: Yes this game has more bugs than Cyberpunk. The amount of times i was shooting at an enemy and a vehicle is also shooting at me just to get a bullet cam or cut scene like an objective for the vehicle to go invisible. Same thing with enemy foot soldiers, they will become invisible, granted they can't harm you though.
Bugs for weapons: You will come across infinite reloading.. Yes it happens.
Bugs for weapons part 2: Me and my buddy were doing challenges to unlock the Karabiner98(Kar98). We did the kill challenge several times just to find out the mission is bugged alone and cannot get the weapon.
Bugged AI movement: Yes more bugs.. so you will come across AI that will break and loop. What i mean by this is some priority targets will get triggered by something like gun shots and will not go back to their coded position for an objective.
Bugged AI triggered status: This one isn't very common but it's more annoying as again me and my friend were doing COOP and we selected a different starting location but upon spawning, the enemies about 100 yards away were already investigating as soon as we spawned. Another time we were doing one of the final missions(8 i think) and had several bugs in combination. We had a triggered AI in investigation mode for about 45 minutes, got combat triggered AI through walls, several invisible enemies and the worst of it all, our objective on the map was in the middle of the room with 2 submarines. when the ACTUAL objective was in a back room which we felt stupid about not checking but they shouldn't say its in a giant room and not actually be there.


So if you are looking for a bug-free game, buy something else im sorry..especially for Sniper-Elite veterans but if you  wanna run and gun and enjoy shooting balls off Nazis then buy the game.

Sidenote bugs:
DLCs: i do not own the Hitler DLC or seasons pass but i have access to the dlc pistol and mission however the mission spawns me in but i fall to my death instantly. For other players who bought the dlc/seasons pass, some don't have access to the dlc pistol.

This game is way more Rambo and Wolfenstein than Sniper Elite. Personally, I don't really mind it but it is way more run-and-gun than Sniper Elite 3 and 4 (the other SE games I've played). The biggest problem I've discovered is the amount of bugs. The most common, and most frustrating, is animations getting stuck. It happens all the time - I'll press the prompt to melee an enemy, and then my character and the enemy will freeze for second, then perform the stealth kill animation. This also happens when picking up items, interacting with the environment, basically anything.

One really cool game mode is called Nazi Invasion, where an enemy player will "invade" your campaign mission and try to kill you. Invading other players is super fun and a great way to spice up the campaign maps. There's even a whole reward system for killing a certain amount of players as the invader. The problem is the multiplayer is very unstable. If I don't get disconnected, the host will quit the game half the time. Also, since the missions are more run-and-gun oriented, it can be really difficult to deal with the NPCs and another player, who is waiting to snipe you from across the map. Really neat idea, but could use more technical polish. 

Is it worth it for $50? I don't know, it's hard to say... I generally like these kinds of games, so I will lean towards yes. There are 9 missions, a co-op campaign, and several multiplayer modes. If the developers would patch some of these problems with the animations and technical bugs, I would be more inclined to recommend it.

Some environments look great like the first mission, and the spectacle of loading into them is always good, but there is always something wrong in them like textures that feel like their taken from a PS2 game (I should note I’m playing on all ultra with RTX on).

Overall the game just isn’t very good, I wouldn’t pay more than 20 dollars for it, therefore I cannot recommend it at this time, its not that I hate the game, it’s just that it feels unfinished and for $50 is simply was not worth it in my opinion.

review_text:
I read the reviews before getting this game and I was a little skeptical but I risked it and let me tell you : BEST DECISION EVER! Personally, I bought every Sniper Elite game since the SE V2. I played all of them for like 3-4 hours so I thought this is just one more for the collection and it will sit in my inventory never to be played. This one hits different though. This is going to be a longer review but I wanted to clear things for people who are skeptical like I first was.

How I play the game:
-I play at sharpshooter (medium) difficulty for everything except the sniping which I play at the hardest difficulty Authentic.
-I NEVER engage in combat and play every mission undetected. It takes me approximately 150-200 minutes per mission (usually 90-100% completion for collectibles).
-Sometimes I take 10 minutes just to do recon and learn NPC's paths from a distance before deciding my next move. Also, I ALWAYS hide the bodies or throw them out of sight when possible as to avoid suspicion.
-Sometimes I stay in a corner encircled by NPC's for several minutes just waiting for an opening. I also make use of ALL of the available equipment (70% is bottles/whistle/sticky grenades). 
-If they find a body or I create an explosion and they start investigating I simply plan ahead where to hide and wait it out.
-I really try to stick to the games script and play it as if it was real. Sometimes I even reload a situation if I don't like the outcome or it comes off too unrealistic. 

With that being said, nothing is stopping me to try and snipe everyone or run and gun in with my smg... But I just find it so much more satisfying when your have to work for every kill. Also that way, the x-ray cam when you finally have the opportunity for a long shot never gets old!

LOADOUT:
-Springfield M.1903 with attachments that maximize long range shooting (reduce bullet drop and add power). I also use the silencer that doesn't affect bullet drop (gun is audible from 87m).
-The rest doesn't really matter lol. But I usually use a silenced pistol and silenced smg.

1st negative point I saw in the reviews: You have to play online to unlock certain things:
-The only things that you unlock through multiplayer are a couple of COSMETIC skins for the guns and some character skins that you can play in the main story instead of Karl.
-Every other gun/attachment that actually changes the gameplay is unlocked while playing the story.

2nd negative point I saw in the reviews: You get less xp when you turn off Invasion mechanic for you campaign. This is true, however:
-The skill tree is like 70% useless in my opinion so xp is really not that important as it is only used to unlock perks.
-When you thoroughly complete each mission, you get more than enough xp to max out the  different skill trees without needing to enable Invasions.
-I am currently on mission 6 and need 2-3 more skill points to max out my skill tree.
-To give you an example, I've only lost like 3 health bars total in all of my 6 missions so far.
-Once I complete the campaign I will try out the Invasion mode to have a change of pace and work towards 100% completion but is really not required to fully enjoy the story and all of the weapons, attachments, etc the game has to offer.

3rd negative point I saw in the reviews: There is not enough sniping from huge distances going on. Instead, game is focused on stealth and sneaking around with pistol.
-Personally I get somewhere between 10-15 long shots (100m-450m), 15-20 short range pistol kills (10m-40m) and like 20-30 takedowns. Tip: when you perform takedowns try to pacify them as it gives you considerably more xp at the end of the mission. 
-Here is the difficult thing : You REALLY have to plan your approach. Sometimes I don't take the cool long shot x-ray cam even though it kills me inside because I know it will screw my whole stealth set up.
-The 3rd mission offers a ton of great opportunities for like 300m-500m shots in the beginning before you start approaching the castle. Just use your binoculars to scout around.

4th negative point I saw in the reviews: There are bugs and you often get stuck on like small ledges.
-Yes you do get stuck on some stupid small rubble sometimes but you just go around it or find another path because the game doesn't want you to go through there. Didn't really affect my gameplay at all.
-There are some bugs that I saw like enemies getting stuck in object or walls. Nothing that prevents you to complete the game properly tho.
-WARNING: In mission 4 (war factory) it took me an hour to complete the kill list target with the special objective (using the rat bomb to kill him). This was the only really annoying bug so far.

I really hope this helps you have a better idea of what to expect from this game! I hope you get to enjoy it as much as I do! :)

review_text:
Sniper Elite is a game franchise that manages to refine itself on every iteration.

2 was linear, but had some nice setpieces, gore, and a focus on sniping, which let it stand out from other WW2 shooters.
3 added bigger maps with different routes between points of interest.
4 had open map design, lots of interesting architecture, and was fun co-op.
5 seems to be a culmination of the previous game's improvements.

Maps are open ended and dense with enemies and terrain. The freedom to move around also means that close combat and melee takedowns are viable and useful. The gore is pleasant as always. There is meaningful gun customization that changes rifles, smgs, and pistols functionally and aesthetically. Coop is back, though I can't speak on its systems without having played it. The new invasions are extremely fun.

Allowing invasions in the campaign game gives extra XP. I played the base campaign solo, and by the last level I had plenty of XP to upgrade all the skills. The game seems balanced around solo XP gain. XP gained by allowing invasions is extra. Unfortunately, many people seem to allow invasions to allow the additional XP gain, but disconnect the moment someone invades. When attempting to invade, maybe 1/2 or 2/3 of players d/c immediately or soon after. Of those who remained, there was a lot of fun to be had. The mechanics support an enjoyable invasion system. Tracking enemy players by gunshots, tagging ally AI to better predict player movement, seeing what objectives are already destroyed on spawn, planting bombs and traps, makes for an exciting and tense game of cat and mouse.

Overall, pretty fun game to wander around and murder in.

I didn't like it. I have played almost 1200 hours on SE4 and still love the game. SE3 was just about as good and just as fun to play. This game didn't feel like Sniper Elite, other than the one map in the castle. I waited anxiously for the release of this game. I bought it immediately when they opened it for pre-sale and waited the months for it's release since it is definitely my favorite series. I am disappointed. 

Let's first start with the characters: This is WWII in the 1940's. There was a French Resistance and by all means had men and women actively participating in the effort. After all, their country was overrun. Main character of the resistance here was a black woman with a Scottish accent who is obviously not from France. Ah, nothing against that but it is certainly out of place here in the 1940's in WWII. It wasn't believable.  In SE4, it was an Italian woman who's father was leading the resistance in Italy and took over his duties when he went missing - believable and accepted. What were they thinking here? Where are the French men? Hiding in bunkers while the women did the work? Through the entire game did I even hear a French man speak with a French accent? I really have to think back on that. I would like authentic, please. Also, they called him the "Shadow" yeah, I heard them call him the "Desert Ghost" in one cut scene but the Shadow diminishes the character to be someone else.

Gameplay: It didn't feel like Sniper Elite. It's not a bad game but it doesn't want me to go back and play another 1200 hours. Where are the designers and writers of SE3 and SE4? It is a little bit of an "open map" but it is more tunneling type of gameplay than I like for this series. In SE4 you can start the map and go in any direction and complete the maps in so many different ways, stealth, loud, or both. SE5 used too many of the same old tricks in SE4, such as "turn the valve, create pressure and blow it all up". A little more originality would have been nice. It felt like rinse and repeat. 

Weapons: Yeah, so many have already commented on how they could have done it better that I don't need to reiterate. 

Skills: I didn't see much benefit from the skills I obtained. More health good - throwing a grenade back that was thrown at me? I never once had the opportunity. A lot of them were useless. 

Rank: 40 is the limit? I reached that before the end of the game. 

Menus: They were a lot more difficult to maneuver through and things lit up for upgrade when no upgrade was available. I'm still confused on some of the selections. Is there a gun based achievement in this game other than attachments? 

Overall: I'm disappointed. I had warned Rebellion on their Discord to not ruin Sniper Elite like they ruined Wolfenstein. If you're going to have a WWII game, in which I love, keep it authentic and if you're your going to turn it into  a wreck like most of the WWII games did, I'm done with Sniper Elite. I'll go back and play SE3 and SE4 for another 2400 hours.

I have honestly been waiting for years for this game. I played through (and re-played through) SE3 and SE4 so much, they were my go-to games when nothing else held my interest. They will STILL be my go-to games over this one. 

What SE5 got right: 
- Moddable/swappable parts for guns
- updated held-breath mechanic
- Removing the "always know where an enemy is" bits. I feel the new wide-circle system makes the engagements far more entertaining and challenging
- Crowbar, Bolt-Cutters, Satchel Charges needing to be found in order to be used. This opens the player up to a multitude of different playthrough options per engagement

What SE5 got wrong:
- Simple mechanics. There are SO many ledges under 3ft in this game that cannot be vaulted/mantled where in SE3 or SE4 you could pretty much climb almost everything, OR the game map was built in a way where the only ledges you encounter WERE climbable. 
- Sniper Posts, or lack-there-of. Finding a good spot to snipe from, with or without noise blocking, was an awesome thing in all SE games until now. It feels more like they focused on the objectives rather than the actual gameplay when the gameplay is what made these games fun
- Map Size/Intricacy? Maybe its just me but I truly feel that these maps are smaller than ones in previous games and don't allow for much fun in setting up a sniping position, grouping enemies together, etc. I felt like I was just constantly moving from one objective to the next which really makes this feel more like a combat game than a sniper game. I ended up using my pistol more than any other weapon, nearly twice as much as my actual sniper rifle.... in a sniper game... because of the constant movement. 
- Time. In SE4 I had the option to race through everything, guns out going loud and insane and finishing in under 20 min. OR I could take my time, scope everything out, snipe everything that crossed my path and move on quietly, utilizing the entire environment, taking an hour or so to get through each level. In SE5 it feels like I'm rushed to get through everything. 
- Silly challenges for weapon parts or weapons. need I say more? Just make them available once you reach a certain gun table or find them within the level.

Possible solutions for SE6 (if it happens):
- Start with simple game mechanics. Copy a game like Assassin's Creed where you can climb all walls, you can jump off things onto soft areas, you can hide, you can sneak around. Take those game mechanics and slap the better features of this game on top of it
- More selection in gun modding. I loved what you brought to SE5, however if I look at other games with similar capability, ones like Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon: Wildlands takes the cake when it comes to modding your guns. The differences in available scopes or magazines made a huge difference to how you would play any given situation. Also add to that the fact that you needed to find them. I did enjoy a good portion of that with the gun tables in SE5 but it still felt lacking.
- DLC Weapon options. I won't deny, once I've played the game through with the base available options, I like to splurge and buy the super silent weapons or the super loud weapons and see what trouble I can get into with those. That makes the game fun. There simply aren't any of those with this game.


Final words: Will I play this again? maybe. At this point its not likely but who knows. Its a possibility. Would I recommend it to others? if it comes out discounted or free, go for it. Its an ok game, but not one I would spend full price on again.

Sniper Elite continues to be the best sniping game available by a large margin, and considering it's name, you can't ask for much more.

review_text:
Some of the best map design in SE to date. Mission 3 Spy Academy is a finely crafted art piece of an excuse to blow chunks out of nazis. Mission 8 is a tight, tense, sprawl through debris and ruined buildings that allows for some creative sniping. We find ourselves going back to missions often to replay them, for the depth of stuff to find, the new challenges different approaches present, and just because it's really, really fun.

The weapons have never felt as varied and distinct with a not insignificant amount of customisation you can apply to each, that genuinely provide choice in how the weapons perform. Unlocking new weapons and customisation options feels very rewarding.

The axis invasion mode was a great addition, in of itself enough fun to warrant getting in now while activity is high.

The game is however full of bugs, from menus, to loading in, to playing the game. Rough edges, literally between aliasing and context grabbing, are easy to find and will occasionally frustrate.

review_text:
As the fifth big installment of the Sniper Elite Series, this game does not contain many surprises. As every Sniper Elite has a bit of an identity crisis, this one is no different. The gameplay of Sniper Elite 5 is probably the most hybrid third person shooter gameplay of the whole series. The sniper rifle is still a trusted tool (also the only weapon with optional aim assist) but submachine gun and pistol work almost equally well - and I like that. I like variety in my shooter gameplay and this game gives me enough choices to fill that want. 

The levels of the campaign are beautifully crafted and offer very different combat arenas/sandboxes/sneaking challenges. I've read the critique that many maps don't offer that long shooting distances as in previous installments and while that is certainly true, I don't think it takes away much. You're still able to fight at ranges of 100-200 meters very often and it isnt like you would hit much beyond that without the aim assist. The story is nothing to write home about but that is also not the point of the game. It is written well enough to justify the mission sandboxes you're getting dropped into and for me that is very much sufficient. 

Also, the invasion mode: Before buying the game, I apparently dodged all the announcements about this gamemode and was pleasantly surprised upon discovering it. In this gamemode, you can join the campaign games of other players. You play as an enemy sniper and have to stop the other player. A simple concept that makes each mission way more thrilling for me. I absolutely love getting invaded in a mission and suddenly having to adapt to the new circumstances, because NOW I am facing not only the AI but also a human player that can do almost everything I can do - and can also kill me in one shot. It is really something else and even if you get killed by an invader, you don't really lose progress. You can still save. 

And you can turn it off. You can turn the invasion mode completely off and be done with it. I don't get the negative reviews where the major critique is this gamemode. Just turn it off. You can also kick an invading player from your game session since you are the host (yes, really. I also don't get why you can do this).

Yes - with caveats - read on.
First off let me provide context. I'm most certain an 'older' gamer, and a casual gamer. I have played and completed all the Snipe Elite series, as well as played many other sniper style games.
Did I enjoy this? Yes, Was it worth the money; not sure.
I know many are waxing lyrical about how good this is, but I'll be honest ... I was 'meh'.
On my older rig I'm probably not running at full detail, so can't comment on exactly how good the graphics can be; for me I'm not seeing a massive improvement over SE4.
In terms of game play, there are a few new elements, but overall it is very much more of the same with some tweaks. I didn't feel the game play was markedly different to SE4, to be honest.
I still felt frustrated that my supposedly 'elite' sniper who has years of experience, is still unable to clamber over rocks, move through bushes or step over small walls. In fact, in one map I 'swapped cover' from one side of an open gateway to the other side and promptly got stuck behind a knee-high hedge garden and had to re-load a save. A well known issue for snipers the world over, I'm sure :-|
The enemy AI also doesn't appear to be that much better than before either. I can shoot a guy in the head, right beside his mate, and there might be a bit of 'searching' but not the panic and calling all troops into a search that, I'm sure might happen in real life. I'd also like to see more missions of having to sneak in and make a kill and extract without any other conflict. One shot, one kill.
Would I buy this game if I knew all the above in advance? Well, probably, because I like tactical stealth sniper style of games. But I'm not altogether convinced it is worth the asking price. If you don't have it already and are curious and not a hard-out fan, then I'd probably wait for a sale. If you are a hrd-out fan, well, then you likely have it already! :)

review_text:
I played Sniper Elite 5 through mostly in co-op with my brother on authentic difficulty.

In addition, I did replay individual missions by myself on authentic to collect any missing medals (we collected collectables during co-op play) while waiting for next co-op session to advance.

I have not played axis invasion, multiplayer or survival... only campaign.

All in all, for what I played, I'd recommend the game and I think it's worth 50 euros.

I did pay the price for the deluxe edition (~80 euros) for it, and even then I'm not disappointed... just dreading to see what kind of dlc I'll be getting for that extra support as dlc nowadays can easily be pretty lackluster.

But that was a risk I was willing to take.

Anyway, here's some pros/cons:
+ good launch experience
+ overall decent technical quality
+ very much like previous installments, which is good
++ map design is impressive
+ fun/enjoyable
+ co-op went overall well
+ sniper rifles are varied and I found some I liked (I prefer long distance)
+ weapon tuning is kinda nice
+ weapon tuning is ok to do only once to suit your playstyle, and not necessary to vary all the time
+ the wolf mountain extra mission was nice
+ overall mood and feel is generally nice

- bugs with co-op that sometimes required loading autosave from earlier parts
- bugs with reloading that required me to get other ammo type to get the weapon usable
- smaller random bugs
- some collectables practically required using online guides to find (may be easier to find on easier difficulties?)
- my fave sniper rifle Mosin Nagant isn't in the game
- the plot and cutscenes are as cringy as one might expect (plot is secondary to me though)
- cannot do axis invasion with selected steam friends, just via random matchmaking

~ sniping of vehicles isn't as fun/cool as it was in Sniper Elite 4 (sniping tank drivers through small windows); on the other hand, vehicles aren't too easily bypassed anymore so it's kinda ok that way too
~ i haven't noticed significant impact from Denuvo, though right after launch my virus protection quarantined the executable
~ i don't know how multiplayer with randoms goes
~ i don't care about comparing real life stuff with this game; one should never mix up fact and fiction... doing that is to me a warning sign of mental health issues

Still, despite its short-comings, I'd say this game is good enough for its 50 euro price tag.

I had fun and played it for over 60 hours, which is pretty good for a recent game release.

It's not perfect for sure, but I believe it's worth the price if you're in the mood for a sniping game.

As such, I'd say this game can be recommended to other players.

review_text:
One quick note before we begin...

[h1]If you are playing this game on Game Pass be warned that your saves are NOT transferable![/h1]

Sniper Elite 5 takes the battle of the Axis to the Northern France during the Allied invasion of France during 1944; what was ultimately considered the World War II's biggest turning point. However, much like all the Sniper Elite games before, the setting is more of a means for some nice scenery instead of telling a factual story. As for the story itself, well, again its barely there because what's there is a plot device rather than an overall narrative. That plot device drives the real driving force for this game; killing Nazis through the scope of your rifle, watching the bullet of your sniper slowly penetrate a soldier's skull as the X-Ray vision highlights someone's brain contorting to the force of a .30-06 going 2800 ft/s and climaxing with an explosion of blood and bone particles coming out the eye socket. It's Sniper Elite's formula and signature style that has kept these games going for as long as they have.

I know that may sound negative and to a point, yeah, it kind of is. Sniper Elite doesn't really change much. In fact, it's changed so little that I haven't really cared about the franchise since V2. I only got interested in this game solely because, for the first time, this game started rippling through the internets in the same way V2 did when it was first coming out. I dug around a little bit, found out the game was on Game Pass, and fired it up. 

Sniper Elite 5 is no longer a game with a sequence of linear environments with a slightly open ended design. Apparently, this open ended design akin to Sniper Elite 1 was re-introduced to the series with Sniper Elite 4, but I sadly have not played that game so I can not give you a fair comparison. What I can tell you, however is that Sniper Elite 5's open ended design is both very well developed and simultaneously frustrating as all hell. What I really love about this change in direction is that now you start a mission with a designated objective but if you go around and explore the map a little you'll end up finding intel that unlocks alternate objectives you can complete to earn additional rewards. Making the missions feel more dynamic instead of static was a phenomenal idea. However, the open ended design is kinda bogged down by the actual new mechanic to this installment; the invasion mode.

Yes, PVP in the campaign. Should you have invasion turned on a player controlled German sniper can invade your game and kill you. I'll go over this mode in a moment, but the reason why it hinders the open-map design so much is that Rebellion needed to add so many restrictions to pathways and there's just sometimes downright invisible walls. You quickly learn that these maps aren't actually big open areas. They are basically arenas stitched together to look like a big map. This is likely due to balance out the invasion mode. But the problem is this restriction with the maps is also present when you have invasion off and its very frustrating when you just want to go somewhere that seems accessible but it turns out you have to backtrack to a different walkway to get to the correct walkway that takes you around the game barrier to get where you want to go. Again, I get why they did it, but it's really an immersion killer sometimes.

Now, how is the invasion. Its good. It's really good in fact. But it does have it's problems. Much like the single player, a well placed shot on a player can lead to a slow motion kill cam with x-ray. While it's not a new mechanic at all, being able to see you inflict that damage to another player is just fresh enough to make these slow motion kills exciting again. The way it works is that, during the initial invasion, the player being invaded is able to use invasion phones almost immediately to track the invading player's location without detection. After 5 minutes, the invading player is also able to use those same phones to ping their location, but they also get a ping right back. The invading player does, however, have an extra trick up their sleeve in the form of ally tagging. An invading player can use an AOE command or ping individual nazi soldiers with their binoculars which allows them to find out where the player is should they get spotted by one of the NPCs. However, this also means that the player being invaded really doesn't have any means of defense other than not getting caught. Maybe it was intentional, I mean, Karl is one American fighting dozens of Nazis. He's already outnumbered, but it's really annoying that Karl can't do something like hide in the tall grass, which is the game's only true hiding mechanic, to avoid a ping through a phone. I think a patch should be implemented to include this as it'd make the game of cat and mouse all the more heart pounding. 

Invasions also have another very annoying feature; the matchmaking. If you are getting invaded, and you die, if you select either "Reload from Start of Invasion" or "Reload Last Save" you IMMEDIATELY get invaded again. If you're in an absolutely awful situation to begin with this can be doubly frustrating and lead to a string of getting repeatedly killed over and over again. Thankfully, you can turn off invasion upon death, but it'd be nice if the game gave you a break after dying. The only way to truly earn a break without turning it off is to kill the enemy sniper. 

I'm pretty sure I'm running out of characters so I will try to wrap this up. Along with the above, Sniper Elite 5 also introduced first person view on SMGs and pistols which is really nice. However I noticed the Thompson's iron sights are just completely messed up and don't line up. Alongside this, these weapons are also capable of achieving slow motion x-ray kills as well. There's also a weapon customization system and, just as a forewarning, you can make some pretty cursed looking guns akin to CoD: Vanguard levels of cringe. They tried to incorporate real attachments that existed during this era but there's also modern ideologies like grip tape which was just not a thing in WW2. So if you're someone who cannot stand anachronistic weapon philosophy I suggest avoiding this one. Much like the dynamic objectives, the provides more incentive to explore the map in form of workbenches. There are 3 kinds of work benches; one for rifles, one for SMGs, and one for pistols. These workbenches grant you new customization options and sometimes new weapons.

There's also the inclusion of different ammo types now too. There's types for penetrating armor good for piercing helmets, soft point for non-armored combatants, subsonic ammo to make guns quiet, non-lethal ammo, etc and all these can be swapped on the fly from your weapon wheel.

Along with this are small snippets of information you can get about a Nazi by tagging them. People are claiming Rebellion is trying to humanize some Nazis but, honestly, I don't think so. It's just there for the sake of adding some depth. Second, you earn MORE exp if you knock an enemy out first and then kill them while they're unconscious. War crimes are rewarded! 

This game also features co-op too! All of the missions in the game can be played with a fellow friendly sniper. And this co-op mode also works in invasion as well. If the invading sniper kills one of the players, the other sniper has 3 minutes to find and kill the enemy or they automatically lose. 

Sniper Elite 5 also introduced a 4 player Survival mode, which I haven't had a chance to try, but I'm sure it's alright. The game also re-introduced V2's team based PVP multiplayer alongside a snipers only mode for it which, you know, is pretty fun if you don't mind extreme camping. So all in all for $50 you get a lot of bang for your buck; 9 large scale missions all playable with a buddy and PVP, the Invasion mode, Survival, and traditional multiplayer PVP.

review_text:
This is just a direct downgrade from SE4. I've clocked a lot of hours in 4 cause the game felt AMAZING, every movement had consequence and weight to it but here everything just feels inconsequential especially getting spotted. There is NO feedback for being spotted, just a white line going red with no audio cue or anything.

Credit where credit is due the game looks good, weapon customization is neat, and the maps are "Expansive" more on that in a second.

The maps, they are supposedly larger... they don't feel like it. You're given a objective and you have to discover side objectives only it feels bland and just uninteresting, a good comparison is the first mission from SE4. In SE5 you're set loose on a beach with no good vantage points or interesting opportunities for kills, in SE4 on the first mission you get TONS of interesting kills and opportunities including dropping a ammo crate on someones head, you get vantage points all over the place and generators are abundant with those positions. In this game however... yea on mission 1 you're just sorta thrown in without consiquence, there is just nothing interesting about the first mission and its side objectives.

Side objectives, in SE4 they felt like meaningful alternative objectives cause they were openly presented to you with a location. If you got lost in either a main objective or a side one you'd either only have a small area to search or it would be pointed out for you, in SE5 not even damn close. The objectives on mission 1 felt directionless like the radio bunker, to sabotage a generator you need a crowbar which I spent 10 damn minutes looking for. I eventually found it and had to hit a fuse box, there was a objective marker over where I was and one adjacent which just made me PROFOUNDLY confused.

Enemy AI and stealth, SE4 had some of the best stealth mechanics I think any game has ever had. It was unforgiving but fun and concise, AI was not the best by any stretch but it was serviceable especially with how the stealth felt. Shooting felt weighty and purposeful, stealth was slow but tense, and enemies felt aware of their surroundings with good placement in their enviroment. In SE5 you just have random ass patrols wandering around seemingly not knowing what they're doing, stealth is just too fast and just has no weight to it. In SE4 you had audio and music cues for when you were being spotted, searched for, and in combat with each being distinct and telling you exactly what was going on. In SE5 you get generic sniper music constantly that just feels out of place, while also getting no audio cues for stealth.

Weapon customization, this is just a straight upgrade from SE4. Each upgrade is at least slightly grounded in reality and in history itself, it feels rewarding and each upgrade has a tangible effect that feels distinct. Shooting feels the best it ever has, it feels weighty and guttural every time you use a gun without a suppressor, the addition of iron sights as well is just a godsend.

The Invasion mechanic. Okay look I get that its a cool feature but here's my problem, when you have it during the first mission of the game while someone is still trying to learn the game? Yea that's frustrating.

The controls. It just feels scuffed and just awkward, it feels like a call of duty game rather than SE4. Stealth should be slow, methodical, you are a sniper after all and your main tools are... ya know a SNIPER AND STEALTH. In SE5 it just feels limp, it feels like its trying to be a intense multiplayer shooter with stealth mechanics and it just DOES NOT WORK.

In summary, go play SE4 its a far better game despite its flaws.

Let's talk about the problems with Sniper Elite 5. Each new version of Sniper Elite has fine tuned the mechanics of the game for the better... until now. I don't know how other people play SE but I play stealthy sniper mode. I take my time. I infiltrate, clear an area with the silenced pistol, set up a sniper nest with something to cover the sound of the shots and terrorize the enemy by picking them off one by one. If I'm detected I either exfiltrate and come at them from another direction or go to ground and wait until the heat dies down, you know, sniper style. This game feels as if it's designed to be more One Man Army CoD like.

Game Play:
I don't know why they felt they had to redesign the AI, but now the enemies are dumber yet more aggressive. They stand around talking to themselves for no reason. They charge and swarm. It becomes a human wave FPS instead of a sniper game. The enemies in SE4 seemed to function pretty logically tactically. Groups had areas they defended, if shooting occured in another area they didn't charge across the map, they stayed in their areas. If they recieved fire they hunkered down tried to identify the direction of the threat then tried to flank it returning fire, moving from cover to cover. These enemies are suicidally brave and mindless. In the second to the last mission in the ruins I was shooting from the end of a street. I miss timed a shoot so it was heard and practically every guy on the map aggro-ed on me. They began pouring down this street. I was shooting so fast I didn't even bother aiming any more. There were 36 guys laying in heaps in front of me at the end of it, THIRTY SIX. I know, I counted them as best I could. There were no tactics involved in that. They just kept running straight at me, ignoring cover, like they were programmed to run straight up to me and shoot me at point blank range with their rifles. 
They don't talk much either. Although like I said they do have conversations with themselves for some reason. In SE4 if they find a dead man they would make comments 'A man's dead!' 'Who is it?' 'Oh my god!' You know, human-like reactions. Yeah, that's gone. 

Let's talk about stuff that's gone.

- Did you like how the aiming reticule would shrink down the longer you held your breath making your aim more precise? That's gone.
- Did you like how you could shoot a grenade on a guys belt and blow him up? That's gone.
- Did you like crouch running from cover to cover to avoid detection? That's gone.
- Did you like throwing rocks to lure guys? That's gone.
- Did you like trying to make that really long shot? Don't expect many opportunities. These maps are mostly cluttered and confined.
- Did you like how you could detect unseen enemies by them clearing their throat, or coughing, or humming to themselves? Well that seems to be gone too.

Story:
The story is pretty dull and feels completely tacked on to try to create a narrative. Some maps have no beginning cut scene just a basic text opening. Some maps feel added on, like they had a map that didn't fit the story but had them and wanted to use them anyway. The D-Day map for one. Black SOE operatives in WWII France? Riiigghhttt. If you want to throw black folks a bone to get them involved why didn't you just have the option to make the sniper black? It's still unlikely but much less unlikely than black spys in 1940s France going unnoticed by the heavily racist Nazis. JS

Graphics:
The textures look much improved, I think they used some filters in SE4 that seem to be missing here. There, done.

Music:
Why does there seem to be generic RPG music in my Sniper Elite game? I finally turned it down to 25% to make it bearable.

Multiplayer:
Not interested, didn't p[ay.


Overall:
This is a somewhat disappointing game that honestly feels like it was designed to appeal to the console market. I'm going to go out on a limb and say that this is probably the last Sniper Elite game that's going to get made, and it feels like it. It feels like a game only made to take advantage of the player base and name recognition. 

Is Sniper Elite 4 worth $59.99? Yes, I'd say it still is, Still.
Is Sniper Elite 5 worth $49,99?  No, I don't think it is. It's not the game I wanted or hoped for. Wait for a sale and prepare yourself to be disappointed.

Being German myself, I'd like to comment on the design of the Germans in the game.

The first thing is the language and voice acting. It's great that German soldiers speak native German, but the actual acting is horrible. Everyone sounds vaguely comical, as if not taking the situation he's in seriously. I have not heard any voice that I could reasonably believe to belong to a real soldier in a serious scenario. There are also literal translations from English expressions in their lines, that aren't proper German, as well as smaller details, like grammar errors in Propaganda Posters.
I know the game had expert advisors on weapons and such, why couldn't they have also had just one or two German people to check for this kind of thing? They would have spotted all of it immediately.

The level design goes for oversimplified Pseudo-German set pieces, like a large sign that just says "Achtung!" in the middle of a camp. I get that this is useful for being recognizable by Non-Germans, but that sign makes no sense. "Achtung!" for what? There needs to be some explanation on what that sign is a warning against. Especially since German is famous for being very detailed and specific.

I don't want to make this too long, so I'll say this in conclusion. In order for me to enjoy fighting enemies in a game, I have to be able to take them seriously and have respect for them. That is what is lacking here. Even though my complaints may be less problematic for Non-Germans, I'm certain that a more authentic depiction of them would make for a much better game for everyone.

So please, pay more attention ("Achtung!") to detail when designing villains, antagonists and enemies.

review_text:
Fans of the series get the short and sweet version. This is much the same as the previous games; mostly like Sniper Elite 4. The differences are subtle. Movement feels different (for the better) and visually it is a slight step up. Alongside the movement, the secondary weapons are more effective and going loud is quite viable, especially in co-op. It can be quite fun to tackle the game in this way. There's not much more to say except for some negatives below. These can be a big deal and may give you pause.

For the benefit of new players, the brief overview is that you'll be at home with this game if you've played games like Sniper Ghost Warrior, Hitman or Splinter Cell. Each have their own vibe, but they are very similar in important ways. It's for patient players who like a slower paced game where you scout out where you're going and pick your openings for sniping or slipping through enemy lines.

The story and characters are the normal trashy mess and not worth any real time investment. The usual low quality voice acting does not help. For example, a long-running relationship is supposed to exist between your character and one of the resistance. They throw out robotic lines to tell us this, but it's not convincing. There is no real connection forged between them and you'll cringe rather than empathise. Skipping the cutscenes is the best option.

The gameplay is where it counts and it's good when it works as expected. This is where it regularly falls apart. The game is playable - even enjoyable - for the most part and you should get through to the end without anything that breaks the game completely. However, bugs and AI problems are rampant.

Some enemy soldiers constantly get stuck in loops between alert and passive modes, switching back and forth every few seconds. Mission targets with movement patterns around a map will break and they'll stay in place, ruining many options for assassination. The higher level AI that tracks the player also gives the enemy what appears to be a sixth sense as to where you are, even if you're not spotted when shooting and then shifting positions.

These issues are constant throughout and it's up to you whether you can tolerate them. For me it wasn't surprising and I'm used to seeing this. SE4 wasn't perfect either and had some similar problems. So, from my perspective I can tentatively recommend it. Your mileage may vary and I would suggest waiting to see if they release a major patch. The AI, triggers and pathing need a lot of attention.

review_text:
I wrote a first impressions post in the discussion for people who were on the fence, and now that I finished the game I want to just put in some final words.

For one, beating this game and all optional objectives took 10 hours.  Its a very short game, however, that doesnt bother me because I treat these games as more of a sandbox experience, and played SE4 into the dirt.  By the way, I got this on green man gaming for 35 bucks, more people should be doing that.  

The missions are very disappointing just in their design style.  Meaning, there is a lot of go here, grab this, then go here and grab this, go turn this valve, go find this paper, etc.  Basically you are running back and fourth across the map at times and its annoying.  I enjoyed SE4 in the sense that often the mission was, go kill this guy, theres a bunch of enemies between you and him, figure it out.  SE5 CAN be played that way, sort of, but not really.  Since every unlock in this game requires you to find workbenches or accomplish tasks in the way they want you to do, you kind of have to play the way they want.  Which is annoying.  I was nearly done with the game before I even realized I was supposed to be collecting paintings, shooting gnomes, interacting with every workbench, killing targets in very specific ways, etc.

Speaking of annoying, the terrain in this game might be the most ridiculous thing in a video game I HAVE EVER SEEN.  I do not understand how this was green lighted??  There are invisible walls EVERYWHERE!  I understand why you would do this at the maps edge, so make it feel open, but all through the middle of the map?  Just running into glass walls nonstop unless you go the EXACT path they want you to take?  INSANE.  Your character can climb up certain tall walls, jump over certain walls, but cannot jump over certain other shorter walls, or entire hallways or rooms will be blocked off by a suitcase, or rocking chair, as if he couldn't negotiate that obstacle.  He also nearly dies from a 15 foot drop, which I find hilarious, as an elite military operative.  Such weak ankles this guy..  

The enemies also have very strange sight.  Sometimes they appear blind, other times they can see you from a mile away through trees so thick you could never hope to see them back.  Their AI is bad but good enough.  They are a tad timid for my taste, they will sit behind cover for many minutes usually, refusing to push.  Other times I have found upwards of 4 soldiers all running nose first in a corner, obviously their pathing goes through a building.  Sometimes you shoot them and they die and immediately sink through the earth, leaving you nothing to loot, other times you shoot them and they just stand in a T pose indefinitely.  Another hilarious thing is shooting enemies driving.  They will stop the car, get out, then fall dead to the ground.  I dont mind that one so much as it always makes me laugh.  I also noticed many times the white/yellow/red circles on the minimap will stay after you kill someone, so you may run around searching for that last guy who died a long time ago.  I also encountered enemies who will shoot at the ground forever, nowhere near you, not sure why.  I'll hear them across the map, go hunt them down, and just stand there watching them shoot at nothing.  Another crazy bug is that sometimes the game will not let you shoot enemies, you literally cannot fire on their body.  you can fire next to them, but never on them.  I hope they figure that out, and its weird to me that your gun firing can be stopped by what its pointed at?  Only thing you can do at that point (and they can shoot you btw) is hope you have explosives, or run away, flank and come back for a stealth kill.  I also think hip firing can work at times.  just no zoomed firing on them.  I'm sure theres other things im forgetting, honestly I cant remember them all but there so many its crazy.  

The gunplay for the rifles and pistols is fine.  The secondary guns are trash, and take like 10 bullets usually to down a soldier.  Which, is totally unrealistic obviously.  I rarely use them because they are so bad.  I like the rifles however, and the pistols, especially once you unlock silencers.  I miss some of the gadgets from SE4, shame they took them out, like trip mines.  Some people complain about lack of wind, and they may have some grounds for that, but honestly, these rifles are powerful enough that in reality wind is not going to push a bullet going that fast for more than a fraction of a second.  So I'm fine with it.  

The level design is a total fail most times.  The wide open maps are fine, but half the maps, maybe more than half, allow almost no sniping.  Thats right, in a game called Sniper Elite, you will be using your pistol or melee for 75% of your kills.  I don't understand the decision to do this?  SE4 felt really wide open, and you occasionally had to dip inside but nothing crazy.  In this game you have entire levels that are inside bunkers, inside very tight cities, inside facilities.  There is basically no sniping allowed for most of the levels.  Thats a head scratcher for me.  And those levels I will just skip now that I've beaten them.

How many of these issues, like with the AI will get patched? Unsure.  I also did not use the focus mechanic even once yet during my playtime, I honestly dont see why you would need it at all.  I didnt use the breath hold thing either.  Unnecessary.  The nonlethal stuff in this game I also never used outside of SHU mines, only because I had them so may as well use them, but they are dumb (they just knock someone out until the next soldier wakes them up).  Theres not alot of good sniper perches in this game either which is sad.  At least I only found a few in my playthrough, I'm hoping to find more.  

Oh another thing that is super annoying is the character movement, especially inside buildings.  He moves like hes drunk off his ass most of the time, and inside buildings he can barely turn around, its insane.  I think it may have something to do with him constantly trying to auto-snap to wall cover or something?  But trying to navigate through a building is very frustrating.  

So final verdict, may surprise you because I just listed a ton of stuff this game failed at.  Because I love this style of game so much, even in this awful, rushed and glitched out of its mind presentation, I still enjoy the core gameplay of stealth and will keep playing it.  Will I recommend this to a friend?  NO way.  Will I recommend it to someone who loved SE4?  Maybe, if they really really loved it.   So I'd probably give this game for me personally a 3/5, but for the average person maybe a 2/5.  If you havent played SE4, get that one first, is better in almost every way.  But if you have played SE4 so many hours you are burnt out on it and want some new levels and guns to try out?  Then try SE5.

Do I like this game? Yeah, I do. But if I pay a hundred dollars for a video game, it shouldn't feel like I'm playing a beta test. The revolver stops reloading and firing if you use an item. Regular, boring house windows are inexplicably bulletproof. The game is much more finicky about what you can and can't climb over which makes the movement much clunkier and less fluid. There's sound bugs, janky animation transitions, and a whole slew of other issues that really detract from the game. Honestly, I'm kind of disappointed. There's a lot of changes and additions from SE4 that I like (bayonets, first-person iron sights, anti-tank rifles, customization, the new weapon pickup system, etc) but in terms of level design, playability and polish, I think that Sniper Elite 4 was much better.

Now I know we live in a repugnant reality where it's the norm for games to get pushed out slightly broken and be fixed over the course of a few months, instead of being perfected for launch, so I'm sure things will improve in time. That being said, I don't have to be happy about it. I like this game and everything, but in some ways it feels like a step backwards and there's plenty of issues to iron out still. I'm hoping that they tweak the traversal and get rid of all the invisible walls, and they BETTER fix all the other issues. I love Sniper Elite 4 to death and I feel like there's a lot of potential here, but this game still needs work. I'm sure they'll clean it up more, but I would hold off on buying it until they do, unless you can get it at a discount or something. In the meantime, I would just stick with 4.

I’m not sure what all the negative reviews are about with this game.  This is my first review on Steam because I had to set the record straight since I am a fan of this series and have played them all except Sniper Elite VR.  Sniper Elite 4 set the standard in my opinion and Rebellion stayed true with Sniper Elite 5.  27 hours in and I’m loving it as much as I loved Sniper Elite 4.  However, I do miss the trip wire traps...frowns.

Axis Invasions is a nice touch which I am finding a blast (another player joins the Germans to try and stop you during campaign missions).  Yes, you can’t camp once someone invades but this makes sense.  The maps are expansive and if camping was allowed, I could see how frustration could ensue hours after not being able to find your opponent.  I can also see how some of us could enjoy an hours-long hunt.  Perhaps a camp setting that can be turned on or off would be a nice addition to this concept.  As of now you can simply turn Axis Invasions off and camp all you want.  In fact, I suggest turning it off if you are trying to unlock weapons, complete certain tasks, etc.  My plan is to finish levels collect and unlock everything then go back to replay with Axis Invasions on.

Rebellion has added the x-ray cam to all weapons to happen more often as well which is awesome.  For example, if you use your pistol at a certain distance, it almost always jumps into effect.  I’m dropping my two cents because the negative reviews almost turned me off this game.  It was inevitable as a fan that I wouldn’t give it a try anyway so here I am.  My point is that if you really enjoyed Sniper Elite 4, you will enjoy this one and I highly recommend that you give it a chance.

review_text:
Just finished my first full game play-through of the single player campaign with a few comments.  I used Normal (medium) to see what the game was like.  I did not do any co-op or multiplayer.

Pros:
1)  Missions and maps are diverse.
2)  Stealth makes you really think and plan out you approach.
3)  Lots of other weapons can be found in the field (though you can't keep them).
4)  Option to heal before you die helps you stay in the game.
5)  Frequent system autosaves.
6)  Graphics were good if your graphics card will allow you to jack it up some.

Cons:
1)  Some bugs, primarily on movement and picking up items.  I realize the game just came out, and I received my first patch today.
2)  The 5th installment is more of a stealth game than a sniper game.  Use of your sniper rifle in most instances is too loud and will attract multiple enemies.  The maps don't allow opportunities for long-range sniping like previous versions.
3)  The terrain in the maps is hilly and rocky with good sniping spots, but you are blocked from leaving the paths to get a better sniping position.  This can also make you more easily located by enemies.
4)  On some maps you are swarmed by enemies if discovered (15 on 1), but other maps have very few enemies.
5)  Not a fan of the weapon options.  Only 3 of each to choose from (sniper, secondary and pistol).  The upgrade format means you have to complete several missions to improve the guns (ammunition clip size, suppressors, etc.).

Overall, it is a Sniper Elite game and it was enjoyable.  Karl is still a stud.  Going to try it again on Hard.  But I don't feel it is the best in the series, and Rebellion had plenty of time between versions to make it better than Sniper Elite 4.

Update:

Went to Hard difficulty.  No change in shooting mechanics or number of enemies, just in damage taken.  Expected more.

If you don't have a satchel charge, TNT won't replace it to open a door, safe or tank/222,  Very limiting.

I was killed several times when the map would stop me from entering trees or getting behind cover, leaving me out in the open.  Very frustrating.

The assault weapon slot is worthless. Use the pistol. That's all.

SE5 has fun moments. Some very satisfying shots, but the satisfaction seems to be offset by all the bugs and multiplayer exploits.

review_text:
Frankly, this is largely either a lateral move from the previous entry in some cases, or a direct step down in several others.  Graphically it looks good, but it isn't appreciably different from 4 unless you have direct side-by-side shots of the two.  Example being is the rock geometry and complexity of some environmental meshes.  They certainly look better, but it doesn't add to the experience to me.  Graphical improvements are nice, but they don't make a game good.


The graphical improvements, while nice, also directly impact the readability of what can be traversed and what can't.  I suppose it makes sense I'd be hesitant to move through some bushes, but there's numerous bits of mildly rocky terrain that is completely reasonable to cross, but you can't.  You can't and won't know until you actually try and it's frustrating.  This issue is pretty frequent and constantly pulls me out of the experience.

Gunplay is pretty good, but again isn't really improved over 4.  If there's been some changes, I certainly didn't register it while playing.  The only notable change I found is you can ADS in first person with all weapons.  It's pretty nice, but it isn't enough to justify the game's price.  Other than that, there's been some minor UI changes, but nothing to write home about.  

You can also change the attachments on all three of your weapons and you find the attachments by discovering workbenches scattered throughout the levels.  On a surface level this works, but is pretty uninspired to me.  You'll be locked out of attachments based on your progress in the campaign and there's no other way to get them.  I would have vastly preferred if you unlocked attachments based on your performance with said weapon akin to the weapon challenges from 4.  This would reward you for using your favorite weapons and lead to merit based progression rather than milestones used to artificially lock you out of upgrades.  You could've also used weapon xp like CoD and I'd feel more inclined to replay missions and try different weapons, but you just unlock the attachments for all weapons at once.  With the combined problem that the workbenches are hidden in increasingly difficult places, it's very easy to just miss out on needed attachments, although most of them are incredibly useless with arbitrary stat increases.

The level design is far more linear and constrained compared to 4.  Some may like this, but I find it limits my options immensely.  In addition to the noted traversal issues, there's basically no viable sniper spots aside from one or two mediocre ones per level.  No sniper spots in a sniping game?  Who thought this was a good idea?  You're constantly forced into close combat due to the confined design of most of the levels.  Again, close quarters focus in a sniping game?  Why?  I'd probably be less bitter if they hadn't also removed most of the secondary weapons to boot.  Shotguns are completely gone and they'd be pretty useful in some levels.  It would've also been cool if you could get various ammo types like slugs so you could use it at greater distances, but I guess that was too much to ask unless they sell them back in the season pass, which it looks like they're definitely going to.  Overall, it's got only one or two intended ways through the levels and you have to choose between them.  There's almost no room for creativity or exploration in this entry.

So, with that said, how about the enemies?  There's a very large number of them placed in each level.  On it's own, that wouldn't be an issue, but when they all have laser aim, can find you instantly, can call reinforcements at will, and can turn around on a dime it becomes a big issue.  There's very few spots in the game where you can reasonably snipe without having to relocate after a single shot.  Once they're alerted, they simply won't stop moving.  I had several enemies in the first couple of missions who proceeded to run in massive circles at full speed, never stopping.  On top of this, enemies can often get permanently stuck in loops of being alert and sprinting.  The enemies previously running laps would run far enough away to forget about their dead buddy just in time for them to find the same dead buddy and become alerted again.  This would happen very reliably and would make it nearly impossible to hit anyone.  It just wasn't fun at that point.  Not to mention the countless times I'd sneak up to an enemy, only to have them make a full 180 in a literal frame and spot me.  Not great.  This issue is compounded with the Jaeger enemies.  These enemies can't be melee killed if they're alerted, so it would be a shame if they could just immediately face you with no warning or reason, right?

Finally, I just loathe the challenge kills in each mission.  The premise is that you kill a HVT in a specific manner, then you get rewarded with a weapon.  Sounds good on the surface, but again I find it frustrating that absolutely none of these challenges revolve around actually doing any sniping.  Poison an enemy, drop a missile on another, or push one into a cement mixer.  They basically all revolve around sneaking in and manipulating some environmental variable. <insert obligatory complaint about the lack of sniping in my sniping game>  Maybe these should of been challenges related to hitting a specific target area or maybe a grenade belt shot, you know, something to challenge my skills as a sniper.  But no, we instead get to put poison in a drink and wait.  If I wanted to go play Hitman, I'd just do that instead.

Overall, I just can't recommend this over SE4.  It's far more limited and regresses in many ways in comparison, on top of the fact they stripped a lot of weapons out with the intent to add them in later dlc.  The levels are mostly worse and the enemies are glitchy and numerous.  Just get the complete edition of 4 and I can guarantee you'll have a better time for your money.

review_text:
What MGSV should've been.

So, to preface, i received this game as a gift from an old friend as something of a surprise; I'd grown long since bored of the recurringly samey installments of the series, loving V2 but not a large fan of 1 or 3, with 4 being passable in coop. 

We haven't gotten to do coop yet, he's been away with work, and I've limited myself (rather painfully) to the first three missions. The first is a large open map style area with a myriad of different objectives and a *lot* of ways to go about them. Not in a contrived scripted 'loud or quiet' way, but more like a blend of dishonored and MGSV. The second map was smaller and more focused, with you simply trying to breach the countryside to arrive in an occupied castle manor..... but the building itself is large and intricate with dozens of rooms, functioning something like a close quarters combat maze, where sneaking starts to require utilizing the various gadgets and tools at your disposal as even a suppressed pistol shot will give you away indoors, when you dont know who could be behind a wall or above or below you and within earshot. The third is a mix, a well fortified and guarded main building surrounded by beach, sea, and urban sprawl that you need to infiltrate. Variety, nothing grows stale, im actually very sad that there are only 10 levels because I know I'll be craving more.

Really, to me, this game feels like what MGSV should have been, rather than a sniper elite game - truth be told I've used my rifle somewhat little in both PVP invasions and the game itself, the pistol and knife tend to be more useful in almost all situations, aside from the odd enemy sniper to take out first. And that's honestly fine, the pistol feels nice, unlike previous SE games where everything but the sniper rifle felt intentionally nerfed to make you not want to use them, guns feel like guns in this game. 

It's grittier and more realistic in both gameplay, tone, and visuals, after 3 and 4 felt quite cartoony and almost light-hearted, it's a delightful return to the seriousness, high stakes, and tension from V2. 

The invasions are really fun, but suffer from the same issue as Elden Ring invasions; they Never. F&cking. Stop. You'll kill one invader to be invaded again minutes later, or be killed and receive the same. If you have invasions enabled, you're going to be playing the entire mission against invaders, rather than the rare and odd invasion which would stand out and be scary it leads to the invasions feeling extremely arcadey, contrasting the rest of the game. So, whilst i do still invade, i have turned it off in my own game so i can play slowly and methodically as befits a sniper. 

Morality?
The game features a dishonored style 4-directional spectrum for playstyle, between Lethal, Nonlethal, Stealth, and Combat. I... don't know why exactly this is a thing or why they added nonlethal rounds and takedowns, aside from to further dethrone MGSV in that regard. Personally, I'm softening a beach so my boys can land with fewer casualties, I'm going to kill the enemy instead of giving them a nice nap so they can wake up when the marines or whoever else arrive. It is a sniper game, after all, so I don't see the purpose of playing nonlethally on a first run... but ill probably do a pacifist run afterwards. 

Skills
The weakest point in the game i think, half are combat, a quarter are about Focus which is disabled on the hard mode like i play and the rest are things like carrying an extra explosive you'll almost never use anyways, so, if you play sneakily on hard, skills are absolutely worthless. So, levelling up is worthless. A bit sad, it'd be nice if all those points you rack up with long distance kills actually mattered.

Gameplay
It's just refined. The best thing i can liken it to, is just MGSV with tighter feeling and more responsive controls. Not that MGSV had poor controls, but it's a noticable difference to someone with a few hundred hours in MGSV with the infinite heaven mod - which i do ALSO recommend to anyone still playing MGSV. Targets are now treated a little more like the new Hitman games, they have routines and there's 'interesting' preset ways to kill them which unlock different things (think i got an MP40 for dropping a chandelier on an officer's head), but I actually do wish I could just actually use my sniper rifle. I intend more than one playthrough though, so I'll try to unlock all the weapons first time and play more freestyle next run, and then my pacifist run.

Alright, I dont really do reviews of my games, did it a bit kind of as a meme, years ago, and I'm not some hardcore Purist of the Sniper Elite games, I only have 5.4 hours on this right now, so that should be obvious. 

  NOW, with that said, I'm going to go ahead and address this game.

Does it look good? Sure, it has some pretty polished visuals compared to earlier games, not that far off from 4, though, really.

Is it fun? it can be, but it's spending a ton of it's effort in trying to be a new MGS installment than being something that furthers this franchise.

  That's the core of it, now, I've browsed some of the reviews here posted by franchise die-hards, and it's not exactly uncommon for core audiences to ♥♥♥♥♥ about how a new game in a franchise is different, or somehow worse than previous games in said franchise, *HOWEVER* in this particular case, I'd pay close attention to the negative reviews on this game, I play Sniper Elite very Casually and even I see that this game is inferior to Sniper Elite 4, when I feel like sneaking around to vantage points and timing a good sniper shot to a busted generator and getting a cool, fun slow-mo bullet cam to a Nazi exploding, I go to SE, the issue with this game is that you dont ever really do that, admittedly I dont have a ton of time in this, but on PC I have 7.5 hours in SE4 (I've also played on consoles, before.) and thats all from positioning and carefully taking out dudes until I've cleared the map, in SE5 I have gotten a handful of decent sniper shots, the majority of the game is built to drive you into Close-Quarters combat with your AR or a Pistol of some sort, the good thing I've noticed about SE5 is that they made a lot more opportunities for you to have some kind of sound masking, which is totally pointless when you're RP'ing Solid Snake with a silenced pistol inside a barracks, or wandering the corridors of some villa, so thats my big up for this installment, my big down on this swing is that they removed other things, I cleared the first map and it seems like they have gotten rid of the trip mines, which were a fun tool to play with in SE4, unless they come in later, like one of the reviews I read here mentioned they dont add Wind into the game until later on here in SE5, but thats why I absolutely think if this game is interesting to you, you should just go ahead and get SE4, you have access to these tool, and others, one other review mentioned that in SE4 you had unlimited Stones to toss as a distraction, in SE5 you have a very limited amount of glass bottles you have to restock in the world.  
 Now granted, maybe some things have been done to make the game more challenging and make you, the player, work harder to get solid stealth sniper kills, but from what I've seen I have to agree with some of the other reviews here that seem to think the game has been dumbed down, while I would say it's optimistic to think a lot of the changes were made to increase the difficulty to seasoned players, I think its a lot more realistic to believe this was all done with the intention of making the game more "action packed" and "exciting" to appeal to a wider audience, while also removing some of the quirkier things that made 4 so entertaining, sort of like the big red highlights on explosive vehicle parts and hazards, I'm pretty sure thats something you can disable in SE4, in SE5 it's practically non-existent, the one time I saw it happen it was on a boat, the red was much more subtle and it washed over the vehicle as a pulse, not as helpful, and not as fun IMO.

  anyway, if this was helpful at all, cool, if not, Oh well, sorry.

TL;DR: Map Design is very on point, graphics are pretty solid, and the gameplay is better in SE4, I deleted this and reinstalled 4 as I was writing. take that for whatever it's worth.

Even finding a place to lie down is sometimes, literally spots on the floor that are no different but no prone. 

2. Open World is not a huge world that is fenced off literally everywhere except where the designers want you to go. A Long vista is expected now in games like this, but SE5 is NOT open world AT ALL. Remember those fantastic trip line mines?  Well they are gone. No more covering a stair, doorway, etc. And lets just talk about why next.

3. No one ever asked for non lethal "things." We never asked for non-lethal mines, bullets etc. Why do we have them? Well, I will guess it made the list because SE5 is woke up the Kazoo. They simply do not like the idea of carrying the series forward as a WAR GAME. There is no excuse for the cost.....those trip line mines were one of them. It is idiotic and ruins the immersion environment and for the old hardcore SE player is so impactful as to require me to say DO NOT BUY THIS GAME.

4. There are so few Germans in some levels as to be comical. There are way too few Germans in every level. This is SE5, for those of us that have supported this series the only hard part of the game is being torn out of immersion and #1. Whole buildings with prime objectives have 15 Germans. Huge trucks travel the roads with ZERO troops in the back. How bad is it? It was only in the Hitler level does the 1st truck appear with soldiers in it. Japanese characters do not show their faces.

I never threw back a grenade, got shot up enough to need some extra whatever....etc. etc.

Look, SE5 is the kind of game that when you read what some of the reviewers say about it, you just can;t believe how little the depth and breadth of their sniper title catalog/experience is. There is literally nothing new here....nothing.  These folks need to get out more. SE5 seals the fate of this series.
