review_text:
TL;DR: Good game, even though it feels like a repeat of the past games. Wait until a sale if possible.

[b]Gameplay-wise, the best Sniper Elite since Sniper Elite 1[/b]:
+ The X-Ray cam has never been this detailed and satisfying
+ Weapons are now extremely realistic, to the point where suppressed shots can still be heard by the enemy from tens of meters away.
+ New gamemode - [b]Axis Invasion[/b]: Any player can 'invade' your game and take a shot at killing you (or getting killed by you). I haven't felt a rush this big since the early days of Sniper Elite 1. I'm not even mad when losing, it's just all-around fun
- Beginner-friendly: Bullet drop and wind direction show up clearly when using empty lung, and Authentic has been made easier. It's a good thing that those that just picked up the game are able to dive straight to the deep end, but it's not as meaningful if the 'deep end' is relatively shallow, is it ? For those that played through Authentic, this is massive downgrade.
- A lack of weapons: Sniper Elite 4 had 40 weapons, Sniper Elite 5 only has 18. You would expect everything used/developed during the war to be available for use by the end of World War II, and surely it isn't that hard to port over these weapons from Sniper Elite 4. Still, as of writing this review, it's only been about a week or so since release, so it's very likely they will add these in eventually.
-Lack of freedom: Sniper Elite 5 was supposed to be 'Sniper Elite meets Hitman', where you could replay a level in hundreds of different ways, and you would be rewarded for trying out different approaches. Sadly, there is little incentive to do that. The best examples are the kill lists, where you get to unlock weapons, but ONLY if you kill them in a specific way. 

[b]Story-wise, the worst Sniper Elite since Sniper Elite 3[/b]:
- Cliche: it actually gave me a good laugh when replaying the story modes in co-op mode with my friends who just picked up the game. They tried to make Fairburne sound badass with lines like "Nazi bastards", or "Wouldn't you like to know", but besides that, there is virtually no character development.
- Historically inaccurate ? On the topic of character development, my favorite character was Charlie, a... Scottish... black... woman... working as a spy ?... The Allies were unlikely to let women serve in the army at the time, let alone send them as part of the expeditionary force. The only exception was of course, the Soviet Union, which had renowned female snipers, but for some reason, Rebellion never thought to follow-up on that trope.
- Nazi secret weapon: This game follows literally the same story as the last two Sniper Elite games: the Nazi's want to turn the war around, and so they build a super-weapon. You've already destroyed a land-based super-weapon (a tank), two aerial-based super-weapons (V2 rockets + guided missiles) and so the only logical super-weapon left would be...  a super-[spoiler]submarine[/spoiler]. I don't think that makes for a bad plot device, but it feels like they didn't even try to make this novel.

[b]Graphics[/b] The graphics are extremely beautiful, which is most evident on Level 5 (Guernsey). Fairburne is as detailed as ever, leaves footsteps and trails, and the environment (especially water) reacts to the player. It's a major improvement from previous titles, but I still wish there was more that set them apart from other games.

review_text:
Despite the myriad of game-breaking bugs that people seem to be having with this particular title so soon after launch, I have not encountered anything seriously game-breaking. A few minor visual glitches here and there, and I fell through the floor into null space a grand total of one time in over 50 hours of play, but nothing a quick re-load of a recent save could not fix. I also encountered the body-hiding bug in which the game auto-saves while hiding a body in a crate, then subsequent re-loads of that savegame show me as still holding the body (despite not actually holding one). Reload of a previous save fixed it.

Many people seem to be complaining about the visual quality of the game being terrible and literally worse than SE4. This could not be further from the truth. The visuals in this game are absolutely stunning, and the views in Wolf Mountain are especially breathtaking. Mission 8, Rubble and Ruin, also has some extremely good visuals with respect to level design. It really hits home just how absolutely devastating the effects of WWII were on once-beautiful places like France. HDR is supported, which makes the daytime maps really pop, but there is a disappointing lack of raytracing and DLSS support. AMD's FidelityFX Super Resolution 1.0 is supported.

Explosions in particular have had a substantial upgrade from SE4, visually speaking. I actually prefer the realtime non-xray explosion visuals. Extremely realistic.

The attention to detail, both visual and audible, of each of the weapons is absolutely impeccable. They really did their research here, and even recorded many hours of real-world audio produced by each weapon in the game. A high-end audio system is HIGHLY recommended!

X-ray cams are now available for SMG and pistol kills, a very nice addition. I also like that you can adjust the speed of the x-ray cam faster or slower in realitme, although I would like to have seen more range in the adjustment.

As for traversing around the various maps... Well, especially (but not limited to) the very first map, there are far too many obstacles that SHOULD easily be hurdled by Karl, but are absolutely impassable. Short bushes less than waist-high? Impassable. A pile of rocks no taller than Karl's ankle? Impassable. Various knee- or waist-height rock walls? Impassable. This particular aspect is a downgrade from SE4. In that game, anything that seemed logically passable in fact was.

Weapon mastering has had a complete makeover compared to SE4. It's much simpler and easier to master each weapon instead of having bonkers requirements like "get 100 ricochet kills in the nuts while hanging upside down from the library's chandelier and reciting I'm Henry The 8th I Am". However, mastering a weapon only unlocks a skin for that weapon (either some super-fugly yellow/green camo for pistols and SMGs, or a ghillie wrap for rifles). No stats buffs are applied. These are only accomplished via the myriad of customizable attachment options, which get unlocked by finding the various pistol/SMG/rifle workbenches throughout the game, 1 of each type for a total of 3 per map, giving the game 24 benches in total.

Expanded weapon stats are actually presented numerically now instead of just arbitrary-length bars, and this is especially helpful with the various suppressors you can attach to most (not all) weapons, including SMGs. I absolutely welcome the ability to see just how many meters away an enemy will be able to hear your suppressed gunfire. Further to this, a black exclamation mark will appear over a tagged enemy's head while aiming any weapon at them, if they're going to hear the gunshot. Very handy.

The P.1938 pistol available only to those who pre-ordered the game is kind of a letdown. It's not a significant step up from the other pistols in the game. IF that happened to be a deciding factor for your game pre-order, you are likely very disappointed with it. I know I am. However, it was not a deciding factor for me, personally.

S-mines and trip-mines are no longer present in campaign mode, only in multiplayer modes, and have been replaced with the schu-mine, which is non-lethal. This is a big thumbs-down from me, as now the only lethal mine option is the teller mine, and you can only carry 3 of them (2 before you've unlocked the extra carry ability). One may put forth the counter argument that you can now booby-trap bodies with TNT and grenades (you couldn't do this in previous games), but it's still not as effective as a trip-mine for area denial. I've seen enemies run right over bodies and not trip the trap. They must actually inspect the body to set it off. Big big big thumbs-down.

The minimap has also fundamentally changed compared to previous games. In SE4, if an enemy was nearby, it would show up as a discrete dot on the minimap, regardless if he was tagged or not. Now, enemies only show up as large nebulous clouds denoting their general area, and only show as discrete dots once they are tagged via binoculars or a scope. Scope tags wear off after a few moments but binocular tags are permanent, at least in non-Authentic difficulty modes. While some may dislike this new operational mode, I find it a more feasible solution to what basically amounts to a superpower.

All in all, I would still recommend the game. I am thoroughly enjoying it, and if my hours logged in SE4 is any indication, I'll be playing this for a long, long time to come.

What I write for this review is the experience I had with the game, everybody will experience things differently. This is my honest review if you don't like it well tough. Also no game is safe from a review whether its early access or full release now onto the review.

Sniper Elite 5 is a great sniping video game. You playing as the famous Karl Fairburne in finding out a secret German nazi weapon in 1944. This game is absolutely amazing-ish. 

The campaign is pretty slandered from the other Sniper Elite games. Find a main nazi bad guy, snipe them & done. You can pick different difficulties from I link lowest is civilian to authentic but they now added more customization options to suit a players comfort when playing. 

Graphics looks amazing even on the lowest setting possible it just amazing. There wasn't a lot wrong with the graphics except for when you join in on other players missions you sometimes will have bad graphic quality for a few seconds. 

Weapon sounds were okay but if I am being 100% honest they all sounded the same to me except the anti-tank rife. I am not sure its just my bad hearing or I wasn't paying enough attention to the weapon sounds but they just sounded the same to me. The rifles sounded the same to each other, the SMGs founded the same to each other & the pistols as well.

Game-play was okay, movement wasn't bad except for the auto cover messing a few things up. Aim movement was actually okay for my default, normally I have to adjust it higher but this was okay. Another thing I had an issue was the buttons being the same for so many different things. Throwing stuff sometimes bugged out to where Karl would just be stuck in the throw animation for a long time. There was the re-load loop issue where you select an ammo type & Karl would just infinitely reload the weapon until you re-select another ammo type. 

Weapons were okay but I didn't like how they were locked through challenges or finding workbenches. Skill leveling would have been nice to do for the weapons & attachments should have been challenges (& some are). 

Attachments are good I guess, I didn't see any issue with them except for the pistol scopes & the pistol suppressors not showing on the gun sometimes. 

Axsi Invasions is where a player is an enemy sniper trying to kill you or your partners if your in a joined match. I turned this feature off in my game but some players I joined has this on & I don't think its a bad idea since it gives a slight more exp reward. The only issue I had was helping a player in his mission & we defeated an invader (damn sounds like Elden Ring & Dark Souls over here) 5/6 times. I would like to see a system where you defeat an invader you can't get invaded again until the next mission. 

Survival is how it sounds, you survive waves of nazi's. I can't remember is this was in Sniper Elite 3 but I know it was in Sniper Elite 4. 

Multiplayer is blank for me meaning I don't know how it is due to never trying it. I my first SE multiplayer was in SE4 & first game there was a hacker which put off multiplayer for SE forever.

Accessories were okay, there were some changes from SE4 to SE5 like no trip wires anymore. The only issue I had with the accessories was the satchel charges unlock requirements were never explained better. It only said complete the campaign to unlock which I did on the easiest difficulty & never unlocked them come to find out it has to be hardest (authentic) difficulty to unlock them since I did easiest to hard & still didn't unlock the satchel charges.  

With all said & done I felt SE5 is nothing new really. Its just the same the previous games. Only thing new (from what I can tell) is the Axi Invasions & thats it. The DLC is the ame & the campaign is just repeat. I would love see Rebellion take a bold move & try something else like a different time era. Don't get me wrong Rebellion does amazing work I think better then Underdog Studio. 

So Sniper Elite 5 gets 5/10 score from me making just average but I still recommend buying this game also the other Sniper Elite games as well.

That's the Pony review for Sniper Elite 5

review_text:
I've been racking up the hours in Sniper Elite since I was taken in by the second instalment, dragged in deeper by the third and positively submerged by the fourth. Like an infatuated lover I would jump at any criticism uttered in my presence, "The huge number of models! The atmosphere! You can practically smell the salsiccia in the tiny Italian kitchens!".

This review is limited by 2.5 hours of game play from yesterday because at this stage I'm suffering a virtual hangover, contemplating asking for a refund and hoping my colleagues will soon forget the praise I blindly heaped upon the series.

Last night she came home drunk and said she was packing her stuff.

I shouldn't have pressed so hard on the authenticity of the signage in Lorino dockyard.

With each iteration the AI became more impressive. Yes, it was far from perfect with bots continually swapping places behind cover when alerted. Yet hearing that the AI noticed their officer was gone it gave them an awareness... personality. It planted the seed for a trained enemy capable of working together. In numero 5 that seed never came to flower. I've not heard a private calling for his officer yet or lamenting over Hans having gone AWOL. Instead of sending in lone wolfs on their r&r in France to challenge the inimical sniper this could have been the basis for an enemy capable of forming up a quick search and destroy party but was squandered in favour of... what? Workbenches for Fairburne to chisel out a new suppressor? Clanging bottles with firecrackers for a Molotov-lite effect?

Again our broad-shouldered stoic crosses paths with German officers carrying highly sensitive information and an even higher reluctance to make an escape when threatened by a unseen yet lethal operative. As soon as their henchmen start dropping the Luger comes out to commence their ritual of diving between two pillars. You'd have thought they would try and make their escape in a  Kübelwagen covered by two motorbikes complete with MG42 toting sidecars. So blizzard, what is it? An officer critical to the defence of the French coastline or the local platoon commander up for a fight, waiting for the quick reaction force (QRF) to join in?
Ah yes, the QRF. Where is it? We're storming a radar site which the allies let know was a priority by bombing it yet there's no QRF when Carl serves them their D-Day taster. Even the site's entrance guardhouse is unconvincingly manned by a single soldier.
Perhaps his buddy is in town enjoying himself at the local house of the rising sun but that's only believable to those who haven't explored the area yet. The town feels like Dieppe on the 18th of August 1942, garrisoned, fully stocked with materiel, devoid of civilians and weapons zeroed onto the beach. It's incongruous with the few Wehrmacht personnel patrolling the area and the messages played over the tannoy for the locals, whose houses are boarded up and seem deserted. At least the constant quips from Fairburn about the mission objectives keep you company otherwise you might have forgotten why you're there while sneaking around the few Germans whose sole mission was to stay as far away as possible from the ostfront.

In SE 4 I would at times go stealthy just to soak up the atmosphere the development team almost magically managed to translate from binary to as close as you can virtually get to smelling the alpine air (Deathstorm: Obliteration). It's easy to reminisce about sneaking around the back alleys of Deathstorm: Inflitration, its labyrinthine university and medieval city walls boasting cannons. The inaugural mission of SE 5 doesn't make you stop and awe at the architecture. Putting a radar site, resistance den, interrogation-slash-weapons storage combi barn*, coastal town and multiple naval gun equipped bunkers close together makes you unable to turn round without hitting an objective, all helpfully narrated. At least the sterility of Deathstorm: Inception was consistent. The oft mentioned arbitrary borders and paths make it suffocating. If only the Germans had known a hedgerow and some prickly wire is enough to block and keep out those pesky commandos.

All of this is forgivable and there are improvements. The SMG's and pistols feel more like small arms. Rate of fire is higher in both it seems (it makes the game easier too, too easy even on harder settings). A Major Winters impression where you're walking around with an unscoped kar98 is now on the cards. Boxer engined motorbikes make an overdue appearance, their manned and weaponized sidecars completing the feel of the occupation force of '44. Oh and swastikas, lots of swastikas. I guess the stock of unused ones from previous incarnations was crowbarred open.

No, the unforgivable is the massacre that is the new multiplayer. SE multiplayer always catered for a specific audience. It would test your skills and mainly your patience when getting repeatedly shot and you couldn't figure out where from. If that wasn't your cup of tea CTF was faster paced. I relished zig zagging the streets of Rat Run, mining the drainage canals in Plantation and tagging enemies among the remains of a pyramid in Ruins. During my SE 5 taster session this game play mode seems to have been taken behind the shed together with the artistic talents of the in game menu developer (there was something about that scene of a search party of soldiers dismounting an Opel truck to comb out a quaint Italian village that greeted you when starting up SE 4). Everything that made it stand out from generic shooters seems gone. Running across buildings in houses in mp Village was a death sentence. No longer. I once saw someone ingeniously using the ghillie suit camouflage in an otherwise open spot on the same map. Kill cams and lens flares have killed it. It's been called a fortnite clone, which is accurate, save the WW2 skins. I guess the whispers of suppressed shots on night time maps like Night Woods are relegated the SE 4 era too.

All in all the dev team seems to have been distracted and Sniper Elite no longer knows what it wants to be having gone schizophrenic between console FPS hit, skilled sniper shooter and multiplayer pulp.

*Who puts a sign for weapons storage on a barn in the middle of the French country side anyway?

review_text:
[h1]Long time fans might find the lack of S-Mines or their favourite rifle being paywalled galling, but SE5 is still a solid addition to the series.[/h1]

Featuring 8 large, and reasonably open levels (plus one little bonus stage), with multiple main/side objectives; each with a couple of starting locations that can be unlocked. All available for 2 player, campaign co-op. None feel as iconic to me as the Brandenburg Gate level setting did, and they lean on accordian music to sell the French setting instead. Barring a couple of Resistance fighters in cutscenes, there is a complete absence of any members of the French populace, anywhere in the game's depiction of France.

It's missing a lot of the series' usual rifles (so they can be sold as DLC) which has driven a lot of the initial negative reviews, but it has a decent enough selection in the base game, although not many French weapons. The weapon customisation is a really big step forward and also removes a lot of the horrible weapon mastery grind of past SE titles. History grumps will be annoyed at the proliferation of supressors and magnified optics in WWII, but it doesn't bother me as much as I thought it might. The sniping is much less exaggerated and the wind and drop indicators on the scope are now totally accurate, which makes hits out to 400m pretty easy with the better rifles. Wind is only a factor past 200m, and only on the latter levels. These are good changes.

Overall difficulty feels MUCH lower than SE4, with enemies now able to be reliably lured one-by-one, instead of usually sticking in small groups, and the skill system making Karl overly robust even on Authentic difficulty. 

Authentic Plus is notably absent, and apparently won't be added due to the high difficulty being 'un-inclusive'. Difficult achievements have also been omitted so no-one's feelings get hurt, leaving only achievements that are... non-achievements? I don't particularly care about achievements, but this design philosophy is maddeningly stupid.

The other truly bizarre addition is the ability to use non-lethal takedowns... Something no one asked for in a series which centres around (very graphically) killing cartoon Nazis. But now you can not hurt Nazi's while not getting your own feelings hurt by too hard achievements. Madness.

These aren't game breaking changes but suggest that Rebellion's culture [i]really[/i] doesn't align with making graphically violent, sniper sandbox games.

Weapons are not as evenly balanced as SE4 which is a shame. Want to shoot accurately at long range? The M1903 Springfield has a [i]clear[/i] advantage in magnification and flat-shooting trajectory. SE4 had a handful of rifles that all made a compelling case for their use, due to closely balanced advantages/disadvantages in optics, ROF and range.

In some ways though, this is irrelevant because arguably, the best sniper rifle in the game is now the M1911 pistol. Slap a scope and a suppressor on it, and you have a pocket-sized rifle that is pin-point accurate as far as the myopic enemies are able to see.

Invasion Mode isn't really my thing, but it's an interesting addition and absolutely adds a challenge that the story mode is otherwise lacking. Balance has seesawed back and forth a bit - generally invaders have played smarter in the beginning, so things have been balanced more and more toward Karl.

The Kill Hitler DLC features the most wacky, Charlie Chaplin-esque representation of Hitler so far, which I don't really appreciate, and it is my least favourite level. Far too much waiting around during Hitler's very long and very buggy patrol route if you are going for one of the set piece kills.

Hopefully, moving forward, the series can balance some of the mechanical improvements of SE5 with the better balance and harder difficulty of SE4. A 50% reduction in cartoony 'Boy's own adventure' tone would be nice, but I won't hold my breathe...

[quote][url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/6142328/][b] With 1,200+ reviews, make sure to follow The Cpt Froggy Club Curator Page for plenty more![/b][/url][/quote]

Sniper Elite 5:
~~~~~~~~~~~ 

The greatest sharpshooter of the second World War, Karl Fairburn, better known by the Axis high command as The Shadow, is back in action. This time around, he is deployed to France from late May to mid-June 1944. His mission is to uncover the latest Nazi secret weapon, code named Kraken! As a master in the art of stealth and sharpshooting, will he knock German Soldiers out from close range, or will he snipe them one by one like ducks at a shooting gallery in a fairground? You'll be the one to decide as you play the deadly Shadow in Sniper Elite 5.

Sniper Elite 5 is a third-person shooter action game developed and self-published by Rebellion on the Steam platform on the 26th of May 2022. The game is also available on PS4/PS5, Xbox One and Xbox Series X|S.

The game consists of a primary campaign of 8 missions that you can play as a single player or co-op. You can also allow Axis Invasion, an online feature that gives access to random players in your current game as an Axis sniper, spicing up the difficulty level. In terms of multiplayer, there are several modes of play. For example, you can team up with another three players in the Survival mode and push back the onslaught of waves of German soldiers and motorised units, or play against 15 other snipers in the Free for All mode, or play Teams vs Teams. If you purchase the Deluxe Edition, you'll have the first season pass and the Wolf Mountain mission, where you have to assassinate the Führer.

I must mention that I was already a big fan of the series, and I wondered how far they would push this game in terms of graphics, AI and gameplay overall. Well, in a nutshell, I was blown away. Using a 3080 TI graphic card on a 4k 144mhz large screen monitor, the graphics are absolutely spectacular! 

Each mission has a large map, and depending on how you want to approach the mission (choosing either the stealth tactic or sniping soldiers all the way through), they will take you around 2 to 4 hours each to complete. Enemy soldiers can hear shots around the map, so it is imperative to investigate each area with your binoculars and tag enemy units and alarm posts before doing anything. In my case, I was mostly trying the stealth approach throughout my gameplay, but in some instances, I had no other choice but to go out with all guns blazing to make my way through the mission, especially when I encountered tanks. Well, you need more than guns to get rid of them! Panzerfaust, mines, satchels and TNT will be the way to go, but you will need to strike twice to inflict severe damage or destroy them. 

New objectives will appear in the mission status when you find intel (documents or letters). They are primarily secondary objectives, and you can decide whether to complete them or not. However, you must successfully achieve the main objectives to exit each map. The other collectables are the Eagle stone statues (three per mission) most of which are pretty easy to find and fun to shoot. You also have three safe rooms to find on each map. These rooms have plenty of ammunition and a workbench where you can upgrade your weapons. And there is plenty of other ammunition to find in buildings and wooden crates. Some can have their locks picked or cut with a cutter, while others will need a crowbar to open. In the latest missions, you'll also find poison that you can use to assassinate high command targets, which is fun. You can even insert an explosive into the Fuhrer sandwich; hot stuff, I must say.

The slow-motion X-ray shots are just super impressive. You can see the bullet's impact when it hits the bone structure, organs, and flesh and see the blood spray coming out of the body. The brain, eyes, kidneys, liver, intestines, heart, lung and the tasty-testes shots are brilliant. The explosive X-ray slow motion is also spectacular. You will see clearly the shock waves and the shrapnel making their way into the body while the soldiers are projected into the air; awesome stuff!

The AI is pretty good most of the time. Enemy units can detect you if you are walking toward their clear 180-degree peripheral views. They can't see you if you hide behind large objects or camouflage yourself in high grasses. They may be alerted by noises you make while running, or they may hear a shot. The issue I encountered several times is when you and the enemy are suddenly face to face. For example, you might enter a house through a window, and the enemy is right in front of you and seems to move around you at least twice before shooting at you. 

The other issue I encountered more than once is sound loss through my Astro A 50 wireless headset. It just goes without any warning. I updated the hardware software, but I still have the issue. I'm not sure why, and I have to restart the game when it happens. It isn't very pleasant, I must say. 

I rarely play multiplayer games in general, but for some reason, I gave this game a try, and I was really surprised with the experience. I thoroughly enjoyed the Survival mode, and it was pretty fun playing against 16 other snipers in the Free for All. I will definitely be taking part in more multiplayer sessions as it seems easy to find a game.   

In terms of upgrade progression, you have the weapons and perks. You have to start from scratch for all modes, which I like as it adds more value in regards to the replayability of the game. And it is the same regarding unlocking and customising characters.

The graphics are super impressive, as are the sound effects and the voiceovers. The story is pretty good and provides amazing cutscenes. Despite the minor fiddly issues, Sniper Elite 5 surpassed my expectations.

Positives:
~~~~~~~ 
+	 Spectacular graphics   
+	Amazing slow-motion X-ray shots and explosions
+	Good story, cutscenes, sound effects and voiceover
+	8 extensive missions
+	Campaign and multiplayer modes
+	 Achievements

Negatives:
~~~~~~~~ 
-	Few issues with loss of sound with Astro wireless A50 headset
-	No trading cards as yet

Sniper Elite 5 is simply a stunning game! A must-have in your game library.

9/10

[H1]Apparently the running while crouching was too much of an extravagance...[/h1]

The game boasts less content than its predecessor, Sniper Elite 4. Apparently, "running while crouching" was just too much of an extravagance for Sniper Elite 5. Who needs innovation and improved mechanics when you can have the authentic "crouch-and-slow-walk" experience that keeps you begging for more? The absence of running while crouching is a bold choice that says, "We believe in tradition and refuse to be swayed by the allure of modern gaming."

Also, who needs vast, open spaces when you can have endless twisty hallways, right?

In summary, Sniper Elite 5 takes all the conventions of open-world gaming and shatters them with the force of a thousand clunky controllers. It's a masterclass in not fixing what isn't broken and embracing the glorious world of narrow hallways. If you're tired of progress and innovation, look no further – Sniper Elite 5 is your ticket to the past.

[h1]Even $1 on Game Pass is overpaying for this scheizz...[/h1]
Pros: [b]#1.[/b] Has everything that Sniper Elite 4 had (but with 300% more bugs)
[b]#2.[/b] Loading and saving a save is very fast (under 7seconds).

Cons: [b]#1.[/b] Infected with Denuvo malware, which prevented me from playing the game on multiple occasions
[b]#2.[/b] The game crashed 3 times in 2hours.
[b]#3.[/b] The game has a huge memory leak, which reduces fps to 15 or so. Once you restart the game, then the performance is normal again. It's very likely that Denuvo malware is the cause.
[b]#4.[/b] Has many bugs. Sometimes the enemies INSTANTLY spot you and open fire, even if you're sneaking. Sometimes you get stuck and can't get unstuck.
[b]#5.[/b] Has Day-One DLC. The practice of developers making content and then separating it from the game that you just paid $50 for and then expecting you to pay for that removed content on Day-One is a disgusting one. Rebellion are scum for releasing such a buggy game AND then having the gall to charge for content that they removed from the game, instead of having rather spent that time just fixing bugs.
[b]#6.[/b] The regional pricing of this game is terrible. This game costs 42USD in Argentina, which is one of the poorest countries on earth. Rebellion KNOW that they've priced the game way, way too high in certain countries due to the hundreds of players from those countries that have commented on the situation in the steam forums, and yet after more than a month, Rebellion haven't changed it (and won't).
[b]#7.[/b] The game is highly linear. There are bushes & invisible walls absolutely everywhere, that prevent you from approaching an objective from multiple angles. It's literally the devs' way, or the highway. This means there's no room for inventiveness when taking on an objective. If the devs want you to enter through the front gate of a camp, then you can ONLY do that, there's no side routes or inventiveness to be found.
[b]#8.[/b] You can't jump over a massive amount of stuff, which you'd normally expect you'd be able to. I'm talking about knee-high stuff, that you can even jump over.
[b]#9.[/b] The animations are borked. Multiple times now, I've choked a guy out, except that the animation shows me choking out his mid-section rofl.

In summation: If you're looking for a good sniping game, then get one of the Sniper Ghost Warrior games, or even just challenge yourself by playing through the entire Borderlands 2/3 game with only sniper rifles... you'll have a lot more fun and you won't be giving Rebellion any more money to make an EVEN WORSE Sniper Elite 6 game, which is a win-win. I was very confused entering this game over the design decisions and gameplay. 
As we all know sniper elite is a game about being a sniper, but the maps and game rules arent designed for it at all.
Lets start with the maps.

The maps are often very tight and cluttered, full of invisible walls, leaving you sniping from 50 meters away some of the time but most of the time its encouraged to use your pistol because of the short distances and all the cover.

Open fields are full of cover so theres no need to improvise or try to make up ways to stealth since the answer is always the same.

In a game called sniper elite you shouldnt be running around indoors in tight apartments half of the time.

The story is very milktoast and none of the characters are likable. The cut scenes were almost painful to watch and the bad character models didnt help at all.

Why use character models that look 8 years old in a modern game like this? 50 dollars is way too much if you cant even get that right.

And gameplay wise, Its just like any other sniper elite game but the trip mine is gone

There is a non lethal option, but why? There is no benefit in going non lethal, the points dont really improve either and the game paints every enemy as a evil dumbass anyways so theres no point in using the option.

In mission 1 you get the option to shut down or blow up a nazi radar and they tease you about it blowing up and crashing down, but you can also shut it down. Choices are great, but both options gives the exact same result. No matter what you do, the radar will still stand there, smoking a little.

Last but not least, the new game mode axis invader is great, but i cant help but feel that they missed the mark a little. You play as a axis sniper hunting the allied one, a bit like enemy at the gates, but as the axis sniper you can't really interact much with the AI. If you see the sniper you cant call for the AI. I feel like they should have set it up in a way where you are more of a commander rather than a counter sniper, doing your best to shoot the sniper personally. I imagine its very frustrating getting shot down and restarting everytime someone joins your game. Controlling the AI soldiers or ordering them around would add more replayability and truly make every mission different and more replayable.

The fact that axis invader forces you to run around and punishes slow investigation or camping for either player further supports my idea that this isnt really a sniper game and more of a stealth game with the sniper elite brand slapped onto it.

I never give reviews of games early until and unless there is something drastically wrong with the game. This is one of those scenarios :(

Rebellion, what have you done to my favourite game? :(

Before I begin...

ABOUT ME: I started sniper elite with SE4. I have more than 4000 hours in that game with all 85 achievements.

WHO IS THIS REVIEW FOR: Hardcore Snipers who love SE4, the kind of campaigns it offers, The bullet drop and wind you get to play the different modes in. If you are a newbie, this review is not for you. Also, this review will not talk about bugs. Every game has bugs, so my review is not based on bugs this game has.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------
-  OVERALL REVIEW
-------------------------------------------------------------------------

If you are from a country where you can get the deluxe edition for say 20 (USD/EUR) then go ahead and buy it! But if it is going to cost you 60-80(USD/EUR) then trust me it is not worth it. You will not be happy. I would recommend waiting for the sale and then buy it.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------
- CAMPAIGN
-------------------------------------------------------------------------

I finished the campaign in Authentic mode very easily (Mind you with NO MANUAL SAVES!). It took me more than a month to do that in SE4. The authentic mode is a joke as compared to SE4. The AI is outright stupid. You can actually run from the front and stand behind them and they end up confused. Reminds me of the cadet mode in SE4.

Pros: 
1. The graphics is really good. Environmental photogrammetry has been put to good use I must say. Good job on this Rebellion.
2. Option to set Axis Invasion. Really loved this!
3. Achievement doesn’t port to other modes.

Cons: 
1. Authentic mode is a joke!
2. AI in Authentic mode behaves like AI of Hardcore mode of SE4
3. Weak story line
4. Unlike SE4, you have very less guns and Explosives. No S-Mines or Trips Mines.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------
- MULTIPLAYER
-------------------------------------------------------------------------

Pros:
1. Ability to start your own games. With the absence of dedicated servers at least you can create your game and turn of the scope glint and aim assist which is by default ON is all servers :(
2. The introduction of accolades. I liked it! It is there in SE4 as well but here it is IN YOUR FACE, if I may say so.
3. Achievement doesn’t port to other modes.
4. Tagging a person now takes more time.

Cons:
1. I am horrified that there are only 2 No Cross Maps. SE4 has more NC maps and we got bored of them pretty soon. If no more maps are introduced for NC then seasoned NC players will very soon abandon this and go back to SE4.
2. Only 5 TDM maps.
3. Is it my imagination or there are fewer hiding spots in SE5 MP? And perhaps this is the reason why everyone is just running and gunning. Very few Sniping. Maybe because of Scope Glint, and revealing the last position of the sniper? People who run and gun will love this I guess but pro snipers will not
4. Need more maps! I got bored in 2 days.
5. Dot Shots, shoulder shooting and spinning still work as it did in SE4 which is really really sad and can cause lot of accusations.
6. Introduced a new focus mode. Users can press Left Alt to find the exact enemy position for about 16 meters. This is so wrong. Might as well allow hacks and cheats. There should be an ability to turn this off.
7. You cannot see the game settings when you join. Only the admin can see it. So, you have to join and that inquire if for example scope glint is on or not!
8. There is lot of stealing of kills. We should be able to switch off Incapacitation. When dedicated servers come, there will be lot of banning if stealing of kills is not stopped.
 
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
- AXIS INVASION
-------------------------------------------------------------------------

A brilliant addition to SE5. I simply love it. Already completed 100 invasions! The only thing I have heard people complaining in discussion forums is that you can get kicked from there. I have personally not experienced it yet.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------
- SURVIVAL

review_text:
I am giving a thumbs down due to steam's dichotomous review system as usual. Otherwise, most certainly, I do have mixed feelings about the game.

SE5 is more of the same, more of the veeery same in fact. It's quite similar to its predecessor SE4 but at the sametime Rebellion somehow managed to take some missteps and downgraded some portion of the game while trying to improve it.

I am not the biggest fan of these huge open areas. Some say the best open world is a closed world and meanwhile I agree with that and think SE5 is somewhat a closed world and is not mind-blowingly huge, in a game where you only can traverse the map with your ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ feet, running around like crazy, it is exhausting. I thought why I found SE4 more bearable and found out the fact meanwhile it had open areas the map design was more concentrated, had more urban and in-door areas, and had also more verticality. In SE5 there are a ♥♥♥♥ ton of rural areas where you simply run around the map until you squash your lungs to death. It is not a huge problem as the map is still quite limited but again, I want to remind you the only way to travel is to run and there are many enemies placed on the map. Luckily AI is pretty much broken also you can be more rambo than a sniper and just run&gun through your way. However, was that supposed to be how things go? I get some people may like the feel of planning their way across a map and try to take different approaches to a target. Well, that's what Dishonored does. Leaves you in a closed world and wants you to eliminate your enemy in whichever way. However, in a game like Dishonored, the map design and enemy placement are very concentrated. Even in MGSV (although you can ride a horse obv.) the open world didn't feel much of an issue compared to SE5. It's just not about map design but also mission design and overall core mechanics contribute to this feeling of exhaustion.

First, mission designs are still incredibly primitive after 5 damn games. You go from A to B and kill some enemies on the way, complete the mission and exfiltrate. I know you could simplify any game just like this but not every game would fit in this model this well. Side objectives are often repetitive and I get that but main missions are just numb. In both scenic presentation and storytelling (the game tries to what you do with the story ofc but blowing things up and harming Nazi operations feels very trivial at this point) and as in gameplay mechanics. You get intel here and there and they rarely affect my game. You, most of the time, need to find either a key or a satchel charge to break your way in. And meanwhile for most of the time satchel charges are nearby and you don't even need a key to accomplish your mission sometimes you just miss it and after cleaning the whole map from damn nazis you just start to run around looking for a charge or a key. Sometimes those keys are on corpses. Well, developers might expect some of us to take our time, search every corpse, look at every corner of the map, and so on. But for me, damn, that is fkn boring. 

So, gunplay is fine and the game could be fun in many ways, I'll acknowledge that. But can anyone explicitly tell me how the SE franchise evolved over the past years? From V2 to 3 and from 3 to 4 there were changes and meanwhile, I felt that most of them were slight they were meaningful and there were more radical ones too. After 5 years of absence, they return with this only to take a step forward and a huge leap forward. At this point, even the bullet-time gimmick is not satisfactory enough. I do not know what the game needs and most certainly that should not be the player's problem but I can't help feeling Rebellion needs to go in a Dishonored/Deathloop route and create a game based on targets. You have a set of targets, you need to acquire intel to know their whereabouts and just eliminate them & exfiltrate. If done right, it could be more intriguing than this. This is just a personal opinion anyway but I want to do things that matter. Except for the DLC and the final mission of the game you just don't eliminate high-profile targets and only ♥♥♥♥ with the troops. Furthermore, the 8th mission is what I wanted from this game. A closed world that was more vertical, tense also visually stunning.

Besides all that they also removed crouch running and that made things worse. Also, you are no longer to carry enemies' arsenal with you as you can only take the ammo off the gun (with a perk) or just use them until you run out of the available ammo. Making enemy weapons disposable is a hard choice to understand. What was the motivation behind that?  I just know it did not have a huge impact on my experience but I felt like it was quite unnecessary, especially when you need to carry a panzerkraft or anti-tank pb but you need to drop them because you don't want to waste them on regular troops but at the same time you need to use your own gun. Try to imagine how frustrating that could be, to do that every time.

About checkpoints, they can be irritating. I figured out there was a fast save & load but have not used it. I savescum in almost every game which presents me this option. But since I was not looking for a perfect playthrough or I was not trophy hunting on PSN or sth, I refused to use it. And, the checkpoints which are given by the game are terrible. It literally created checkpoints where it spawned us in right front of the enemies, under a crossfire. I and my friend had a mental breakdown there. I had 3 saves in a mission where all 3 of them were ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up and this happened just because I have not taken any save file on my initiative. I do not remember this happening in SE4 and I have completed it on Sniper Elite difficulty. We were playing down on Sniper Elite difficulty this time too until I had to lower it to Cadet and be bulletsponge enough to run to the exfiltration point. This experience alone made me feel sick of the game ngl. But it is also true I could have utilized manual save files. It's just hard to understand how can a game create save files this badly? There were times it did not give a checkpoint although we have completed an objective and there were times it did although it did not before and it was almost like the game pitied us. There may be a technical aspect of it and I would not be surprised. But it's their job to figure it out. Please just f5 and create your own save files, save yourself from this pain. Also figured out that although you can lower the difficulty then increase it back just before exfiltration and the mission acknowledges you have completed it on that difficulty. I have not tried it on authentic though but if you are able to do that, you have a free achievement. If not, then why this is such a thing for the other difficulties? Not that it matters as there are no achievements for them, but why?

I believe there still might be tons of things to discuss regarding the overall messy nature of the game. Whether it be design wise, story, core gameplay, or technical parts, SE5 is a letdown across many areas and I am not even delving into the bugs. I have found some but none of them were gamebreaking, fortunately. I also gotta applaud the art direction in this game while technically it's not the strongest game visually, its art direction is unique to each map with strong lightning and color range, better than ever before. Looks glorious with HDR on. Animations could have been better tho.

As closing arguments, long story short, SE5 could be fun but it is messy, buggy, and although competent still very limited. Rebellion made just another SE very similar to their old catalog. It should have been on an AA level, it's getting hard to justify unpolished games to promote as insta-buys where the market is flooded with great games.  Play it on game pass and pray for it to come to PSN Premium. Or obv. wait for a sale

ps: Axis invasions are cool and all but too damn frequent. I turned it off eventually.

68/100

Invading/being invaded are some of the absolute best experiences this game has to offer.  The process for playing this way is seamless with load times being incredibly fast.  Being the invader seems to be significantly more fun than being invaded simply because you can kind of cheese the player you invaded by sitting near where objectives are and killing them before they even see you.  Survival mode is fun with friends (AS LONG AS THERE ARE NO GAME ENDING BUGS).  Multiplayer is okay, the only mode that is any fun is no-cross which is essentially just long range TDM.  Overall the game is a solid 6.5 close to a 7.  If there were significantly less GAME BREAKING bugs and glitches the game could easily be an 8/10 however until those are fixed it is around a 6.5.  

Verdict:  The game is semi-fun by yourself, way more fun with a friend.  If you like to shoot people in the head with the cool bullet cam then get the game but if you're looking for rich story with replay-ability, this game is not it and you should look for something else.

review_text:
I really wish there was a "Meh" button on Steam for games like this, because while I think there is enjoyment to be had with Sniper Elite 5, I don't feel like this game lives up to its own name.

I bought this game on a whim without really doing any research, which is rare for me, but I've played a handful of hours of Sniper Elite V2, so I sort of felt like I knew what I'd be getting here: an open-world stealthy romp with baddies to shoot from a long distance with my long gun. And I guess that is... technically correct here? But after making it to the third level, things just feel wrong.

For starters, maneuverability is all over the place in this game. One of the main selling points on the store page is the "advanced traversal system", which seems to refer to taking a page from games like Assassin's Creed or Hitman and giving you ledges and vines to climb all around. It works fine enough on the clearly marked pieces of level made for those mechanics. But then you encounter a small pile of stones on the ground, and your character can't quite seem to figure out how to deal with it. Getting stuck, whether due to bad geometry or invisible walls, is a major issue in this game from my experience. This happened SO MUCH during the first level, and really left a sour taste in my mouth early on. When you are trying to maneuver tightly in between patrolling guards, the last thing you want is to be blocked from proceeding to a spot that appears to be safe.

Speaking of getting stuck, the "open-world design" could use some work. There were so many times while playing the first few levels where I had to stop and ask myself "why can't I just go this way?". Each level so far has been large in scale, but limited as far as where you can actually go. Strict paths are present in ways where they just don't make sense, funneling you more or less to into areas with objectives in them. Pathways lined with indestructible rows of bushes or insurmountable waist-high fencing just feels like they couldn't think of ways to make these large levels feel more interesting. 

Touching more on the levels specifically, for a game called "Sniper Elite 5", the levels don't seem to encourage you to use your sniper rifle all that much! The levels feel utterly devoid of spots to actually post up and snipe from, instead pushing you towards using stealth to directly insert yourself into hostile areas, relying on your SMG, pistol, or hand to hand combat for the entirety of levels. Most combat engagements take place at pretty close range, meaning mechanics like bullet drop or wind don't even come into play. This may change in later levels, but I feel it's important for these concepts to mean something for the entire game. This makes the game feel like its lost its own identity in an attempt to emulate what works for other games, which comes off as very generic.

A few more minor gripes less worthy of full paragraphs:

 - Enemies being master trackers even on lower difficulties, able to perfectly pinpoint your location and mobilize after a single shot
 - The existence of a non-lethal weaponry and techniques which doesn't seem to have a purpose, especially when the game seems to award fewer points for using them
 - Gun customization where your changes don't seem to matter outside of things like magazine size and scope range

I realize I'm probably parroting a lot of the same points people have made over and over already, but I have to say as someone who hasn't played the other games in the series, coming in and being this disappointed might speak to how much a fan could be letdown by the game in its current state.

I can't comment much on the multiplayer as I haven't played it yet, but it seems to be pretty divisive. The PvP invasion mode for the campaign is a pretty sore spot for some people. It sounds cool to me in theory; you have the option to allow other players to invade your campaign as an enemy sniper looking to ruin your day, and you are granted additional XP for playing with this option enabled. Whether you view it as a bonus for playing with it, or a penalty for playing without it boils down to your personal preference, but locking certain progression items behind it is sort of gross in my opinion. 

To sum it all up, Sniper Elite 5 less of a sniper simulator and more of a simple military action sandbox. And that is okay. I just wish it was a bit different is all.

Sniper Elite 5 feels really scuffed. Despite having a lot of legit improvements and QoL changes from Sniper Elite 4, and the gunplay being significantly improved, this game feels like it SHOULD be better than it actually ends up being.


The main issues of note (imo):

- AI absurdly over-perceptive compared to SE4, as well as other general AI issues (Even on normal/medium difficulty they spot you very quickly, even through foliage you can't even see through yourself. AI frequently flipflops from braindead to picking you off across the map like Simo Häyhä).

- Enemies wearing helmets are an annoyance (Funny flak/shrapnel helmets shrugging off high powered rifle rounds like they're made out of titanium. Makes shooting for the head (especially from behind) on most enemies an issue. I don't remember helmets being nearly as much of a problem in SE4).

- Movement feels far more sluggish than previous titles (Animations much slower in general, and too easy to accidentally do the wrong action, particularly with things like dropping down from ledges and climbing vines).

- Confusing map design, and lots of invisible walls (Plenty of areas you have to go the long way around to get into, and barely any shortcuts to connecting areas. Also, lots of fences and railings that you can't vault over, which forces you to go all the way around them).

- Lots of OOB spots in the terrain, and general stuck spots (Such as running too close to a wall and glitching out of bounds accidentally, which more often than not ends up with you perma-stuck and you're forced to reload a save. This ended up happening several times in different levels during my solo AND co-op playthroughs).

- Generally plenty of bugs, especially in co-op mode (Glitched animations, slow LoD fade-in, netcode issues, unkillable enemies, even as far as some softlocks in modes like survival (e.g: 2 tanks becoming unkillable and making finishing the mode impossible)).

- Lackluster ending (even by sniper elite's usual "B-movie" plot standards).

Game is pretty fun however when it's not being buggier than a Bethesda game. If you really want to buy it, I'd recommend waiting until rebellion fixes some of the more significant bugs with the game, or just wait for a sale.

review_text:
It's a fun sniping and stealth-game. My favorite type. You can go Rambo too but it can become deadly (for you) real fast.
I like putting down mines, covering my spots. AI react to their friends blowing up by trying to take an alternative way towards you. If they know where you are. If you play more stealthily and don't trigger fights or AI looking for you, you get to experience more of the story. Some "extra" conversations.

I have no-lifed the game since release. There is replayability. Huge maps, different approaches, different routes to take. Spy Academy and Rubble and Ruin are my 2 favorite maps. Especially Rubble. I love the blown up city where you can shoot from window to window or window to the street. I say window but its basically a hole in the wall or a frame for a window.

I kill like 100+ enemies on every  map. And if you manage to trigger 10-20 enemies, it gets very hectic. You have something like 6 sniper rifles that you can customize. Do you go for range and damage or maybe less zoom but fires fast? I like using both options, depending on the map. You can change your weapon choice midmission if you go to a Workbench. Theres 3 on every map. Except map 9 but that is a short filler to finish the story or something. 1 objective, no collectables or anything. On top of that you have SMGs and Pistols to unlock and customize.

Performance, I feel, is very good. At 1440p I can run all maxed except AA to have a steady breezing locked 75 fps on an Nvidia 2080. GPU isn't fully utilized, just the way I like it, fan stays quiet. Ryzen 5600X, 32 gigs of 3600 Mhz HyperX Ram. The game loads really fast too. I have it installed to a regular slow harddrive but even then, loading into a map takes 15 seconds. Crazy fast.

Bugs, there are a few I can think of. Nothing showstopping to me. From what I have read, Easy Anti-Cheat seems to have issues. I chose not to install it during game installation. I can still play online. But EAC can crash your game or just not load the game at all. Weird issues. The "forever reloading" bug was fixed 2 days after release but a new bug was introduced. Sometimes, when you want to throw a grenade or TNT, you get an arc showing you where it's going to land. Well, that arc can randomly disappear. You see no line. Then there's shooting from cover. Sometimes you press the shooty shooty button and nothing happens. To fix that, you gotta move to the left or right a bit more to be able to shoot. It's quite rare but it happens. Speaking of that, I was using some pistol and it would randomly stop shooting, I click left mouse click but nothing happened, I almost died becaause I was in CQC at the time. I just never use that pistol any more. I can't remember which one it was. I think it only happens with normal ammo. Anyway, I assume these little ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ will get fixed.

I can't wait (well, I will have to) until more maps and weapons are released. 

Great game, great fun. More, gimme more!

review_text:
SE5 is pretty fun. I am glad gun customization has been added to this degree. You've got scopes, stocks, mags, weapon skins and much more. It is a nice touch to give you the edge you prefer. Every time I find a workbench I am excited to see if I unlocked anything. Throw on the new piece and see what it looks like. Although every attachment comes with pros and cons to your weapons overall stats. As it stands, cons feel kind of random. As an example, throw on a cheek pad and reload slows down.. K? But these cons are not ruining my fun by any means. So far the maps are very nice. My only gripe is they come with choke points between major areas. So you have a playground halted by a very narrow road, then it opens again to another location. I wouldn't mind this sometimes, but here, it is too much. SE4 had a more preferable balance with this. Also, I did NOT download the anti-cheat, so I am not playing online. Understand in this game, that means I have chosen to be punished by being rewarded less XP for everything. I just want ppl to understand, this is a real thing, in a single player game. Which I highly disagree with. 

I also have to say, so far it feels sniping has taken a back seat in SNIPER Elite. I guess Rebellion is handing the crown over to Sniper Contracts. Not to be mean, but in Sniper Contracts 2, that game came with the longest shots I've ever taken in a game. Meanwhile, in Sniper Elite, the longest shot has been 180 yards so far. I truly hope there is more to come. 

Frustration aside, as I have had more time with SE5, I actually really like the guerrilla warfare style here. Close or far (if it permits) can be really fun. Granted I shoved every difficulty farthest it can go. No hud, no sniper assist, enemies at max, lose remaining ammo in mag when reloading. I think Rebellion could do something with this. Tighten up both close range fighting with more take downs, tactical reloads and better animations (opening a door while crouched), and this could bloom. Heck. Even the bottles I am on board with. Look, I know it sounds weird to carry 4/5/6 empty glass bottles around in a loose sack when you're trying to be stealthy. However, lets be fair here, constantly having a rock is just as immersion breaking imo. Although no, I didn't use rocks in SE4. Still, I found out real quick you could just spam rocks and get soldiers to, one by one, walk right up to you for a stabby stab in the tall grass. Making close quarter combat trivial if need be. Bottles make sense. Well, not the loose glass that would clank around every half step in real life, but replace it with a finite item. Granted, I think they knew there would be some backlash so you still have your whistle. So calm down there buddy. (Sorry, honestly the rocks truly bothered me. Back to the review).

What brought me over more for my review was the map design. It looks very authentic and pulled me in. The music feels right for the time period and fits perfectly. The guns sound crisp and when he drops the slide on his .45, after loading in a new clip its sounds well oiled. Time was put into this and it shows. I was complaining about this on another game. Why do devs focus hard on one aspect (in this case, long range shooting) and slide on the other (short range)? Why not zero in on both combat styles and allow the player to choose? I understand maybe with time constraints, but outside of that, its a win/win. It seems Rebellion read my mind because this is pretty good. I just hope later levels really open up the long range (which I expect them too) and they didn't just trade one for another. 

All in all, if I find long range in this game with some beautiful shots, I'll be truly happy. As of now though, it is fun and I am enjoying my time. I still have to say, Rebellion, please, stop with the massively expensive DLC and punishing us who just want to play the game solo. I am a very talkative person, I meet people with ease. Game time is my time. This isn't to say invasion isn't a cool idea, it is. But to basically force players to opt in, is pretty egregious imo. 

Hope this scattered review helps!

review_text:
My choice for a new game would have been, in a perfect world, "please can we have MORE Sniper Elite 4 for the single-player campaign?"

Rebellion delivered!  

It's more SE4 but even more gorgeous (except that distracting AA shimmer) and with lots of small enhancements, like 'focus' where, when especially close to enemies, you can press focus to gain a faint outline of where the enemy is on the other side of a wall or barrier.  It's a bit of a cheat and you don't have to use it, but I liken it to assessing where someone is by their footsteps - so yeah, I'm using this!  Other new things include weapons now carrying an indication of hearing range.  If a rifle has a hearing distance of 130m, you need to be at least that far away from the nearest enemy for your gunshots not to not be heard.  Even the trusty Welrod suppressed pistol can be heard within 14m by default, so it's not quite so much of an easy way out in this game!  The game now offers workbenches in the locations where you can upgrade and swap weapons mid-mission (love this).  You can now sabotage vehicles as well as generators to mask sound, though nuisance soldiers will insist on poking at the noise and trying to fix it as in previous games...  There is the polarising addition of non-lethal weaponry and attacks - polarising because why wouldn't you kill off someone wearing a Swastika?  But it adds a new gameplay option, and you get more points for non-lethal combat.  Polarising yes, but you have total freedom to play how you want - and who doesn't want extra choice in a game?!  Finally, you can now also upgrade Karl as well as your weapons - by earning skill points, providing enhancements such as the ability to carry more ammo, or to automatically mark an enemy that takes a shot at you.

The maps are again HUGE with plenty to do and to find (each, when played properly as a stealth operator, taking several hours to complete - easily 7 to 10 hours for me per map).  I'd estimate the title divides game-play into around 60% sniping and 40% close-quarters stealth (or combat - choice is yours).  A lot of reviews are panning it for not enough sniping and there probably is less in this one, but it's also a lot to do with how you play.  Like the previous games, you CAN run-and-gun, but the way you're supposed to play is to scout out some suitable vantage point (if lucky, with sound masking) and pick off enemies at distance.  Unfortunately, the story, map and objectives unwittingly steer players straight into direct routes leading to close quarters combat and that's probably why there are so many complaints about lack of sniping.  Ignore where you're supposed to go next.  Take your time, pick high points, mark enemies through your binoculars, and pick them off at a distance.  

Along with the good is a little bit of bad too.  Karl's impediment for climbing over small walls is back (he really suffered this in SE3 too).  This time, the 'wall' might only be an ankle-high pile of pebbles around a tree and the gap looks easy to traverse, but nope, Karl cannot go there.  He cannot climb low rocks, squeeze through what look like decent gaps in hedges etc.  It's a tad frustrating.  I get why it's been done but I think, in SE4, it was better disguised by blocking off no-access routes visibly with barbed wire, fencing or other obvious barrier.  Another issue is trying to interact with things like opening doors or picking up ammo.  There seems to be some issue where you keep having to spin round and find a perfect position to trigger the interacting prompt and, if you're in a hurry, this is beyond maddening and ideally needs to be fixed.  One thing I DON'T like: if you opt out of playing "Invasion" (yes, players can land right in your game and kill you), you earn less points.  In my opinion, a game mode should be able to entice people to play without gating game rewards behind the feature.  But that said, even without invasion points, you will ultimately find enough points to unlock all upgrades before completing the game.

The AI is a bit hit-and-miss.  Sometimes, creeping up on a foe unseen launches the red COMBAT! alert without you making a sound, and other times, the AI can seem a bit confused and bewildered before shrugging their shoulders at the dead body in front of them and assuming it was nothing.  It's not ALL the time, but it does happen here and there. 

The NPCs are a little bit wooden, but they always are in SE games.  There's a nice mix though.  You'll see complaints about some, like the black woman you first encounter because "unrealistic".  I have NO time for people who whinge about this sort of thing.  It's a fictional game with fictional characters and a whole fictional resistance.  If it was realistic, then Karl would be kicked out from the off given his lack of fitness, huffing and puffing after 10 yards of running and not even able to hop over a short stone wall, so...  I like what Rebellion has done. 
 Why can't Rebellion fictionalise it as much as they want?  I 100% support their decision and welcome it.  I can count the number of games with a black female primary on the fingers of one hand from 40 years of gaming which is shameful, so it's about bloody time!

People are commenting that bullet physics are a bit off.  I only play medium difficulty so wind direction isn't a biggie for me, but it's worth bearing in mind what others are saying.

Final criticism others make is a greatly pared-back selection of weapons.  That's true, but honestly?  All the hundreds of weapons in the previous game were just clutter and most were not used.  The weapons in this game might be fewer, but they vary in a meaningful and interesting way.  I almost feel like I've had MORE choice because the differences are greater (whereas in past games I just shrugged them off and played mostly with the default load-outs).

So, should you buy it?  If you enjoyed SE3 and/or SE4, then an absolute yes.  It is more of the same but with enhancements.  If however you found the earlier games repetitive, you'll be no better off here either.  It IS more of the same and, for that, I'm very, very glad!

I have to adress most of the negative reviews first:
There are many reviews that say that the axis invasion feature is ruining the game. If you turn it off you don't get the bonus XP.

Now that said, the bonus XP don't matter at all because the campaign XP only unlock the skills which you still get enough XP for anyway and are really not necessary. Therefore you can just turn off the axis invasion if you don't like it. The dev's even put the button on the starting page of every mission.

Positives:
Now that I've got that out of my system, the game feels like the culmination of the whole stealth genre in almost every way. They took many elements from MGS, Splinter Cell, etc. and put it on the already solid foundation of the older sniper elite games. Ontop of that they decreased the extreme bullet drop from past games, making it easier to estimate it if you come from a game with more real to life gun physics like Escape from Tarkov or Squad. The difficulty customization is maybe the most important feature that the last games made popular and is now even more detailed.
The art design is beautiful with vibrant colours and really detailed environments and the level design improved tremendously over the last games as well, making each level replayable for at least three times without using the same route.
I haven't encountered a single game disrupting bug.

Negatives:
The only real thing I have to criticize is that the devs removed the ability to sprint while crouched which was my prefered way to go from cover to cover. 

I haven't played much multiplayer so I won't comment on it right now.

To sum it all up, I believe that this is the best game in the series to date.

review_text:
It's fun for one playthrough, but prepare to be frustrated if you want replay value, especially if you want to complete the challenges. To begin with, the game has some poor design decisions. Just off the top of my head: if Fairburne knows he'll need a crowbar and bolt cutters in every mission, why doesn't he just include them in his loadout instead of having to search for them in every level? 

Pressing E to search bodies gets tiresome very quickly, especially because if you have a body and a weapon close together, you can't just walk up close and press E - you have to aim precisely or you might pick up the weapon instead of doing a search. A small irritation, but when you have to do it hundreds of times, it adds up. It would've been a lot better if the keys for searching and picking up weapons were different. It would've been even better if the body-search mechanic was removed entirely and replaced with ammo resupply crates where you could replenish your entire loadout with one keypress. Having to search enemy bodies for ammo and items is one of the more tedious and annoying things one can do in a game. The same applies to searching for workbenches, collectibles, etc. 

There aren't that many opportunities for actual sniping. Most of the time you're better off using a scoped, suppressed pistol.

The night vision scope is just badly done. The effect looks like something from 2000.

Bugs are quite frequent: bodies and weapons fall through the ground and disappear. A tank firing right next to you doesn't create a sound mask. If you're crouched and approach an interactive item on a table, very often you can't interact with it - you have to stand up. The map marker representing your objective is sometimes precise, and sometimes only in the general area of the point of interest (See the submarine pen mission).

Some bugs are much worse and ruin your entire mission: in the Wolf Mountain mission, you're supposed to be able to kill Hitler in a variety of ways. For instance, you can painstakingly make your way to a teahouse, where you can poison his breakfast. In a properly-designed game, this would trigger Hitler's arrival in the teahouse where you could then observe the culmination of your efforts. In this game, you just wait and wait and Hitler doesn't move an inch. 

There just isn't enough innovation: the game feels like a mission pack for Sniper Elite 4. This might be just me, but it's getting tiring playing with the same old WW2 weapons, doing the same old WW2 stuff. It would've been fun to be able to use a wider range of weapons, like mortars, artillery, fictional Nazi weapons (an experimental .50 caliber rifle, for instance.) Either that, or I wish Rebellion would drop the WW2 theme entirely and make a game that's set in the present or maybe even the future. With all the advances in weaponry, there is so much more a game could be.

Finally, the worst thing of all by far: buggy challenges. Completing these challenges is the only way to unlock certain items, but the game often fails to detect when you've completed a challenge. 

Example one: in the Secret Weapons mission, there's a challenge to kill an NPC "with a V2" (you have to drop a wind-tunnel-suspended V2 on him when he walks under it). There is a switch on a gantry above the rocket that drops the rocket. I go there, wait until the scientist shows up, drop the rocket. The game says [i]Challenge failed[/i]. I reload the previous save, drop the V2 on him again. [i]Challenge failed[/i]. I restart the mission, play all the way through to the same spot, drop the rocket on him. [i]Challenge failed[/i]. I switch to a lower difficulty so I can get to the challenge faster, drop the V2 on him again. [i]Challenge failed[/i]. Finally, instead of pressing the button, I try shooting the hooks holding the rocket up. This time, [i]Challenge completed[/i]. So dropping the rocket on him by shooting a support works; doing so by pressing a button doesn't. 

Example two: In the Festung Guernsey mission, there's a challenge to kill an NPC by causing him to fall into wet concrete, when he's leaning on a rickety wooden railing. First attempt: I wait for him to lean on the railing, then shoot the railing. The railing falls off, the NPC stays there, leaning on air. [i]Challenge failed[/i]. The second time, I weaken the railing beforehand by kicking it, then trigger the sequence that causes him to lean on it. This time he falls in, but the game says [i]Challenge failed[/i].

At which point I quit in frustration.

review_text:
[h1]Mediocre game that leaves mixed feelings[/h1]

[u]What I liked very much[/u]

Graphics: In the era of questionable attempts at Global Illumination and fifty thousand image filters, SE5 surprises very pleasantly with needle-sharp textures and well-chosen color palette. It's a gorgeous game, at least when it comes to map and texture work, even at huge distances.

Sure, the characters shown in cutscenes look quite outdated, but that's not really what the game is about and not a big deal. If anything, they could just pre-render the cutscenes to smoothen out the experience a bit.

User interface: Is simple and functional, with tons of tutorials for newcomers and so on. Again, really good.

[u]What felt lackluster[/u]

X-ray vision has now way more organs per enemy soldier. Which makes it somehow worse, because you're not feeling like you're hitting a vital organ, but just a mess of human anatomy. X-ray thing was always something to tip serotonin in player's head, a gamified reward of doing something well, and now it just doesn't work.

Audio feels lackluster, too. First mission had supposedly music, but it was just some sort of weird jungle howling that I tuned down a lot. And I never noticed any music after that, in other missions, even if it was there, it was so dull that it never added anything to experience nor registered in my brain.

Older games had sort of screaming sound effect effect accompanying "X-ray shot", like death coming after enemy. It was very well engineered and added a lot to the feel of taking down an enemy. That, too, is gone now. How could they mess up the most distinctive element of their series, is quite puzzling.

There's a talent/skill tree, but skills feel totally pointless, and do little else than alleviate bad game design decisions that could have been avoided to begin with.

[u]What I don't like at all[/u]

Well, you're not a Sniper anymore. Most missions require you to infiltrate complex, narrow mazes of buildings and interiors, packed to the brim with enemies, while wielding loud, inaccurate firearms and very aggressive AI. It's puzzling, really. And unlike Hitman or Splinter Cell series, there's no gamified reward system of avoiding the enemies and going just after targets, nor even good map design to attempt it, so I really don't get it. Game asks you to collect all sorts of intel, which means - "kill everyone, explore everything". Then makes killing anything quite difficult and messy (poor weapon choice, aggressive, telepathic AI, endless reinforcements). It's just bad game design.

Levels are supposedly open-world, but in reality, feel quite linear, with hedgerows and chest-high bushes forcing you to choose from only 2-3 linear paths at most. It's quite annoying, as is lack of high ground to snipe in a game called 'Sniper Elite'. 

I played for 5 hours, but I still can't figure out breath-holding sniping. There's a diamond over enemy. Then there's a double diamond. Sometimes the bullet kills enemy, sometimes it does not, no matter which diamond you see. What does it all mean and why couldn't that be solved more elegantly?

There's non-lethal options for melee attacks and even... "non-lethal bullets"! I have zero idea what led to such laughable decision in a game where main attraction is seeing a well-placed bullet crush an eyeball or kidney. Feels like yet another half-cooked, "have it to have it" idea. 

Why would you go non-lethal [b]at all?[/b]. In Hitman series, you're hired to kill 1-2 people. Rest are either civilians or security guards or otherwise quite innocent people. In Metal Gear Solid V, you spare soliders to evacuate and turn and hire them to your side. In Splinter Cell or Alpha Protocol, you're a spy/saboteur and evading enemies makes sure that if you learn intel, they won't know you learnt it and change the plan. 
In Sniper Elite, leaving Nazi soldiers alive.... [b]why[/b] exactly? First mission of this game tasks you to sabotage coastal defenses and radar to make landing easier for Allied troops. Why would you leave enemy infantry there? To help Third Reich win???

I'm sure nobody thought about this question while making Sniper Elite. Which tells the tale of this game.

Sniper Elite 5 is quite mediocre and disappointing. I enjoyed previous titles way more.
