review_text:
TLDR: This is a step back from Sniper elite 4, and shows severe signs of being rushed after SE VR's failure. Gone now is the fun sandbox design of sniper elite 4 with huge massive maps that may contain outposts that exist solely to be eye candy and world building, or target practice, instead we now have dark souls invasions. Metal gear solid 2 Non lethal ammo, with the same fatal flaw as metal gear solid 2. And XP nerfs that encourage charging in with a maxed out SMG and rifle with non lethal ammo to get that sweet chunk of XP you used to get for farting in time with an ambient sound. 

The long versions: 

Map design: The maps are HUGE, EASILY some of the biggest of the series that aren't called "San Celini Island" and "Aquaduct". But the problem lies in the fact that every map is so JAM packed with side objectives that if you see a Nazi walking around somewhere you can bet your ass there is an objective there. Alternate paths have been SEVERELY limited based on this fact, likely due to the dark souls invasion mechanic which can be opted out of, (more on that later). 

  You get about 2 alternate paths to each objective which consists of climbing walls that are poorly indicated by white objects such as dead vines, smears of white paint, or French resistance graffiti tags that the Nazis don't seem to give a ♥♥♥♥ are plastered all over the place, or you can just run across the fields and you MIGHT find some broken fence somewhere you can crawl under or a waist high fence that CAN be vaulted over, as opposed to the 30 feet of the exact same fence beside it that you CAN'T vault over. 

Weapon selection (Warning: gun collectors and sniper elite veteran's rant ahead): Remember the Mosin? The gun in almost every sniper elite game since the first game? Rebellion doesn't, or more accurately cut it to package it into a DLC (this was written prior to the DLC all being released If I'm wrong, I'm wrong, but I am willing to bet steam points I'm not). You have a narrow selection of about 4 weapons per category suited to the french theater, kinda. Instead of things like the liberator or M3 grease gun that were air dropped for french resistance fighters prior to Operation overlord (D-day for the non historically inclined) You have an american selection, a German selection, a couple british guns, and a French RSC from 1918. A gun that barely saw production and was, had WWI not been declared, planned to be the first ever Semi-auto rifle. The m1 Garand from sniper elite 3 (and 4's DLC), the king of ping, has been replaced by the M1a1 Carbine. 
    
  The Thompson is obscenely powerful when maxed out and I often found myself, instead of sniping, running around like an idiot with a rapid fire Thompson with a suppressor and a 100 round drum cutting down entire patrols before they can raise an alarm like scenes out of a gangster movie instead of a WWII sniper game (more on why later). 
    
  The 1911a1 also makes a return and honestly, except the welrod from the prior games and the Mark 6 Webley revolver, the pistols all feel no different from each other, so I'm not going to go too in-depth on them, the first example I've cited of a rushed game. 

  The German list isn't really worth going into too much detail in. A Kar98, a G43, a walther P.08 an STG44, and an MP40 that I can think of off the top of my head. All fairly unremarkable and standard for the series at this point. 

  Silencers are more accurate to reality, they are SUPPRESSORS, not SILENCERS. Hollywood silence is only achieveable using ammo that doesn't break the sound barrier, IN conjunction with a suppressor. And even then only on certain calibers. For example the .22 long rifle. Suppressing an m1911 and still using supersonic ammunition still results in the sound being about as loud as a lawnmower.

  Honestly I could, and SHOULD go on, but I'm not getting paid for this and I have limited space that I have somehow managed to hit. 

Weapon unlocks: THANK GOD THE WEAPON CHALLENGES ARE GONE! Oh God, now you have to unlock weapons by beating missions, you can't just pick them up anymore due to how small the weapon pool is. And here we have the second example of a rushed game -- arbitrary limitations that were lifted in the prior game in the series (not including SE VR). The kar98, which is POSSIBLY one of the better guns in the game tied with previous installments variants of the mosin, isn't unlocked until almost the final mission -- assuming you even get the record for completing it which I'll cover later in bugs. 

  In order to unlock upgrades for the weapons you have to go on an easter egg hunt for the weapon workbenches in each level, I'm not sure how to feel about this as I like the idea of having to scavenge the equipment and not having SOE resupply you like in SE4, and it gives incentives to find intel documents and officers with the keys to FIND said workbenches. This illusion however, is then destroyed by you walking within 20 feet of the workbenches location, and it being marked on the map. Then you can either find the key or, since half the map is likely aimbotting your location at that point anyway unless you are carrying non lethal ammo with a silenced weapon, just throw a satchel charge on it and go in. I have mixed feelings on this. But I DO lean towards it being a pro since I had to farm liver shots to max out the mosin in SE4. And the horrid "high heart rate challenge" massacres that consisted of setting the game to cadet, sprinting everywhere and emptying a mag into people's heads.

Story: Let's face it, we are all here to shoot Hitler in the balls, listen to Karl crack one liners (Which he doesn't do very often in this game) and kill Nazis. It's a standard sniper elite story. Nazi has secret project, Karl finds info on it, you go to win the war single-handedly. Moving on.

Bugs: Todd Howard called. The rental of bethesda's QA team is up.
  Where do I START? You go to open a door, hit whatever button you have bound to interact, and Karl stands there admiring the French architecture for about 30 seconds before he opens it. In the meantime some Jerry from the other side of the map has spotted you because apparently EVERY German in 1944 decided that carrots were their ONLY food, called reinforcements from Fallschirmjäger, and now the entire base is emptying bullets into your dome. You get into the door with ONE bar of health, maybe less, pull out your trusty WAY OVERPOWERED maxed out thompson, and it seems Karl has retained EVERY SINGLE EMPTY MAGAZINE EVER AND WILL RELOAD INFINITELY UNTIL YOU CHANGE AMMO TYPES. You change ammo types, Nail the active reload taken from gears of war (A nice addition, by the way) to reload faster, go to a wall that you climbed up before and hurl yourself over the side to escape the swarms of fire coming your way, And because you have to hold space to vault, Karl immediately pulls himself BACK up the ledge, and dies. You reload, fix the reload bug, and just decide to execute everyone before they become a problem, then proceed to admire the door for 30 seconds again. Remember how I said I often ended up just gunning down entire squads with the Thompson? Yeah this is why. I'm sure -- Actually I'm HOPEFUL these bugs will get fixed. Especially the infinite reload as it means that if you get this bug on ANY gun and you are OUT of alternate ammo, the gun is now broken entirely. I've had pistols do it, I've had rifles do it, I usually end up seeing it on the SMG's because they end up being my most used weapon. 
  
I don't know if the AI's eagle eyes are a bug or intentional so I'm putting it here, because ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ these guys can spot you at a range and hit you with irons that would make Simo Häyhä, Francis Pegahmagabow, and Carlos Hathcock, jealous. Forget the war, Hitler should have invested in a trick shooting team to push his ideology.

In summary:
  Since I'm at the character limit: wait for a sale. Use non lethal at all times you can because it gives more XP.

review_text:
Sniper Elite 5 plays really well on my PC.  The scenery is beautiful and the game feels more fluid.  I prefer single-player campaign and have no opinion on the invasion or the multiplayer mode.  Having played this for 4+ hours at the first review time and 24+ hours for the second review, I have overall enjoyed the game's smoothness, graphics, and I like the improvements over the previous installments.  The game feels even more modern, but still retains the original Sniper Elite characteristics, such as x-ray cameras, bullet ballistics, difficulty levels, and traditional stealth or loud options with multiple ways to progress through each mission, which makes this an all too familiar game and genre.  I have not encountered any crashes, frame rate issues, or errors.

Pros:
- Beautiful scenery and graphics
- Massive levels with multiple approach and tactics
- Different ammo types
- Rifle iron sights and first person view for all weapons
- X-ray camera for all weapons

Cons:
- No crouch-and-run mode (this was a great ability in SE 4)
- No Shooting Range to practice with weapons and earn medals
- Too many invisible walls and inaccessible terrain
- No customization for Karl (no different outfits, jackets, etc., which was great in SE 4)
- No AP or tripwire mines
- Limited distraction objects (SE 4 had unlimited rocks, while SE 5 has limited bottles)

Neutral:
- Silenced weapons are not truly silent, but this keeps the game interesting.
- There is not enough weapons to choose from, and weapon modifications do not make up for this.  SE 4 had more rifles, pistols, and SMG's to select from.

Thank you, Rebellion, for delivering such a great game, but some improvements are definitely worth including in SE 5, especially the crouch-and-run option for stealthy approach.  Perhaps, these will arrive in the future updates or DLCs.

review_text:
Far from perfect at launch, but fun enough. Some glitches, fell through the ground once and was left "hanging" on the edge, but couldn't get up - happened to have saved just a few seconds earlier so not too bad.

Haven't yet figured out exactly how to customize the difficulty to my liking, and a few other such small things, but after playing the first 2 missions I can say I had fun.

Worst part so far is that dead bodies, vehicles, etc. just randomly disappear, even undamaged vehicles can randomly despawn when you're standing within 20 meters of them and just looking the other direction. Probably second worst part is that the AI cheats. Bushes etc. regularly obscure your visibility, but some enemy is busy shooting you through 7 trees and 15 large bushes as if they were not there.

There's other things that are less than perfect, rocks have been replaced with glass bottles, but nobody seems to ever hear them, even at pretty short distances. The only time I had someone react to one was when it accidentally hit their head.

The weapon customization seems nice, but I can't seem to be able to actually switch weapons .. I can pick up a panzerfaust, but if I want to put it on my back, it's just dropped on the ground instead (and the one time I tried that it fell through the ground into the void).

Maps seem reasonably large, but random areas are blocked off for no good reason, and the slightest incline on the side of a ditch is blocking you from climbing up and instead you can only slide down.

This game is so good in many ways, but also so terribly buggy and clearly rushed.. I kill literally everyone in the map, but it counts people I tagged with the binoculars anyway as "spared". Similarly I can tag the same person over and over again and get "ribbons" for "tagging 20 enemies". Probably because tags don't actually do anything on the difficulty I'm using.

There's the xray kill camera, which now has some speed controls .. they seem to do nothing.

There's regularly cases where I sneak behind an enemy that is crouching digging through trashes or something, and so I can't stealth kill them, the action option just isn't given to me, and then when I bump into them, they get up, stand in front of me, point a gun at me, and I just gotta wait keep tapping E hoping that at some point the stupid buggy thing will let me kill them before they can shoot me .. this goes on for multiple seconds.

The item highlighting is also incredibly flawed, it used to work great in SE4, but it's constantly refusing to highlight items for me to act on, or is constantly selecting the wrong thing. Particularly bad in a box that has like 5 items in it, trying to select the one thing you can pick up and want to is sometimes near impossible.

If you accidentally step too close to some hole, the character may decide to start hanging off the ledge, and then refuses to climb back up. There's hidden back entrances where e.g. you open a grate to go through, but due to bugs you can't always actually fit all the way through and so can't use them.

Doors require an action to open, which takes control away from you, and you can't close them.

Actions regularly animate poorly, and sometimes due to the animation glitching you just can't perform them - searching bodies in certain positions is impossible, throwing TNT doesn't always show the arc, and when you release the button he just tosses it in his feet, etc.

Still fun, but in its current state very flawed. Don't buy until the devs clean up their act and fix it - considering the amount of bugs I keep running into, it's months away from being really enjoyable.

One REALLY big minus - it attempts to force an unwanted multiplayer invasion system on you, and for that system, it attempts to force one of those rootkit DRM piece of trash cancerware things on you. It seems you can avoid this by checking the settings BEFORE launching the game, but it's far from obvious.

UPDATE: 1.5 years later, the game still has most of the same issues, there's a few less issues with clipping through the world or being blocked from a few areas you should be able to crawl through, that's it. All the other bugs and issues mentioned above are still valid. I keep regularly bumping into new bugs that have been reported long ago that the devs have completely ignored. Very disappointing behavior from the devs.

YET ANOTHER UPDATE: I **just** realized that the game has Denuvo and not just anti-cheat, I thought you could skip Denuvo in the launcher but that's for Easy Anti-Cheat. Sorry, can't support you anymore Rebellion, you guys suck.

review_text:
My thoughts after 90 hours or so:

The Good:
Distances have greatly improved over SE 4 and so have the bullet physics, no longer do you need to zero a normal rifle for 50m to hit someone, meaning you get to shoot at longer distances now, although it is still very much dependent on the map design for performance reasons.

Gear overall has seen an upgrade. with pistol and smgs being capable of holding their own, combined with the gun customization you can actually make quite diverse loadouts (especially if you got the dlc). A big bonus is that the customisations also work on authentic which wasn't a thing prior, basically completely removing that element of the game on higher difficulties. I think the devs found a good middle ground where optical zoom and silencer capability is limited on authentic now (still makes the game incredibly easy on anything below that imo)

The new secondary objectives, kill list and workshops incentivise exploration and I enjoy them.

Maps are varied and overall fun.

The new invasion mode is a good addition overall and I hope for it to return with some tweaks.

The Questionable:
Some of the weapon upgrades and cosmetics are very jank and questionable, we got magazines inserted the wrong way, rifle silencers on pistols, extended mags for welrods and blue electrical tape as grip tape that lets you aim better.

The maps are riddled with invisible walls making traversal intuitive and frustrating sometimes.

The addition of "non lethal" ammo and mines (?!?) for every gun was not needed and it leaves a bad taste in my mouth that we now have non lethal weapons in a game about killing Nazis. Furthermore the game doesn't do anything with it, you can't interrogate them, there is no optional mission to kidnap an officer or something. It just is in there because modern stealth games need to have this cause of MGS.

The Bad:
Authentic Plus is gone. The highest difficulty in this game is authentic and it is too easy and lacks features from authentic plus in SE 4. Most notably it lacks the perpetual search enemies would start if they got made aware of you, this made the game more immersive because enemies didn't just forget you sprayed their friends brain other them 2 minutes ago and if you weren't careful you could easily have the entire base look for you. It added a lot of variety to the game and it's just gone. 

Most special enemies are gone. Older entries would have enemies calling in support like mortars to flush you out of position even if they don't know exactly where you are. Shooting officers would also delay enemy response and have them act less aggressive. This is gone, apart from snipers there are no meaningful enemies, this makes the game less dynamic and easier on all difficulties.

The range adjust doubles as a rangefinder even on authentic, letting you line up both the range marker and the wind marker essentially giving you aim assist even on authentic (because the wind marker is now 1 to 1 where the bullet will go), this makes authentic easier than it should be (especially since all the weapons got stronger too). This also goes for all the other difficulty modes ( I think they even added a new easy difficulty) making them all easier than they used to be and adding more and more help like a sort of xray mode, aim assist even on sniper elite difficulty etc.
I am not saying we should remove the easy mode but please give us back the actually immersive authentic plus mode with the search feature from SE 4, combined withe SE 5s better ballistics that would make for a great combo.

Also the invasion mode lacks a difficulty filter meaning you get put into a random game. I don't want to play with aim assist and xray mode and I am sure people who do don't want to paly without them, please let us pick a difficulty here.

Overall I want to say that is is my favorite SE but all the stuff missing from SE 4 and 3 makes this hard, I still like the new ballistics and being able to make various loadouts, but with the lack of enemy variety and the removal of the search mode it just doesn't feel as dynamic and fun anymore. I want a sniper game not a passable stealth game with aim assist snipers.

There are a lot of mid stealth games out there, there are barely any good sniping games.

review_text:
[i](Disclaimer, i've played the game for 13 hours, no clue why Steam says 0.2 hours)[/i]

I love the Sniper Elite series, but they certainly messed up this time around.

For starters, the game plays like a generic action-stealth MGS V  clone, instead of a Sniper Elite game. 

99% of all combat takes played within 50 meters, making rifles pretty useless compared to a pistol. The maps are also lacking in verticality, which is bizarre for a sniping game.
Also, in the past you could take a shot on Hard difficulty and the enemy would only be alerted. Take a few shots, and they would pinpoint your location. Only on Authentic difficulty would the enemy immediattely pinpoint your position and run towards you en masse. In Sniper Elite 5, now a single shot will immediately alert the enemy of your exact position, making sniper kills only viable from a few pre-orchastrated locations (the ones with a soundmasking generator). 

This means that apart from a few pre-orchastrated locations, you’ll be using the silenced pistol for the entire game.

They’ve also removed S-mines and Trip Mines from the game, to “streamline” the experience for new plyers. In previous Sniper Elites, you could cover your sniping location by laying those mines in doorways/stairs/etc and could make some really awesome traps that way.

Now the opportunity of trap laying is gone since you only have 2 teller mines at your disposal. What makes this even worse is that they’ve convoluted the game with all kinds of new ammo types, all of them having no de-facto advantage over the normal and subsonic ammo. They’ve also added the Shu-mine, a non-lethal mine.

However, playing non-lethal has no advantage whatsoever, since the total XP you get from that playstyle is always lower than playing lethal. 

You can also no longer replace your weapons with enemy weapons. Enemy weapons now function as disposable items; You can finish off the magazine and than they’ll disappear, Use your own weapon or item and the character will drop the enemy weapon. 

What makes matters worse is that there are a ton or rifles, smg’s and pistols in the game, but the player has only a handful of them in the load-out screen! Why create so many types of rifles, smg’s and pistols if the player can’t use them? 

The new weapon customization sounds great in theory, but the difference in stats are so little that it basically has zero use. 

What makes it worse is that they’ve removed all the different reticles you could select in previous SE games. Why would you do that? Why would you remove the Sniper out of Sniper Elite, and replace it with generic MGS/CoD stuff?

Also, the new X-ray vision looks graphically great, but all the added veins and muscles make it impossible to discern the organs and bones from it, so the X-ray vision is less conveying in damage and gore than the X-ray vision in Sniper Elite 3 and 4.

There is also an issue with enemy bodies disappearing. To unlock a new weapon, you must kill a high-ranking officer in a specific way. My tactic of preference is to pacify the officer and kill all other enemies in the area so the killing of the officer by explosion/falling objects/etc makes no sound.

However, bodies disappear very quickly after pacifying or killing them, so that officer you pacified is disappeared by the time you come back to him. You can also no longer wait to loot the body of an enemy, since the body will disappear ASAP.

What is strange is that this was an issue in Sniper Elite 3 as well, and fixed in Sniper Elite 4. Why did they revert back to a known game problem?


[b]Conclusion[/b]
If you love generic action games, buy this game for a few bucks after all the DLC’s have come out.

If you love Sniper Elite, stay clear of this entry.

This is Sniper Elite 4 but in France. The game side-actions have been " re-balanced " with some items being removed, new items added, weapon customisation, workbenches being divided into 3 different types ( which then gives you even more incentive to check out all the massive/beautiful maps ), and Not every vehicle can be explosion exploited by shooting the gas tank ( fair enough ).

Weapons now emit " noise ", yes, even when silence ( realism huh ), but you can reduce the sound distance with various types of mod's depending on what you want.


Overall, I give it a 3/10 ( still a bit buggy, but its a brand new game ), but players expecting a " new Sniper Elite " game shouldnt have their hopes up, as there isnt much " new " about it, even the graphics ( I am running 3070 RTX )

- Traversal is terrible. Less buildings to climb even though you can see the pipes, map templates such as cutting fences sometimes dont have the trigger or take several attempts to activate the animation, a fair few open farm field maps where your forced down road choke-points with nowhere to hide even though you can see a stone fence that you should be able to jump over, hedge templates in one map will work in one area but wont work in another area even though you can physically walk around the hedge and go to the place you were looking at 30 seconds ago.... to sum this comment up, Map beautiful, traversal garbage.

It's super janky, glitchy, and a downgrade from SE4 in every regard. Last time the graphics was warm and vivid, now they make my eyes bleed. Mechanically, they are trying so hard to copy the recent successful stealth titles that it's not even funny. The game now has convenient boxes to stuff your enemies in. I suppose the next one will feature disguises as well. Oh, and Rebellion are being greedy as usual and are cutting their game into chunks before selling it once again. It's the second time in the row they're throwing Early Access at us under the guise of a complete product. Refunding.

Upd: I rebought on sale and finished it. Long story short - my opinion holds.

The reason it holds is because this one doesn't know what it wants to be. Plagued with the modern devs' disease of chasing the widest audience, it tries to be Sniper Elite and Hitman trilogy at the same time. Yet without the experience or understanding of IOI, all Rebellion could do are massive, bloated (yet somehow still linear) landscapes, clearing each is gonna take hours. The maps feel like checklists - destroy AA guns, radar towers (hello Ubisoft), assassinate some targets the game doesn't care to introduce enough to make you care about. Rinse and repeat. Even though 8 levels might not sound like much, this leads to the game massively overstaying its welcome. 

A supposed star of the show here is the weapon upgrades system, which looks intriguing at a glance, but ends up being whatever. That's because all the choice the game seemingly offers gets invalidated by the design decisions behind it. Shockingly for a game called Sniper Elite, there's almost nowhere to snipe as most of the action takes place in tight corridors. So the best way to mod the sniper rifle is to take off the scope. Ammo is rare, which I wouldn't mind if all the mods that seemingly promote the spray&pray playstyle did not exist. Attaching a bayonet to a shotgun and using it like a spear is fun... what's not fun is every enemy having a fixed health pool, leading to absurd situations where said shotgun needs 2 shots point-blank for the most enemies in the second half of the game. Indeed, once you realize the magic number of 130 damage needed to one-shot most enemies, the entire arsenal gets forever split into weapons what can be modded to achieve that, and those that can't. 

Some 5 years ago I went out of my way to praise Sniper Elite 4 for how combat feels. Officers commanding their men, radiomen calling reinforcements if they are alerted... Different enemy types was a big part of that game, and 5 unfortunately does not live up to that. Officers are still there but don't really impact things anymore. Radiomen don't exist at all. I think I encountered 1 spotter in the entire game, and never had artillery called on me. And Jagers are just bullet sponges. Occassionally the game tried to spice things up by throwing in an armored car or a tank, which are hard countered by moving around them faster than the turret... eh.

My Sniper Elite V5 Experience. A story for the ages.

I am going to be refunding this game as I was willing to give it a chance, but as most of the reviews here have stated, the traversal in this game takes me back to the Playstation 2 days. Im honestly quite shocked on how much of a step back they have taken compared to Sniper elite 4 in terms of blocking certain paths. This made it "difficult" for both myself and my co op partner. The first mission right off the bat has me in tears of laughter however. Upon us exiting a SUBMARINE with our allied friends onboard, one of them shouts something on the lines of "Dont get us killed by getting alerted". It couldnt have been 15 minutes later, that a German artillery gun fires a single projectile onto the SUBMARINE and killing the entire crew. My friend just goes "you guys were in a submarine, why the **** didnt you go underwater.

After that PTSD causing event, the main objective now requests us to enter a base to blow up some huge electrical dish  (I dont even care at this point for proper terminology of that thing) but instead, we decided to do optional missions. Out of the 8 "destroy aa guns" that I believe there was, we only blew up 3 because the game did not give us enough satchel charges (and we did explore to try to find some). So after making the easy decision to not let this game waste anymore of our time, we decided to push forward. We kept to the left side of the map, this time, heading straight for the main objective. Before reaching the main objective, we navigated ourselves through a labyrinth of evil bushes that blocked easily openable areas not considered by the devs. We attempted to climb the treacherous "10 degree incline of doomed dirt" that Karl is somehow unable to climb (I suppose we forgot to equip the climbing gear before starting the mission).I myself got stuck on the "infinite reloading" animation on my rifle. And finally, we were forced to open our maps numerous times to see our current location and strategize  a game plan to overcome the evil dirt and bushes.

So we did this, and after navigating for 10 minutes, we finally made it to the main objective. Or so we had thought. As we stood there, on the main road, both my friend and I looked at eachother in a state of disbelief. Presented before us was this massive steel door that casted its gaze menacingly. It was so massive that we knew something fishy lurked in the air............and fishy it was.

 It had 2 of the same symbols painted onto it. "No entry".

My heart sank. The journey that led us here was all for nothing. I thought about my non existent wife, kids, brothers, and most importantly, my love for my country. I decided to walk further down the road to see if there was a hidden path, but it was to no avail. We were now back to square one. We busted out the map and devised a plan to take the main road. I told my partner "This life as a sniper isnt for me anymore, screw the stealth approach". He nodded as we pushed forward. Every enemy that entered our line of sight, we layed waste to.  The evil bushes and dirt tried to come for us again, but I was determined to complete the mission. In the midst of me trying to complete it, I decided that after I escape this horribly designed map, I was going to shoot myself in the foot so that I could go back home. 

So now, here we are. Ending right on back to where we first were before doing the side missions. I said to my partner "I wont make the same mistake twice; well take the right side". He agreed. After partially letting out our frustration along the way, we finally arrived. We immediately opened fire,  killing everyone in sight like we decided not long ago. We realistically disabled the dish with a crowbar, then we destroyed the circuit breaker (with our bare hands). As we nagivated  to the end of the location, we saw it. The menacing steel door. I was on the other side now, how could this be a "no entry"?!?! I shouted. Then I heard it say to us quietly. "No entry".  Just as I was about to take my own life, my partner spotted a hidden bunker beside it. We investigated, and came to the conclusion that this indeed would take us to the other side where we first met the steel door. We entered the rabbit hole, and after about 40sec of jogging through the concrete jungle, we reached the other side. Once we exited the bunker, we indeed were on the side we thought was a dead end. I stopped and put my hand on his shoulder. I looked at him in the eye and said "how the hell were we supposed to know we had to go even further down the road to the right to see this?". "It makes no sense" I further added. 

It didnt matter in the end, nothing did. After busting out the map the 3rd time, we finally made it to the rendezvous point, only to be greeted by some angry french woman that had no reason to be angry. After speaking to her, I shot myself in the foot and I am now talking to HQ. They say my refund is being processed.

After 20+ hours:

With the exception of some lagging grenade throwing, melee, and killcam jankiness, the game feels really slick. The gunplay is incredibly tight. It rewards practice and makes you feel like John Wick vs. the nazis. There is a lack of equipment at the moment, but missions and weapons will clearly be added.

Overall, the game is good and will only get better. I will now list my gripes, which define the game for me at the current time.

Removal of trip mines, crouch-running, stuff like that: You suck, Rebellion.

When it comes to difficulty: Authentic mode is kind of a joke. Missions in SE4 are very tough on authentic+ mode. It takes real planning and nerves of steel to beat them. For a combination of many reasons which are tough to fully articulate, anything below authentic in SE5 is a cakewalk. I would say that overall this is a negative.

Level design: My biggest gripe with this iteration. Invisible walls are my least favorite thing about this game. The stupid 3-foot-tall objects and fences that should be easily vaulted and invisible walls are extremely immersion-breaking. Being constantly funneled through chokepoints is awful. The levels appear open but feel much more linear than SE4. It is a shame, because they are absolutely gorgeous. 

The Target: Fuhrer mission feels like a jumbled mess with only a few approaches compared to the gargantuan sub base of SE4. Gives us missions like Deathstorm: Infiltration or the SE4 Target: Fuhrer, please. Whoever console-ized the level design needs to be fired and blacklisted from working in game design ever again. You are part of the problem with modern games.

Multiplayer: No hardcore mode. I don't want to play with magic scope glint and hud markers and stuff like that. I know we can do custom lobbies, but it would be real nice if there was a decent preset for more serious players. And, you released with only 4 maps? - come on now! 

Weapon customization: wow, you can install a little leather decoration to your rifle that will make your aim worse for some weird reason! The customization system needs work, but there is greatness here somewhere.

Otherwise, I pretty much love the game. Fix, please.

SE5 could have been just SE4 (which was superb) with new maps, but Rebellion have continued to evolve the series, and Karl's latest adventure is highly enjoyable so far.  

Other reviewers have held up bottles replacing rocks as a problem; I think it's an excellent change.  A thrown rock never did strike me as something a German would react to; it's a neutral sound, and would blend in with the ambient sounds of nature.  Breaking glass is the complete opposite; it's guaranteed to attract attention, and the fact that your supply of bottles is limited forces you to choose your moment carefully rather than just hide somewhere and throw endless stones until one of them has the desired effect.

Weapon customisation at the workbenches is great.  Tough choices have to be made, as most of them penalise you in one area to improve another, but you're now able to choose how you want your guns modded to suit your play style.  If you're run-and-gun, choosing lighter weight at the expense of accuracy or range, or the patient assassin camping out for the perfect shot, going for the ultimate long range kill at the expense of a heavier gun and less mobility.

review_text:
Ultimately, I will have to leave a positive review for SE5 because while it has a LOT of glaring issues at launch, I'm sure most will be fixed over time through things like patches or content packs. There's definitely a lot more polish to be brought to the game. Now with that out of the way:

Bugs:
There seems to be a good chunk full of bugs in my playthrough so far. Karl getting stuck on slight geometry on paths that are clearly meant to be walked through. Being caught on an infinite slide animation because of one stray rock. Enemy bodies completely disappearing when I take them down in tall grass. Animation locks when hugged up on cover. Enemies just not registering the fact that you're right in front of them sometimes. It's a good handful but that being said, I do expect these to be addressed later on and as of right now, none of them feel super game-breaking.

Gameplay:
SE5's big new appeal is having this new hitman-inspired approach to the missions, basically taking SE4's maps and then making them a bit bigger and a lot more open-ended for player agency. It actually works out a lot and makes it feel a lot more fun planning approaches or having a completely different approach to go with the next playthrough. It really does encourage replays of missions and that'll help SE5 in the long run. The new weapon customization is also extremely rewarding and fun to tweak BUT it's completely stunted by two things, a complete lack of weapons to experiment with (there's 15 weapons total, 5 per category) and no shooting range to test out your new build like you could in SE4. Hell, I realized there weren't even any shotguns in the game and that sucked because I LOVED the M30 drilling. Also, they got rid of S-mines and Trip mines and only brought back the Teller mine, we got the Schu mine but that's just a non-lethal mine. Rocks were replaced with bottles (now a limited amount) and added the decoy which is eh. I hope a lot of this is addressed over time but I'm skeptical, though the gameplay is still fun.

Setting:
I think this is SE5's saving grace, the authenticity of WWII is so prevalent here and I absolutely love it. I liked Italy in SE4 but it felt weird for a WWII setting. You are experiencing everything from a German war factory, to the Atlantic Beachhead of Normandy, the Occupied Austrian Alps, to the French Countryside akin to Operation Market Garden, all militarized by the German occupation of the area and it was just so completely atmospheric. The German's have proper loadouts for their time and I found that extremely impressive because it's the entire standard issue equipment for your basic Wehrmacht soldier on the western fronts. Your Jaegars and Vampr Soldiers actually look authentic this time around vs SE4's style of just a basic get uniform. I personally found that to be an extreme nod to historic authenticity. 

Conclusion:
The game is pretty good as is but there's definitely a lot more polish and a lot more content that needs to be added to further reinforces the game's gameplay systems.

Almost.)
- Then there's the elephant in the room - invasion mode. To be fair here, I am in no way protesting its existence, and I wish anyone excited by it a jolly good time - but to have singleplayer PvE unlockables gated to not only participation, but performance in a PvP mode, that's gonna be a hard yikes from me. Insult to injury that turning it off results in a penalty to all xp earned.
- Along with reloading enemy weapons, our protag has also forgotten how to pick up rocks from the ground for easy throwing, and must now rely entirely on whatever glass bottles he can find along the way.
- (As a trade-off, he appears to have learned to harness his latent psychic abilities in order to sense enemies through walls. YMMW on this one)
- Your mileage may also vary on the gun customization feature. While it's not COD-levels of bad, it's certainly taking some historical liberties - and every single attachment available somehow make some aspect of the gun worse, a design decision I personally loathe.
- Traversing is great, until it ain't. When it works, traversal feels... very decent. But there's a lot of times where there are no visual cues and even less logic to what you can and can't climb, and at least the first map is plagued by knee-high impassable obstacles, invisible walls, and long stretches of ditches, vegetation or fencing that any normal human should be able to traverse with ease, but our protag inexplicably cannot.
- Finally, there's a lot of things that, while not outright bad, also just aren't as good as they were before. Tagged enemies don't show up as they used to, making visibility sometimes an issue. Empty lung looks and feels just a little worse than before (in part because it now has a wind-up time of sorts, making repeat shots less fluid). The kill-cams, while now available from just about any weapon (which is great) just look... jankier, somehow - which is kindof impressive, to be honest.

All in all - it's hard not to come across as someone with a vendetta writing this, but I feel it is an accurate representation of the game in it's current state. It's not that the game is not fun, and I definitely plan on putting more hours in it - but I've already paid for it, and I'd be lying if I said I wasn't disappointed. I feel overall let down with some of the choices made by the design team. I'm sure a lot of this will change and improve with patches and DLC, but in its current state, I really cannot think of a reason to recommend anyone buy this over Sniper Elite 4.

review_text:
There are two big problems with this game, and it isn’t the invasions nor the freaking traversal mechanics; it’s the obtuse way that the game has to present its mechanics and systems, one, and the other, is the absolute horrid progression and unlocking systems in this title.

The way you unlock attachments and weapons in this game is by progressing through the game and finding workbenches in the levels corresponding for each of the three types of weapons you can carry (rifle, assault rifle, pistol). The guns are varied and the attachments are detailed and change your weapons significantly, not only in how they worked but also on how they look. The issue?

The best attachments and weapons can only be obtained after the halfway mark of the game, literally the most silent silencers and rifles, the more damaging machineguns, and the best attachments for your pistols, can only be obtained after the third mission or so. This missions also last around two hours long or so by the way… What does this mean?

It means that the players will get a really bad first impressions from this game, and most people won’t make it into the 6 hours or so it takes for the game to supply actually good equipment that you can use to experiment with the game systems and mechanics and… It’s a shame.

It’s a shame because I persisted after the third mission despite wanting to quit the game, partly out of curiosity, partly out of desire of wanting the game to become better, and it eventually did; I loved Sniper Elite 4, now I think this has taken the throne as the best one in the series, even surpassing its predecessor.

Just know it takes a while till you can actually sneak around and stuff. The game also makes a poor job at emphasizing how important the new bullet types you can use are, subsonic ammo is essential in stealth approaches because it literally makes it so your gun is virtually silent, you can shoot an enemy from 20m away and they won’t hear you, armour piercing ammo by comparison makes it so you can take out vehicles in just a few shots, assuming you’re targeting their vulnerable parts, which you can see after you mark them either with your binoculars or weapons… This last thing is never explained… Might be common sense to some but, the last couple of games never had this mechanic, all you had to do if you wanted to destroy a vehicle was to shoot at its vulnerable sections once with simple, regular, ammo.

So, yeah… This is going to be yet again another underrated game from Rebellion and in a way, it’s entirely their fault. I don’t agree with the complaints about the invasion mode because you can turn it off, the same as you can choose to not install easy-anti cheat (thank God for whoever in the dev team suggested this). I also don’t agree with the traversal being worse here because it’s not a matter of the mechanics being worse is a matter about the game not explaining them enough, not in tutorial sections, not in its design, you can still drop from high ledges and Karl (protagonist) will hold on to ledges below him breaking his fall in the process, you can also jump from one ledge to the next, climb through vines, etc. The issue is with how these systems and mechanics are delivered, not in the mechanics and systems themselves.

It’s a shame, because if you persist with it, it truly becomes a fantastic game, but I’m nearing the end of the game, sixth mission or so, and only 17% players have reached it to begin with…

Ok, so this time we're in France, and not a single bread is found to be edible, that's not very lore accurate of you.

The Nut Cracking Elite 5, definitely another go-to Sniper Elite to pick up if you love huge area for long-distance sniping shot, and exploration for additional missions, which, they all can yield additional exp and a little more for one to do in each mission, which is really great feature they still carrying over since Sniper Elite 4.

Now, the goods, they finally let us pick up guns with "ACTUAL" ammo inside, like 8 to 15 rifle rounds and 20 to 30 smg rounds, rather than, picking up a random dead enemy weapon, and it's only just 5 to 12 bullets to be found in the chamber, while you only pick up 3 to 6 rifle rounds and 10 SMG rounds from corpses in previous games.

Invasion! Can be enabled or disabled for one's campaign run, however, I suggest you turn it on, or at least, do it with your friends to have a friendly competition. Invading-player will be spawned as a Sniper, which can interact with fellow on-site German troops to get them into better positions, whether to ambush Allied players or directly engage them, in short, spice things up for additional fun value for campaign.

I wish they do that for Survival in the future, that'd be fantastic ngl. 

What's even better, the picked up weapons are expendable, modified, and even experimental, meaning, you will be preserving your ammo for equipped guns entirely, and even better, you can use them to your advantage depend on maps. Also, these expendable guns, their bullets can be then added to your ammo pool.

Improved enemies, and their equipment, yes, seriously now, you may need to be careful when shooting enemies into their helmets, and even berets, as they may deflect the shot, which can get you into trouble at times.

On higher difficulties, any squad of German infantries will know if they have a squad member gone missing, so plan your execution even more carefully, as they'll get alerted and look for the missing member.

Also, they'll become more tactical when you're spotted, not only they'll spread out, they'll attempt to flank you when chances are given.

However, worry not, because we also get additional bullet types for even SMG and Pistol this time aside from Rifles, and here I put it simple as possible.

FMJ: Default bullets for all guns, can't be discarded.
Armor Piercing: Good at penetrating helmets, and tanks in the rear.
Non-lethal: Just simply knock your opponent out, and the guys are not really dead, so be wary.
Sub-Sonic: Basically the "Silence bullets" from Sniper Elite 4, however, not entirely quiet this time, also less penetration against helmets.
Softpoint: More velocity, but still, weak against helmets, quite good if you wish to take out enemies from afar.
Match: More velocity and damage, but also louder when fired, good against targets from afar as well.


Now, the cons, I must say, I really hate to say this, but the cons are not only the take down methods but also the gun modifications.

There are stealth kill and pacify as silent take down against opponents, however, pacify is really unnecessary as the better way would be simply just stab your opponents to death, I'm not even sure how much exp per each pacified enemy is given, but imo, it's just not worth it.

I assume people feels bad of stabbing people or cracking these Germans in the nuts, but, come on, this is war, what do you expect?

Gun modification in Sniper Elite 5, IS TERRIBLE, utterly unnecessarily TERRIBLE...

Wait, what and why? Increase dmg, less recoil, and more zoom-in from scopes are good, isn't it? Yes, I hear you, but the problem is, almost every upgrade has downsides, making it really at times, you best just stick with the default gun instead, because what you gain is so pointless that downside are just making your weapons terrible despite with the positive stats you get.

And seriously? Please remove silencers from modifications, and make it only available on guns you can pick up on the map instead, this just makes the guns in Sniper Elite 5 MORE CHEESY than Sniper Elite 4 already, with every gun's noise range down to less than 40 meters, with sub sonic bullets or non-lethal one, the noise range is even further decreased, which can just make the game effectively a cake walk.

At times, they also don't make any sense, seriously, why would pasting some ribbons or tapes on my Werlod make me move faster while pulling it out slower? Or, somehow has stronger recoil despite I have extended magazine that supposedly adding weight to reduce the recoil?

However, I am actually having fun, so these cons really don't bother me much, along with some glitches I legit cracked up so hard that makes me love the game as much as I do for Sniper Elite 4.

The game is definitely worth picking up if you enjoying sniping them Germans in the head

Or nuts :)

If you like Sniper Elite games you will like this. It does what you expect if you are familiar with the titles. The gameplay fundamentals are the same, with some improved graphics, some new mechanics, and a new invasion mode (that you can turn off). Don't expect anything groundbreaking just a solid game done well and has great performance minus a few bugs they will patch. The co-op campaign is probably the best working one in the series, and the new invasion mode works pretty well, but I can see it being plagued by people abusing this system for XP or hiding in areas you can only get to with a ladder/etc.

A lot of people are coming here expecting assassins creed traversal, AAA studio graphics, along with other unreasonable expectations. This studio is not massive with the funding of a AAA title like battlefield, but that being said it doesn't look bad at all, even one of the worst aspects graphically being some animations or player models aren't bad at all. People have way higher standards for this game than others for some very strange reason... I think the game looks fine it has never bothered me, if anything I'm enjoying the performance.

Some of the worst aspects of this game in my opinion revolves around the traversal and map systems. It is like an open map of connecting linear ones and it gives the illusion of an open world type map but the climbing, vaulting, and pathways are heavily restricted which is super annoying to me. I can also tell that they kept out some content because they want to add season pass weapons/dlc. Also I would be surprised if the multiplayer lasts at all if you are coming here for that, although most people don't. I think because this game is sort of a niche, diehard fans are getting butthurt at any changes whatsoever but at the same time they are complaining there aren't enough. 

My advice is if you like Sniper Elite games buy it, if you aren't sure try it for under 2 hours and refund it if you don't, it doesn't take long to get right into the action.

The only thing I prefer over SE4 is the fact that you can now ADS in first person as well. Invasion mode was also a cool addition but that's about it.

Honestly, just play SE4, no need to have this leave a bad taste in your mouth.

Despite what I see on here I think this game is way more engaging in everyway and I believe a lot of that comes down to the level designs which I feel are a mountain above the last game which I thought was boring. The story isnt any better but thats not why I come here.

There are certain aspects of levels where traversal could definitely be improved but overall the maps have fantastic landmarks and aren't just filled with a butt load of vantage points to make things super easy.

The objectives have commonalities but there is enough variety amongst the levels that it keeps it engaging and different with each map. Speaking of objectives some of the "explosive" ones are a bit of a letdown which ties me into destruction. Other than the vehicles exploding there really isnt much of it at all, would have been nice to have some reactive descruction of the environment.

The invasion mode is fantastic and I really don't know why people are upset about it. EARNING EXPERIENCE IS NOT HARD. So don't give it a negative review because it gives you less XP when you play the game with it turned off... it really does not matter. I know there are weapon attachements that require you to kill players in invasion and well sometimes if you want something, you gotta earn it.

Now speaking more about invasion its done pretty damn well, where it lacks it seems is in the community. The game will save from the moment an invasion starts so if YOU are the one getting invaded and you die? dont sweat it. Just load back into the save before it happened. Finished the invasion and you won? either continue on or you can load the save before it happened THE CHOICE IS YOURS. This means you wont get punished for playing the fun invasion game mode in terms of your progression, if anything it makes it more challenging, more exciting and furthermore gives you an actual challenging sniper battle. BUT like I said, the attitude towards this is the problem. People kicking other people out of games because they want invasion on for the XP but DONT want to actually play it or people getting themselves killed either by AI or suicide on purpose to end it ASAP is seriously just ruining the experience and players doing this should be punished to stop ruining the PVP for everyone else.  The anti camping mechanic is a nice idea but it can also be a bit of a pain when it thinks your camping whislt you're literally in the middle of a firefight with the other sniper forcing you to have to move whilst under fire. 

!!!!!!!!!!!!BUT HERE IS THE BEST BIT!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
If you DONT like PVP or you feel like you're not very good at it, or the game. YOU CAN DO INVASIONS WITH A FRIEND (or random) simply load into co-op and if you get invaded... well guess what pal!?!? ITS TWO AGAINST ONE. I think its a great idea because it allows those not wanting much PVP to get the help of a friend who either likes it or feels the same about it to have a fair fight against someone who literally just wants to PVP the hell out of the game.

Overall I think this is the best SE I have played and it really saddens me that the reviews are saying how bad it is. I really just dont see it. Deffs worth the price IMO and I hope you enjoy it too!

End Of Game Life Review (Dec 2024)

***Bear in mind, this review is a result of my owning, and playing, this game since it's release. Of course I have over 2K hours game play. I STILL DO NOT RECOMMEND THIS GAME.

This game is alright for single-player. Nothing special. Decent sized maps, albeit, nothing that screams "Awesome". NPCs have been dumbed-down in comparison to SE 4 (and even SE 3) NPCs. Ballistics have been simplified somewhat as well.

Biggest downside is the inability to freely replace your weapons by picking up dropped weapons from NPCs. You can pick theirs up, but it is a limited use item, then it's right back to your gear. Hence, don't expect to be able to tote an MG42 or Panzerfaust as a secondary while you play. Flare-guns are no longer treated as equipment. They, too, are an item meant to be used, not carried to where they are useful. You will find yourself constantly toting useful flares, panzerfausts, and MGs a few feet, dropping them, picking them up again, and repeating just to get them to where you want to use them.

A lot of the old SE 4 game mechanics never were incorporated into this game, or were half-assedly added in so they failed to function properly. Best examples of this would be the lack of ability to jog while crouched (perhaps the most used feature of SE 4), and the lack of an ability to toggle-aim via a hotkey (either you set toggle aim on, and your regular aim key has to be pressed to aim, and then again to go back, or you get used to holding the aim button all the time, and ignore the toggle-aim setting).

While the weapons sandbox is pretty big once you include all the upgrades each weapon can have (especially with DLC packs), only a handful of the customizations are worth use in both MP and SP modes, or even at all.

Customization of your weapons is nonsense, too. Suppressors might cut sound, but unlike their IRL counterparts, they DO NOT reduce recoil, making your weapon more controllable. In fact, they do the opposite. Additionally, a component that on one rifle makes it equip/aim faster will on another rifle have the opposite effect. Needless to say, anyone who spends enough time playing with the sandbox of weapons and their component upgrades will find the whole of it generally counter-intuitive.

Add to this the fact that some weapons/upgrades have a massive advantage in MP, in the most ridiculous of ways, and your MP experience is guaranteed to agitate most players. Example: Sten Mk II submachine gun can kill at 200 or even 300 meteres, on full auto, with little need to actually adjust your aim. Bayonets can drag the user through walls to kill other players. The list goes on...

MULTIPLAYER IS RIDDLED WITH CHEATERS, AND NEITHER EAC NOR REBELLION WILL ADRESS THE ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ISSUE!!! This is the game killer. There are entire, known cheater clans (such as the 2 NOV clan, and the DcS clan) against which MULTIPLE REPORTS, INCLUDING IMAGES, AND RECORDED VIDEO HAVE BEEN SUBMITTED BY MULTIPLE PLAYERS. What was the result, you ask? Nothing. No bans. Neither by their individual platforms, nor by Rebellions servers. There are few to no repercussions for people who cheat/hack in SE 5. If you play this game for the multiplayer, you will get pissed and quit more often than not. Especially since many players are UNWILLING TO VOTE TO KICK THE KNOWN CHEATERS.

Rebellion was visited by the "Good-idea Fairy." They thought a Peer-to-peer MP experience was a great idea. Spoiler alert: IT ABSOLUTELY SUCKS. Connections drop all the freaking time. Oh yeah....forget browsing the active games to find the lobbies you want. It's all randomized, unless you goto a separate MP submenu (Custom Games). This means you WILL get stuck in numerous lobbies with cheaters you can't get rid of.

Unless you intend to devote significant time on this game, and most of that time on Campaign mode, this will NOT be the game for you. Unless you are OK with playing with cheaters and hackers, this game IS NOT for you. DO NOT WASTE YOUR MONEY UNLESS YOU REALLY ENJOY THE SNIPER ELITE FRANCHISE.

They somehow managed to take a great game and gimp it into what looks and plays like a poor console port.

They added a white outline around objects like doors and dead bodies, and to your character when your moving through brush, that looks ridiculous and is distracting as hell.  They added an almost forced PvP 'invasion" mode that lets other players camp in your single-player mode, and they gimped the xp ratio if you turn the mode off to block other players . . . seriously?!

First off, the special pistol that was supposed to be included in pre-orders is nowhere to be found, and the developers haven't addressed it despite hundreds of posted complaints about it . . .

Then the other issues, most from ignoring the "if it ain't broke, don't fix it" approach . . . 

No more trip-wire or pop-up mines, rocks for throwing are gone, lots of odd terrain issues trying to move over/around objects and landscape, but hey, the anti-aliasing still sucks as bad as a game from 20 years ago, nice job . . . not enough time in the 2-hour refund window to discover all the issues, but these are enough.  Why remove great features, replace them with sub-par, unwanted items, and make it look like a bad console port?

SE 4 was the best in the series so far, and I had great expectations for this one, but it falls WAY short of what I was hoping for . . . refunded, maybe I'll try it again in a year or 2 when it goes on sale . . .

review_text:
Completed all the objectives in the first level. So far, the game is undeniably fun, I just wish there was more freedom when exploring the map. It appears "open" however the developers made it so that you can only choose between a few predetermined paths. This does not bother me that much, as the core gameplay experience is exciting and addictive. Hopefully in later levels the map becomes more open.

UPDATE:

This is my first SE game. Over the last few days a lot of my free time has been spent playing this game. Simply put, it is fun! There's a good mix of realism and arcade-y elements which makes it so that it's always a breeze to pick up and play for short or long periods of time. 

I have to add how well optimised this game is. My rig is about 8 years old and it runs between 60-70fps on medium settings.

The MP is surprisingly good. It is slow paced, which I prefer. You can attempt to "run-and-gun" however that'll usually end up with a you dying swiftly. Careful positioning and environmental awareness is rewarded handsomely. I have yet to finish the SP campaign because potshotting players is just so much fun honestly. Even just assuming the recon role with your binoculars and marking players is satisfying as you see your team pick off the targets you've marked. The only thing lacking is map selection. Hopefully they'll add more in future updates. I also appreciate how you can host and join custom games with custom rules. 

Currently, I'm on mission 4 in the campaign and I can happily say that the first mission is the most linear. As I progressed the levels seemed to open up more. There are numerous ways to reach and complete your objective. I'll get back to the campaign eventually, once I've had my fill of MP for a while!

Please don't let the negative reviews dissuade you from buying this game. It is well worth your time.

UPDATE 2:

Finished the game on hard and currently playing through on authentic. (mostly co-op with invasions enabled.) Feels like I'm playing a different game to a lot of naysayers. I have encountered a few bugs however some of the points made about the AI being broken I simply have not encountered. They do not see me through terrain and respond according to my visibility (terrain and shadows) and stance. Can't get enough of this game! Invasions are intense and honestly a game changer. I can see many franchises such as Hitman or Splinter Cell including this mode in future iterations.

The game is fine, but that's not what this review is about.

The new 'invasion' mechanic is implemented horribly.  I don't know who worked on it, but it suddenly expects you to play like you're in some battle royale arena instead of Sniper Elite.  I was invaded in the first level, died because I tried to be aggressive, and was immediately invaded again, so I decided to find a defensible location and watch my angles of approach (y'know, like a sniper, in my sniping game) but was immediately penalised for 'camping' by having my location revealed.

It wouldn't be so bad if there was some incentive to approach each other over time, but with open maps the size of some small countries, no time limit, and no regular hints about where the other guy is hiding (unless you use telephones, which can be booby-trapped), dealing with a single invader can take upwards of ten minutes.  And this, in turn, wouldn't be such a big deal either, if you didn't get XP docked for playing with invasions disabled.

If Rebellion is so proud of this new "feature" that they'll punish you for opting out, you'd think they'd have made sure to iron out the kinks first.  I'll review this game properly if they find some way to make the invasions fun, or stop punishing people who opt out, because right now, they're a stain on the whole experience.

Unfortunately a 6.5/10 for me at the moment. Core elements remain the same as in previous iterations, but new mechanics are implemented very poorly and detract from the overall experience. Most notably, the developers added vertical movement (a la Assassin's Creed), but--unlike in AC--while you can climb *some* surfaces such as vines, you can't even walk up the bank of a road or hop over a small pile of rocks. This leads to extremely awkward gameplay where you are never sure whether you can climb over something or not (usually not), and have to try first to find out.

The aforementioned problem also means that the large open map, another new feature, is actually not large at all. For example, there are some roads that you simply cannot walk off of because you are somehow unable to ascend a 15 degree incline, despite being able to climb the side of a house. Compounding this problem are barriers that have absolutely no reason to be barriers, such as slightly-dense foliage and low walls. Why can I climb over medium walls but not low walls?

The worst is when you find out you can actually climb something, such as as a side of a house--only to realize that it leads to a dead end (i.e. you cannot top out) and your only option is to climb back down. Remove the ambiguity, please.

The redeeming quality is that, once you get past the fence that could only be cut in one place but not another, and actually get sniping, it's the same old goodness as before.

So day 1 i gave this game a drunken negative review, then i removed it thinking i was being drunk and having unfair expectations of a game ive literally waited years for. Ive put about 30 hours into game so far, on Sniper elite 4 between two systems i have over 1500 hours, and sniper elite 3 i have probably 1000. This game feels like a downgrade to sniper elite 3.5, and not an upgrade to 5. There are some new mechanics, and obviously alot of work went into the map design and such. But there are many elements of this game that frustrate me as a fan of the series. 

1, it has always been a complaint that the AI is either retarded or terminators, and this installment is no exception.

2, bugs, still after weeks of being out has bugs, like hardcore immersion ruining bugs. Infinite reload animation preventing you from shooting, landmines blowing up after successfully disarming them, being seen and shot through walls, nazi steps on your landmine and suddenly the entire map knows exactly which bush youve been hiding in for 5 minutes. Like I dont get it, wasnt those sort of things iron'd out in testing and could you patch it in some kind of quick manner? And the graphics, man, already seem like a downgrade from 4 but textures flicker and strobe out at the worst of times.

3, shots to the face not killing. Like, nazis face is the only thing visable above a brick wall, no helmet, 30 meters, full powered ammo, rifle shot directly to the face, nazi doubles back, just looks surprised, and returns fire. SE#4 was bad for this as well. 

4, no 500m zero? like was that oversite or did somebody go, naw theyll never shoot around 500 meters, lets go from a 400m zero to 600m, so nazi shows up at 527 meters and I gotta kentucky wind the hell out of it because a proper adjustment isnt there. I dont play with the diamond that tells you where to shoot, defeats the point of having to make adjustments in the first place.

5, this game dropped without content that was Pre-ordered and I understood to be released with the game. its not a big thing but a disappointment none the less to see all the hype and buildup and realize its just not there.

6, Clunky movement. The main thing that this game reminds me of SE#3 with is the movement. Its, blocky, fake, exaggerated, and its a game mind you, so forgive some of that, until the movement is what causes you to be spotted constantly, like try to climb over a wall when you have like 5 seconds of time to sneak past a patrol, and hold the space bar just a millisecond too long, well now you are flipping yourself over and over on the wall side to side like a madman, and suddenly you start getting shot. Why does steam *still* not have a "neutral" review score? Its 2022 and valve can still not understand that people have opinions that differ from "good" or "bad"

Anyway, so far it's been a mixed bag. I'm liking the customisation and the more personalised game experience with custom difficulty and all, but the game itself is pretty lacklustre. As of the completion of mission 2 a few things stand out to me the most.

-The AI

The AI is either aimbotting and hits every shot it takes the moment you step out of cover (snipers especially) or cannot see you when you're crouching literally at it's knees. There is barely any in between and it almost ruined the experience for me at times.

-The map design

The maps feel almost claustrophobic, especially mission 1, where you can't move through or hide in incredibly thin bushes and are railroaded to running often 40+ meters around hedgerows and stupid walls that you for some reason cannot vault, coupled with weird terrain that you can relatively easily get stuck on. I'm hoping since I've only completed mission 1 and 2 that this is just an issue in those examples.

-The visuals

The game kinda looks like ♥♥♥♥. The textures and lighting are all *fine* but the anti-aliasing implementation really genuinely hurts my eyes at times. That bundled with the fact that it runs at just over 100fps (ultra, 1440p) on my 3070ti and lacks *any* DLSS implementation at all is grating, although considering the job they did with AA it might be a good thing after all that they didn't implement DLSS. FSR 1.0 is there, though. For some reason.

-The bugs

I know it's day 1 but.. come on. The x-ray camera doesn't really work right a lot of the time, enemies just ignore shots at some angles (an infantryman i encountered was manning an mg42 and shrugged off 12 headshots in the first mission) and killing some enemies breaks others pathing. It's kinda sad that this is the state of almost every newly released game these days, but i trust these issues will be ironed out over the next couple patches.

-On the other hand, the good

I still like the game so far and despite the issues i have with it, i'm having fun. that being said, i cannot particularly recommend the game in its current state due to the aforementioned issues, especially at the price point they are presenting. The classic SE gameplay loop is still as good as ever (it wouldn't have survived like 7 games if it wasn't) and the new customisation options are pretty cool, but the game has pretty big issues, most of which I'm hoping get patched in the near future, but some I'm more worried about being permanent dampers on the overall experience.

Finished the campaign, updating the review. Yes, indeed, this is a good one. Sniper Elite as a series finally finished its growing pains and developed into a remarkably nice stealth action game. One that I might just put on the level with other pillars of the genre.

First of all, this game is finally a proper sandbox. The levels are vast and complex, to the points of being a bit confusing on your first run. There are multiple entrance and exit positions, and enemies are semi-randomized, which makes replaying them still feel fresh. And you will want to replay them, because there are collectibles, additional objectives and lots of other stuff you will probably miss on your first run. Especially since a lot of objectives can be completed in different ways — for example, you can climb up to the radar and set charges, which you will later detonate with a precise shot, or you can fight your way into the bunker underneath and overload the generator. 

The enemies are smarter than they used to be, they now flank you and organize proper search parties. You can still setup maneater bushes and serial killer corners, but be prepared that while you are having your fun, you are probably getting pincered by the other squad. Mobility is key in Sniper Elite 5, especially since there are very few truly silent ways to kill an enemy — even the best silencer in the game is only rated for 8+ meters.

All of this creates a very addictive type of gameplay where planning really pays off and you need to think through both your approach, execution and escape from each encounter. Especially if you are going for the challenges — some of which are really ridiculous in the best possible way. 

But it isn't all about sneaking — sniping is still the name of the game (literally). It can be as complex or simple as you want it to be, but I highly recommend you to set its difficulty at least to Hard. Having gravity and wind pull at your shots makes sniper duels a lot more satisfying. And there are some shots in this game that are truly rewarding to nail.

As for the rest — Sniper Elite 5 is pretty par for the course. It probably won't blow you away with its graphics, story, music or characters. All this is perfectly servicable but overall par for the course. But it has amazing gameplay and that is by far the most important part.

Download SnakeBite. Get yourself that mod that let's you wear a skull prosthetic mask, and the Cyborg skin for the MSF sneak suit. Roleplay as a cyborg assassin. Be a villain and build Outer Heaven. Maybe Kojima really believes the game is as it should be, but this game should've been about being a super villain. 

You should not use the tranq pistol. The game should've made stunning and sleeping enemies more difficult, given the tranq pistol more limitations. You should have every reason to murder your enemies, the demon that you are. Use only limited stun/sleep grenades to kidnap soldiers to build your private army. Everybody else dies silently or in a blaze of gunfire (your choice, "Venom" Snake). 

You even look like Eggman when you pilot D-Walker. That's what this game should've been like; an open world littered with "Eggman Moments". You are literally playing as a NES era super villain.

The gameplay is really tight and the story, which is OK but not exactly stellar, doesn't get in the way *too* much like it does in 4. If you are into it for the story, it is structured almost as if it is some kind of ARG. You piece things together with casette tapes, and the cutscenes don't reveal, like, anything. The twist, which is frankly the gamer equivalent to the Empire Strikes Back twist these days in terms of how hidden it is, is pretty cool but it should've had more of an effect on your in game avatar. Rather than a dumb, surface level character creator, you should've had a "Snake editor" where you edit Snake's appearance in ways that make sense for a 9 year older Snake. Eyepatch optional, scars are editable, hair color can be changed to reflect age. Stuff like that.

The online elements show some really interesting potential. You build the new Motherbase and compete against other Motherbases, foreshadowing the coming war economy of the later games. I never played MGO, but it looks like generic deathmatch stuff. Not my thing. The "Journey/Death Stranding" like multiplayer should have been MGO's whole thing, and with concentrated attention being given to it, I honestly think that the system could've been something really special. Frankly, as it stands, it is pretty cool and a little addicting. But it is little more that "number go up".

As it stands, this game is fantastic, but the story it tries to tell is caught up in trying to portray Snake as a legendary mercenary while also somehow turning him into a villain. Give us more villain gameplay. Let me be the supervillain "Big Boss" is in the MSX games. 

Check it out and kill a bunch of dudes. Have discretion when it comes to the men you enlist for your Outer Heaven. Create your own scenario where you imply that Venom Snake is the first Cyborg Ninja. And don't become addicted to silencers or tranq guns.

review_text:
It is difficult to recommend a game that is unfinished, pretentious, and poorly written.
This was the first Metal Gear game I played (it came with my GPU back in 2015), and I certainly don't *dislike* the game, but I find it much harder to enjoy after having played the rest of the series. MGSV's entire conceit is silly! Characters and concepts are sloppily retconned into older stories, the new characters don't have any impact beyond this game's very loose plot, and the game's themes are conveyed in such a haphazard way that I'm not sure the average player picks up on *any* of them. To top it off, the plot doesn't even have an ending! At least, not one that you can find in-game. It was never finished! We only know about it because an unfinished version of the non-existent last mission's cutscenes was included as a blu-ray featurette on PS4.

And that's not even all I have to complain about!!! What about the fact that Quiet is a blatant sex object that was passed off as serious storytelling? What about all the wacky Metal Gear ♥♥♥♥ that's nowhere to be found here?? The constant shallow references to previous games?

The stealth gameplay is refined, sure, but the level design is extremely repetitive and the gameplay *variety* is pretty poor. It's rare you're doing something other than regular stealth through functionally identical open world enemy camps. Lots of tools at your disposable are basically worthless, like camouflage, which confers such a tiny bonus to the player that they may as well just not use it at all and stick with the sneaking suit (which silences all of their footsteps while crouching!).

I want to be clear, again, that I don't dislike this game. I just think it's one of the weakest entries in this series, and by a pretty wide margin. Mechanically it's a great foundation for a game, but structurally and plotwise it's a huge mess.
