4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie

Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

review_text:
To say that this game is "unfinished" is a misnomer. It's less that the game is unfinished, and more that the game had a lot of cut story content and a rough development cycle. Which pretty much every finished game has. There is no such thing as a game development cycle that goes perfectly smoothly. Kojima himself has said that the game is finished. HOWEVER, that doesn't mean the story ends any less abruptly. The game is divided into two chapters, and each one feels like it ends with an obvious fakeout ending. At the end of Chapter 1, you know the game isn't actually over. At the end of Chapter 2, you can't believe the game is actually over. 

The gameplay is first-in-class for the MGS series, going back to the stealth sandbox nature of 3, except even more expanded, with a massive open world for you to experiment with to your heart's content. However, I can't really give it extra points for that, because the stealth isn't at all mandatory. The game has the best stealth gameplay of the entire series, but suiting up in several metric tons of kevlar and riding around in a miniaturized Metal Gear with a minigun that never needs to reload isn't just a viable strategy, it is the best and most straightforward strategy. And when this franchise's iconic tagline has always been "TACTICAL ESPIONAGE ACTION" then I feel like disproportionately rewarding you for going monkey brain mode and just whipping out a gat is worth docking points for. 

I can't recommend this game, but only just barely. If you're a fan of the MGS series, this is an easy purchase. But also the game is seven years old now, so if you ARE a fan of the MGS series, you likely already own it.

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/38888018-United-Critics/] Please follow [b]United Critics[/b] for quality reviews[/url]

[h1]Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain Review[/h1]

[h2] Questions you might have if you're interested in playing it[/h2]
[list]
[*][b]What is it exactly that you do in the game?[/b]

MGSV is a game about war where you spend most of your time infiltrating enemy bases and exploring the huge but empty open world. Like most games from Hideo Kojima there is a huge pool of mechanics for you to discover and master.

It's a game about freedom of choice. MGSV gives you all the tools to achieve your objectives in the way that you find more fun for you: If you like to kill everything that moves, the game allows you to do it, if you want to be a stealthy ghost that leaves without a trace, the game allows that too.

So you can play it as stealth or as an action game if you are good enough.

[*][b] Will it make my eyes bleed?[/b]

MGSV even today looks stunning. Some models may look a little bit dated for modern standards but it’s a game that looks amazing and clean. I particularly love the forest levels in the later parts of the game and the weapons models are amazing!


If you don’t like ugly games, I don’t think you will have many problems enjoying it. It truly still holds.

[*][b]Does it have a good story?[/b]

This may be the most controversial part of this review, the enjoyment that you draw from the story of this game depends on how deep is your knowledge of the Metal Gear lore and how sensible you are to crazy and convoluted plots. As someone that loves crazy and weird stuff and has played most of the Metal Gear games I think it’s OK, a bit lacking since you can feel how the drama between Kojima and Konami hurt the endgame, but enjoyable.

This is the kind of game that you play for its gameplay and you can mostly ignore the story. Again, it is not bad, just weird and convoluted.

[*][b]Does it have a good soundtrack?[/b]

Yes! Sometimes it enhances the game and makes it feel like a spy movie. I particularly liked the licensed, one of the best games with 80’s songs ever. I tracks love [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MWCoDpwvWo0] this song [/url] 		


Most of the time it does what it’s supposed to do. But when the soundtrack slaps, it truly slaps.

[*][b]Does it have replay value?[/b]

Yes! You have so many optional objectives, collectables and cool stuff to find and collect that you can spend hundreds of hours in this game and never get bored, that is if you liked the basic gameplay loop of infiltrating enemy bases. And you can replay all of the missions with new gear, companions and spawns anytime, is truly amazing!

[*][b]Does it run well?[/b]

This one of the most optimized games that I ever had! I haven’t encountered a single crash, bug, stutter or freeze in the 200 hours that I spent playing this game. And it runs fine in relatively low end hardware. I have no complaints about this game on this topic.

[*][b]Is it fun?[/b]

Hell frickin yes! From a purely gameplay point of view, this game is flawless. With the amount of creativity that you can use to solve most of the problems that it presents, it’s a testament of how flexible the game design is. Still today, this is one of the most fun games that I had ever played.
[/list]


[h1] So what is Metal Gear Solid V: Phantom Pain?[/h1]

At their core MGSV is a different take on war than most mainstream games. Surely you can play this game like any third person action shooter but this game rewards you for playing stealthy and for not killing enemies. Thematically Metal Gear always has anti war themes, from the extra goodies that you can get from spearing and interrogating enemy soldiers to recruit them and making them part of your staff in mother base, the game gently pushes you to find more alternatives to the challenges that the game presents. I genuinely love this.

In case that you don’t know MGSV is an incomplete game, due the drama between Kojima and Konami. The last act of the game had to be scraped and the last half of the game is just the first half of the game but in “hard mode”. For doing that your reward is about 2 or 3 hours of cinematics with plot points that never get resolved in this game. Like I said before, the enjoyment that you can get from the story of this game depends on how much you know about the Metal Gear lore and how resilient are you to the way that Kojima likes to tell their stories. I’m going to give you a fair warning, the first hour of the game is a glorified cinematic mixed with a tutorial and the tutorial officially ends 4 or 5 hours into the game. So that have in mind if you are interesting in picking this game up.

This game offers you DLCs that are basically worthless, so don’t bother, they are just stuff for the online mode and believe me it’s, not worth it. And that reminds me… The last thing that I want to you know before buying this game are the online elements. This game has a PvP mode that nobody used, even when this game was brand new. The “Base invasion mode” that lets players go into the bases of other players and steal and kill all their assets, and in case that you are wondering: yes, its glorified griefing. The “good news” is that Konami offers you the opportunity to buy “insurance” (for real money of course) so you don’t really lose anything if another player decides to visit your base, but nobody uses since you just can log out of the Konami servers and opt out of the mechanic all together. I did that and I recommend you to do the same, this game is a blast without any online stuff and I recommend you to play it as a purely single player one.


[h1] Things that I like about this game:[/h1]

[list]
[*]MGS5 is a bug free experience. It runs amazingly even on low end hardware.

[*]The amount of stuff that you can do in this game is mind-blowing, not as much as MGS3 but for modern AAA standards is amazing.

[*]The AI is really good, never too smart or too dumb, it’s really fair.

[*]AMAZING OST!

[*]The gameplay is near perfection, the game truly allows you to play however you want, there is always an optimal way to beat certain objectives, but if you are really good you can play naked without any weapons.

[*]There is plenty of equipment, gadgets, weapons and vehicles for you to unlock and experiment with.

[*]I wont call the story of this game “good” but it’s certainly entertaining.

[*]In my opinion this is the best stealth based open world game ever.

[/list]

[h1] Things that I dislike about this game:[/h1]

[list]
[*]After the first half of the game, it feels unfinished (because it is).

[*]The second half of the game is repetitive.

[*]The DLCs are really bad.

[*]Most of the online features are useless.

[*]The plot is a mess.

[/list]
[h1] Is this game worth my hard earned money?[/h1]

If you loved the other MGS games: yes.

If you are curious about the series and what to pick up because it is the newer and shiny one and looks amazing: yes.

If you love stealth games: yes.

If you just want to screw around with all kinds of weird and fun gadgets: yes.

If you can’t tolerate 1-hour cinematics with a convoluted and weird plot points: no.

I love this game, for me it is basically flawless. I don’t mind the “weird” story and the repetitive second half of the game because the gameplay makes up for it. Sneaking around or just running and shooting is that fun.

Rating: 9/10

review_text:
Phenomenal. Absolutely phenomenal. Right beside Red Dead Redemption 2 as my favorite open-world do-it-yourself game, and definitely one of the best gaming experiences I've had in a while. Story was just wacky enough for my taste, yet knew its limits (to an extent), and I loved the plot twists close to the end of the game.

The characters were just awesome; I'm 100% a Revolver Ocelot fan, with him spinning and handling his revolver like a natural and having the 'calm gunslinger' demeanor down to a T, complete with a light Southern U.S. accent...just love it to death, reminds me of McCree from Overwatch. Big Boss was great, too, as he was mostly a silent badass, speaking only when he needed to, making him incredibly fun to both play as and watch in cutscenes. All the other characters were praiseworthy, Miller, Quiet, Code Talker and Skullface (towards the end) particularly, thoroughly enjoyed observing them throughout the game's plot; while Part 1 was where they were introduced, and had some standout moments, Part 2 had some of the best character development and most unforgettable scenes in the game. Listening to Code Talker critique Miller's burgers. Watching Big Boss and Quiet have fun in the rain. [spoiler]Witnessing the entirety of the laboratory mission[/spoiler]. Observing Paz's realizations through her interactions with the photos. [spoiler]The final reveal, at the end, that you are not actually the real Big Boss[/spoiler], which caught me completely by surprise and explained quite a bit of the plot's happenings. The elaboration regarding Zero and the creation of Big Boss' "sons", Solid and Liquid Snake ([spoiler]who, apparently, was Eli...another great reveal[/spoiler]). Yeah...Part 2 was pretty f*cking great.

This game has some seriously cool moments, too; immediately coming to mind are the two battles with the [spoiler]Sahelanthropus[/spoiler] and the Skull encounters. I'll never forget the one fight with the Skulls in the deserted airport while defending Code Talker, the action and music combined made Big Boss feel all but unstoppable. The gameplay was more fun than I thought possible; nothing beats creeping up to an enemy inside a cardboard box, capping him with a sleep dart, and watching his friends go berserk when you shoot him into the sky with a balloon. The options are endless, and the game gives you the tools to go from full pacifist, kill-no-one, exclusively using riot weapons to Fulton-crazed melee lunatic, riding across the desert on horseback, beating up and extracting the entire Soviet army back to Mother Base, to standard stealthy killer who leaves a trail of corpses from guard post to guard post. Obviously giving the game bonus points for the [spoiler]Sahelanthropus[/spoiler], giant robots in a game set in a semi-plausible (emphasis on semi) Cold War scenario was EXACTLY what I was looking for in MGSV. Soundtrack was excellent, as a combination of action-packed and suspenseful ambience and not-quite-old-school popular music, and I loved being able to listen to the latter on cassettes during the long rides through Afghanistan; many of the story-related tapes helped me understand the at-times hilariously convoluted story of the Metal Gear saga up to this point. Yeah, safe to say, as one of the many people whose first Metal Gear Solid game was V, if this is what Metal Gear Solid is, then I like what I see. Hope the other games come to Steam soon!

Essentially a modern retelling of Moby Dīck through an anarchist's point of view and all the ideals that come with that as well as the creator of the game Hideo Kojima supporting it so much as to self insert himself into the game just to help the protagonist accomplish his goal.

With this being Moby Dīck, it's completely about revenge and how to pursue it, while also being completely detached from the government. It's great to see the characters, and therefore Hideo Kojima, know that morality is a sham to keep you from doing what you desire, that it is a piece of socially acceptable government propaganda, and without the government there is no need to keep yourself chained down.

It also helps dispel the completely uninformed, uneducated, and near braindead opinion of "You need morality to be not be a wild serial rapist." Snake is very much focused on his goals and desires, and yet always stops to help people because that is what he wants to do, not because he feels obligated to. It's great that these sentiments are showing up in popular media nowadays, sadly lots of people seem to misinterpret or purposefully misconstrue them either out of sheer maliciousness and their innate need to try and satisfy people above them, or plain ignorance.

This game is great if you take the advice and message for what it is rather than trying to make it into something that it isn't. It's definitely the type of game that can change your life and your complete outlook on it if you let it. It's never too late to throw off your submissive bonds and become a better person out of desire, rather than out of obligation.

Note: Hours in game is innaccurate due to playing while disconnected from Steam.

What can I say about MGSV? Well, Hideo Kojima made it, though you wouldn't know it had any real relation to the previous games besides Ocelot being involved. The intro is insanely long and tedious (Ever wanted to play Hospital Invalid Simulator? Look no further than the Prologue!)

It is still a Tactical Sneaking game, however, with RPG aspects sprinkled in all over the place.

Story side: This game falls well short of every other entry in the Metal Gear series, bar none. The worst story of any of the MG/MGS games I have ever played, and I have played all of them. The story felt like Kojima just wanted an excuse to make an open world MGS game, which is pointless because there wasn't a need for the excuse. Add to that the addition of Keifer Sutherland as Snake rather than the true voice of David Hayter, and fans looking to reminisce about wandering through swamps and having slightly inappropriate conversations with your support staff will not find much here.

Game side: Technically a masterpiece of sneaking and gun play, Tons of customization options, and an expansive map set in Afghanistan during the Cold War, the game blends Action and Stealth extremely well, and veterans to MGS's system will find much to recognize in the tactics and strategies used to overcome your enemies.

Overall: Do not buy this game if you're looking for a good story and bittersweet remembrances, but if you're just looking for a good stealth action game, it's not the worst you could do by far. The UI is a bit clunky, but that's to be expected with how much crap Kojima crammed into this game.

review_text:
This game saved my life.

I am 41.

My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.

When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.

After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.

Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.
After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.

Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.

I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.

Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.

Thank you

review_text:
Oh boy, where do I even begin with Metal Gear 5: The Phantom's Pain? This game took me on a wild ride filled with laughter, absurdity, and a whole lot of cardboard boxes. It's like Hideo Kojima decided to inject the game with a dose of pure comedic genius, and I couldn't stop laughing my way through this wacky espionage adventure.

First things first, let's talk about the protagonist, Big Boss, a man who takes stealth to a whole new level. Not only does he have an arsenal of weapons and gadgets at his disposal, but he also knows how to rock a mullet like nobody's business. I mean, who needs a stealth suit when you have a hairstyle that distracts enemies? Big Boss might as well be a walking disco ball!

Now, let's not forget about our trusty sidekick, Ocelot. This guy is like the James Bond of the Metal Gear universe, but with an obsession for spinning revolvers and a penchant for dramatic monologues. I swear, every time he appeared on screen, I couldn't help but chuckle at his over-the-top theatrics. I half expected him to break into a song and dance routine at any moment!

And speaking of over-the-top, let's talk about the game's villains. Metal Gear 5: The Phantom's Pain introduces us to a cast of eccentric bad guys that would make any Bond villain green with envy. We have a fire-spewing maniac who thinks he's a god, a guy with a metal arm who can summon lightning, and a quiet sniper who can disappear faster than my will to exercise. I couldn't decide if I should be terrified or laughing uncontrollably every time they made an appearance.

But perhaps the greatest source of hilarity in this game is the cardboard box. Yes, you heard me right, a plain old cardboard box. It's not just any box, though. This magical contraption is like a Swiss army knife of absurdity. Need to hide from enemies? Use the box. Need to travel across the map undetected? Just hop on the box and roll your way to victory. I can't count how many times I burst into laughter as I witnessed Big Boss engaging in intense cardboard box shenanigans.

Metal Gear 5: The Phantom's Pain is a game that doesn't take itself too seriously, and that's precisely why it's so much fun. It embraces the ridiculousness of its world and characters, delivering a hilarious experience from start to finish. If you're looking for a game that will keep you entertained and laughing, then grab a box, put on your best mullet, and dive headfirst into this madcap adventure. Just be prepared for your sides to ache from laughter and your face to hurt from smiling. This game is an absolute riot!

No, I will not talk about the online component/base raiding/multiplayer etc... because A) I came too late to the party so it wasnt supported anymore, and B) imho it was a great idea but terribly underutilized. I don't know where to start there are so many things you can do aside from missions and free-roam. You are given a base that you can upgrade and manage, many ways to approach a mission, and despite all the possible action and gunfight this game rewards you for minimizing enemy casualties. 

The open world looks nice but there are almost no other presence other than enemy soldiers and animals, even if you capture an outpost it will reset when you left the map and enemies will re-occupy the outpost. But the catch is the enemies felt real, their reaction towards your action may vary, they can surrender if you point your gun close enough from behind, they fell asleep or unconscious and you can wake them up, you can interrogate and abduct them (like seriously, you can), they can be heavily wounded and crying for help, you can hear dialogues in their native language, one enemy soldier is different than the other in terms of class and skill, they can be fooled around with (cruel but trust me its fun), you can hear them calling for help and report to their higher-ups, and so much more. The enemy AI is the main reason why I like this game so much

the gameplay is good because there are so much freedom that even the dumbest and goofiest plan might actually works. You can go non-lethal in assassination mission (you abduct the target instead of killing them), you can airdrop a tank and wreak havoc, or simply sit back and call for artillery fire (if you have too many resources). you can even told your pilot to drop you in the middle of the enemy base while you mount on the minigun with "take on me" playing on the helicopter speaker, this game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awesome. What I mentioned are merely few of the possible approaches.

you are also given a base that you can upgrade to help you performing mission and do researches to unlock gears, weapon, and upgrades for you, companion, and your helicopter. The base perform based on the staff that you can recruit from rescued prisoners, captured enemies, or reward from missions, you can also play as your crew in the open world. You can visit the base regularly to increase staff morale or simply to fool around with them, exploring your base can be as much fun as exploring the area of operation. There is also a separate base for PVP that has separate progression so nobody can mess with your singleplayer base (except when the story decides to).

The story itself is unusual and silly, don't even bother to understand why there is a flying girl that can summon a fire whale while a man on fire approaches you riding a horse that is also on fire. the cutscenes can be serious and comedic or both its hard to tell when ♥♥♥♥ has gotten serious, just flow with it. It is a rather long story especially if you try to max out your base and character first, in my 56 hour of "leveling the character first" gameplay I only managed to complete the first chapter. There are secondary missions but they are rather repetitive with few unique missions, despite it having the same objective but they made it less boring by changing the mission location. Can't get enough of it.

overall it is an awesome game with a questionable plot but still awesome nonetheless 10/10

review_text:
Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain

1. Gameplay - The changes to the gameplay in The Phantom Pain seem like a welcome one at first, yet wears on you mentally over the course of the game, however, paradoxically also contributes to the quality of the story. As opposed to earlier games in the series, The Phantom Pain deviates by borrowing from the open world, chaotic style of games such as the Far Cry Series in which spontaneous innovation and creative problem solving are the central factors in gameplay, rather than a game in which being methodical and perfecting one's execution of their schemes are the central factors. The problem one encounters with this style in this game, however, is the conflict between scripted story and gameplay and difficulty tuning issues. By default, players come into a game with the main intention of winning the game, and so are most likely to take the path of least resistance. Players also want chaos to happen organically, as there'd be no logical reason to create chaos and innovation when no conflict is had. How games like the aforementioned Far Cry aforementioned deal with this is by making the open world dynamic; so, for example, the player's original plan may be thwarted by a random attack by an elephant onto a guard. A whole series of these random mishaps means the plan needs to be innovated using the creativity of the player. The first problem occurs when this style is inhibited by scripted story beats, which cause the mission to become too much of a delicate scenario for a dynamic world to have any real baring, meaning no creativity. Another problem occurs with difficulty tuning, as the game is far too easy to create any real sense of spontaneity. Enemies feel as if they can only see two feet in front of them, and most missions can be solved by simply crouching and shooting everyone in the head with a dart gun as they run one by one to the location of the first guy who fell victim to said dart gun. Because one takes the path of least resistance, this means that missions feel consistently monotonous and repetitive, and are just a roadblock one needs to hurdle to get to the next bit of story. Because of this, one also doesn't feel the need to upgrade or engineer new weapons or go on side operations, which might actually provide the player with vital intel or perks. The substinence levels, in which you are provided no additional tools at all, are the funnest missions in the game due to the fact that the harder the game is and the more restrictions you have the more you feel the need to do things creatively. Back to the difficulty tuning, The Phantom Pain switches between numbingly to infuriatingly difficult from mission to mission. These difficult missions are so extreme that most even B rank guides on them require you to divert from the mission plan laid out by the characters themselves due to the fact that the developers had no actual idea how the player would beat it. One of these levels is one where five almost invincible enemies (eight missile shots to kill) who can also teleport and kill you in almost one hit jump out and surround a car you have to extract. Another missions is an entire motorcade of almost eight waves each containing at least four tanks and one helicopter surrounding you at every angle.

2. Plot - The plot is the central appeal of this game and what solely motivates the player to complete the missions in the first place. Despite possibly not being one of the best plots compared to other Metal Gear titles, the plot is an exceedingly well structured and well-done plot in a sea of extremely well structured and well-done plots. The story starts off with an almost cinematic bang with nearly nothing being explained, thus building intrigue. Then, the episodic style of the missions in part contributes to the quality of the story, as the investigative spy thriller genre unveils itself bit by bit, thus quenching your thirst for answers near the beginning and reopening new ones. The monotonous and grinding nature of the missions also make you feel a strong emotional connection to your companions, such as Quiet and Ocelot, over the course of your long journey despite limited interaction with them. The first part of the story ends with an astounding speech from the primary villain of the game, which provide incite and dynamics to a character who seemed lackluster in the beginning. The main problem occurs in Chapter Two, though the [spoiler]twist[/spoiler] is excellent, where some vital story threads are left untied.

3. Graphics - The graphics are of course stunning if you couldn't already tell by just gazing at it. In the beginning segment, you can see muscles contracting and stretching on Venom Snake's naked back. The only qualm is that texture resolution is low by default and can be quite jarring in a scene that's realistically lit. You can tell that the graphics team put a great amount of effort into making it look as detailed as possible.

4. Overall Grade - A-

To note that yes, I am recommending the game, but that's because it might be the best stealth open-world game ever made. There are massive issues with the game's storytelling and setting, so if you care about Metal Gear for the story and build-up, please avoid this game entirely.

Now, Phantom Pain is the "fifth" game in the metal gear solid series, if you ignore a few games here and there that seems to be not as important even though they contain critical character for this game. Now, not to dismiss Konami, the engine they had built for MGS V is nothing short of incredible. The game looks fantastic, has huge open maps, and offers insane possibilities with tons of interactions with the world and its NPCs that would make Far cry games jealous by comparison. Gameplay wise, the game has it all. Base building, upgrading your equipment via capture and conquest of enemy resources, kidnapping enemy personnel that are highly competent and making them join your side, really cool gadget and tools to make your experience unique. You can make your horse poop to make a jeep slip off road. I'm not even joking. The freedom this game offers for strategy and problem solution is to be lauded, and it will take quite some time for a game to offer such an incredibly amount of freedom in its sandbox.

However, came the Konami and Kojima dispute. Now, Konami is a big greedy publisher, so that's bad. Then, Kojima is a visionnary who also doesn't know when too much is too much, which can also be bad. Pair the two up, and give MGS V a nearly decade old development cycle, and you start to understand that there must've been some pretty big issues in there. To be honest, it's incredible these issues aren't noticed in gameplay - maybe that part had been done and tested first. But the story and plot of the game... that's where it all breaks loose and turns to crap.

MGS V tries really hard to tell a cool story... but then only offers it via tapes you need to sit down and listen to, sometimes for almost 5 minutes at a time. Other times, you'll have to watch a really weird cutscenes that doesn't make much sense or seems just out-of-touch with the theme of the game. Sure, some beats of the story is competent or interesting enough to warrant attention. But then you arrive at the ending... and realise it's all a cliffhanger... for a sequel that will never be.

Yep. For all your hard work and effort, the end of MGS V has been cut and placed as a cliffhanger for MGS VI, which, let's face it, will never happen. Or if it does, it will be without Kojima, since he left Konami after being mistreated by them for years. An entire third and final arc of the game is missing, and will never be explained or given. The game throws you back into some missions that are harder versions of the same one you've already completed. Force you to watch an entire cutscene again just for 1-2 minutes of new footage, or a new development. The game becomes an absolute mess by that point... and it's seriously sad.

It's one of these games where the gameplay is so so so good that you can somewhat ignore the story and just have fun. But for Metal Gear Solid fans, some who has been part of the franchise for 20 years, this game is a serious case of heartbreak and broken promises.

review_text:
The game has you playing as Snake, after many years and severe Injury you find yourself trying to escape from what can only be described as a mental hospital. Snake is clearly hallucinating as we endure an hour of butt clenching, hospital gowning, linear murder marathon as you try to escape from said building. Its a terrible awful prologue that drags on and on. Then after they hold your hand for what seems like an eternity, you are finally released into the big wide world to do your own missions. 

This game had a lot of potential, but its clear someone intended this for console users. The Xbox controller map is one of the giveaways, the multiple cut scenes are the other, the checkpoint system is so irritating as well. but that is console limitations for you. 

On a pc, the keys are just terrible, I suggest you either use a controller (as was intended), or remap the keys or use a game pad like the nostromo or tartarus if you have one of them available. Will save you a lot of pain. Multiple keys get confusing real fast, as literally picking up items and interacting are two different buttons. I can see why they did it, but its still bad pc keyboard management. (again intended for console).

So you are running around in Afghanistan on a horse and pretty much no one notices this till the mission requires it. (massive plot hole). You can steal other vehicles, so I suggest you do that so you do not look so stupid in a war zone. Outposts can be captured along missions, goodies can be found and with these materials, you can do research and development for better weapons and mission items. This part is pretty good. The bad part is the ridiculous balloon kidnappings you can do, steal animals, equipment, soldiers and no one again notices (even though they scream for miles).

There are lots of different missions, some are easy, some are hard and some are very important to your equipment and research division for later in the game. you can also find collectables, money, materials etc lying about in odd places, its also possible to recruit pets for training (again mission dependant).

The game allows you to play any way you want, as long as you do not play the way you really want to, you are prevented from thinking outside the box too much by walls. In some missions you can just avoid whole checkpoints and in others you are forced into checkpoints with mission failures (how convenient).

Stealth play is a lot of fun, or you an mow everyone down, its up to you. Equipment and supplies can be dropped if you have earned enough points, be it heroism or cash etc, but this gates a lot of stuff early on in the game. Snake can also wear different outfits, which have some extra abilities to enhance combat or stealth. Again this is the good stuff.

Now the really bad stuff, the cut scenes are annoying as there are so many of them, the end title sequences again are many, the checkpoints are specific and irritating and really have no place on a pc game. Its also disheartening when a mission goes wrong and your only checkpoint is right at the beginning. There is no way round it. This turns this mission into a chore. The missions are fun and you can have fun, but the way you set it all up is not, its console and tedious. It is such a shame as when you are in a mission you forget about all that stuff. 

The interface for upgrading and research is again a mess and for pc users its a chore to use. 

I like the game style, I love the research aspect, I love stealth, I love the multiple weapons and drops, but the game became tedious after just one mission. So many cut scenes, end scenes, end titles for every mission? Even the Terms and agreement to start the game is tedious, three whole pages and you have to agree to each one to just start the game.

If you can forgive the console crap, you will love the game. Buy it when its on sale though. This game feels like a movie that has been badly edited. The prologue almost put me off playing, glad I stuck it out, but I have never been bombarded with so many titles and cut scenes before on a pc title.

That is consoles for you I guess. I would still recommend the game though.

review_text:
[h1]Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain[/h1]

The game is over 6 years old and there is nothing new to say but I still want to add my two cents here. While MGSV has certainly been and still is the benchmark for every stealth game out there in terms of gameplay, it unfortunately falls flat on the core elements that made the franchise so great in the first place. That's the story, the boss fights and the main villain. 
Although I haven't played  its immediate predecessor, Metal Gear Solid: Peace Walker, nor the successor MG1, I have multiple playthroughs of MGS1, MGS2, MGS3, and MGS4 over the years. And 100% in MGSV on my PS4 and on Steam.
So, let's break it down a bit.

[h1]Pros:[/h1]

[b]1.) Gameplay:[/b]

Every stealth game fan's wet dream comes true. The possibilities of embarking on a mission are sheer endless. The possible equipment you can use, the items, the weapons, the vehicles, the approach. Everything is there. You can even choose your own "partner". It is the benchmark for the perfect stealth game. Even today.

[b]2.) Immersion and tension when you are on a mission:[/b]

The immersion and tension of a mission are priceless and I haven't played many games where I got the same feel and excitement. When you first play the mission and don't know what to expect, that feeling is just pure gold. The same is true if you play the mission again to find the perfect path and complete your tasks.

[b]3.) Most of the NPCs:[/b]

Well. They do lack some background i have to say. This is even more true if you haven't played any of the other titles in the series or don't want to listen to the hours of recordings that make up most of the background. But they are still well implanted and worth mentioning here.

[b]4.) Base building and the "Forward Operating Base" missions:[/b]

Building a base, watching it grow, with all of the new staff you "recruit" over time is just such a fun part of the game. And so are the FOB missions to get new staff and resources.

[b]5.) Fulton extracts people, animals and vehicles:[/b]

It really never gets boring and I can do that all day.

[b]6.) Quiet and D-Dog[/b]

[h1]Neutral:[/h1]

[b]1.) Side missions:[/b]

Well the side missions are just tedious and there are 157 of them! And without a good way to fast travel, most of them are no fun at all. I would put that in the Cons section, but I needed something for the Neutral section as well. So here we are.

[h1]Cons:[/h1]

[b]1.) Story:[/b]

Some might say the story is fine, I've seen worse and I certainly won't contradict you there, but for MGS standards the story is just underwhelming. Ok. I didn't play Metal Gear Solid: Peace Walker, or MG, so I miss some parts of it, but from what I've read, I didn't miss much. Because that's certainly the least interesting part of the MG timeline. There's still potential here, but when you think about the complexity and depth of the previous four MGS games, you can see a huge difference.
There are also plenty of filler missions that completely break the story time after time. If you take away the missions that offer little or no story, there just isn't much left in the end. And when the story finally takes off, which is AFTER the maingame, it just stops with one of the worst cliffhangers in video game history. So sad! 
All that remains is to listen to all the tapes. Which is a must, but you have to spend hours listening to recordings. Hours!

[b]2.) Main villain:[/b]

I don't know how they did this, but they introduced one of the worst villains I have ever met. He's just pathetic, downright boring and can't do anything special. All minor villains outshine the main villain when they first appear on screen. I really have no words for it. 

[b]3.) Boss fights:[/b]

Oh yeah! One of the core elements of the series and some of the most memorable that I have come across in my gaming life. Just think of those epic boss fights against the - more or less - superhuman encounters you've experienced over the years. That epic fight against "The End", or Sniper Wolf, Psycho Mantis, Vamp, Liquid Ocelot, Fatman, Solidus  Snake, or The Boss. These fights very much define the whole series. 
Why they deviated from this path in MGS5 is a mystery to me. Ok, it's more like MGS4 which actually had some good boss fights and maybe they wanted to focus on the missions and stealth gameplay instead. But why not both? Why?
Instead, we don't get any "real" boss fights at all. More like a couple of half boss fights where running away is a better option or even having to run away to advance. And you have to face the same "boss unit" multiple times in the game, even more so with the extrem missions. And when you finally face them for real it is no epic showdown at all. V/5 would play again.

There are a million different things that can go wrong with a video game. There may be a glaring inconsistency in plot with respect to previous titles, you may become a meme developer for releasing a plague of bugs upon launch *coughBethesdacough*, or you may allow your game to become so enveloped in microtransactions that your game may become a pay-to-pay-to-play game, with the release of endless DLCs, skins, or some exclusive in-game currency to speed up wait-times or just to make any progress whatsoever. Not this game.

Everything this game does, it does it right. The first thing you notice about this game is that it's shiny. The first impression you get from this game is the psychological tale of the valor and toiling of the main character, Venom Snake. Upon successfully escaping the hospital in the introductory chapter, it seems that no emotional stakes have been established to be able to root for the main character. Does he have a past? Does he live for some quality or value that his home country told him to fight for? Or does he fight for some earthly spoils like money or jewels? The answers are, his past isn't discussed, his home country isn't discussed, and it's not explicitly told what he's fighting for. But there is a look on Venom Snake's face, through the scenes, the gameplay, and through Keifer Sutherland's silently anguished portrayal of Snake, which is anything but stiff, that should tell you all you need to know about the reason Snake is fighting.

Kojima's direction in terms of the camera and also the general feel of the game, is very grounded but still very interesting and immersive, which is an accomplishment in and of itself, given the general market is focused on the fantastical, the superficial, and the Freudian. Kojima's camera for a lot of the game is like another person with a camera just filming the characters. The camera, sometimes, is never further than 5-6 feet from the floor and follows the characters around like a documentarian/journalist/war movie handicam operator, and sometimes, the camera has long, broad, sweeping, endless, and cinematic shots, which give the impression of the first ever 3D animated movies when directors no longer felt the restrictions of shooting in the physical world. Kojima's direction in the atmosphere and lighting of the game is grounded in realism, which may turn alot of people away, but Kojima strays just enough from the realm of the real to ramp up immersion and give the impression of a familiar but uneasy and involving reality, such as when these strange psychic human-but-not-human beings seemingly have something to do with Snake or the plot, maybe, who knows, it was visually and aurally pleasing to pay too much attention to the "why," which may be the effect Kojima was going for; keep the "why" to yourself, or just be very implicit, and showcase the amazing "how," "when," "who," and "where."

The gunplay, the sneaking, the open world, the vehicles, and various bits, bobs, toys, and gadgets are like one of the best grown-up toyboxes in gaming history. There's something about the items in game that satisfy both the desire for a serious game, and also the desire for some arbitrary silliness every now and then. One minute, you may be ghosting your way into an enormous and vastly crowded enemy base to rescue a doctor, and the next, you are playing with a cardboard box that has the option of effectively deceptive decals, like an enemy soldier or a woman in a bikini, which is totally necessary for the gameplay (so I've heard).

Virtually every other game bears a necessary criticism, it could be about an inconsistency in pacing, battles may be unnecessarily complex or needlessly long, maybe there's a point where your brain just turns off and you're playing on autopilot, thereby souring immersion. The only criticism I have about this game is that it ended just too darn soon. Every now and then, something gives you an experience which you wish you could just keep in a bottle and live over and over again. This was one of those games. No reason not to play.

review_text:
This is my first MGS game, and honestly, I love it. There's plenty of chances to be sneaky, and plenty of chances to just gun folks down like a badass. The characters are all pretty good- though I personally think Ocelot needed more screen time than he got, and I think Miller should get kicked in the balls for constantly trying to overrule Snake's decisions and actions, despite all of his talk about "being loyal"- and both Quiet and D.D do their jobs well enough to be useful for all sorts of missions. However, if you're going to use explosives, don't take D.D with you. He can and WILL walk into explosives you've put down like a dummy... because he's a dog and likes to follow Snake a little too closely sometimes.

Combat is solid yet challenging, and at first, the story is pretty good. But there are parts of the story that I don't care about, but that's a personal thing. See, I play this game to shoot the bad guys and occasionally punch sheep in the face, not so Miller can get his rocks off with his revenge plans. And if you're wondering why I'm so hard on Miller- especially considering his multiple wounds and the torture he went through- it's because in the story, he interjects so much because he's just so focused on revenge and is thoroughly jaded about everything. I much preferred Ocelot's interactions because he's calmer, not as focused on getting back at those who did him wrong, and actually wants to help not only other people, but the group he's loyal to, the Diamond Dogs. He hasn't lost as much as Snake and Miller have, and as such, I appreciate that he's not as out of touch with his humanity because of it. And yeah, Miller's been through some ♥♥♥♥, but so has Snake, and Snake isn't as utterly ruthless as Miller is about Quiet, Emmerich, and others.

However, Miller's not totally heartless, which makes him redeemable, and Ocelot's not a total nice guy. He can play hard ball just as well as the others, and Miller is fully capable of compassion and understanding. He just... gets a little too heated. When he's calmer, Miller is actually a decent character in my eyes. But when he's riled up, I just want him to zip his lips.

But this is just my opinion on the game, the characters, and the story, and I've tried to not spoil anything... even though this game isn't exactly new. I definitely think people should play it, though be warned: the online servers were shut down recently, so you will be losing on a cool part of the game, admittedly, but that's hardly a necessary part of the game, in my experience. Just some additional fun that was nice to have around while it lasted.

Definitely pick this game up sometime, though wait for a sale. It's old enough that it should be on sale fairly often, so might as well save what money you can!

It's hard to recommend this game because it has a lot of ♥♥♥♥♥♥ parts alongside some really good parts. Despite the incredibly glitchy conversation tasks and questionable f2p mobile game design choices this game has some of the best implementations of stealth and sandbox mechanics I've seen. While the story didn't seem to be well received I actually found myself enjoying it and mission 43 hit harder than I expected. All in all, it has incredibly enjoyable base gameplay riddled with unnecessary systems that drag down the overall experience. I'd recommend using mods to remove less desirable gameplay mechanics like the No Timers mod to remove offline timers and Infinite Heaven to skip the helicopter rides when you're replaying missions.

[b]Likes[/b]

The sandbox fun is great and the amount of detail in missions is incredible. The game really awards you for trying to take alternative paths to missions with story tidbits and hints. It's really nice to listen to peoples conversations because it does make it feel like the world is dynamically changing around you and the conversations random NPCs have do reflect that. Kinda weird though when you hear the same conversation with the same voices in different missions. 

Tasks for missions can require stuff that is not developed yet or force you to play differently. Initially, I was put off by this but it really helps produce variety in your playstyle. Like I would initially play full stealth but depending on the task I could go in loud with a tank, go in for one shot one kill with a sniper, or fultoning every vehicle in the mission while tanking shots from tanks lol. Tasks keep it feeling like a game rather than a mindless simulator which is an issue I have in some sandbox games.

People mentioned a lot of the time that the enemies are dynamically adjusting to your tactics. I'm not sure if this is true because sometimes it feels like enemies are just progressing alongside you with better gear and tools, but it still is refreshing that the game forces you to adapt your tactics instead of just sticking to one method to whole time.

FOBs are pretty fun if you want something extra and challenging to do alongside the main game while also being a good source of resource and GMP income. Really helps to have enough money to do multiple developments at the same time when they take 1+ hour to complete.

Despite Huey being a piece of ♥♥♥♥, D-walker is beautiful and my favorite buddy.

[b]Dislikes[/b]

I would recommend to use mods to skip loading times, however I do not feel this is necessary at the start as they are mostly negligible (half an hour or less) and you will spend a lot of time figuring things out in game so you don't really need to rush development. Towards the end of the game when I barely had any missions left I just kept the game open to finish 1-2 hour long item developments and the 2 hour long dispatch missions which have around 50% chance to fail. If you don't want to deal with that then start using mods because I sure did after this.

This game really does feel like an unfinished buggy mess at times, but I don't know how much more they were planning to add. Like you can use the helicopter to travel between landing zones on the motherbase, but not in Afghanistan/Africa?? Conversation tasks are buggy as hell because of the butterfly effect lmao and capture cages are peak laziness in terms of adding more ♥♥♥♥ to your game. Also Eli's storyline is pretty much abandoned. 

A Quiet Exit is the worst part of this game and should have been done differently. It's not that hard if you can prepare but the way the mission was implemented ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sucks.

You lose too much if you want to stick in offline mode and lose even more if you want to stay in offline mode after playing a while in online mode. The game regularly moves your offline resources into an online stock which cannot be accessed while offline, the reason for this I don't know but you are ♥♥♥♥♥♥ if you ever try to play game offline and want to progress development. This game unfortunately has too much of a reliance on online stuff and a lot of functionality you can only access while online, like rewards for completing tasks,  daily rewards, and FOBs. It is super easy to get resources from FOBs and FOB events that it can trivialize resources for a good bit.

Checkpoint system is stupid. I fultoned all the kids in the mission for a task, but had to restart from a checkpoint halfway through. It seems that the game had unfultoned a whole camp of child soldiers and wanted me to ignore it.

Despite pretending like nukes are a deterrent in game, nukes are the exact opposite of deterrents and I have no idea why you'd make one apart for the achievements.

[h1]Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Review[/h1]

165 hours flat to finally finish the story. I may have gotten distracted by the hundreds of side ops.

This game has a troubled history, corporate politics and stuff. So it's an unfinished game, where the second half is largely repeating the story missions on a higher difficulty. But what we do have is plenty fun. Breathtaking visuals, shiny cinematics, solid physics. Runs like hot butter on my old gaming laptop from college. And having only completed 72% of the mission objectives does still mean I finished the story. 

The storyline twists and turns at a dizzying pace. This is currently my only MGS entry. It flows with the series, as I understand, adding depth and hidden details to the overarching plot. Some major reveals are buried in the cassette tapes, so I recommend taking the time to listen, at least to the interesting sounding ones. Who's building a what to destroy which country? Why should I love or hate this character? Am I a heroic rebel or a terrorist? The cassettes are a lot of dialogue to slog through, but it adds significance to the characters when you hear the backstory and behind-the-scenes conversations. (Especially the hamburger saga. *chefs kiss* That is peak art.)

The gameplay is phenomenal albeit wacky. Third person shooter with an overwhelming array of options. Develop weapons and gadgets to suit a playstyle of action or stealth, though stealth tends to be preferred. (ie: The game gets harder the more you kill, which is a genius progression system.) Some gadgets seem silly, like how there's an entire development tree devoted to cardboard boxes, but can still be used legitimately. (Tactical espionage cardboard > helicopter machine gun.)

PROS:
First off I’d like to say, out of all the metal gear games I’ve played (MGS3, PEACE WALKER, MGS4, Portable Ops, Metal Gear Ground Zeros and Metal Gear Solid 5) this to me is by far the best one in many ways. Not only is this open world vast and realistic, it really captures the atmosphere of what it’s like to be a solo badass taking out literal armies. The scenery is amazing and the animals, plants and resources you find throughout your journey are all useful and plentiful. The combat system in this game is very cool, the first person or over the shoulder choice was a big stand out for me, the hit reg is great and the guns are somewhat realistic. The companions are actually useful and well as your home base, or should i say mother base. The progression of your base is visible and materialistic, making you want to get more materials to make ur base cooler. The enemies adjust to your play style therefore making it harder for you to win gunfights, meaning you need to think about your next move

CONS:
The story in Mgsv is a little underwhelming, most mission are go here and collect intel to then go to another play to collect intel about another place to get more intel etc. Although that might sound boring I found the majority of it to not be too bad and honestly wouldn’t count it as much of a bother. The ending however feels rushing and unpolished. After reading up about it I found that this was due to budget and time restrains on the studio creating this game, so I can understand the untidiness of it all. 

VERDICT
MGSV is not only an absolute masterpiece for it’s time, but it also keeps up with current day games and if you can buy it for $25 and under it is 1000% worth it. Amazing game

If you're wondering if you should play this game if you haven't touched the first four, dont bother worrying about that, because even as a standalone game Metal Gear Solid V hits every stealth game check box and leaves more of them in it's place.  

First off the setting itself is always unique in a Metal Gear Solid game, The phantom pain is no exception.  Taking place in 1980s Afghanistan during its Russian invasion it nails this aspect right off the bat. Secondly, you have locations in Africa and a humongous base known affectionately as "mother base" where you amass an army of mercenaries of no nation.

First thing you notice is that this is a story driven video game. It takes a few things to liberty but it positively hits everything a game should have.  It includes dossiers, collectible audio tapes, a badass prosthetic arm that our main character "Big Boss" uses to beat the everliving ♥♥♥♥ out of everyone he comes into contact with nearly.  The arsenal is another aspect altogether. Weapons get addon parts through upgrades and mother base herself is never a forced thing to go to, because theres plenty of violence to get up there too (namely on your own employee who'll gladly take you smashing them in the face and shooting them with tranquilizer pistols.  The ammount of abuse you can give these people is astronomically funny and some aspects of the game have some hilarious comedic effect.

MGSV doesn't fall into the trope of being too many things at once, while at the same time giving you way more than most games do.  I was concerned about the smallness of the map but then I came to different maps altogether which assauged that fear.  Mother base is a reason to play the game altogether and each of the divisions you create have a unique purpose to your missions.

Characters are another strong point of any MGSV and this once is no slouch,  Revolver Ocelot and Miller are masterfully voice acted and interact with Snake in realistic method.  This brings to the front the buddy system in this game.  In other games the "follower" npc is almost someone you have to walk around and constantly gets in the way or shoots you in the back of the head 30 times while trying to kill an enemy.  The buddies like everything in this can be upgraded. The amount of love put into the creation of this game is apparently. 

I wish any company but Konami had made the cash off this one.  But I wont get into that in this review because I want you to form your own opinions about the events in which Kojima was fired at the end of development for this game.

Probably the worst MGS, not because the game's unfinished but mostly because of bad direction. It's fun for the first 10-15 hours or so, but newcomers and series veterans alike will be bored and confused by the end of chapter 1.

The gameplay offers some fun with freedom and experimentation, yes, but the aimless open world pales in comparison to the very intentional and methodical pacing of 1-3. By the end of the game, everything feels like a chore and you have so much at your disposal that neither stealth nor combat is a challenge to the point that they have to make the final combat segment about protecting a braindead AI companion rather than fighting anything interesting.

By subtracting where it is from where it isn't, or where it isn't from where it is (whichever is greater), it obtains a difference, or deviation. Six years later, there are still things I discover that delight me in a way only a Metal Gear game can. That is precious. 

I would readily recommend this game to anyone. If this is your first Metal Gear game, be warned that it'll suck you in. The PC port was flawless at launch, and remains flawless to this day. I honestly wish I could go back to 2015 and tell myself that the game is not as bad I thought.

review_text:
I paid 7,49 euro for this game + all DLC and Ground Zeroes on a sale, and holy cow this was the best deal ever. I feel like I paid too little for this, I'm 184 hours in and there is still content and things to do. This isn't just a game, it's a wonderful experience, it's art, if an extraterrestial species asked me what our greatest achivement is, I would show them this gem of a game. I didn't play any other MGS games so I approached this without expectations and I LOVED LOVED LOVED IT!!!!!!! Balloons pulling people away to the sky, a husky dog knocking out enemies, hiding and sliding in a carton box, running around with a chicken hat, driving in pink tanks, running around in a  small robot with a machete and a flamethrower, GIANT robots, a burning monster man or whatever,  shooting your prosthetic arm out like a rocket, two entire open worlds to explore and have fun in, but also tear-shedding moments at some points in the story - That's what this game is. People say the story is bad or whatever but as I said this was my first MGS game so I really didn't care about the story and I liked it, I don't think this game should be viewed as worse because of the story or anything because it really makes up for it with the fact that this game is pure gameplay and pure fun, I don't recall a single moment where I didn't have fun in all my 184 hours. Even the hardest battles that took me many many tries and where I died a lot were a lot of fun and felt very rewarding to finally beat. You can carefully plan everything out, knock everyone out and pull them away on balloons to achieve your goal, or you can go full berserk in a tank, both are super fun and the game lets you do whatever you want. Anyway, I could really go on saying how fricking good this game is for another 2 hours. This game could have 100 times less content and it still would be worth the tiny price I paid for it. But it didn't have 100 times less content, it had it all. It is everything I would ever want out of a game, it is MORE than I could have imagined a video game can be. This is no doubt my all time favorite game ever, and will stay that way for a long time. Thank you Hideo Kojima and everyone else who is behind this game. BUT IT SUCKS THAT YOUR CUSTOM AVATAR CAN'T HAVE LONG HAIR, but that's just a tiny tiny tiny remark of mine :) 

EDIT: I FORGOT TO ADD that this game's optimalization is out of this world, it's the best optimalized game ever I think, it looks beutiful and runs butter smooth on my 6 year old budget laptop, every other game from 2013 onwards rarely runs at higher than 20fps even on lowest settings and in lower than 720p resolution, so I don't know how this game manages to run this well and still look this beutiful and run in 1080p. Also I love the controlls in this game, very responsive and smooth, I saw someone complaining that you can't jump whenever you want in this game, but I think this works amazingly in this game, think of it - how often do you jump in real life? Yeah. In this game you only jump when there is need to jump, for example running and jumping off from a ledge, you do this by running towards a ledge and holding the E key, and it's awesome. When you want to get on something tall you climb on it instead of jumping and it works very well too. Hitting the space key instead of making you jump in the air, makes you jump to the ground in front of you into the crawling position, at first it can be confusing when you're used to normal jumping, but you will get used to it very quickly, because it just makes sense, more sense than normal jumping you're used to at least I think. I know this review is kind of a mess and it's just some of my disconnected thoughts and rambling, but whenever I want to end this review, there's still amazing things in this game I remind myself of and want to add. I know I said "anyway" too many times in this review but, anyway, I think I've said enough for now. :)

review_text:
Metal Gear has always held a special place in my heart for its rich story and deep narrative that has always gone out of its way to have the viewer question their own morals, ethics, and political views of the world. Hideo Kojima was excellent with his world building in pacing in Metal Gear Solid 1, 2, 3 and 4. Even though I feel like 4 got a little cluttered near the end, it has a story that in short and sweet terms, talks about the good and bad of what make us all human to the core. Both in good and bad ways...and that's something that Metal Gear Solid 5 struggles with, it's pacing in story as well as keeping you intrigued in it.

Metal Gear Solid 5: The Phantom Pain is suppose to be the final link to the Metal Gear Saga's timeline. Talking about the fall of Big Boss as a hero. And also giving us details into the rise of the Son's of Big Boss. Liquid, Solid, and Solidus Snake and their pivotal role in the series and how they begin this sort of rise to put an end to Big Boss as well as the Patriots. But you don't get much information about any of the sons besides Liquid Snake. And I suppose that's where the story struggles a bit. You get a handful of cassette tapes to try and fill in some of the gaps to the timeline. There are also a handful of new characters that don't really help progress the story. And it didn't help that Konami rushed Kojima to push the game out, where there was clearly going to be a sort of more full conclusion to the story with a Chapter 3 ending the game. But was pulled out because it was not finished. Instead opting for paid cosmetics and rather flawed multiplayer DLC.

BUT...this does not mean that MGS5 is overall a bad game. Far from it. It by far has the best stealth of all of the series as well as control scheme and an arsenal of toys to play with. The physics is probably my only problem with it. But the game allows you to do a stealth mission in the way that you want. Quick and quiet with non-lethal rounds or go in guns blazing with an LMG or Rocket Launcher and kill everyone in sight. The choice is yours. And the sandbox only opens up the more you continue to play. The missions being fun but lacking a firm story for most of them.

I played this game on Xbox back in 2015, and starting from the begging again and raising an army and getting all of the good weapons and achieving an S rank was challenging yet fun still. If you love open world games, stealth, or even just want to go wild with guns. I highly recommend this game.

If you are looking to know more about the Metal Gear Solid Saga and its story and don't have a console to play the old games, I highly recommend emulating them as they run flawlessly. There haven't been any sort of remakes or a new Legacy Collection since 2012, which makes these games often hard to play and experience because some are limited to old consoles. So emulating these games is often or not your best alternative.

And not only using resources of singleplayer world, but also via invading other player's FOB's (Forward operation base).
So, developing and maintaining your Mother Base (that exist in the form of MB itself that is unraidable by other players online, plus FOB online bases that gives you expansion space and automatic procurement of resources) is a very big, and truly interesting part of the game.
To be fair, this base management thing has started with 2 other MGS games (MGS Portable ops, MGS Peace walker), which were on mobile playstation - PSP.

So try this game - it still contains a lot of cinematographic cutscenes and just enough plot to nearly justify it's "MGS" name, but you would enjoy gameplay part in it even more. Fox engine still looks very good and is an evident upgrade to MGS4's graphics. In game's open world, stealth action gameplay elements are implemented very smoothly, and new CQC (melee strikes and takedowns, hold ups) looks realistic and cool.

The main voice actor (David Hayter) has changed and was replaced with Kiefer Sutherland, who made himself known by his very convincing play in "24" TV show (which is a meme in itself and I recommend to start watching right away also, if you missed it). I'm far from judging the main game creator (H. Kojima) for this decision, even though D. Hayter still is very legit "Snake" voice for me and every hardcore MGS fan - Sutherland sounds more dramatic, mature and very convincing too. It's just that he didn't get much dialogue in this game, to be judged fully if he a good Snake replacement or not.

(quick note, don't let my hours deceive. I put well over a thousand hours on the console version. Also, apologies for any spelling and formatting mistakes, doing this in kind of a rush.)
For general amusement, this game is solid. It's very fluid, feels good, and dispatching enemies is pretty damn satisfying. A little clunky with how enemy detection works and the AI can be.. Well, questionable. But it's definitely serviceable.

As a long time fan of metal gear, though? This game breaks my ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ heart. This game could've been; needed to be, so much more than what it is now for the last entry in this series. It lacks so much about what made MGS great, the charm, the mystique.. The characters are so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ flat, even flatter than 4. There are no breaks from the "pain" and the "revenge" ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, it's so exhausting hearing Miller cry about it every time he's on screen or in a Codec. And even despite of how obnoxiously seriously it takes itself it doesn't go nearly far enough to encapsulate just how much of a monster "Boss" became and how he became one. So badly did this game need chapter 3, and maybe a 4th. Was supposed to be the bridge towards Metal Gear 1, buuut it wasn't that at all. In the end, it's like a filler arc. And good god almighty, don't get me started on the cassette tapes.

Let's see.. Most of the guns are utterly useless, you don't even need to upgrade the base kit. You can literally go through the entire game with the windurgur and the mrs-4 unupgraded just fine. The staff management tab can be pretty annoying to manage, and the fact that there isn't a filter based on skills is kind of dumb. Seriously, scrolling through hundreds of dudes to weed out the troublemakers is annoying. The maps are gigantic, and almost entirely empty. Vehicles are fun, but mostly, entirely, worthless. There aren't really enough zones with enough situations to justify bringing a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ tank, which brings me to:

Battle Gear. What a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ waste. I WOULD understand not letting us use this in the overworld, but when we get access to tanks, apcs, missile trucks, and the ever broken and busted walker gear, it becomes apparent that the reason this isn't available for use outside of a few niche combat deployments is NOT because it would be underpowered; but because of technical limitations, or they just didn't feel like doing it. Wish they were upfront about that to begin with though, like sooo many other things. Lmao.

Ah right; another disappointment, mother base. Literally, just a giant ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cosmetic with nothing to do on. We were promised a more modular motherbase, for a more dynamic experience when dealing with invasions. That didn't happen. ♥♥♥♥ this place, ♥♥♥♥ the fact there's nothing to do and explore here, and ♥♥♥♥ the fact that i have to go here to shower after dusting a mission. It takes like a solid minute just to load into the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ place because of the helicopter cutscene (well, everywhere else too.) FOBs are such an amazing concept that didn't receive nearly enough attention and love, now it's just all cheated in S++ staff and hackers. And on console it's just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ dead.
P.S. a little side addendum, development time for "online" items. 12 days for a gun, 6 for a bathing suit. Lemao.

And don't even get me started on the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ multiplayer. MGO3 is- was, such a cluster ♥♥♥♥. Lag no jutsu. ♥♥♥♥♥♥' stealth camo. terrible maps. And aside from that, it just turns into your average cookie cutter third person shooter. ♥♥♥♥ was dead on arrival and the most support they show it and the base game now is routine automated updates, what a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ mistake and a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ shame. Bless the community for MGO2r.

I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ love Metal Gear. I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ love this game. But I also hate it dearly. Though, it is eerily similar to 4, just as this was not the way the Big Boss saga should have ended so to was 4 not the way the Solid Snake saga should have ended. I could probably ♥♥♥♥♥ and moan for hours about  V but honestly, I've been doing it for 5 years now and I am so over it. Just wanna get my summed up thoughts somewhere.

As a general conclusion, this is a game I would not recommend to anyone who has been a long time fan of this series. It is not a good Metal Gear game. But for those of you who are very casual with this series, or don't really play MGS in general, you may like it.

The thing that almost ruined the game for me, and required a few internet guides, was trying to get the real ending - required quite a bit of grinding. Otherwise a really solid package, would recommend!

review_text:
♥♥♥♥ Konami, but I too would be severely pissed at if my project overran its time and budget and after 5 years and 80 million dollars, I had the project lead/director come to me and ask 2 more years and 50 million more dollars.

Kojima really carked this up. The game is so unfinished it's not even funny. Screw his supposed avant-garde auteur meta-narrative, this was fundamentally supposed to be a game about how Naked Snake became the Big Boss of Metal Gear 1 till Metal Gear Solid 4, along with dozens of threads along the way to be neatly wrapped up. Revolver Ocelot, Kazuhira Miller, Liquid Snake, Solidus Snake, Patriots, Cipher, Zero, there were DOZENS of questions that needed answers. 

We got almost none.

Or rather.... We got some of the answers. Implemented as shoddy "recorded cassettes" of conversations you can play back. Like something cooked up very last minute with the script, just to justify Kiefer Sutherland's voice acting fee. 

But the rest is all just....missing. Its not there. It's so not there that it's absence feels like a huge gaping constant hole in the game. Phantom pain indeed. Phantom pain of the narrative and answers that should've been there and aren't. If this was the meta-narrative that Kojima was aiming for, honestly ♥♥♥♥ him. I'm too old to have stuck with this series for 30 years and gotten this as a result.

The game is phenomenal from a gaming mechanics stand-point. Besides the age old question of why game characters can't jump or perform complex maneuvers such as grab someone on the other side of a corner and drag them around and shut them up, the game is near perfect in terms of mechanics. There isn't a lot you could as more. Fox Engine is technically amazing, the draw distance and tactical options are vast. The customization options are vast, though the deployment costs can feel really punitive sometimes.

But mother base feels like an empty hollow vessel. There is almost no interactability/interactiveness to it. I personally don't even visit it unless I'm explicitly forced back by cutscenes etc, specially due to the deployment costs. The management is barebones, most of it I'm content to let run on automation, only needing to intervene to optimize once you reach around mission 40.

Coming back to where we started though, the incompleteness...yeah. Play this for the bizarre present-but-not present story. Look up chapter 3 and mission 51 on google to see just how incomplete this is.

Enjoy the game itself. Play it purely for the infiltration mechanics. Worth a buy on sale.

Going into MGSV GZ/TPP, my only experience with the MG series was MGS3 on the 3DS. I was vaguely aware of the story of the MG series, but without having played most of the titles, I had little idea of what to expect from the title. MGSV came readily recommended from friends and people in the community, so I took a crack at it from that alone.

Just wow. Not even sure where to start - the graphics for a game from 2015 are immaculate, immersive, and downright impressive. The gunplay, stealth action, and various other gameplay elements are easily some of the best I have ever played with, let alone from an open world title. The story is by far some of the best writing I have ever experienced in the medium with much of the game being a legendary example of cinema's "show don't tell". 

I went into the game tepidly expecting to hate it given its emphasis on non-lethal, stealth-based gameplay.
