I have and will probably always love the Metal Gear Solid series, but this game seems to share more DNA with ARMA than it does Metal Gear Solid. The best way I can explain my expectations of the game, and what this game is would be summarised thusly:

Metal Gear Solid 1-4 were somewhat linear, camp spy/action anime adventures. After MGS4, it seems like all the anime and campness was poured into the Raiden spin-off (Revengeance?) and all the serious mil-sim stuff was poured into this.

This game feels like sitting in an immensely large, mostly unpopulated desert, playing with a bucket of little green army men whilst Troy Baker reads you an extensive and utterly exhaustive history of modern warfare - occasionally, like once a fortnight, the ghost of Hideo Kojima comes out and makes spooky noises at you for like a half-second.

Overall, I'm sure this is a very good game - well put together, and just insanely well thought out (for instance, all the guys in gas masks fire their guns sideways - this is the only way to get a good sight picture through a gas mask. The military nerds went to absolute town!). It's just a terrible Metal Gear Solid game. The pacing is glacial, the structure is completely absent (no call to action, no drive, just piddly little missions) and the charm is just not there.

I'll happily recommend this game to anyone with 150+ hours in ARMA, but if you loved MGS 1-4, maybe give this one a miss.

I want to make some things clear before i go ahead with my complaints. I have not played any other MGS games, but from watching footage of other MGS games, MGS 5 plays more like an open world Dishonered game with guns, than a metal gear game, which is why i bought the game. 

This game is not fun. After having played this game for rougly 26 hours and completed about 2/3 of the story (based on the number of missions), i cant go on any longer. 

I have heard all kinds of crazy ♥♥♥♥ about the story in metal gear, which is to be expected, considereing its produced by Hideo Kojima, and i was having a fun time just going with the wierd and crazy story and the slightly off voice acting (the game was produced in japan, after all). The gameplay was pretty fun in the beginning too.

But, then i realized, that once you've played 1 mission, you've played them all. Its the same objective every time. "Hey Snake, i got a mission for you. Go to the _____ outpost/encampent/base and extract the commander/prisoner. Dont let us down."

The open combat in this game is EXTREAMLY janky and unfun. The guns handle very badly, and the crosshair is TERRIBLE, its like a giant square, it serves no function. So youre basically forced to use first person view any time you want to kill someone thats further away than 10 meters, and you better hope you hit them on your first try, cause the weapon sway and recoil is insane, and you aint unlocking a scope before level 10, and thats merely a reflex sight. Also there is no hipfiring, and every single time someone spots you, that annoying MGS spotted sound rings and time is slowed down, which gets very annoying if youre just trying to rush through an outpost

My point is: you want to avoid open combat, cause its not fun, and the checkpoints are often far between, so dying could mean loosing a lot of progress. 

Now you might be saying "so what, its a stealth game dummy, of course im gonna avoid open combat." and i would say yeah youre right, but its a little hard sometimes, when your supressor B R E A K S after count em 1234567891011121314 15 FIFTEEN SHOTS, THATS HALF A MAG BRUH, YOU BETTER HOPE THAT ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ DONT TURN AROUND JUST WHEN YOU ABOUT TO SHOOT HIM, CAUSING YOU TO HIT MISS HIM, CAUSE YOU GON HAVE TO WASTE HALF YOUR SUPRESSOR ON HIS ASS. Now you might be saying "well i heard you can upgrade your gear, cant you upgrade your supressor?" and yes, you can. Except, for that you have to have RnD division in level 30+, and i can tell you right now that aint happening before AT LEAST mission 20. 

On the topic of RnD, why. Just why. WHY is 75% procent of the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ research tree weapons WITHOUT SUPRESSORS, THAT HAVE NO OTHER ADVANTAGES WHAT SO EVER??. All in all , I would recommend this game because the game's campaign missions and stealth factors are phenomenal , but those who are expecting more of a detailed open world game and with really diversified missions , then I wouldn't recommend it , but feel the game is worth playing only for the missions and the story .

I'm writing this review 80 hours in. Mind you, I've only completed the main campaign of the game and haven't worked very far into the second part, but I feel like I have enough time to at least be able to accurately grasp the majority of the game. As a whole, MGSV is a fantastic game through and through, and it's wholly different from almost every military shooter I have ever played. While similar looking games like CoD and Battlefield offer heavily scripted and linear missions, MGSV pretty much dumps you into the open world, tells you to accomplish a certain task in a certain place, and then lets you figure out the details and how you'll use the games vast array of mechanics to accomplish the task at hand. In both the main and side missions, the game offers some of the wildest, most genuinely fun gameplay sequences I have ever experiences, mostly because I feel like I made them happen, instead of them happening to me. I don't want to throw out too many specifics, since I think the game is best enjoyed with zero prior knowledge of the mechanics, but suffice it to say, this is some of the most fun I've ever had just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ around with a game's mechanics and seeing how far the game will let me push them. 

Moving on from gameplay, I'll briefly talk about the story. To be totally honest, it sucks. It's super overly convoluted, there are far too many factions and characters to remember, and I just barely understood what the main villain's goals were and his reasons for them. The big reveals are cool, but almost everything else is some degree of strange or incomprehensible. I guess Metal Gear fans are kind of used to this, but I'm not.

That aside, I still wholeheartedly recommend this game, purely on the basis of its core gameplay being that good. Stealthing through enemy encampments with my customized arsenal and buddies is immensely satisfying, as is coming up with new infiltration strategies by piecing together the items the game gives you into your own unique play style. If you even have the slightest interest in anything I have said, play this game.

review_text:
First off, the negative. When Konami decided to part ways with Kojima, they didn't give him time to finish up the story. The trademark Kojima ending full of 40 minute long cinematic cutscenes is nowhere to be found. Instead, the game sort of sputters out. It's a heartbreaking way for the story to end.

At this point five years from release, you've largely missed the fun that was FOBs -- base defenses in particular were great fun. But if you're trying to unlock the various overpowered endgame items available you'll probably still find yourself grinding through a bunch of AI FOB events that are still fun, if lacking the P2P charm of the launch.

That all said, this game is the magnum opus of the stealth action genre. The sheer variety of ways to approach every mission is astounding. From the very first mission you're thrust in an open world with a few mission objectives and myriad ways to achieve them. Even after nearly 200 hours, I find myself routinely replaying missions from early in the game and finding things I missed the first time around.

At this point I've completed all the missions, with S ranks on all the main missions. I've got three fully fleshed out bases working for me. I've got all of my buddies fully-upgraded. I've got more powerful weapons and items than I know what to do with. I could've quit a long while ago. But I keep coming back to this game because there's so many variations and permutations to each mission, and therefore so many ways to play the game, that it never really gets old.

The game takes a bit to get used too, especially for those who are new to MGS games. I'll be honest the prologue early on in the game was too story heavy with forced stealth & combat scenarios, but its understandable since it is the tutorial. When you entered the open world part, damn "this is where the fun begins".

Some game play mechanics and controls need quite some getting used to and there were a lot of things that weren't mentioned in the tutorial, though most tips do appear on loading screens (take your time and read these, helps alot later). 
But the game is very forgiving to new players. If you bungled up on your stealth, no worries and keep on finishing the missions. You can always redo them again for a better score.

Wide open space and fun stealth and combat mechanics. Gives you a lot of freedom to play with and customisations are aplenty. And don't forget the cool story lines and amazing voice acting.

Overall fun game, highly recommended.

review_text:
[h1] The [i] Big Boss[/i] of Stealth Games [/h1]
After getting through that 2 hour intro sequence, which can simply be described as [b] insane[/b] , I knew that I was going to be experiencing something special in a world that's absolutely bonkers! 

Having been introduced to the series with Peace Walker on the PSP, i was extremely excited to see the continuation of the story even as convoluted and non-sensical as it all is - the world remains highly intriguing , and the characters it introduces are charming and personable. Quiet [i] especially so [/i]. I really appreciated the generally darker tone and atmosphere of the story, something that was certainly hinted at already in Ground Zeroes ; those Paz scenes and the audio logs are certainly something O_O . Whilst those missing the more campy nature of the previous games need not be too  put off, as some of those moments are still present from time to time. Overall though, it's not the best story in the world  - especially when you take into consideration the fact that the game just seems to abruptly end with no sense of conclusion at all. But that's okay because...

The [i] gameplay[/i] is where it's all at! Seriously, i have yet to have this much fun sneaking around in games besides in maybe Dishonored. Everything just feels so smooth and fluid from the way your character moves around, to the weapons you've equipped and are using, to the optional vehicles if you so please, to teammates you may opt to bring into the field with you. Hell , to the return of the Fulton system! It's the melding of all these dynamic game systems that ultimately allow you to forge your own tale of war and glory! Couple this with more of that beautiful base-building and expansion and it really comes together and starts to feel like an RPG; possibly why i enjoy it all so much honestly. The plentiful amount of SideOp missions also provide significant replay value and some change of pace from the mainline missions however they do tend to get monotonous after a certain point. Trying to go for the S Rank on missions is challenging , requires skill and careful preparation but ultimately pays off and feels rewarding especially when you get them optional objectives and recruit an S rank soldier into your Diamond Dogs band of mercenaries. 

Is it a perfect game? No. The bosses tend to more or less be quite disappointing save for a couple and as i mentioned the story can get too confusing and convoluted at times , but hey, that's Metal Gear for ya. But I'll be damned if this wasn't one of the most fun experiences i had in my gaming career.  

[b] F*ck Konami. Hail Kojima. [/b]

review_text:
The game's mechanics are the best compared to any other Metal Gear game. It's so much fun to control Snake, and mess around in the game with all the equipment and weapons you can unlock. There are a lot of downsides to this game, but just being fun to play outweighs them all for me.

To sum most of my criticism up in one sentence, world in MGS 3 Snake Eater felt more alive and detailed than this world. 

The biggest problem is that the missions are very repetitive, and there is no reason to explore the two game maps, outside of missions. There are a few interesting locations in the maps, but generally, it's mostly small outposts and empty space, with no indoor locations (besides the occasional set of small rooms). 
Mother base is almost completely empty of anything interesting. There are the target practice missions, and one single point of interest, but other than that, there is no reason to explore Mother base.
The sparse animal life have almost no purpose in the game, and, unless they are able to attack you, can usually just be ignored.
Driving was mostly unneeded, since you can't be stealthy while driving, and using a buddy, like your horse, is usually better. There are only jeeps, trucks and tanks to drive, no motorcycle or any other type of cars. Also, you can't obtain helicopters, which was disappointing to learn, as  a MGS Peace Walker fan. 
Interrogating enemies is very repetitive after a while, since they are very limited in their response. 
Traveling from Mother base to a game map is an unnecessarily long process, since it always starts with credits during a long helicopter ride to the location.
And my final point isn't really a downside, but it's weird that most MGS games have it, and not this one. You can't swim in this game.

MGS on the PS1 is solid! 
MGS 2 and MGS: Snake Eater on the PS2 are both solid!

To its credit there is a little freedom once your character gets outside.

The mouse and keyboard character movement is clumsy. Some mouse keys can't be rebind. The mouse doesn't work when one goes into the options menu to change the settings around. I am a big Metal Gear Solid fan but I cannot recommend this game on PC unless your willing to use a controller instead of mouse and keyboard. 

PS: I started this game on hard difficulty and still this game was way too easy. No, challenged to be had at all. Clearly Kojami was more interested in telling a story rather then given the player a challenge here. The enemy A.I. is dumb, blind, and deaf. U will really have to go out of your way to be seen by these enemies. Thumbs down

I'm a huge MG saga fan. Over the years I greatly enjoyed MG games, and this one marks a special place for me. I remember waiting for it to come, only to discover what Konami did. It was heartbreaking, I'm not lying. 
This game is not bad per se, it's amazing, well directed and very appealing from a design POV; "it won't stop hurting" seeing the game's artbook only to realize how much is missing, and what amazing epic finale we could have got. 

The gameplay follows the classic MG setup, only this time bringing it to a much, much larger scale, with many open world elements and a tremendous freedom of action. I enjoyed having to find new strateties as enemies started to adapt to my playstyle, it kept things refreshing. This however doesn't redeem the core the slightest, which soon starts to get old. You go in the wild, find a base, "capture it", steal resources, steal best men, vehicles and so on. That's the core. Missions start to feel the very same (because at the end of the day they are) pretty quickly, especially side missions. 
Luckily, story keeps things from becoming unbearable, and especially in the first half the game does a remarkable job at keeping you in. Problems kick in with the second arc, only to partially fix themselves with the 2 last missions. 
Let me to say, having us to repeat missions, only harder, is NOT what I'd call good design, especially if they're mandatory. Yes, it's all of course due to Konami rushing things.
The finale is acceptable; I liked it and I liked the way Kojima wanted to thanks us after all those years.

I'd lie if I said that I didn't enjoy this game, but overall I don't know if you should play it. So much is missing. So much will forever stay as is. The pain, it will never go away.

review_text:
Despite the understandably disappointing aspects regarding this game that include a massive twist in the plot and the controversial relations between franchise owner Konami and franchise creator Hideo Kojima, Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain properly serves as what is likely the final chapter in the main saga of the series as far as Big Boss and Solid Snake are involved as protagonists, and connects even more dots in the franchise behind the events of previous games that chronologically take place later in the series.

Though you probably already know this if you are interested in buying the game, if you value a heavily detailed story in your games, Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain will be right up your alley. Unfortunately, several prior Metal Gear games that could be crucial to fully understanding the story for this specific game are not available on Steam, or PC as a whole for that matter. To fully understand the story of Big Boss in this game, I recommend checking compilations of cutscenes for Metal Gear Solid 3: Snake Eater, Metal Gear Solid: Portable Ops, and Metal Gear Solid: Peace Walker, all in that order on YouTube, if you haven't played the games on any of the platforms they are available for. Additionally, you may want to play Metal Gear Solid V: Ground Zeroes first, as it is also available on Steam, and serves as the prologue to this game and sets up some key plot points, in addition to including extra missions that will unlock content such as a retro PS1 Solid Snake costume to wear in-game. Putting important understanding of the plot aside, this game once again delivers for the Metal Gear saga as more than just a game. The influence of Hollywood action films is easily noticed in the detailed cutscenes and talented voice actors, which include Kiefer Sutherland taking over the role of Snake from longtime actor David Hayter, and Troy Baker taking over as Revolver Ocelot from the now-retired Patric Zimmerman. Despite the controversial voice change for Snake, Sutherland is a fantastic fit for the character, and it's a considerable shame that most speaking is instead covered by Ocelot and Snake's second-in-command, Kazuhira Miller.

As for gameplay, several elements of the Metal Gear saga are present in this game, but the new focus on an open-world opens up a lot of possibilities for the franchise. Additionally, many aspects initially introduced in Metal Gear Solid: Peace Walker have returned for this game, specifically the secondary focus on building an army by recruiting volunteers and convincing enemy soldiers to join via extraction during missions. The other thing to note is that this game is jam-packed with several hours worth of content. I'm not even finished with the game and currently have almost 170 hours of total playtime. Of course, that does include having to restart missions after getting killed, but not many games in my library tend to reach over fifty hours if I do a single playthrough of them.

The other really great thing is that my laptop isn't exactly the greatest piece of hardware for gaming, but completely against expectations, MGSV: The Phantom Pain ran surprisingly well. In fact, it runs better than most comparable big budget games can. I can easily recommend this game for anyone who's PC isn't the mightiest, but still able to handle a handful of games, especially if it can run Team Fortress 2 with little to no issues. I'd highly recommend this, regardless of whether it's on sale or not, if you are looking for a great action game with an equally great story, and having difficulty finding games that will run well on your device.

review_text:
I played this game on PS4 when it released back in 2015. After 100%ing it, and spending a fair bit of time on MGO and FOB, 1300 hours between the both, I felt like it deserves a review.

I really love this game, and I think it's probably one of my favorite games of all time. That being said, it is also pretty flawed, mostly because it just doesn't feel complete. Most likely because it wasn't completed.

A lot of people say there's virtually no story in this game, and I just don't think that's true. Chapter 1 feels like an entire Metal Gear Solid story that's much easier to understand. There are a lot of missions in between that don't exactly make the story flow, but I would really hope you'd like the Metal Gear gameplay in general because this game offers you a lot of it. 

But then, as you keep playing Chapter 2, you get sucked into the story. It seems like more things are going to happen and that things are going to get solved or change a little. Even though I knew it probably wouldn't go anywhere, I still fell into it, and its just a shame. The story builds you up to all sorts of things, but then just is over out of nowhere. Like it was just really very incomplete and very unfullfilling. I almost wonder why they didn't just cut the entire chapter 2 out, but I suppose that would be a decent amount of content wasted. This is a pretty big flaw and I really don't blame anyone for disliking the game because of this, but I find myself able to look past it since I enjoyed the gameplay and Chapter 1 so much.

To add on to the gameplay, the open world is actually really cool. I do realize that everything between guardposts and things like that is kind of dead ground, but it makes the world feel a lot bigger and part of something. My only complaint is it's just not fun to travel around. Most open world games give you a fun way to travel from place to place. Take Saints Row or GTA, you can drive around quickly and run people over or just narrowly avoid traffic while trying to get from mission to mission as quick as you can. In this game, you can't really do that. If you try to drive through an outpost, you'll almost certainly be spotted and lose a tiny bit of heroism for it, which isn't much of a problem. But then, they tell EVERY outpost and guard to be on the lookout for an intruder, so every base is now on alert.

Traveling around just feels like a chore and you aren't rewarded well for doing it. All those complaints aside, I still really appreciate the open world aspect of the game and love that I have a big open Metal Gear world to do whatever weird Metal Gear things I want to do.

The missions are just boring at times. Extraction and elimination objectives make up 90% of the missions, but the gameplay makes up for it.

I really recommend this game to fans of the series, or at least people who love the gameplay of it. The second chapter story is clearly not finished and I don't think it will be, but chapter 1 is great. There's only maybe 3 bosses in the game too, which is a bit of a flaw depending on how you feel about Metal Gear bosses. I'd say it's worth full price, but it'll for sure be going on sale to 40 bucks and below more often and on different sites, so maybe look out for that.

MGO was a direct downgrade from MGS4's online game mode, it's a glorified run n' shooter, whether you play stealthily or not, it doesn't matter. Just play Scout, use the UN-ARC, and you'll dominate. No depth to the game, CQC is broken, all that jazz.

The base invasion game mode, FORWARD OPERATING BASE INFILTRATION, is very interesting, but as expected from this company, it's pay to win. If you have a weak base, other PFs will breeze through it like nothing, and if they open a wormhole, it won't matter if their base has custom mines placed all over, top tier armor, S++ soldiers, and strategically posted guards. The PvP aspect is VERY very flawed, but it's really fun sometimes, unless it's a Stun Grenade Launcher Gamer™. 

Very very fun game, but also very flawed. Tons of content, but at the same time, it's unfinished.

This is one of the best Metal Gear Solid games, gameplay wise. One of the best modern video games I have played, period. It's so well optimized. Now this is what a game should strive to be mechanically. I cannot emphasize this point enough which is that the controls FEEL GREAT. the input latency feels nice and low, the camera movement is so smooth and responsive which is what makes this a great shooter especially at 60 FPS. What it lacked was just a tad bit in the story because I believe the game was rushed or they had disputes while making it. but what it lacked there, it for sure made up in gameplay. This is a really good stealth game, Hideo Kojima is a genius... really pays attention to the details. 

I know this is a stealth game, but it has a bit of horror aspect to it too. I don't know what the right word for it is...it has a hint of psychological thriller or psychological horror? makes sense right? since Kojima likes to work on horror games too. Like the boss battles of this game really had me on alert, as in I didn't want to die cuz I really don't wanna lose >_>  such as while fighting the skulls. I know I can restart from checkpoint when I die, but I was actually worried about dying and tried my best to survive cuz yeah, fighting The Skulls was terrifying lmao. The way the music/sound effects play at certain moments of suspense, the way the environment gets fogged up when the Skulls show; it all has a scare factor/element to it. Throughout the progression of this game, I was worried about what's going to happen to Snake and his allies because the game introduces the characters really well, actually makes you care about them... cuz people can get hurt in this game real bad; we've seen that in Ground Zeroes. I'm saying that cuz the enemies did some f**ked up s*** (torture) to the good guys. this is the reality of war.

I don't know any other game that comes near this one. You have the option to engage in battle with enemies/engage in combat/go in guns blazing and kill them OR you can be complete stealth and sneak past them without even triggering a fight. you can do that for some of the boss fights too. And yeah, you can subdue the enemy in so many ways too...i don't know any other game that does that...this game is truly next-gen and a modern masterpiece imo. one of a kind.

The only thing I miss is the old sound effects like when Snake alerts the guards (!), the old music that we experienced in Metal gear solid 3 or 4, was not present in this game. They really changed it up in this game, even Snake's voice actor is not David Hayter anymore. But I suppose this isn't really the same type of game as the previous Metal Gear Solid games...Kojima really went for the horror aspect in this one. so it's different... Anyways, overall, gameplay is good and well worth it. I recommend it (Y). The game is a steal on sale.

-Checkpoint locations for side-ops spawn me a few miles away from the actual mission. If I get caught and want to retry at the latest checkpoint, I'm more frustrated when I realize I'm really, really, really far away.

This is more of a yes with caveats, I did not like the game myself, but I think other people may enjoy it more.

This game had the best stealth moment-to-moment gameplay in the entire stealth genre by far, but it has a number of weaknesses.

The save system saves depending on whether you leave a location (say, a base) and go to another, with some mid mission checkpoints. It’s very unreliable and makes you waste so much time, It’s my single most hated aspect of this game.

The game's open world design means that it reuses most of its maps a lot. To be fair, the developers try to use the various bases in different ways in each of the main missions, but it’s not just the main missions, it’s also the side missions and free roam and it can get very, soul-sucking over time.

The game's presentation is very stark, a lot of the story is described to you and you fight mostly the same soldiers over and over again, with most of the levels having one-off stories that are only tangentially related to the plot.

The game has an impressive amount of freedom, but that isn't necessarily a good thing. Traditional stealth games tend to rely on restricting the player to force them to make their way through the maps and find solutions to their problems, MGSV's freedom means that one can easily bypass most of the problems by using overpowered tools, so you have to (or, from another viewpoint, are able to) set up both the challenges you face and the ways that you overcome them.

This means it offers a lot room to be creative, but not so fun for those who like their games to be more directed. It’s a game for those who like playing [i]with[/i] their games, rather than those who like playing [i]through[/i] their games.

Cutscene direction is very good at the beginning, but as the game goes on, it tends to overuse flashy light effects and slow-mo and the limitations of the one-shot style affect the quality more.

I’m not a longtime Metal Gear fan so I can’t comment on the story from that point of view and I’ve only played until the end of chapter one, but my take on the story was that it was very, ahh, thin. Snake, as you know does not express much personality (I also wish [i]someone[/i] would call him punished venom snake, it’s a cool name they never use.), Miller and Ocelot mostly serve you loyally, with hints of their deeper personalities coming up in the tapes.

Eli’s silence was more annoying than Snakes-no scratch that, Eli was just annoying (good boss fight though). Skull Face lost his mystique from Ground Zeroes and was reduced to a remarkably stupid villain who constantly tries to impress Snake, to the point of not killing him for no reason twice and constantly, hypocritically monologues about revenge and demons and fire and the other pretty words this game likes overusing.

I really did not like Quiet. I found her obnoxiously fanservicy, I think the decision to recruit her by Snake and Ocelot was boneheaded and I find her childish, excitable behaviour creepy to think about. There is a misogynistic association with women and children that comes into full force with Quiet.

The tapes are not a good way to convey the story. They worked in System Shock 2 because the player found them one by one in the map, so they served as natural stopping points for the player to listen to them. They also tended to be short.

In MGSV they are given to you in bulk at the end of missions, tend to be rather longer, and because the game has you, sneaking, fighting, driving, Punching Mother base soldiers in the face, so there aren’t natural stopping points, so it becomes very boring to just stop whatever you are doing and listen to Miller and Ocelot drone on about what’s actually happening in the plot. As a result, listening to all of them to get the story becomes a chore. Also, you have to go through a bunch of menus to get to them, which in turn discourages listening to them.

It’s weird to have a positive review that mostly goes over the negative aspects of the game, But I've only thought in detail about this game's failings. You may have to read another review to get an idea of this game’s positives. I should not have to rely on that, but I honestly haven't thought about this games's strengths enough to comment on them. It’s a good game, but not the kind I could enjoy.

A Hideo Kojima Game

What skills?

For players who, like many, find that this massive game is too small for how well it immerses you in battlefields of 1984, there are mods for dozens more missions to explore.

All in all, this is a game I can see myself still playing for many more years. 7/5, perfect score.

Two things are wrong with this game. 

The narrative isn't finished so sections are rushed and unpolished. Where it holds up its on par with Kojima's typical storytelling but its probably the worst best example because sections are missing context and pretty much any chance the game gets to tell you something historical or factual is used to bludgeon you with dialogue. I'd imagine that a sequel or grand second half of the story with more locations was probably planned but it just isn't there so things got chopped. 

The gameplay is fine but because of the unpolished narrative there are several sections where the difficulty depends on what equipment you have and how well prepared you are heading into a story critical mission. So it suffers from a lack of balance but not in a completely negative way its just a by product of having open world stealth having to reign you in to add challenge or danger to some sections. Sometimes it works and sometimes it just doesn't because you either have the exact right thing or you are able to get the right thing you need but then you can end up unable to get what you need or you've spent it all. 

Other than that its got a tight gameplay loop that tries very hard to make you feel great about sneaking around and rewards skilful play. It will run extremely well on most hardware made after 2012 and the sound design is great. 

Pick it up if it goes on sale.

Playing this game reminds me a lot of Far Cry 2: the combat engagements are pretty similar, the intel-gathering mechanics are a step above, and after the fighting is done just go around the guard post like a madman picking up every scrap of loot, ammo, or secret treasures (including rough diamonds). I was hoping this game could be just a casually-sitting-on-the-bed-with-a-controller-and-zoning-out kind of game, and it can be, but it doesn't feel optimized for controller play (not messing with the online component; idgaf about it because I have other online competitive games to play if I'm feeling it).

People talk it up a lot, but I couldn't appreciate it at first; it was not all that fun. Lots of instances of restarting missions/checkpoints to improve your rank, increase your fame/heroism, or to get certain achievements; which isn't necessarily bad for an open-world game, but only if that game allows you to keep multiple save slots so you can have more freedom to go back. It's really annoying that there are only three options: you can load your most previous checkpoint; you can restart the whole mission from when you first land in the mission zone; or you can abort the mission entirely just so you can change up your loadout. Thankfully the game is generous with its checkpoint/save frequency, but it's far from ideal. It's also a pain that you can't change the control scheme beyond the two controller layouts that are available (thank God I got a Steam controller before they were phased-out). Controls for switching between support items, weapons, and tools was clunky at first, but it became manageable after playing with it more. The game is semi-brutal in the beginning, and you have to drill yourself to make it fun. It's a chore in the beginning, but once you understand more of the ins and outs, the game can be really fun. Unfortunately, there will be points where you want to repeat missions and go to certain zones to collect resources - it's a PITA to grind; especially if you want to develop your base to full capacity. Furthermore, the missions have to be completed *very precisely*, which is annoying for repeatable missions - like if you need to rescue a prisoner from possible sites around the map, but they only ever pop-up in the same place each time, you will *still* need to act as if you don't already know where they will turn up, just so you can trigger the events that get them to spawn in. You can't just go directly to where the prisoner will spawn; you have to do a bunch of boring and mundane crap to get to the rescue part: interrogate the right soldiers who would know the prisoner's whereabouts; wait for some officer to have a meeting with other officers/soldiers (maybe spy on the meeting so you can learn some mission-details that you can't get any other way) and follow that commander to the prisoner so you can rescue them. Playing this game off-and-on leads to forgetting that mechanic; tried to pick up a prisoner after trekking 20 minutes across the map, avoiding enemy camps and remaining undetected, only to get there and realize that the prisoner wasn't there - because I forgot to interrogate any of the soldiers at either base before killing them all. 

One last thing to know before buying: the cutscenes in this game are epic; they're cool, don't get me wrong, but they are "epic" in the classic sense - they are long, and they are excessive. If you want to try this game out on Steam, you ARE going to miss your window for a refund. To be honest, one of the only reasons I stuck with the game this long was because it was too late to refund it. I don't know if this game will exactly be life-changing for me, but I'm stuck with it now, so I'm trying to enjoy it - so far, so good.

- Story pacing + “unfinished” feeling late-game

If you want a perfectly complete story, manage expectations.

review_text:
I really recommend to anyone that likes stealth or shooting games to give Metal Gear Solid V a try. Here's a brief description of what I have experienced in the 200+ hours I've played.

Pros:  The game gave me a plethora of emotions throughout it's storyline. The prologue is honestly one of the most intense moments i've seen in a game. The story perfectly combines the harsh reality and the cruelty of war, with science fiction, and even paranormal stuff. On the one hand you have to save child slaves from the warzone, or fight against a nuclear threat, and on the other hand you get these quirky and funny moments, it's just great how the mood is always changing. Gameplay is easy to learn and not too complicated. There are numerous ways you can infiltrate a base and the game helps you to explore ways to do it and be creative too. The graphics are also very good, and the sountrack is really awesome. The story is well written, and it helps you somewhat with the complicated storyline of the previous games, so you don't get really lost.

Cons:  The end is not dissapointing, but a bit of a cliffhanger, since the game creator never got to finish it for the well known reasons. In order to "save" this, they just added some repetitive missions and a cutscene. Now, I don't really consider this a con, but the game also feels somewhat more "independent" from the previous games of the series, and I guess fans of the series will see that it's not really connected to the complicated MGS plot. Finally I just have to comment on some drawbacks on the gameplay. First, the game basically forces you to visit your mother base often and literally greet any soldier you come across, or else they lose their morale, which is really annoying sometimes. Second, the game progresses a lot better if you play online, because you get online missions and rewards, it's not really that you can't play offline, but it's definitely not the same. Finally, sometimes the immersion to the story gets interrupted by a dude trying to infiltrate your online FOB platform. So you have to stop the storyline and go defend your resourses.

Just to note here, I have only talked about the main game, and not Metal Gear Online, which I didn't quite explore.
Overall it's a great game, and I will definitely remember the moments I lived playing it. It's definitely worth a try.

Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain[b] is an open world stealth game developed by Kojima Productions and published by Konami. It was released worldwide for Microsoft Windows, PlayStation 3, PlayStation 4, Xbox 360, and Xbox One on September 1, 2015. It is the ninth installment in the Metal Gear series that was directed, written, and designed by Hideo Kojima following Metal Gear Solid V: Ground Zeroes, a stand-alone prologue released the previous year, as well as his final work at Konami.

Set in 1984, nine years after the events of Ground Zeroes and eleven years before the events of the original Metal Gear, the story follows mercenary leader Punished "Venom" Snake as he ventures into Soviet-occupied Afghanistan and the Angola–Zaire border region to exact revenge on the people who destroyed his forces and came close to killing him during the climax of Ground Zeroes. It carries over the tagline of Tactical Espionage Operations first used in Metal Gear Solid: Peace Walker.

The Phantom Pain was critically acclaimed upon release, with praise for its varied and interconnected gameplay mechanics and level of player freedom. However, its narrative received polarizing opinions, with some finding it lacking for a Metal Gear title. Further scrutiny targeted the story's repetitive second half and ending that left several plot points unresolved, which was linked to conclusive evidence of removed content and led some to suggest that the game was released unfinished. Despite this, The Phantom Pain received perfect review scores from several publications and was described as one of the greatest stealth games of all time. A complete edition that bundles The Phantom Pain and Ground Zeroes together, titled Metal Gear Solid V: The Definitive Experience, was released in October 2016.

MGSV is a deeply flawed but amazing game. The stealth gameplay is unrivalled in its creativity and endless in its possibility. From the interrogation mechanic to the variety of hi-tech gadgets you can employ, the stealth in this game is next to none. The many gameplay systems mesh and interact together in continuously fresh and unique ways, making this game a joy to come back to, if only to methodically slaughter your way through one of the many military bases. As Todd would say, "It just works." Developing Mother Base is always fun and as it grows, so does your arsenal, allowing Mother Base to become a visual milestone of your progress in the game. Diving into soliders and watching them thank and salute me will always be fun. The directing and plot in this game is, of course, stellar, as Hideo Kojima's stylings especially shine here, making for both visceral action and powerfully gut-wrenching scenes.

This biggest complaint I have of this is the horrendous boss battles. These boss battles are repetitive, dull and always infuriatingly difficult. Unfortunately, the freedom of gameplay of normal levels works against boss battles as it's never really clear what you can or can't do and if a strategy feels legit or just cheesing. The open world can also feel very dull at times and the different areas of South America and Afghanistan feel the same, aside from obvious aesthetics. The obvious detracting point of this game is the quite clearly unfinished plot, and while I don't hold it against Kojima and anyone who worked on the game, it does take away a more satisfying conclusion for an otherwise great plot (although I quite enjoyed the ending).

However, these negatives are blown out of the water by the amazing stealth and patented Hideo Kojima flare that makes this game stand as not only a great game, but an extraordinary Metal Gear game that holds its own with the rest of the iconic franchise.

A Hideo Kojima Game.

Now that that's out of the way, this game runs like hot butter on a variety of rigs from what I've seen, and the gameplay design is smooth, intuitive, and flows well in a number of situations. The feeling of growing power as you progress your gear, your Military Company, and Venom Snake's capabilities to deal with ever-escalating threats is palpable. 
The only complaints I have in this game are three: One is that the game seems to prefer console-style gamepads to keyboard/mouse, and thus it was initially difficult to figure out the controls for that control format. Second: Konami seems to have forced upon this game a large amount of MMO-style time and resource gating grinding elements to facilitate microtransactions in the form of MB Coin sales to develop resource generator FOBs and speed development timers. Third, and related to the start of this review, Konami very blatantly did not let Kojima finish his game here - the entire third act and finale of the game is outright missing, and the released design footage is clear proof. 

However, these flaws to not detract from the fact that this game is very masterfully crafted, and I would like to pay my respects to all members of Kojima Productions, Present, Past and Future here. 
Thank you for your dedicated work! I wish you all success in your future endeavors. o7

This game has left me with mixed feelings. This was my first introduction to the franchise and I have since become an huge fan and worked my way through most of the back catalog. Having that context has changed how i feel about the game.

easily the best gameplay in the series and the best stealth game i have ever played.
mechanics are deep and constantly provide you with novel and interesting ways to accomplish tasks.

Cons:

The game also does some thematically interesting? things depending on your perspective that seem to interfere cannon and undermine other established story elements. Personally I don't have a huge issue with this but along with the lackluster story in this game compared to the rest of the series and that development I can see why people do. 

Verdict:

Despite its flaws this is still one of the best games I have ever played. I have 100% the game and played in excess of 200 hours at the time of writing this review. The core gameplay is so incredibly strong that I am willing to overlook many of the games flaws. Where Kojima had previously delivered linear and very directed gameplay experience, this game offers you a set of tools and allows you to craft your own experience.

This is a compelling if deeply flawed game. Performance is smooth, and still looks good nearly a decade later. The level of detail here is insane at points.

Story-wise, it is one of the most interesting and frustrating games I've played. Kojima's dynamic use of the camera during the cut scenes, and the narrative's brave stance to actually question the military industrial complex and the horrifying forces of ethno-nationalism that underpin it are impressive (Something COD and others would never do). There's some genuinely confrontational/borderline horror movie stuff in this game and as a writer I'm really impressed with a game this big actually going there.

However the storY padded as hell (Half of Act one in Afghanistan could have been cut back considerably) and Kojima's script lacks subtlety at numerous points. At some points I was amazed and stunned about what was happening on screen but probably not for the reasons Kojima intended.
 
Also, yeah there's no ending (Due to publisher drama) so i'd recommend finishing the game at the end of ACT I (Still 30 hrs by that point). It's not totally complete, but it's better than the non ending we've got. 

Gameplay-wise it's one of the most dynamic stealth action games i've played. Tonnes of options, smart A.I and at least half of the campaign missions are really great. Unfortunately the side quests are padded, repetitive and grindy. 

Two recommendations. Turn off reflex mode (Slo-mo) and use the tranquilizer gun as little possible. More challenging that way.

Honestly worth a play, and not a bad a game, just a deeply flawed one. 
7/10

Bottom line: I hate it. 
Actually, that's the top line. 
Here's the thing: The first 60 minutes is essentially a long series of civilians being brutally murdered one after the other with all the gory brains splattering outside their bodies, mixed with some weird superstitious nonsense. I kept thinking: when does this 'game' actually start?? Once it does start, it's more like looking for needles in a haystack than an action-packed spy thriller. 

I read that this iteration of the series actually has fewer cutscenes than the previous ones. Really? That means that the previous ones must have been 99% cutscenes.  It's such a shame,  there is so much effort and detail and work that goes into all these cutscenes, but in the end they feel both never-ending and totally meaningless. review_text:
Phantom Pain is one of the most ambitious and well-realized stealth action games of all time.
-
Takes place between MGS Ground Zeroes and the original Metal Gear, Phantom Pain tells you the story, through the eyes of Punished Venom Snake, of his missions to rebuild Outer Heaven and defeat the main Villain, Skullface. Traditional to Hideo Kojima's games, there are a lot of weird/ fantasy and scifi stuffs going on in the game despite having a gritty story and a lot of military elements based on (or inspired by) real life armed forces and conflicts.
-
The game's structure is a massive change from traditional MGS games. There are 2 big open world maps that you can roam around in, with side and main missions taking place in. It can take up to 20-30 hours to finish the main story line, and around the same amount on top to clear the list of side missions. The game also has an important but a simple RPG system of your base's stats. By recruiting soldiers into your base, you will gradually grow your base's strength and unlock perks that will aid you on your missions as well as develop equipment and weapons for you to use. So capturing soldiers rather than killing them is highly encouraged.
-
The moment-to-moment gameplay in Phantom Pain is very well polished, character movement is responsive and button layout works great. The mechanics that are included in stealth are realistic and make sense, but not too punishing for a videogame. Enemy AI's adapt to player's tactics over the course of the game (wearing gas masks to be immune to gas and smoke, wearing helmets to negate headshots, etc.) which really spices up the gameplay and make the experience more immersive. Individual AI works great too, soldiers with poor training can only spot close-range targets and aren't very attentive to abnormal situations, Meanwhile soldiers with good stats can spot the player from longer range and react to hostile elements quickly. Enemies do check on each other and can notice that their buddies have gone missing. It is safe to say that Phantom Pain's stealth gameplay is one of the most satisfying, realistic, immersive, and fun experiences you can have from a game of this genre.
-
There is also FOB infiltration gamemode where players can invade and steal other player's resources, this acts as the persistent pvp-ish mode in Phantom Pain and is completely optional, but I highly recommend giving it a try.
-
It's a shame that Phantom Pain's development was forcefully halted before it was properly finish. The last chapter of the story was cancelled, leaving the ending somewhat unsatisfying.
-
Overall Phantom Pain has a ton of content for you to sink into. The story is interesting and the gameplay is among the best of the genre. It can get repetitive and dragged out by the long story line and side missions, but the refined stealth gameplay is worthwhile enough to keep playing it all the way through.

review_text:
Lots of challenging missions. Timing is key to slip between enemy patrols and ace missions. Getting that perfect shot is satisfying and a relief. There is no other game where you can get that feeling of close call after close call, where the difference between a perfect rating and a mission failed is a split second, and finally your chopper comes, you pile the prisoners you saved into it, and the tense soundtrack fades into a heroic & uplifting one as you fly off. Everything falls quiet on a black screen, and then your after action report comes up. You did it - perfect score.

This is a great game to just take a step at a time and enjoy. If you're new to the stealth genre, this game will be tough on you, but there are some "training wheels" that will help you understand exactly when you made a certain mistake. It will reward you for not needing those training wheels anymore when you no longer need them.

The experience is well rounded, immersive, and fulfilling, and the gameplay itself is solid and speaks for itself. Most of the fun is in the main missions, even if the story and characters are a bit eye-rolly (at times ludicrous even by Metal Gear standards). Some of the boss designs are a bit annoying, but if anything gives you trouble, you'll eventually get the hang of it, or find some trick you didn't know about yet. 90% of the game is focused on stealth action rather than these boss fights anyway.

I bought this game for $5 or $6 when it went on sale, but I would have paid full price for it. I've only just finished the main story a day or two ago, and I still plan to replay a lot of the missions to get my score up, use new weapons and tactics, or complete tasks I missed the first time around.

MGSV runs very well on older machines. I played it on a GTX 970 with an i3-4150 processor, did not use an SSD. Very good performance and basically instant load times.

I like it when a game has a cooperative mode but it's rare to see that nowadays. MGSV gives you some seriously powerful buddies, your ace in the hole; if you had to play without them and instead with another player, it would probably still be a very challenging, satisfying game, where timing and precision are paramount to your success.

Everyone should give the game a go at some point, and enjoy it for what it is: one of the best stealth action games of all time.

review_text:
A Phantom Pain indeed
One of the most addicting games that I've ever played.
Stealth, action, smooth gameplay and plenty of content to delve in. What's not to like?
I originally played this on the PS4 in 2015 for over 100 hours. But I've also got it on PC to try out some of the mods. As usual, it makes the game better.

Overview:
Metal Gear Solid V is the last son of Kojima in the MGS series. You return to the battlefield as Punished Venom Snake, an older and colder Big Boss compared to Metal Gear Solid 3.
Before playing MGS V, I highly recommend you play Ground Zeroes first as it sets up the story and leaves you less confused. The game looks phenomenal, plays great, plenty of things to unlock and cool ways to approach each mission. MGS V is a titan of a game that ended up as a tragedy due to a rushed development with an unfinished story. That being said, the game is still worth every second of your time. If you do care about the story, however, you'll end up being in a bit of a disappointment as MGS V won't hold your hand at all. It won't bother explaining much at all besides repeating some dead points. There's plenty of things, story elements that won't make sense as almost every cutscene and line are throwbacks to an older MGS game. MGS 1,2,3,4 and Peace Walker. If you care about the story, then I highly recommend watching a couple of youtube videos to catch up.  

Positives:
+ Game looks great.
+ A very smooth experience.
+ Addicting gameplay.
+ Interesting ways to tackle each mission, all of them at your disposal. Sneak in, bombard them, use your buddies to help you out, call in a chopper. Pretty much anything you have in mind is indeed possible here.
+ Some great songs can be found on the tapes in this game.
+ It has some really tense but scarce moments in the story.
+ The Mother Base (your own base) can be customised, upgraded, etc. This offers many hours of gameplay.
+ It has two online modes. FOB and MGS Online - Unfortunately, MGS Online lacks players on PC but you can get a few hours of gameplay out of the FOBs which are quite fun ( Essentially you attack other player bases in order to steal their resources or soldiers).
+ Many unique elements that would take too long to elaborate on. But, from the use of weapons, units, buddies, tanks, cars, trucks, rocket launchers, stealth camo, etc, will make most people wish to unlock these options and try out various missions with them.
+ The AI is capable, while not the best, they will react to pretty much any action that you do. They're well voice acted so it keeps the world alive.

Negatives:
- Don't expect a fleshed out story. If this is your first MGS game, most of it won't make sense at all as many of the characters in it were in previous MGS games. That makes it more difficult to care for what's happening.
- Story is left unfinished...yet finished? The game is split into 2 chapters none of which does the game any favours.
- You will be left with a Phantom Pain if you loved this game, as the only thing you'll be left with in the end is the gameplay loop.
- No character development for Snake. The way he starts is the way he ends. The same can be said about every character in this game. This is truly sad for an MGS game.


Final thoughts:
MGS V has many layers to it but you have to dig in deep in order to spot them. The game looks and feels so good that you can't stop playing it after you picked it up even if you're not an MGS fan. But sometimes, along that spectacular gameplay, you wish for a solid story to keep up with it and it simply doesn't do that. What's there isn't enough unfortunately though the beginning of the game may fool you. 
Many people are divided with this game and after playing all of the MGS games, I can easily spot why. 
And yet, it's still worth it. There's no denying that this Phantom Pain is one of a kind. While not the most memorable game of all time, it sure stands in its own league.
Perhaps if they merged Chapter 1 and 2 together while switching a couple of events around, would've worked for a better closure on this franchise. Though leaving it open-ended gives the title of the game a strong meaning.
If you have doubts still: Buy MGS Ground Zeroes on a sale. If you like that, then you'll love MGS V as it's Ground Zeroes but with more content. 
I'll always love this game, personally it's one of my favourites and I always come back to it every now and then...
Why am I still here...?

Now I can say that i am a pretty seasoned Metal Gear fan. I've played all of the original games, loved the hell out of Metal Gear Solid 3 and played through 4 in a single day (crazy I know). Jumping into this game i was really excited to see what Metal Gear Solid in an open world could achieve and let me just say, i was plesently surprised. 
To start off i want to talk about what i like about the game (so far in my playthrough). I love the open-world aspect as it lets you combat your missions in a variety of ways. You could use your sniper rifle and take out the gaurds from afar, or you can sneak in and take out the gaurd's one by one quietly. I also really like the Mother Base aspect and how when you develop your base you can unlock more weapons to develop. I love the characters as well. Ocelot is an amazing side-character and Miller is extremely well written (i mean he can still feel his arm and leg). Quiet, although she has no voicelines in the entire game is really well written and her relationship with Snake is really good.

review_text:
9/2/20 
Metal Gear Solid V is the last Kojima entry in the Metal Gear saga, and it is sadly the worst one in the series other then Survive. MGSV:TPP was rushed out mid-development due to the Kojima / Konami debacle that resulted in Silent Hills being Cancelled, and that caused this whole game to be an casualty due to them being forced to release early, and it destroyed the game's plot and structure, along with it's gameplay systems. You can blame Konami 100% on this game, as it's just completely unfinished and full of filler missions and padded gameplay to extend the playtime, and has somewhat broken mechanics. But the game is still pretty awesome, with 2 Open-worlds to explore (that's kinda dead) and full customization and Mother Base systems, along with Online play, it's still pretty fun. But the game just feels kinda sad.

Story : MG is known for it's rich story and War-type mentality. This game was ment to be HUGE, but it's so sad how the plot was mangled and had tons of things cut from it.
MSGV takes place after Ground Zeroes, and follows an wounded Snake after an 9 Year Coma, where he wakes up, survives the attack of an XOF Agent in a hospital under siege with the help of an man in bandages. After escaping the Hospital with an Nemesis-kinda dude after you, you meet Ocelot, who helps you get back to the new Motherbase. He introduces you to the systems, and then your off to rescue Miller from Russian soldiers. After rescuing Miller, your sent to do tasks to rebuild Motherbase and go after XOF after the events of 5. There is SO MUCH filler in the plot. Like, things you would see as End-game Time wasters are shoved as Main Missions that you have no choice of doing because they didn't have time to finish the main missions, resulting in the Central-plot missions probably only being 2-4 hours long.
The bad part is that Snake does not talk at all, or very little. This was because Kiefer was ment to come in to record lines but they had to cut it short and he only recorded half his lines in the plot and they had to scrap almost all the recordings and remove the face-movement, hense why he seems so deadpan sometimes.
Now onto Spoilers, skip this unless you wanna read.
--
The plot centers around XOF and an Vocal Parasite, which will wipe the English Language off Earth, for some reason. It's never really explained and it's just big bad enemy doing evil things I guess, but the plot-sense is extremely dark. The theme of the game is oppresive, and an War is Bad mentality. You got Child Soldiers in the plot, enemies who would rather kill everything they see then think, and Nanomachines slowing becoming an thing. The antagonist, Skull Face, is never seen much in the game either, and there is no other antagonists like the other games. Like, if you expected like MGS3 with multiple antagonists with different patterns, nope. 
There's an thing about this game's ending which is neat, and ties into MG1, which is The Boss, 
He's not Snake.
The ending is where your actually the Medic from the crash in GZ. He was burned badly, and had surgery to look like the Boss, and fill his role, for some reason or another while the real Snake escapes and lives his own life. It's dumb, but I don't care for it much, as it's what Kojima envisioned. There is an cut ending that came with the Collectors Edition called "Episode 51" and involved Liquid's evolution but all that's left is 2 cutscenes on a disk, and an cut chapter 9 called "Peace", but all that's left is a titlecard. 
There is hints of this game being an Alternate Reality though, as the intro, you die but it suddenly snaps back to the cutscene before the assassin chokes you out.
--
The plot gets an 5/10. It's dumb, and full of padded gameplay. But it's fine I guess if your an fan, as there is an little of MGS charm in it, but the game just feels lacking and is more of just "Oh it's artistic". 

Gameplay :
MGSV plays in Thirdperson and is mainly Stealth oriented. And it's Openworld. Yes, an Openworld Metal Gear game. The game is not Fully Openworld, and it's kinda Lifeless but it's an openworld. There's 3 maps to explore (Afghanistan, Central Africa and Motherbase), and it's mostly just an huge terrain with Animals and Bases around, and empty villages that seemed like it had something in it at one point but was just scrapped, along with AI that is kinda, meh. It's recycled from Ground Zeroes, but they are pretty smart. But if your expecting some hightech AI where they are like "What is that smell?" and stuff, nope. That's not here.
The game features and Buddy system (3 Character Followers total, an 4th being an robot that has no bonding rank), and all of them are Unique. You got
> D-Horse
An Horse. That's it. You can ride on him, and do commands such as Poop, sprint, and follow. 
> Quiet 
An highly suggestive (and has been used in R34 to death) sniper, who used to work for XOF, but defected and works along side you. She is mainly just an faraway scout that will headshot enemies for you and take supportive fire. She has weapon customization, and outfits to choose. 
> D-Dog (DD)
An lonely 1-Eyed Wolf Pup Venom extracts to Motherbase, and Ocelot looks after for you. He is an dog, and acts like such.  He has an variety of outfits, and movesets, along with customization for some outfits.
> Walker Gear
An mini-metalgear! Enemies use them, and you can too. It has no bonding system, and it's an small mech that you can customize with guns and attachments. 

And this game has weapon customization, and it's actually really good surprisingly, and indepth. Day 1 had the WORST and most broken systems though, IE where you could put Shotgun magazines to Revolvers and put Pistol Clips on Snipers. It was so bad, it was patched and fixed up, and it's way more refined now. Although, the game is pretty decent, and is fun to mod.

And there is Motherbase systems like in Peacewalker. You can fulton soldiers, assign certain ranks, and expand bases. And even build nukes (Which will make you instantly an demon with the Karma system), and with the Invasion system, players can go in and steal it from you. 
Gameplay gets an 8/10. It actually is fun, but the whole game just feels weird and an bit jank.

Online :
MGSV didn't have just an singleplayer. Like MGS4, PW and Portable Ops, this game has an Online mode. 
Metal Gear Online 2.
It's dead. You'll find an few servers here and there but it's kinda dormant.
Konami ditched support, and there has been no updates since 2016 to it, but there is some neat stuff, such as Character Customization, Weapon systems coming back, lots of gamemodes and maps, and also throwbacks to older games with a selectable soundtrack.
--
You can play as your MGO character in Singleplayer also, you just have to complete the game. Whoever you made as the MGO character, is Medic in the plot.
--
Online gets an 6/10. It's fine, just hard to find anyone anymore.

Final Verdict is an 4/10.
The game is really good in the gameplay department, but the game is just full of filler and does not have that MGS charm to it. Like, Rising plays more like an Metal Gear game then this sadly.
If Konami gave Kojima another year or as much time as he wanted to finish this game, it could have been great, but it's just an released, touched up Debug Build of what MGSV could have been. It's really sad, knowing this is the last MG game in the series, even though Hideo has been wanting to end it since 4, this is the last true entry. Hopefully Konami outsources or sells the property so the series continues (Like an actual MG game, not Survive which sold worse then Darkness 2.) but an Metal Gear fan can dream. I say try it out if your curious, but if your looking for an true Metal Gear game on PC, go try Rising or download an copy of MGS2 off an random site since the PC version is Abandonware (No idea how it would work on Windows 10). Or invest in an 360/PS3 and get the HD Collection or get the other titles on PS3, because Konami will never release MGS-HD on PC.

I'm sure actually playing the game is fun, but you have to jump through so many hoops to get there, that I don't think it's worth it. review_text:
I'm very torn about my review of MGSV: TPP because there are some truly standout experiences and gameplay features gamers will enjoy...but the game is just unfinished in so many areas that I cannot recommend it to anyone that isn't a hardcore Metal Gear fan and is well aware of the lore.  I've briefly listed strengths and weaknesses about the game:

Strengths:

The gameplay is excellent - the ability to go entirely stealth or guns blazing makes approaching missions unique.  Additionally, leveling up items and researching new equipment continuously makes you want to try new strategies.

Graphics - I ran this on 2060 and it looks fantastic.  Cutscenes are slick and the game ALWAYS runs at a smooth 60 fps.  The lighting, weather and other atmospheric effects are excellent and it certainly adds to the immersion the game wants you to feel

Buddies - The ability to bring along buddies is another unique feature to this game that I found very enjoyable.  You can bring either a mech, dog, a sniper, etc to join you on mission.  Although I found some buddies to more useful than others (D-Dog FTW) and others just odd (Quiet - in terms of appearance and gameplay use) this was a great feature implemented to the game and it provides a ton of replay

Base building - Capturing soldiers, resources, etc to improve your base is awesome.  It's so cool to see it grow from a dinky platform into all these different research areas with soldiers walking.  Finding soldiers during missions that can improve your base also makes it very fun!

Weaknesses

Missions - You will do a ton of extraction and elimination missions.  Mission objectives are repeated too much and you will constantly visit the same area over and over and over again.  Yes, sometimes they may be a bit more challenging, and there may be a boss fight, but you won't really do much outside of extract or eliminate

Story - Honestly, it's just a mess.  The fans on Reddit, Youtube and other sites really helped to explain it and provide value/context but without this...holy s$%t will you be lost. Also, the pacing is very poor imo - the last 3 missions things really start to happen but that's like 40+ hours into the game.  I'd encourage anyone to research the fallout between Kojima and Konami because I'm sure that had to do with it.

Story  - The game is essentially repetitive, so I'll make this point repetitive too.  It's a mess and very difficult to understand/appreciate without researching the lore.

Base Building - While a lot of fun....you have to put a lot of time into maintaining it.  Soldiers get sick, fights breakout, resources get low, the base gets invaded, etc...it's a lot.  Also, I found myself constantly returning to base which broke up the pace at which i wanted to play the game.

Overall, it's a lot of fun.  For casual players - grab it on a sale.  For MG fans - get it right away because you'll understand and appreciate the references and gameplay

Metal Gear Solid V is quite possibly the best stealth-action game I've ever played.
It has near flawless gameplay, a fantastic and bizarre Hideo Kojima story you've come to know and love from the Metal Gear series, and incredibly beautiful graphics.

Half of act two is just previous missions with a difficulty tweak, and act three is non-existent due to Konami's rushed development.
Act one however... is simply flawless, in my opinion.

The open-world style gameplay is a new approach for the Metal Gear series, and it executes it perfectly. There is so much depth to the gameplay mechanics, it makes every mission and outpost infinitely replayable.

All in all, this game is a masterpiece despite missing a good third of its original intended length.
Just imagine if Kojima got the chance to fully finish development.

A rather nice game. Everyone knows, that this game could have been the final love letter to the Metal Gear-Series. Instead it became the forefront of one of the bigger gaming controversies: Kojima vs Konami. The less said about that, the better it should be (#♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥). The Story of the game is unfinished, but there are some really good scenes in the game. But you really shouldn't buy or play this game for the story or the atmosphere, you play it for the gameplay, and that is quite good in this piece of software. You have a lot of options when it comes to taking out your adversaries. These options can be either explored or you stick to one little gimmick you enjoy. it strays far from ye' ole' metal gears. You have to harm some people and are discouraged from sneaking through enemy lines completely undetected. The base-building means for you, that you need people ASAP and it is rewarding to find some good personal up-and-about.

review_text:
I've suffered through a lot of games which felt like distractions rather than entertainment. I felt obligated to complete them, as if it were my job or some sort of meaningful accomplishment. MGS5 reminded me what it felt like to be genuinely excited to play a game. I was surprised that I enjoyed the gameplay so much, when Metal Gear games are usually more story driven.

Pros:
* Gameplay stands apart from most other games - stealth and even combat feels different in a good way
* Deep plot (though probably not the best in the series)
* Fox engine is great - I wish more games used it
* The game looks beautiful, and small features like water glistening on skin really make visuals stand out
* A ridiculous amount of features and tricks (the "horn" on your head grows if you kill a lot, enemies sleep at night, you can shoot out lights, you can add pictures to cardboard boxes to lure enemies etc.)
* Controls can be somewhat odd but strangely easy to get used to
* Works great with a controller
* The base building aspect really adds some variety and longevity to gameplay
* You can pause cutscenes
* A decent selection of "buddies", each having their own strengths
* Smart AI difficulty which adapts to the way you play
* The many upgrades to your base, weapons etc. will keep you busy
* Quiet is cool
* Lots of side missions and an online component which create a decent endgame
* Night and day, along with a weather system affects gameplay

Cons:
* Chapter 1 was great but Chapter 2 was a mess. It would have been better to include all critical story elements in Chapter 1 and wrap up the entire story
* Helicopter rides take way too long - you're often forced to sit through long chopper rides, or wait for supply drops etc.
* Too many minor features which probably took a lot of development time away from creating missions/ story (you could lean sideways on your horse to avoid enemy detection, you could climb cracks, you need to wash off blood to feel mentally and physically refreshed, morale system for soldiers in your base, the horse can poop and enemies will slip on it)
* Maxing out upgrades takes very long - you'll be way past the the end of the story before you start getting the best items in the game, and by then you won't really need them
* It takes too long to gather resources and earn in-game currency
* Weapons, supplies and even the helicopter all cost in-game currency. It doesn't usually make much sense to max out the items you carry. It also defeats the purpose of upgrading items, since they then cost more to equip
* Bad fast travel system
* Side ops are trickled in, stretching out the amount of time you'll take to complete them

La novità più eclatante di questo capitolo è la gestione delle navi con equipaggio.

La qualità delle quest primarie e secondarie è sempre di alto livello come ci ha abituato da tempo obsidian,come osare di pretendere di più?
Se non fosse chiaro,non c'è nessun aspetto dove poe2 risulti inferiore al primo capitolo.

Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain is not only the most "game-y" of the Metal Gear series, but it is actually so good that it outshines all the others in both good and bad.  For those new to the series, you'll DEFINITELY want to pick this one up first.  (I haven't played Ground Zeroes yet.)

First off, those lengthy cutscenes that get drawn out more and more for each main MG game actually serve a purpose as they make you feel like you're a fly on the wall and actually feel like you're there in all the gritty universe this game sets itself in. You're not just sitting back and watching 2 characters in action or talk or hearing long speeches.  In fact, the cutscenes are actually short, simple, and to the point with hardly any dialogue. And yes, you can skip them if you like (which will probably be necessary anyway if you want to replay certain missions).  All the expository dialogue is communicated via cassette tapes which are ENTIRELY optional if you so choose to listen to them.

Second, I haven't had this much fun infiltrating a base in years since the first MGS1 game.  You can do anything to your heart's content and ANYTHING can happen ANYTIME.  Want to go it alone?  You can?  Want to change the weather?  You can.  Want to go in guns blazing? You can!  It's all there and fun to enjoy.

But for every improvement this game has from its predecessors, there's always the bad, but I won't go in too much detail as it's basically been said before: cut and repetitive missions, voice actors not returning for their roles (except f**king Otacon, I always hated him in MGS!), wonky controls, etc. etc.  The only REAL issue I have is that you don't start any missions with a FULL CLIP of ammo.  Every gun you have has 1 bullet less of a full clip.  How the hell do you mess that one simple programming error!?

But other than that, this game is worth getting on sale for the Definitive Experience.  I managed to get it for only $9.98!  How can you beat that!?

This game is good, but there are some major inconveniences that keep it from being great. I'm probably in the minority here, but I actually think Ground Zeroes is the better game in the MGS V chronology. That's not to say this game is bad - it's not - this installment just tends to be much more frustrating than its predecessor. In terms of storytelling, this game is top-notch (of course it is, it's MGS after all), but there are a handful of things that bug me to no end:

First off, the easiest way to score an S rank on missions is to run in guns blazing and not worry about being spotted or shot at by enemies. Speed is the name of the game here, which is disappointing for a series that defines stealth gameplay. 

Second, the maps are too big for no good reason. If you were rewarded for exploration or if the enemy bases served a purpose other than farming resources, then the enormous size of the maps would be justified. As it stands however, the amount of time you spend travelling from point a to point b is tiresome. Overall, the worlds feel empty and the repopulating outposts are more of a nuisance than anything.

Lastly, some missions are frustrating to the point of wanting to rip your hair out...not because they demand a high level of skill and preparation, but because they seem to be up to luck more than anything. Every time you see the words Skulls, Mist, or Parasite in your mission intro, prepare to have a bad time. Combine that nuisance with the baffling decision to lock the true ending behind more difficult reskins of past missions, and you will start to resent the amount of time you've put into the game.

If you ignore the baffling insistence of going in guns blazing all the time, and you can be bothered to look up tips and tricks for completing the most obnoxious missions, then you'll be rewarded with a solid stealth shooter. Just don't expect it to stack up to the rest of the MGS catalog.
