review_text:
The game isn't bad per se. EDIT: oh god yes it is. All in all, it's a less well done Far Cry.
The problems start with the intro. The whole hour of intro mission is neither really connected to the rest of the game, at least not as far as I came yet, and it's "Cutscene: The game". for each 5 minutes of gameplay, there are 10 minutes of cutscenes. There are nonsensical things galore, like sprinklers not starting despite the fire all around but suddenly doing so when the main char (not you, as you can't play that part) shoots them, or people, not superhuman ones, being ablaze and still pretty determined to move towards the character, again in a cutscene.

Later in the game, many problems arise because it's an awful port. For example, in the menu, switching from one category to the next has you press the 1 and 3 number keys instead of, you know, using the mouse. Switching weapons in game can also only being done the same way, using the mouse wheel is way too novel a concept. In fact, the mouse wheel has no use at all, not for zooming (with weapons), not for switching, not for scrolling in menus, only for zooming with your binoculars.
The other things are mosty small problems that amass. Enemies being able to shoot you with an AK47 at a distance where you have problems hitting them with a sniper rifle, not being able to jump without any AC-style freerunning, having to slowly walk (or horsey ride) vast distances which are often long for no reason, like in your own base, because there's no usable fast travel system (there is a way with the copter, but it requires you to first go to the 'aerial command centre' and all in all takes ages), a checkpoint system that has it's checkpoints so weirdly set that I had to repeat 3 side missions at once because saving between them never occured to the devs (why can't console ports give us free save FFS?) and so on.
One last thing that bugged me were so many cutscenes that had cool stuff to play in them that would be playable in any game but this one.

Let me give you an example: There I was trying to go to a side mission. What looked like a way to squeeze in between two mountains wasn't so I had to use a huge detour. Suddenly at one place I was stopped dead in my tracks because a sniper shot at me, which started a main mission, 11, while I was at 6 or so. This in and on itself wouldn't be that bad, I would just have liked a warning because, well, I was trying to do the side mission. Anyway, a fight later and the dilemma of letting the sniper live or kill them comes up. Ocelot and a Miller (which I don't remember, maybe he appears in a mission between 6 and 11) both take the opposite position and tell me to kill or capture them respectively. I decided.. I decided for jack sh*t because the game didn't let me decide, it was all in a cutscene. After putting them in a copter, I ride off towards the side mission I was planning to do on my trusty steed. As soon as I leave the area, a cutscene played and the horse transformed in a copter, aparently, because I was flying it with the sniper. A jet attacks. All the while I was like "grab that friggin mounted machine gun already and let me shoot it!" Quite a while later, snake doesn't seem to be too fast on the uptake, he did grab the gun. And fell over. And grabbed it again. And fell again. And the same thing yet again. As so often in the game, I was screaming at the screen 'get ON with it!". Alas, instead of a sequence where I was shooting at the jet and letting loose flares when a rocket came, which would have been sweet.. none of that happened. it was all just a cutscene.

It's like that several times through the game.

The good parts of the game are pretty much points you could make about far cry. I enjoyed far cry so that's great, but it didn't feel any different. 

To wrap it up, MSG V is NOT a bad game. but it is way less than I expected from the hype.
Why do I downvote it when I didn't think it was crap, you might ask. It's because steam gives me just the absolutes of recommend or don't recommend, no neutral. I'd do neither if someone asked me. But I'd probably say something like "get far cry instead", which is pretty much equal to "not recommend"

EDIT having played some more:
The game is repetative as all hell.
You have a pool of like 5 different side objectives, basically all "kill all of them" or "rescue that guy" or "optain that ressource". Stuff like "Eliminate the heavy infantry" and "eliminate the tank command" are really the same, just one with tanks, so I don't count them as different.
You have a whopping 157 of them. And they all play in the same ~20 bases/towns, and for most of them, the bases are just restocked with the default staff and a prisoner put somewhere or a "highly skilled soldier" is among them (fun fact, nearly every time, that one was less skilled than all his buddies, aparently because it was skilled for the starting hero level you have, even if ou just unlock that side mission way further in the game. The game is riddled with such little problems, as I said).
Hell, you even have stuff like "extract a guy from OKB0" and as soon as you get back to the chopper, you get a new side mission: extract a guy from OKB0!
Ths one really got on my nerves as that base is freaking huge and as soon as you finally managed to get through it, you have to do this again.

You do the ame stuff time and time and time again, it's just artifically prolonging the game. 

Also, the game punishes you for not going non-lethal. That would have been kinda OK, if all he non-lethal weapons didn't suck and people wouldn't wake up from tranquilizers way too fast. I spent much money developing a stunning assault rifle only to find out, not only is it not silenced, I can't put on any silencer from any other gun, making it pretty useless. Maybe the version of the gun at higher levels has it, but I had already go to level 5 or so just to get it non-lethal.
One time I tranqued two guys from like 15m away and before I got to them they woke up again because a tank beeped its horn for no reason (I wasn't discovered, neither were they, putting them to sleep again I could even extract them without someone noticing). There's not a single thing that will keep them knocked out. I like to clean out bases, but as soon as the base is a bit bigger, there's no chance to do that.
but if you go lethal, you get less score, less "hero points" which means worse staff and on top of it, you get a bloody skin permanently put on your char. Game, why don't you let me play the way I see fit? Why give me 90% lethal weapons and tanks and stuff if I can't even use them? Why do you make non-lethal weapons so bad?

So, after putting more time in the game, I'm a bit of a completionist or I would just not care about the side ops, I can recommend this game even less than before. play far cry, it may not have 157 side missions, but those it has are actually a bit different from each other

Some other edit:
If you plan to play the game anyway, research the CGM rocket launcher and the battle suit as highly as possible. Because if you play stealth and ignored those, the game ♥♥♥♥♥ you over royally.
There is a mission near the end, one that you get booted into without preparation because it's started by a side mission (beware of side mission 150), in which you'll be put against an army of tanks.
You cannot prepare for this mission, because you were not aware it was gonna start. You get in this mission with whatever you've had when you did side op 150. You cannot quit this mission, like any other, by going back to the chopper. You cannot research the stuff you need and do some side missions. you cannot exit this mission no matter what you do, and it's probably the hardest mission up to then.  and airdropping your best RL doesn't mean a thing when it's a bad one.

There is also no audio mixer apart from adjusting tapes/music volume but that's a minor issue.

Most of the story is the usual high production value cinematic nonsense but not in a cheesy fun way, just a "takes itself too seriously" way (but it is still very enjoyable).
It's quite disappointing that they got Kiefer Sutherland to voice snake but he says very little throughout a lot of the game.

review_text:
Utterly ridiculous, vulgar, irreverent, laughable, and shameless: Metal Gear Solid V. In it, doctors perform hypnosis and plastic surgery on a medic loyal to the PF corporation commander Venom Snake so he can create Outer Heaven, a utopia of warriors with “No greater good. No just cause.” In the words of his enemy, Skull Face: 

The chain of retaliation is what will truly bind this world together as one … Sans lingua franca, the world will be torn asunder. And then, it shall be free. People will suffer, of course - a phantom pain. The world will need a new common tongue. A language of nukes. My Metal Gears shall be the thread by which all countries are bound together, in equality. No words will be needed. Every man will be forced to recognize his neighbor. People will swallow their pain. They will link lost hands. And the world will become one. This war is peace. 

This game is, undoubtedly, a masterpiece. The gameplay is incomparable. Every subtle shift in the route of an enemy, the redirecting of a turret, the coming of dawn is fluid and graceful--something lacking in many other stealth games. In MGSV, time seems to condense and expand at the sight of a chopper, a trigger, or the sudden recognition of red light blinking discretely in the foliage--blink, blink; be careful. But more importantly, the game is weird. No, absurd. It has the je ne sais quoi one sometimes witnesses in a certain an image, a 10-second sound, a story--anything, but very few things. This has it. It gives the deep impression of a long past and a bad future. Something bigger always seems hidden from view, poised, but ready to crash down at any moment. It seems important, that something deeply unsettling are at the center of Snake's actions. People complain about the story. The story is not about events, but a certain feeling or fear that lingers. Moreover, this game is deeply melancholy. Motherbase is silent except for the mechanical whirr of helicopters and the bark of a soldier. It has long, dead avenues. This game regrets life, but lives it to the fullest. MGSV is, in the best sense, a somber paradox. It is adolescent and immature on the surface, but has unintended valleys and trenches. People complain about the story because it seems giddy and cheap. Life is cheap.

review_text:
// Alright, I just realised somehow I'm writting more and more in each review, I don't know why I feel I should explain what I meant. Maybe it's me getting old. Also, before you read on, spoiler alert.

Talking about old, MGS series certainly is. The last major canon was literally about getting old. And it sucked! so hard.
But this game is solid! (see what I did thar) 

p.p.s. I don't know why the game keeps titling 'solid' even though we all know the most interesting character in the genre is Big Boss (and maybe Ocelot too).

This review is a comparative opinion on the series, with highlight of this game.

The series spans decades and multiple shifts in style, both in gameplay and story-telling. There are ups and downs. This game, MGS5, is definitely an Up.

The Up is firstly the gameplay, this game plays like a modern action game: with enough degrees of freedom, a sense of streamlined action to consequence feedback loop and impactful tactical elements. Previously in gameplay, either it was too tactical or non-actionable. 

Next Up, is story, the essence of MGS. Story is a sum of plots and character. We have plots deepening since the MGS1 but the characters start to shine when the serie take a look at Big Boss in Snake Eater. In TPP we get to witness a few fantasitic, lively characters that previous MGS games don't even have the materials for. In my opinion, the MGS series ended with Sons of Liberty in New York Manhatton. That game was more about philosophy than story, and was certainly entirely about post-modernism. The lack of character was on purpose. However Konami drags on to Guns of the patriots, so Kojima fill up all the plot holes to justify the drag. The TPP, however, has all the freedom it needs because it's not about Solid Snake the uninteresting, but the confounded yet determined 'freedom' warrior Big Boss (alert, there is a catch). So the character is a real person, flesh and blood real: we get to experience the bloody path he walks, understand his mission and give out sympathy as a human being. Drama, is an upgrade to this genre.

Finally, style. The setting sets the style. Blizzard (not the company) sets the tone for MGS1,  Ocean and sense of Isolation sets for MGS2, Jungle for 3 and Sand and Savanna for 5. There are limited factors in previous works that those settings are not well presented and resonated in the game but for TPP, with open world (somewhat) mechanism, they form a good synergy and it plays great.

At the end, MGS5 TPP is a fun game to play and thus time flies. 

p.p.p.s. I need to bash MGS4 before I hit the submit button. That game tarnished the MGS legacy, although I enjoyed the clichés and the plugged plot holes... But come on, MGS2 was an art. MGS4 was a forced interpretation of the said art.

God I can't believe it's been 9 years...  

Being that this was my first MGS game, I originally gave this game a negative review, because despite the game-play (largely) being fun, I also thought the story was a mess. 

A couple years later, and after beating the other games, I decided to play MGS 5 again, and my mind has been changed.
I won't say that the game is an utter masterpiece, it still feels a bit under-cooked, but as a final product I do see where the game was headed.  Especially since the game exists as both a sequel and a prequel... which is quite perplexing.  

The problem with talking about a game like this is that on the surface it seems lacking in substance, presented as a militaristic semi-sci-fi-fantasy game that pays homage to 80s action flicks and American culture.  In reality, the game contains layers and layers of coherent themes and subtext that are otherwise harder to understand if you have never been exposed to the other games, and if you otherwise ignored listen the to cassette tapes that you unlock.  Such themes include:

- The cold war 
- Nuclear deterrence (Remember, the game was created by a man whose country was hit by nukes... twice)
- Militarism and nationalism
- Colonialism
- language
- identity

I also really liked the twist.  I've always known about it, pretty much since the game came out, but the way that they revealed it by just recontextualizing the prologue was really satisfying.  

Least to say, I'd recommend playing the game.  If not for the story, than at least for the gameplay.  The way the game plays is really deep, like immersive sims level deep, and how you control Snake is really nice and snappy.  Just running around feels good.

review_text:
Although MGS V may not have as much of a well developed story as many of its predecessors, its still a fantastic experience i would highly encourage everybody to play. For anybody unaware, Metal gear solid V: The Phantom Pain is a sequel to MGS: Peacewalker and a prequel to MGS 1, featuring hugely different gameplay to other metal gear solid games and an heavy emphasis on freedom while maintaining signature mechanics of previous games, and further developing Metal Gear Solids  lore while attempting to make sense of many plot elements and character arks.

The gameplay in MGS V feels far smoother and more modern than any other game in the franchise, while implementing a massive list of interesting and useful game mechanics that can be used to carry out the games massive amount of missions all accessible from the I droid, which is the players way of controlling the many variables of there very own mother base and developing a vast number of weapons and items to bring into the field. This includes a very interesting staff management mechanic that allows the player to extract targets in the field to be recruited as soldiers, much like the system from MGS: Peacewalker. Snake has a vast array of options when completing missions in mgs v, as the game is now fully open world, allowing the player to enter outposts and fulfill objectives in which ever manner they see fit. This make the game feel far less linear than previous entries in the series and allows the player to experiment to their hearts contents. Another new feature in MGS V is the buddy system, which allows players to recruit and fight along side a Sniper, a Dog, a horse, and a robot, which ads a new dimension to gameplay and allows for even more play styles while allowing the player to form a bond with your buddies.

MGS V's story is where the game starts to fall apart. Although the first chapter of the game is fantastic and the second chapter holds a lot of potential, chapter 2 feels very unfinished and rushed likely due to Konami losing their minds and kicking Kojima out of the team and pushing an early release date due to the projects high costs. This is a massive shame, as it is very clear that there was supposed to be a different ending to the game due to the sudden introduction of copy pasted missions just with a higher difficulty, the sudden ending, and open character threads or character threads with sudden, nonsense conclusions (Paz, Quiet). To make things worse, the physical definitive edition of the game featured massive amounts of unused dialoge and concept art, and even a cutscene from a cut mission that ties up Eli's insulting 
loose threads. Overall I think the story could have been incredible if Kojima productions were given a chance to u know, finish there game by the people over at konami and its a real shame that it ended the way it did.

MGS V's Graphics are still incredibly impressive even today, featuring high detail texture work, realistic shading and great modeling. Overall, there isnt much to say about this games graphics, other than that they add to the games immersion and differentiate the game from other entries in the MGS franchise.

Overall, MGS V is one of my favorite games of all time and I would highly recommend it to anybody. If you are reading this, unsure if you should buy this game, do yourself a favour and do it.

Pretty good game don't get me wrong, but barred by some highly questionable (downright infuriating) design decisions that soured my experience. Since i'm going to give this a bad review, i'll skip over the pro's and give my reasons as to why. As those are the things people will want to read if they agree and thus avoid it. I don't hate the game, but this can't be allowed to continue. And if I give this one a positive review, it will be swamped. I also like to state that it's probably the publisher, Konami, that is at fault for most of these gripes. They seem like tacked-on afterthoughts.

1; the fact that every main mission needs a creditroll. This whole game reeks of Kojima self-congratulating himself at every corner. Be it cameo's in the demo, or having to have his name plastered on the screen every mission. It was fairly obnoxious to be honest.

2: Overly long chopper transitions. Yes you can teleport to ACC, but you still need to wait for the cutscene of the chopper flying and touching down. If you could skip that whole thing, it would speed up the already lengthy playtime.

3: The base management/idroid screen is way, way too cluttered and the whole mechanic of base management I could do without. It's not fun and it's tedious busywork that you have to do in order to get any decent upgrades. It feels like a unncessary barrier between you and the gameplay. 

4: and this basically singlehandedly forced this negative review, the absolutely hamfisted approach to online play. First off, they don't explain what the online mode does, and default it on.
What it does is save about 90% of your GMP (the ingame currency) into a online depository which you can't access in offline mode. It does this every time you launch, sync or play the game in online mode. And it leaves you open to being attacked by online players. What essentially happens is that people just enter your base and steal all your stuff. Meaning you get interrupted in your game and have to either stop the player or get your stuff taken. You can also just use real-world money as insurance (wish I was joking). Chances are, by the time you get invaded by players, and decide you'd much rather play offline, that GMP amount which you lose is going to be substantial. Basicly meaning that they intentionally designed it as ransom mechanic to punish you if you decide to take it offline. 
Now comes the kicker. In order to play offline you need to disconnect in-game via the menu, do something that requires a checkpoint which needs to be synchronised next time the game goes online. Restart the game and decline the UELA license agreement, every single time you launch the game. Otherwise it will always first sync up before you enter the game and reset your online balance. 
Oh, and you can't drain that online GMP without getting a severe hit to base morale. Since you need to go into the red on your main account so it drains the online portion. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, this is some next level villainry if I ever saw one. What were they thinking. To sell those shekelcoins?

5. Another reason to dislike the game are the arbitrary timedelays for upgrades to your base or equipment that can take literal hours before they complete. So if a particular mission would go better with a specific upgrade to your silenced sniper rifle, prepare to do vapid sidequests or exploration for a good hour for that upgrade to finish. And no you can't speed the ingame time to get it to finish. And no it doesn't continue to run the timer if you close the game.  #♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.

6. Resources, especially Fuel, are scarce by design and required in every major base upgrade, again forcing the player to play online and steal it from others. The alternative is grinding ad nauseam for boxes and containers. My current gametime is 125 hours (though probably 50% of that is just idle time) and I still hadn't gotten enough materials to even max out my base. The latest upgrades to your base can take literally hours to grind/farm, and they've even patched in diminishing returns if you try to repeat missions to farm them. How nice of them. #♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.

This game has honestly been the biggest dissapointment to me out of any game i have ever player.  I say that not because its starts out as a terrible game and continues that way.  No, i say this because it is an amazing and beautiful game that murdurs itself at about 30% completion.

Allow me to eleaborate...
 F...O...B's  Forward Operating Bases... These are a multiplayer element introduced by the game to allow player to play together and raid other players.  Thing is, what you do not know, is that you have no choice but to participate in them.  Period.  After you progress so far into the game fob building becomes enabled.  YOU LITERALLY CAN NOT SELECT ANYTHING IN THE MENU BUT THIS AT THIS POINT!  Once built you no longer can progress any further untill you play the multiplayer training.  Again you can not select anything in the menus untill you do so. Personally... i absolutely HATE being forced into something and this has soured my tase for the game.  Top this all off with the fact that while you play online... ALL of your resources are connected to the online.  If you go offline you lose everything.  If you are offline and have already cunstructed an fob.  Then other players can raid your resources and staff.  Everything you have done the grind to achieve.  Again you can be raided even when you are not online so as soon as you connect you lose everything they took anyway.... RAGE!  I have no interest in multiplayer games.  I hate that a wonderfull singleplayer game forces this on you.

Now... that i have finished my rant.  Here is a legitimate review.

Pros:
Most engaging FPS/ stealth game ive played in a long time
Storywise id give a 7/10  It has its moments, enough to keep you interested in it, but it pretty much ASSUMES your viewpont and playes accordingly
The non lethal aspect is a hugely fun deviation from the norm. Love it.
Wonderfull single player experience

Cons: 
Multiplayer is forced upon you
Resource gathering is extremely tedious later in campaign without playing online and garning challenge op rewards (again only reclaimable online)
Once story missions missions are complete you can play them again but at incrementally reduced rewards untill it literally costs you to replay them.  So offline play is reduced eventually to farming secondary ops for gmp untill you have enough to play a fun story mission.. basically game death at this point unless you play multiplayer.

 I for me will keep playing, but i now have lost 26hours of progress so that i can start over without the online bullcrap.

[b]TL;DR[/b] - In my opinion, the story is the worst of the entire series and really insults all that Kojima has done so far, but the gameplay is the absolute best in the series and likely the best of any third person stealth game ever made (as of 2017). However, a lack of any PC support outside of just being able to run on the PC (no mouse support in menus, no FOV changing, button prompts are half controller / half keyboard) further drives the negative vibe I get from this game down to a strong "Do not recommend". Only get this if you plan to play it like a console game but don't own a PS4/Xbox One.

[b]*EDIT[/b] - I should add that I played this on PS4, that is where my knowledge of the game comes from. I got rid of it a while back and thought maybe I would enjoy replaying it on PC, that maybe I could finally give the story another shot and like it more this time around. Unfortunately, the bad PC support and ridiculous opening of the game almost immediately turned me off and I am left not recommending it unless you know what you're getting into.

Gonna keep this one short, because most people probably know what they're getting into at this point.

I'm am/was a HUGE fan of MGS because of the characters and the story, but the story in MGS5 feels like (I'll be humble here; I could be completely wrong) some of the worst story I've seen in a game. It feels like Kojima, in his frustration with Konami, just kind of gave a huge middle finger to players and put zero effort into the story, meanwhile ensuring the expected Metal Gear twist at the end. However, the twist is so insulting that it's actually retroactively made Metal Gear a series that is difficult for me to enjoy anymore. Knowing that Metal Gear Solid 5 exists and is a terrible (imho) cap on an otherwise amazing series is just such a let down that I've lost all interest in playing MGS again, and I routinely play through the entire series most years, sometimes more than once.

That said, the gameplay is probably the best open world / third-person stealth gameplay I've ever played. It's so responsive, it's so varied, the animations are amazing, the amount of things you can actually DO is pretty incredible. The gameplay, for once (come on, until MGS4, the series had ♥♥♥♥ gameplay), is absolutely amazing. But man, that can hardly redeem such inane plot and characters this time around.

On top of all of this, I could PROBABLY get past all the negatives if the PC version was actually a decent port. The ONLY reason you should play this on PC is because you don't own an Xbox One or a PS4, or you intend to run it at 4k. The framerate is 60fps on all platforms, there's no FOV changing, and there's no mouse support during menus. Some of the button prompts in the game also show for the controller, while some will be for the keyboard. It's just a half-assed port that, while able to run well and be played with a controller, doesn't take advantage of ANY of the reasons someone would want to play on a PC over a console. It's basically the console game on PC, and you better expect to play it with a controller and sit 5ft back from your screen unless you can stomach the ridiculously close FOV while crouching and in tight spaces.

It's a shame, because MGS5 has plenty of reasons to be amazing, but story and characters are absolutely not one of them. Also, originally, I was pretty damn stoked for Keifer to voice Snake, and while I think he does a passable job, it highlights the HUGE disconnect MGS5 has with the series; they try to make it hyper realistic while also maintaining the hyper style and goofiness that the series is known for. review_text:
Metal Gear Solid V is a great but very flawed game. I'll divide my review into two sections, gameplay and story.

Gameplay

While it does have the best gameplay in the series, it suffers from the usual problems of open world games. These problems are the open world being fairly empty, and gameplay repetition. MGSV has two big hub worlds, and inside both of them are outposts and more large scale bases, which you can infiltrate. These are all over the map, and in between them are vast expenses of nothing except scenery. This makes the open world kind of pointless, seeing as you only really want to get to the places you can infiltrate. Any time spent in the world besides infiltration is just a time consuming trek from one base to another, and all it really acts as is filler. Now getting to my other point, the repetition. MGSV has 50 main missons, and 37 of them are related to the games story. These missions are unique missions with different objectives, though they do usually share a similar theme of either retrieving a target, or eliminating a target, but this isnt always the case. The other 13 are challenge varations of the missions. I have yet to do them all, but they up the difficulty of past missions, and add a new twist to keep thing interesting. An example being a mission where you have to destroy a target located in an enemy base, but can now only use weapons and items you find while doing the mission. The ones I've played have been extremely fun, and a fresh challenge which still feels new, because of the added difficulty and new mission rules. These 50 main missions are the highlight of the game. Now lets talk about side-ops. Side-ops are very hit and miss. They have similar objectives to the main missions, but with no story. The problem with these side-ops is that they reuse many of the main mission areas, but just reuse them. No new rules or anything, just the same area with a different objective. Also, some side-ops sometimes have you go to random places in the wildermess on the map, only to usually do a quick 3 minute objective. So most of your time doing these ops is just spent traveling. And then the next side-op you want to do could be half-way across the map. So you either travel all the way over there, or call down a helicopter, which acts as the games fast travel and is used to leave the hub world. The problem is this still takes around 3 minutes. You need to travel to a helicopter pick up point, wait for the helicopter to arrive, and then your taken through another loading screen, and after that your finally allowed to pick another destination. Yet even after that you need to wait for the helicopter to make its way to the ground to drop you off. Travel time in this game is simply too long and tedious. So basically, main missions are good and side-ops are pretty boring and very repetitive. Now that I've talked about the basic aspects of the game design that effects the gameplay, I'll discuss solely how the game plays, and it plays beautifully. MGSV gives you so many options in how you can take on these missions, with multiple points of entry in a base and multiple ways to manipulate things inside and around the base. You also have a plethora of weapons which get better and better over time, giving you a great sense if progression. This progression also links with the motherbase building part of the game. This part being building your own mercenary group, Diamond Dogs, along with its base of opeartion. Throughout the game your able use GMP (the games currency) to expand your motherbase, allowing you to obtain more soilders. You obtain new soilders for your base by doing missions and recovering enemy soilders out in the field. You can scan any enemy soilder while in the hub world, check his stats, and knock him out and extract him back to mother base, he'll then be convinced into working for you, and become part of your team. The better people you have, the better your weapon and item arsenal. This is once again great progression, as it incentives not just running and gunning, but carefully considering your options when taking on a mission, as you'll want to maximize your rewards. There's also a multiplayer motherbase invasion mode, where people can invade your base, and you can invade theres, but I've had fairly little experience with this, as I've stuck mostly to the singleplayer, so I have no real opinion on it. So that covers the gameplay, MGSV does have some poor game design choices, along with some bad side-ops, but the gameplay and core 50 missions are more than worth the money, and has some of the best stealth gameplay to ever grace the industry.

Story (No Spoilers)

I've played every canonical Metal Gear game, and story wise, MGSV is the second worst, only beating out MGS: Peace Walker. MGSV's story is made up of two chapters, with chapter one consisting of 30 story missions, and chapter 2 consisting of 7 story missions, along with 13 missions that are past missions with different rules. Chapter 1 is pretty good, it has an interesting story and a solid antagonist. Though its not nearly as good as the other MGS games, its entertaining. The problems begin in chapter 2. Chapter 2 has pacing issues, where story missions just kind of appear after doing other various missions, and it all feels very loosely connected. Like, the ending mission of the game literally comes out if nowhere, and has absolutely no build up. Though I do like the ending itself and I think it sort of makes up for a lackluster chapter 2, it still feels out of left field. Also, one of chapter 2's arcs is unfinished. There was supposed to be a mission 51, which would explain a few stroy details in the game, but it was cut because of time constraints. Cutscenes and story details were released by konami though, so after finishing the game, be sure to look up these details for a better conclusion. Chapter 2 really isnt that good. But overall, I'd say the story isnt terrible, just really lacking, especially by MGS standards.

Conclusion

MGSV is an ingenious stealth game, muddled by some poor design choices and a lackluster story. So I'll sum up the game like this. If you solely play a game for gameplay and are a fan of the stealth genre, then this game is for you. If you play a game for story more than gameplay, and havent played prior MGS games, I wouldn't recommend it. Though I'd recommend MGS 1-4 as they are far more story rich. If you have played prior MGS games, I'd recommend this game either way, as it does give some story details MGS fans will want to hear, and I assume you like stealth games if you've played the other games, and the gameplay is great. So in conclusion, V delivers on gameplay but falls short on story, but I'd still recommend, as it truly is one of the best stealth games from a gameplay standpoint.

I haven't played any other MGS games before, so this is my first hand experience on the series, and I can tell you its probably the best one can have stepping into a agme series you haven't played before. I fully enjoyed the experience from start to finish, listening to all the tapes, doing the side ops, returning to mother base,and trying to get S rank for all the missions. It was in my opinion a worthy investment of your time, I hadn't known these characters before, but as soon as I began playing, I was hooked, the game has a few flaws, but its overall superbly done,the only disapointment I had was that I had not played the other MGS games and I could not understand some of the refrences to what was going on( but there was really only so little that i did not catch).

Moving on to the pros and cons

PROS:
- Good gameplay mechanic and how there is no difficulty setting, but the enemies gradually grow harder to beat.
-A really good story, there was many twists and suprises that just made the game flow smoothly, really gota give credit to the minds who were behind on this.
-Diversity in how you want to play, although this is a stealth based game, you are given the option to play the game the way you want it to( except for some total stealth missions...those require you to be extra sneaky), but other than those, there is a ton of ways to kill and have fun, some of them you probably won't even think of until you happen to see them on youtube and then realize what a wonderful way that is.
-Good voice acting( I was playing the english dubs), the characters voice acting were spot on, full of emotion and emphasis,it really fits in with the situation.
-Good amount of easter eggs and little details, making it a well polished game, I won't list them because it might be potential spoilers, but mostly you can youtube or google to know the whereabouts.

CONS:
-The FOB system, its a system that pretty much forces you to play a part in the multiplayer game mode known as FOB mode, which other people can invade your FOB and steal your staff and resources, and if you just want to enjoy the singleplayer mode, it might be a bit of a annoyance.( If you marathon the game you can probably finish the game without ever having anyone come steal your stuff)
-Online and offline mode, even though its a singleplayer game,there is a requirement to connect to the internet for some features, probably influenced by the FOB system, you can choose online and offline mode, and there are pros and cons for each, but you are punished quite a bit for using offline mode, you cannot access some features and you your resources and more limited because there is a cap for resources in offline while you have no cap in online mode, and the only pro of offline mode I have discovered so far is that there is no lag when playing due to server loading or slow internet connecction when you use your idriod, the slight loading in between the page switches are because of online mode, and you don't have to wait for that delay when you are in offline mode, the idriod switches instantly.Online mode has online mode dispatch missions and daily rewards.

TL:DR- Really enjoyable game as you can tell from the amount of hours I have, I haven't even 100% the game, only at 72% wthe moment that I'm writing this review.

review_text:
Phantom Pain is my lifestyle game. At this point, almost a decade after release, I don't think I'll ever stop playing it.


[h1]What Made Me Fall In Love[/h1]
[hr][/hr] 
This game has unexaggerably THE best third person player locomotion system in the industry, not topped since 2015, and you simply will not find any other game that gives you more movement freedom and such a rock solid, slick yet precise and robust feel to it. All options are always to your disposal, and once you learn the controls, your character will always do exactly as you say, and you can even learn to command every singular step.

That's not all for freedom, of course, since this game also gives you one of the widest and deepest arrays of possibilities to interact with enemy characters. As a war game, you can expect to be clicking on their heads with many weapon types, sure; but then there's also CQC, you can 5 string combo them unconscious, pointing your gun to interrogate them, or stealing their weapon to interrogate them with it, also grabbing them with a choke-hold, and drag them around with your pistol pulled out for scouting, or use them as a meat shield when in combat, make them trip with a leg swipe, or pushing them to the ground with a dive to their stomach, and so much more. Let's not even get started with the amount of stealth gadgets, you can't even imagine.

But primarily, what really kept me playing this game for all these years were 2 things: the FOB endgame, and the modding community.


[h1]What Kept Me Coming Back[/h1]
[hr][/hr] 
To briefly explain this game's endgame; as you can imagine, sh*t's not over after the credits roll; not even after 100% completion, because of this game's multiplayer PvP mode, FOB invasions. Many people think of it as merely an opportunity for random players to pillage one's own base and opt out of it, but this is a common misconception. Maintaining an FOB risks it being invaded, sure, but FOB soldiers and materials can't affect your single-player experience in any other way than positively, since it will give you more material storage AND personnel capacity, and anything you could lose due to invasions is strictly limited to FOB bases and capacity. Multiplayer brings over the winnings to single-player, and keeps all the losses to itself.

Even if you don't ever interact, it will provide a net positive to your base economy overall, and if you do interact, you'll quickly be convinced that the winnings always far outweigh the losses. Sure, when invading you risk being detected and so opening up a revenge invasion, but until you get to the higher ranks, most bases you'll invade will be abandoned, owned by one-time players that left them there vulnerable forever. Even if you do get the weird invasion, recouping would at most take 2 invasions. FOB invasions are really fun and also really short, and the fact that you only have 1 shot gives it real stakes, and then the even weirder defence PvP encounters are really fun, and it's very rewarding to master the possible strategies and get into the meta.

Lastly, there is an entire aspect of the game that locks a huge part of it behind FOB base capacity, and that is the R&D higher grades of weapon and item upgrading; a great way to give endgame players one last long term checklist to complete. It's genius, since you can't really see the tree much further away from where you've so far made it, so you never really feel like you're missing out on the possibility of that much higher grade levels. But even if you did know, those levels would realistically only serve to be more effective at FOB PvP, since using such high gadgets on the single-player only makes the game way easier, which is the last thing you'd want at a point when you've dominated the game enough to unlock power levels that high, paradoxically. In fact, at that point you'll naturally try to challenge yourself, by limiting the equipment you bring to missions, or outright playing OSP, and perhaps even going the extra mile: modding.


[h1]What Made Me Settle Forever[/h1]
[hr][/hr] 
MGSV has one of the best modding communities on the internet, and I mean that on many levels. The game has been cracked open in so many incredible ways, to the point there's an entire community of people pumping out content that pretty much feels like official free DLC. New missions, new Side-ops, and even new entire maps, with someone currently working on a full re-implementation of Ground Zero's Camp Omega, which is already out and available for download, with frequent upgrades and a really high quality catalogue of Side-ops.

Many dreams left over by this game's troubled development are becoming true thanks to its modding scene, which found ways to add content to the game that doesn't need to replace any existing assets; for now these are maps, missions, side-ops, textured models for NPCs and soldier characters, and we're soon to be able to add new player costumes, vehicles, weapons and items. It's wild, and it's gonna get wilder.

You can mod your game to make it the experience you want. Tune up the difficulty by increasing enemy cone distance, reducing player health, removing NPC overhead markers and heat auras, and you can even download a mod that disables health regen, and another that adds a First-Aid Spray for healing (I made that one rawr). You can also enable random item drops when incapacitating enemies, random skull invasions on free roam, and even random landing events that force you out of your routine and mixes up the experience. And if you have your own mod idea, you can probably make it yourself rather easily.


[h1]What Made Me Feel Like Home[/h1]
[hr][/hr] 
And here's the other side of the coin; not the mods, the makers. Modders' Heaven is one of the most welcoming places I've ever found on the internet, and I'm not saying that just because I'm a part of it, I promise. Modders are really open to dumb newbie questions about what's currently possible and what stands on our way, and that's precisely how I interacted with them at first, and it was because of their hospitality that I got into making my first ever mod. 

Whenever you come up with a new mod idea, you can share it with the community and enough people will give you the assistance you need all the way until you have everything you need to carry it out. And even if you're shy, there's great effort in maintaining good documentation about the community's findings and useful tools. Though there are figureheads, there's no elitism; it's just good vibes all around. Hopefully, I've convinced you to come around!

[hr][/hr] 
Metal Gear Solid V quickly became one of my favourite games the first time I played it; player freedom, base building, army recruitment and its thought provoking story about race & language, dissociative identity disorder and the fruitlessness of revenge really grabbed me and kept me engaged all the way to the credits, then its great endgame experience, PvP meta and the drive for a "true" 100% completion turned it into my comfort game and kept me playing way afterwards, and it's now been the community of those like me, who enjoyed the game so much to make new content for it and urged me to do the same, what's made me stick around for so long and feel like I'm part of something greater.

Sorry for the gayness, and thanks for reading.

review_text:
Let me preface by saying that I've not played any other Metal Gear Solid title; I have no real basis of comparison.

This is a decent stealth/cover 3rd person action/shooter.  

Pros:

The gunplay feels fairly satisfying, and while the game would certainly prefer for you to take your enemies alive and Fulton them away to safety/employment, you're not really obligated to do so.  

The weapon customization is welcome.  Many of the choices are largely cosmetic, but the ability to choose a short barrel vs a long barrel, or swap your medium-power combat rifle ammo for a smaller supply of high power sniper rifle ammo, is helpful.  The most important aspects of customization, for me, are suppressor, optics, and underbarrel attachments.

Mission rewards feel tangible.  You do something, you get paid for it.

Lots of side missions that let you experiment with different play styles.  Open world lets you wander around and kill/extract whoever you want at your own pace.  Not a great way to make money, but a good way to get personnel and resources. 

Cons:

The cover and stealth mechanics don't feel as tight as those in, say, Splinter Cell: Blacklist.  They're functional enough for the game, but I frequently find myself trying to stick to a wall and getting spotted by an enemy 150 ft away, despite the fact that every other time I've immediately covered next to that wall.

The tech tree unlocks are clearly resource/time sinks, and unlocking the various trees frequently doesn't give any new customization parts, just a new base model.  As the game has no resource or time cap, it makes everything feel a little... unimportant.

I have no idea what the ♥♥♥♥ is going on in the story.  None at all.  I'll admit I haven't prioritized it heavily, but I went from apparently nuclear powered robots the size of skyscrapers with unpronouncible names in Afghanistan, to rescuing war orphans and avoiding gratuitously nude zombie snipers in Africa, and there was something about a disease whose infection vector is the language you speak?  Like, this is all over the place.  What the hell?

The online connectivity is a little unstable.  Not usually a huge problem, but when a large portion of your cash and resources are stored online (why, exactly?), it's frustrating to suddenly lose access to them due to server instability.  Oh, also, if you are doing a FOB mission (Adversarial PvE with decent rewards) and you get disconnected?  Instant fail with maximum penalty.

Overall verdict: It's not a compelling narrative, but it's good casual fun.  I'd personally recommend picking up on sale, and playing with a gamepad.

Before I get to the review, I am aware that the game wasn't finished properly, and that Konami made some big mistakes. However, nonetheless, this game is still an experience to behold.

Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain is definitely one of my favourite games I have played this year. At the time of writing, I have been playing this since Halloween, all through November. I had a bit of a horror binge throughout October, and I should have totally been playing this instead.

MGSV has shown me some of my most enjoyed storylines, settings and characters this year. Additionally, some of the characters and themes explored within MGSV have made me feel so much more empathy, horror, dread, joy and countless other emotions. I'm not saying avoid this game. Just make sure this sort of game is for you before buying.

review_text:
MGS V was a game, that both pissed off and in retrospect impressed both it's core and new audience. The characters were mostly less engaging, the story less intense, so, even if there may have been a subtle reason for it, whether on purpose or not, the overall narrative was less engaging than the previous installments. That being said, it is still interesting enough in my opinion probably above average on the industry's scale. 

On the other hand, this may well be the best transition of a traditionally somewhat (less so in MGS 3) directed level based gameplay to a vibrant, memorable open world ecosystem. From screwing around with your horse's crap to jumping into a walker and shooting up an enemy base, there is much to do and most of it is damn fun. So if that is what you are looking for, this is an amazing game made for you.

On the other hand, Konami can be a cruel mistress and the tacked on annoying online base is just as intrusive and pace killing as it needs to be to piss you off. If the first complaint would mostly be made just by veterans of the series, this is a global annoyance. It did not ruin the game for me, but it tried hard to do so.

TL;DR Overall, if you want an open world stealth game filled with many interesting interactions and tons of options for overcoming your adversaries, this game is for you, if you want an OK narative attached, it is still probably fine. If you want a fullfledged MGS narrative, I hope you still have your PS2 around.

review_text:
The story is ludicrous fantasy, even by MGS standards, but it's the only blemish on what is undoubtedly one of the best games ever made. MGSV brings the series' unique blend of "tactical espionage action" to Africa and the Middle East, in a vast open world reminiscent of the Far Cry series.

With hundreds of pieces of equipment to chose from, you can complete each mission however you would like, be it perfect stealth or all guns blazing. There are countless ways to approach a situation, giving this game stellar replay value. Unlike other stealth/action games, MGSV doesn't pigeonhole you into a stealth mechanic: given proper preparation, all approaches are equally viables. Sometimes I'll go the "perfect stealth, no kills" route, carefully choosing camouflage, silenced tranquilizer weapons and non-lethal riot guns; wearing night-vision goggles, interrogating enemies, and scrounging for intel. Some other times, I want to get it over quick, so I drop in with a helicopter in the middle of the enemy compound, triggering a combat alert, and pumping round after round into waves of enemies with a LMG whilst wearing full body armor. Most often, I vie for stealth, but end up being detected one way or another, which spices things up.

Other highlights of the game include a kickass 80's New Wave soundtrack, [b]INCREDIBLY GORGEOUS GRAPHICS[/b] (don't forget to enable [u]Ambient Occlusion[/u] in the NVIDIA Control Panel), a fun staff management system (improving upon the system they developed for MGS: Portable Ops), decent online features (inluding free DLC you get for participating in events), tight controls, and an unbelievable attention to detail (as is cutomary with the series).

Don't forget to play [url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/311340/METAL_GEAR_SOLID_V_GROUND_ZEROES/]MGSV: GROUND ZEROES[/url] first!

review_text:
I'll start by my favourite aspect of this game: gameplay. It's by far its best feature, full of different approaches and options of advancing through the game. There's a huge amount of weapons, items and tools that grant such variety. As a stealth lover myself, I've been very pleased by the gameplay. The AI is also good, especially when they go on alert, and really act as a group, making it more believable.

Now, its story and ambientation are, IMO, good for the first half of the game (Chapter 1), but then they fall amazingly short. The story begins with lots of mysteries, which are solved little by little, but towards the end things get simply ridiculous, making it overall not a good story.

Another negative aspect of this game are its Side Ops, or secondary missions. At first they are presented with variety and they're cool, but after you've rescued your 10th prisioner, extracted your 10th soldier... it gets really repetitive. There are simply too many Side Ops with too few different types of them for them to be enjoyable.

Main missions are good, they range between infiltrations, extractions, boss fights... just that sometimes you'll need to restart the mission to go with different equipment, if you don't want to spend money on its delivery.

Also, the FOB mechanics, being forced, is just wrong. Basically, you can invade another player's base, and steal their resources and soldiers, and the same can happen to you. If you don't want to take part in it, you must play offline, which limits your max money earnings and locks challenges. I haven't been invaded ever, but just the possibility of it happening makes me hate that decision.

Overall, I give this game a recommended rating because of how fun it is to play, despite its shortcomings in some aspects. If you're a stealth fan, you'll enjoy the game for sure.

[b]Short Version[/b]: Play the game. Its probably one of the best open-world games out there. Great Characters and Story and an Engine that's easy to understand within a few minutes.

[b]Long Version[/b]:

Despite being partially incomplete, this is probably the only thing that connects makes the entire Metal Gear Timeline complete and is considered as the Final Game in Big Boss' Storyline.


[b]Gameplay[/b]: Like the game before it, The Phantom Pain uses the new FOX Engine. If you know how to actually play Metal Gear then you can easily understand the controls within a few minutes. Compared to Ground Zeroes, The FOX Engine is more developed and updated as this time the engine is tuned to for the open-world environment of Afghanistan and Africa. Mission-Wise, Its pretty well made with the right kind of difficulty and there are only a few times with some cheap deaths. Also Kojima's in the game (again).


[b]Story[/b]: [spoiler] Nine Years ago, Militaires Sans Frontières (MSF), A Private Military Group led by the Legendary Soldier Big Boss was attacked by an unknown force known as XOF. The attack led to the destruction of MSF and Big Boss fell to a coma. The Year now is 1984, Big Boss awakens and was attacked by XOF again, He escapes with the help of an old friend, Revolver "Shalashaska" Ocelot, who then brings him to Northern Kabul, Afghanistan to rescue MSF's Second-in Command, Kazuhira Miller. After his rescue, They return to Mother Base, the off-shore base of their new Private Military Group, Diamond Dogs. Back on his feet, Big Boss will take revenge on those who destroyed MSF and take vengeance for his loss. [/spoiler]


[b]Connection with the next game[/b]: If you have Ground Zeroes, You can upload your save data to The Phantom Pain. Items acquired from the game such as the Uragan-5 Pistol can be in its default form. Characters extracted from Ground Zeroes can also be transferred to TPP such as Intel Agent Kojima, Glaz, Palitz, and The undercover CIA agent.


[b]Online Features[/b]: In TPP, You can extract enemy soldiers and prisoners from fulton packs and they can be Mother Base Staff Members. These are divided into Five: Combat Unit, R&D, Base Development, Support Unit, Intel Unit, Medical Unit. The Combat Unit can be used online and offline for Dispatch Missions where they can destroy enemy storage units (Offline), Get Resources, Recruit New Members, VIP Protection, etc. There are also FOB missions where you can infiltrate an enemy base. Finally there is Metal Gear Online (MGO), where you basically battle other players in a battle royale kind of thing. However most of the time (in my experience), Servers are mostly empty or have Pro players beating the ♥♥♥♥ out of you.


In Summary, If you want to complete the Metal Gear Series or get a taste of Metal Gear and the New FOX engine then play this game.

I have played every single cannon Metal Gear released, and I have to say, this was good, but didn't live up to the hype generated by it. I wanted Metal Gear to go out with a bang, something MGS4 did perfectly, along with it's MGO2. This, felt like half a game, sold at a full game's price-tag.

THE BAD
For those who didn't know, MGS 5 had a good third of the main plot missing. Chapter 3 was cut due to the lack of development as Konami forced Kojima to finish the game for The Game Awards 2015. The first chapter was okay, but it's only until the second chapter where character developemtn begins to occur. Funnily enough, chapter 2 was mostly recycled content from chapter one, with different objectives and NPCs. MGO3 is unbalanced and currently, dead. MGO2 was the true experience of Metal Gear multiplayer, and for now, I'd simply stick with the FOB missions, if you're looking for some type of multiplayer.
The main plot of MGS 5 doesn't do what everyone wanted out of MGS 5, to explain the downfall of Big Boss. Instead, we follow 'Venom Snake' explaining how Big Boss died twice (MG1/2). That would be great and all, but I wanted a game explaining why Big Boss suddenly turned against the world. You cannot say that it was MGS3, as in PW he was all for world peace. 

THE GOOD
Metal Gear 5 is pretty much the best playing Metal Gear known to date. The graphics are gorgeous, the weapons are fun to develop (heavily enspired from PW, but PW was also great), along with Mother Base, and suits. Snake himself is very responsive and satifying to play as. The game itself is very enjoyable. 

I know the good seems outweighed by the bad, but I believe this game deserves a upvote, simply how it wasn't absolute ♥♥♥♥♥, like I know Metal Gear Survive is going to be. And yes, I do have more hours on PS4, but I felt obliged to review it on Steam aswell.

review_text:
An army without borders, a game without an ending - a tragic conclusion to the true Metal Gear series. This game was sliced in two with the precision of a high-frequency katana from Konami's apparent distaste for their employees, the franchise, and fans alike. Without the creator behind the wheel and the talent that made the world come to life, I fear profits will be the only driving force of another game sadly (cough).

Having played this from end-to-end on a PS3 from day one and now on PC since the console's untimely death, I am still utterly in love with what this game did. The game was much more in depth and intriguing without the need for 40-minute cutscenes in between 10-minute action sequences. I have always been an 80's guy (wihout bonitis) and adored being able to play some classic tunes during a long trip between destinations. Playing "Take on Me" while driving a jeep through a sun-lit desert was not lost on me.

The only quirk in this game for me (apart from having no ending) was Quiet - I understand the logic Kojima tried here, but the baser side of mankind won through for the most part (lets face it, it always will, but it got sales). Having said that, I was heart-broken at her loss and considered her an invaluable ally - this in itself, and the reason she ended up as she did in the first place was also tragic.

Don't let Konami or the lack of an ending put you off though, this game is well worth the price and it will keep you thinking after you turn it off if you're at all inclined, and keep your heart pumping with adrenaline when you're being pursued by a gigantic Metal Gear or even when you're spotted!

[b]Simply one of the best games I've played in my life![/b]

First of all, this is the first Metal Gear game that I have played, so don't expect me to compare it to other Metal Gear games. Second, for me gameplay is more important than story, so this is why I think this game is great: cause it has simply the best stealth/action 3rd person gameplay ever made

[h1]Story[/h1]

In this game, you are the mercenary legend Snake. You wake in hospital after a long come just to find out that your precious motherbase was destroyed. Then, you team up with your buddies Oceletot and Miller and try to rebuild Motherbase and puersue your dream of creating an army without borders. Along the missions you will also find out clues on who tried to kill you and destroy your base. You will meet up with interesting NPCs, like the sniper Quiet and the treacherous Skull Unit.
Now, I saw some people complaining that there is very little story on this game and so on... Well, I have to disagree. The long cutscenes are there, but they are split among the 50 missions, so to see the big picture you have to finish the entire game, instead of doing just the first missions, like most people do. The story is good and makes sense even though it has some exaggerated anime-esque stuff. Just the ending is kinda of dissappointing, like really bad... 

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]

Now, the gameplay is what makes this game amazing: you press the button to shoot and Snake shots, you press the button to run and Snake runs immediately. It might sound dumb, but it's really impressive how responsive and precise the controls are in this game. The actions are fast and quick, with no winding up moves, unlike other games. Also, every time you are performing an action, like reloading, you can immediatelly interrupt that action with a defensive one, like running or taking cover. It's a really impressive work on what the devs have done with this game's controls.

Also, bear in mind that even if the game rellies heavely on stealth, you can also try other approaches to completing missions. You can even go Rambo with heavy weapons and heavy armor. I mostly played the sniper approach, taking down enemies from a distance, it kinda of worked for me

[h1]Motherbase management[/h1]

Now this is a game inside a game. To build the new motherbase is kinda of a strategy game by itself, and it's highly addictive! You need to find resourses like oil and metal to build base platforms, then you have to recruit men to work for you, then you can build stuff like new weapons or security items... The possibilities are nearly endless in how to improve and what to build for your motherbase.

[b]I give it 5.0/5.0[/b]

review_text:
*Note: I received this product for free via purchashing a new graphics card.  The inclusion of the game had no impact on my choice.  Budget and specs did.

Colonel...Can you hear me?  As a gamer who grew up with the NES, SNES, and the introduction of the first major 3D systems (N64 and PS1), I definitely played the original MGS back in good old '98-'99.  As is widely known, the original was amazing and introduced unique gameplay elements (I'm thinking of Meryl's frequency on the jewel case, Psycho Mantis 'moving' your controller, etc.).  The core gameplay itself was fairly groundbreaking but its presentation was where the game broke true boundaries.  In any case, I've obviously been a fan of the series, and have kept up with most releases.  With this almost certainly being Kojima's last MGS foray, is it worthy of a true finale?  Does it still retain the MGS flavor? 

Yes and no.  Gone is the strong narrative and linear gameplay.  This sounds like heresy but the storyline is actually mission based.  You can also explore the game world at your whim; think of something akin to a Metal Gear GTA with bases to avoid or destroy, vehicles to shoot up or capture, etc.  Surprisingly, this doesn't feel like a Battlefield clone because the game stays close enough to its roots to give it that MGS feel; albeit in an open warzone.  There are too many details to describe how MGSV walks the line between your big budget military shooter and staying true to the Stealth-Action genre (Mother Base, FOB missions, weapons development) and they are almost all new to the franchise.  Having played the game fairly extensively, I can say with confidence that Kojima was able to create a MGS-esque type game with the aforementioned additions of generic action game type elements.  I have to admit my skepticism, but Kojima and friends pulled it off.  

With all this being said, I would recommend the game to MGS fans and action fans alike.  For better or worse, it will appease MGS fans (while feeling slightly watered-down), and invite those who prefer a more action-oriented playstyle (while feeling somewhat obscure).  Some missions do require absolute stealth (the vast majority do to get the best mission rank)  but it won't be the stunning stealth narrative you've experienced in the past.  However, I dare say it has enough of the latter peppered in to still feel like MGS.  The gameplay can be described similarly.  In fact, I was surprised by how much it did feel like MGS given it's GTA-like foundation.  It will give you plenty of Michael Bay-esque 'Wow! Explosions!' moments (Kojima does them well), while also giving you a healthly dose of the sneaking, hiding, and fear of capture that the series has evolved around (that can be optional given the aforementioned equipment development).  Frankly, that's exactly it.  MGS has evolved to accommodate modern gaming, and perhaps Konami's business model(?).  While still an enjoyable MGS game on a gameplay, presentation, and technical level, it has accomodated nonetheless.  Take it or leave it.

One last note: buy with the understanding that while the storyline reaches for excellence, it fails and is clearly unfinished (but not horrendous).  However, most other details (including the technical ones) are what you would expect from Kojima and crew; top notch.  Sad to see David Hayter not voice Snake as well.

This game shows you a lot of things that you will wonder very deeply about and uses the rest of the series, in my opinion, as an explanation without always needing to shove the answer right in your face.

MGSV is the antithesis of the linear stories of MGS past. Cut scenes are shorter and can be sparsed out due to you having a choice of when you progress to the next main story mission. This can make the plot appear jilted at times but for those who care about the creative process, you have to appreciate Kojima for trying something new. The game plays out almost in episodic fashion, which actually compliments the open world gameplay.  To me this seemed natural, and quite frankly preferred. You aren't Solid Snake sneaking your way around Shadow Moses, you are Venom Snake building an army, interacting with local private forces, maintaining commucation with Mother Base, and on a whole different level of operation than any previous game save Peace Walker. The cut scenes we get are framed brilliantly and are great to watch. The visuals are SHARP and there is a real sense of gravity in the tone of the story and the way in which the characters carry themselves. The acting is superb and pushes video games forward as a medium of storytelling. The greatest artists always are in an effort to push their own envelope, and Kojima certainly does that with his one. His biggest project yet none the less.

I've heard a lot of people say they feel the game is unfinished. It could be true to some extent, but I feel all of the story elements are there and all the arcs presented as intended. Think someone wasn't explained fully? You can see what happens to them in other games. We don't know where every character was at every point in history. That is actually the point. Have some fun with the gaps and be creative in how you imagined events unfolded. What Phantom Pain is is that its as challenging as it is engaging and it says a lot more than most people are giving it credit for.

I am not a Metal Gear Veteran. I have played one before but that was ages ago (Gamecube I think). 

This isn't one game. This is multiple games, roled into one.

The first game you will play is about a badly hurt soldier who encounters supernatural enemies, where you can never be sure what is real and what is PTSD. That was fun.
Your protagonist then recovers by the time honered method of getting shot at, mauled and generally getting abused and goes on to play the next game.

Game two is an openworld, sandbox stealth affair that takes you into afghanistan und afrika. That part almost takes itself serious if it wasn't for the serious breaks in immersion. The same soldier that just smartly called in another soldier to check the location where I just messed up my approach is completely unfazed when I use a box to hide. I whipped the box from my magic pockets and am running quite invisibly past him, because hey - whats strange in a camoflage box in the middle of the desert that wasn't there before.

Once you settled in there (and wonder idly if the PTSD soldier from game one was the same game) you get game three: half-arsed base building and online grindfest. Oh the joy! It even has microtransaction that allow you spend real money to speed up the wait for 'send X soldiers to do Y and get Z results without further interaction'! How very Farmville!

After that, the games start to mesh somewhat but it never feels like one game with different aspects but at least two horribly grafted story shooters and one farmville (you even get to collect sheep)

Everything is designed as a time-waster. Even by helicopter (which you are only a passenger in) it takes multiple minutes to get from one end of your base to the other, during which you can do little but look out the window. Missions have side objectives which are only revealed after finishing the mission so you either guess, check online or play every mission twice (or you don't give a rats ass about ratings). 

Best point of the game: There is a valid reason why the fanservice waifu 'Quiet' insists on running around in pantyhose and bra in a warzone - She is powered by photosythesis and clothes would kill her

- I wasn't used to the Metal Gear Solid universe and the story is just fruit loops crazy; none of your missions really link to any story so it's just random sneaking missions...

I sort of finished MGSV with mixed feelings. So, if I recommend it, than not wholeheartedly, but for some fun aspects of the game design and the idiosyncracities injected by the japanese producer Hideo Kojima. 

I am saying "sort of" because once the story finishes, the title screen tells me i have completed only about 58% of the game even after clearing a significant portion of side missions and all main missions relevant to the story. 

clearly, it is meant to be played on and on after story finish, perfecting your mission scores and clearing all side objectives and hunting the last animal that roams the semi-open world. 
this is strange to me and unexpected, since the other MGS game i played (MGS 4) was so story driven, to a point that it felt like watching a movie sometimes with gameplay sprinkled between rather than the other way around. 

to me this also illustrates the bipolar character of the game itself which in this open world setting seems to not fit quiet right from the story telling point of view. 
we have the stangely anachronistic world of MGS, with its typical humor (the first "end" for instance made me laugh out loud), the over the top heroes and characters, faithfull simulation of its time etc. yet, all this only exists in cut scenes wich are surprisingly disconnected from the world simulated. 
look at the motherbase for instance, many cut-scenes, many characters, but they are not actually to be found in the vast expands of the base. where are all your collegues and friends all day? where are conversations and interacions with them?

this is the main reasons i cannot wholeheartedly recommend.

let's look at the "end" of the game as another example. rarely in recent times, i have seen a more depressing conclusion to a game. i am not refering to the overall MGS ending of "truth" which was all nice and well. presumably, it satisfies die hard fans who played from MGS1 even more. 
no, I refer to [spoiler] the ending that strips off the only regular glimpse - or lets say - prospect of human interaction between missions from you. [/spoiler] 
how one could continue to play the remaining 42% is almost a mystery to me. 

yes, MGS5 presents an empty world devote of normal human interaction. the open world is not really a world. there are no stories to be discovered nothing there except plants, animals and soldiers. all there because they need to be collected as ressources.
in reality, the world only connects the tactical military simulation areas, but there is nothing in it like a simulation of a living environment. it often feels like an empty stage that would be filled in main story missions with at least a little life. 

compare it to the open world of the witcher 3 for instance which came out about the same time. there we also have a war torn country - yes, but there is life in it, too. there are actual people, third parties to be found with different stories from the main narrative. In MGS5, i have not seen a single civilian in it except burned corpse. everybody you "meet" is a soldier and will shoot at you immediately.
what difference would it have made if one of the groups of sheep that roam the world was accompanied by a shepard with dog, perhaps, or what about an actually inhabited village, i imagine... 
wasn't this even part of MGS4 where you would be punished for accidently shooting civilians?

what is working fairly well is the simulation of infiltration missions and military action in general. surely it is not an entirely realistic portrayal but it is immensly satisfying to clear out an enemy outpost with tranquilizers without being noticed once. 
granted, this will not work the first time around, since the game tends to throw a surprise boss fight in occasionally where you are than somewhat underpowered with your standard tranq gun...

well, expectations are a difficult thing. yet, i can't get over the open world failure. it seems such a waste to create a vast environment just for harvesting items. perhaps, the game Kojima imagined wasn't finished in time for release. some not fleshed out aspects of the story seem to indicate so, too. 
it is kind of sad because we can assume this is the last we saw from snake.

I know these games have a lot of fans, but as far as I'm conserned, Hideo Kojima is a hack who wants to make movies and doesn't understand the basics about games. Playing this game as a shooter is a miserable experience, you keep getting interrupted all the time by these stupid cutscenes, that try to tell this inane story about something I struggled to care about. Sure you can skip the cutscenes, but when you have to do it every 30 seconds for half of the duration of the first mission, it gets old really fast.

Now, don't get me wrong, this is a well-made game from a technical standpoint. But the way its parts are designed... The way you're punished for using your equipment (NVGs overheat, suppressors break after the first 10 shots, vehicles attract attention in an of themselves, even though they belong to the faction itself, so there would be no way for them to know who's actually behind the wheel, etc.), the way some objectives are placed, the way resource gathering is set up, even the base upgrading stuff is unintuitive, and to me felt simply tacked on for the sake of it, not having any inherent value.

And then you get to the juicy stuff, which is missions in the open world. And oh boy do they suck. This game revolves around stealth, but stealth is made unbelievably hard. You character moves very slowly, enemies are superhumanly perceptive and can hear you walk past them from dozens of meters away. If you dare and peek around a corner, they'll instantly see you from 20-30 meters. You're punished for the smallest mistakes. But if you just go "loud" and kill all of them, you're punished again (reinforcements come in in huge waves, also, you lose the ability to recruit anyone, because that requires subduing your targets and not killing them.

But what really sealed the deal, was the fact, that, as far as I can tell, the game is designed around completeling the same missions multiple times (you get tasks that you can complete in an area, but you don't have the means to do it on first try. You have to keep coming back for them. The thing is, if it was a seamless world, I'd have no problem traveling to the same location, but you actually have to go back to your base, pick your mission again, and start from the one of pre-placed insertion points (meaning you have to endure all those loading screens and cutscenes again).
